comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
DEPENDENCY NOTE: Content Hash and Canonicalization

bd-3w1.4 (content-hash deduplication) should use the same SHA-256 content hashing
as bd-3un.42 (text canonicalization pipeline). The canonicalization must happen
BEFORE hashing for dedup to work correctly:

  canonical_text = canonicalize(raw_text)
  content_hash = sha256(canonical_text)

Without canonicalization first, trivially different versions of the same content
(different whitespace, markdown formatting, etc.) would produce different hashes
and bypass dedup.

The dependency bd-3w1.4 -> bd-3un.42 ensures the canonicalization pipeline is
available when the dedup layer is implemented.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
REVISION (review pass - cross-codebase verification):

1. CANONICALIZATION-BEFORE-HASHING REQUIREMENT: The content hash MUST be computed on the canonicalized text, not the raw input. The pipeline is:
   raw_text -> canonicalize() -> canonical_text -> SHA-256 -> content_hash
   This ensures that formatting-only changes (extra whitespace, markdown formatting differences) don't trigger unnecessary re-embedding. Two documents with different raw text but identical canonical forms should produce the same hash.

2. HASH CRATE: Use sha2::Sha256 (the sha2 crate), which has hardware acceleration on x86_64 (SHA-NI extension) and ARM (SHA2 extension). Performance: ~2GB/s on modern CPUs with hardware support, ~400MB/s without. This is more than sufficient since hashing time is dominated by the much slower embedding step.

3. EMPTY CANONICAL TEXT: If canonicalization produces an empty string (low-signal content like "OK", "Done", etc.), the DeduplicationDecision should be Skip, and no content_hash should be computed or stored. Empty text is not a valid state for the content_hash field.

title: Add frankensearch-durability crate for RaptorQ integration
description:
TASK: Create the frankensearch-durability sub-crate.

This crate provides the RaptorQ integration layer for self-healing search indices. It wraps FrankenSQLite's SymbolCodec trait and provides high-level APIs for adding repair symbols to arbitrary binary files (FSVI, Tantivy segments, etc.).

CRATE STRUCTURE:
  crates/frankensearch-durability/
    Cargo.toml
    src/
      lib.rs              -- Public API re-exports
      codec.rs            -- RaptorQ codec wrapper (wraps fsqlite-core SymbolCodec)
      repair_trailer.rs   -- Binary trailer format for repair symbols appended to files
      file_protector.rs   -- High-level API: protect/verify/repair a file
      tantivy_wrapper.rs  -- Tantivy-specific segment protection
      metrics.rs          -- Durability metrics (encode/decode counts, repair events)
      config.rs           -- Durability configuration

CARGO.TOML DEPENDENCIES:
  [dependencies]
  frankensearch-core = { path = "../frankensearch-core" }
  fsqlite-core = { path = "/dp/frankensqlite/crates/fsqlite-core" }  # For SymbolCodec, RaptorQMetrics
  xxhash-rust = { version = "0.8", features = ["xxh3"] }  # Fast checksums for corruption detection
  crc32fast = "1.4"                     # CRC-32 for header validation
  tracing = "0.1"
  serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }

FEATURE FLAG:
  The durability crate is feature-gated:
  [features]
  durability = ["dep:frankensearch-durability"]

  Consumers who don't want erasure coding overhead can omit this feature.
  When disabled, all durability operations become no-ops (trait provides defaults).

DESIGN RATIONALE:
  We reuse FrankenSQLite's SymbolCodec trait rather than implementing our own RaptorQ.
  This gives us:
  1. Battle-tested encode/decode implementation
  2. Deterministic repair symbols (same seed = same symbols)
  3. Configurable overhead (DEFAULT_OVERHEAD_PERCENT = 20%)
  4. Metrics integration (RaptorQMetrics with atomic counters)
  5. Proper error handling (DecodeFailureReason enum)

  The durability crate adds a layer ON TOP of SymbolCodec:
  - RepairTrailer: binary format for appending repair symbols to existing files
  - FileProtector: high-level protect/verify/repair workflow
  - TantivyWrapper: hooks into Tantivy's segment lifecycle

KEY INSIGHT -- WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT FROM TRADITIONAL CHECKSUMS:
  CRC32/SHA-256 can DETECT corruption but cannot REPAIR it.
  RaptorQ repair symbols can both detect AND repair:
  - With R=2 repair symbols and K source symbols, any 2 corrupted source symbols can be recovered
  - With 20% overhead (R = ceil(K * 0.2)), up to 20% of the file can be corrupted and recovered
  - Recovery is information-theoretically optimal (approaches Shannon limit)
  - No coordination needed: repair symbols are deterministic from the source data

  For a 73MB vector index (100K docs x 384d x f16), 20% overhead = 14.6MB of repair symbols.
  This is stored in a sidecar file (.fsvi.fec) to avoid modifying the main index format.

File: crates/frankensearch-durability/src/lib.rs
acceptance_criteria:
1. `frankensearch-durability` crate is added with clear API boundaries for codec, trailer/segment metadata, and repair orchestration helpers.
2. Crate integrates with selected RaptorQ primitives without introducing forbidden runtime dependencies.
3. Feature flags and workspace wiring allow durability to be optional while keeping compile behavior deterministic.
4. Error taxonomy and tracing are consistent with core `SearchError` and diagnostics conventions.
5. Foundational unit tests validate crate wiring, encode/decode call paths, and failure propagation.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
REVISION (review pass - FrankenSQLite API verification):

1. DEPENDENCY ON asupersync: The actual RaptorQ encoder/decoder lives in /dp/asupersync (a sibling project), not directly in fsqlite-core. fsqlite-core provides the SymbolCodec TRAIT, but the concrete implementation wrapping the actual fountain code math is in asupersync. The durability crate has two options:
   a) Depend on fsqlite-core for the SymbolCodec trait + asupersync for the impl (2 deps)
   b) Depend only on fsqlite-core which re-exports asupersync's codec (1 dep, if re-exported)
   Check: does fsqlite-core re-export the concrete codec? If not, we need asupersync directly.

   Updated Cargo.toml:
   [dependencies]
   fsqlite-core = { path = "/dp/frankensqlite/crates/fsqlite-core" }
   asupersync = { path = "/dp/asupersync", optional = true }  # For concrete SymbolCodec impl

2. PageSymbolSink AND PageSymbolSource TRAITS: In addition to SymbolCodec, fsqlite-core also exposes PageSymbolSink and PageSymbolSource traits for streaming symbol I/O. For our use case (protecting files), we likely want to:
   - Implement PageSymbolSink for writing repair symbols to the .fec sidecar
   - Implement PageSymbolSource for reading repair symbols during decode
   This is more efficient than loading all symbols into memory at once.

3. RepairConfig IS CONST-CONSTRUCTIBLE: All creation methods are const fn. Use this:
   const DEFAULT_REPAIR_CONFIG: RepairCodecConfig = RepairCodecConfig {
       symbol_size: 4096,
       overhead_percent: 20,
       max_repair_symbols: 250_000,
       slack_decode: 2,
   };
   This enables compile-time validation and zero-cost construction.

4. RaptorQMetrics SINGLETON: FrankenSQLite maintains a global GLOBAL_RAPTORQ_METRICS atomic counter set. Our DurabilityMetrics should be SEPARATE (not sharing the global), because we want to track frankensearch-specific repair events independently of any FrankenSQLite-internal operations. The global metrics are always active and can't be disabled.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
REVISION (review pass - FrankenSQLite API verification):

1. AUTH TAG HANDLING: FrankenSQLite's SymbolRecord always includes a 16-byte auth_tag field (zeroed when auth is disabled). Our .fec sidecar format does NOT need auth tags since we're protecting local files, not transmitting over networks. The sidecar format is simpler than SymbolRecord: just raw repair symbol data without the ECS envelope. This is correct as designed.

2. SYMBOL SIZE ALIGNMENT: The symbol_size must be compatible with RaptorQ requirements. From the PipelineConfig in raptorq_integration.rs, symbol_size should be between 512 and 65536 bytes and ideally a power of 2. Our default of 4096 is correct and matches typical filesystem page size.

3. STREAMING ENCODE FOR LARGE FILES: For indices > 100MB, loading the entire file into memory for encoding is wasteful. Use memory-mapped I/O:
   - mmap the FSVI file (read-only)
   - Pass mmap slice to SymbolCodec::encode()
   - Write repair symbols to .fec via PageSymbolSink
   This keeps memory usage at O(symbol_size * R) rather than O(file_size + R * symbol_size).

4. VERIFICATION FAST PATH: The xxh3_64 hash in the .fec header enables a O(1) integrity check without decoding any repair symbols. On a 73MB file, xxh3_64 computation takes ~10ms (limited by memory bandwidth, not CPU). This fast path should be the default verification mode, with full symbol-level verification only when corruption is suspected.

5. FSVI FORMAT BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY: The .fec sidecar is a SEPARATE file that doesn't modify the FSVI format. Consumers without the 'durability' feature simply won't have .fec files. The FSVI format remains unchanged. This is a key design principle: durability is additive, not intrusive.

title: Implement self-healing Tantivy segment wrapper with RaptorQ
description:
TASK: Implement self-healing Tantivy segment wrapper with RaptorQ repair symbols.

Tantivy stores its index as multiple segment files. Each segment is a set of files (postings, positions, terms, store, fast fields). This task wraps Tantivy's segment lifecycle to add RaptorQ protection.

CHALLENGE:
  Tantivy manages its own files via the Directory trait. We can't simply append repair
  symbols to Tantivy's files because Tantivy's merge process creates/deletes segments.
  Instead, we hook into the segment lifecycle and protect completed segments.

APPROACH -- SEGMENT LIFECYCLE HOOKS:

  pub struct DurableTantivyIndex {
      inner: tantivy::Index,
      protector: Arc<FileProtector>,
      data_dir: PathBuf,
  }

  impl DurableTantivyIndex {
      /// Open a Tantivy index with durability protection
      pub fn open(data_dir: &Path, schema: Schema, config: RepairCodecConfig) -> SearchResult<Self>;

      /// After a commit, protect any new/changed segment files
      /// Called automatically after writer.commit() via a post-commit hook
      pub fn protect_segments(&self) -> SearchResult<SegmentProtectionReport>;

      /// Verify all segment files, attempt repair if corrupted
      /// Called automatically on open()
      pub fn verify_and_repair(&self) -> SearchResult<SegmentHealthReport>;

      /// Get the inner Tantivy index for search operations
      pub fn index(&self) -> &tantivy::Index;
  }

  pub struct SegmentProtectionReport {
      pub segments_protected: usize,
      pub segments_already_protected: usize,
      pub total_source_bytes: u64,
      pub total_repair_bytes: u64,
      pub encode_time: Duration,
  }

  pub struct SegmentHealthReport {
      pub segments_checked: usize,
      pub segments_intact: usize,
      pub segments_repaired: usize,
      pub segments_unrecoverable: usize,
      pub verify_time: Duration,
      pub repair_time: Duration,
  }

TANTIVY SEGMENT FILE PROTECTION:
  Each Tantivy segment has an ID (UUID) and multiple component files:
    - {segment_id}.pos   (positions)
    - {segment_id}.idx   (postings)
    - {segment_id}.term  (term dictionary)
    - {segment_id}.store (document store)
    - {segment_id}.fast  (fast fields)
    - {segment_id}.fieldnorm (field norms)

  For each segment, we create a single .seg.fec sidecar that contains repair symbols
  for ALL component files concatenated. The sidecar header maps component files to
  their byte ranges within the concatenated source:

  .seg.fec Header Extension:
    component_count: u32
    For each component:
      filename_len: u16
      filename: bytes
      offset: u64 (within concatenated source)
      size: u64

  This means one .fec file per segment, not one per component file.

LIFECYCLE INTEGRATION:
  1. ON COMMIT: After writer.commit(), enumerate new segments and protect them
  2. ON MERGE: After merge completes, protect the merged segment, remove .fec for merged-away segments
  3. ON OPEN: Verify all segments, repair any corrupted ones before search
  4. ON DELETE: When segments are garbage-collected, remove their .fec sidecars too

  The protect step is asynchronous (doesn't block the commit path) but must complete
  before the segment is considered durable.

CORRUPTED INDEX RECOVERY (from cass tantivy.rs lines 110-121):
  If a segment is corrupted beyond repair (RaptorQ fails), fall back to:
  1. Log WARN with corruption details
  2. Attempt Tantivy's built-in recovery (open with FORCE flag)
  3. If that fails, trigger a full index rebuild from the document store (FrankenSQLite)
  4. This is the fallback of last resort -- the document store IS the source of truth

  This integrates with the schema versioning from bd-3un.17: if schema_hash mismatches,
  the index is rebuilt anyway, so corruption during a schema migration is handled.

PERFORMANCE CONSIDERATIONS:
  - Tantivy indices are typically 10-100MB (much larger with store enabled)
  - Encoding a 50MB segment at 20% overhead: ~200ms (4KB symbols, parallelizable)
  - Verification (xxh3_64 fast path): ~10ms for 50MB
  - This is acceptable because it happens at COMMIT time, not QUERY time

acceptance_criteria:
1. Tantivy segment wrapper stores/loads repair symbols for segment artifacts and tracks segment metadata required for repair.
2. Segment-open path performs integrity checks and attempts automated repair before hard failure.
3. Successful repairs are swapped in atomically and preserve query availability guarantees.
4. Repair attempts/failures are logged with segment identifiers, timings, and reason codes.
5. Integration tests inject representative segment corruption and validate detect-repair-recover behavior.

title: Implement corruption detection and automatic repair pipeline
description:
TASK: Implement the corruption detection and automatic repair pipeline.

This is the high-level orchestrator that ties together the codec (bd-3w1.6), FSVI protection (bd-3w1.7), and Tantivy protection (bd-3w1.8) into a single coherent repair pipeline.

FILE PROTECTOR API:

  pub struct FileProtector {
      codec: RepairCodec,
      config: FileProtectorConfig,
      metrics: Arc<DurabilityMetrics>,
  }

  pub struct FileProtectorConfig {
      pub verify_on_open: bool,           // Default: true (verify indices on load)
      pub protect_on_write: bool,         // Default: true (generate .fec after index write)
      pub auto_repair: bool,              // Default: true (attempt repair when corruption detected)
      pub repair_log_dir: Option<PathBuf>, // Optional directory for repair event logs
      pub verify_interval_secs: Option<u64>, // Optional periodic verification (e.g., every 3600s)
  }

  impl FileProtector {
      /// Protect a file: compute repair symbols and write .fec sidecar
      pub fn protect(&self, path: &Path) -> SearchResult<ProtectionResult>;

      /// Verify a file's integrity using its .fec sidecar
      pub fn verify(&self, path: &Path) -> SearchResult<VerifyResult>;

      /// Attempt to repair a corrupted file
      pub fn repair(&self, path: &Path) -> SearchResult<RepairResult>;

      /// Full pipeline: verify, repair if needed, report
      pub fn verify_and_repair(&self, path: &Path) -> SearchResult<HealthCheckResult>;

      /// Protect all index files in a directory (FSVI + Tantivy segments)
      pub fn protect_directory(&self, dir: &Path) -> SearchResult<DirectoryProtectionReport>;

      /// Verify all protected files in a directory
      pub fn verify_directory(&self, dir: &Path) -> SearchResult<DirectoryHealthReport>;
  }

  pub struct HealthCheckResult {
      pub path: PathBuf,
      pub status: FileHealth,
      pub details: String,
  }

  pub enum FileHealth {
      Intact,
      Repaired { corrupted_bytes: usize, repair_time: Duration },
      Unrecoverable { reason: String },
      Unprotected,  // No .fec sidecar found
  }

AUTOMATIC REPAIR PIPELINE:

  The repair pipeline is invoked:
  1. On index open (if verify_on_open = true)
  2. Periodically (if verify_interval_secs is set)
  3. When a search returns unexpected errors (SearchError::IndexCorrupted)

  Pipeline steps:
  a. FAST CHECK: xxh3_64(file) vs stored source_hash (~1ms per 100MB)
     - If match: file is intact, return immediately
  b. SYMBOL-LEVEL CHECK: Compare individual source symbols against stored checksums
     - Identifies which specific 4KB blocks are corrupted
  c. REPAIR ATTEMPT: Feed surviving + repair symbols into RaptorQ decoder
     - If decode succeeds: overwrite corrupted file, verify again, log event
     - If decode fails: log error, return Unrecoverable

  All repair events are logged with full context:
    tracing::warn!(
        path = %path.display(),
        corrupted_bytes = corrupted,
        repair_symbols_used = used,
        decode_time_ms = time.as_millis(),
        "index file repaired after corruption detected"
    );

REPAIR EVENT LOG:
  When repair_log_dir is set, each repair event is appended as a JSONL record:
  {
      "timestamp": "2026-02-13T20:30:00Z",
      "path": "/data/search/vector.fast.fsvi",
      "corrupted_symbols": 3,
      "total_symbols": 18688,
      "repair_succeeded": true,
      "decode_time_ms": 450,
      "source_hash_before": "0x1234abcd",
      "source_hash_after": "0x5678ef01"
  }

  This provides an audit trail for understanding corruption patterns
  (hardware issues, filesystem bugs, etc.).

GRACEFUL DEGRADATION:
  If the durability feature is disabled at compile time, the FileProtector becomes a no-op:
  - protect() returns Ok immediately
  - verify() returns VerifyResult::Unprotected
  - repair() returns error "durability feature not enabled"

  This is implemented via a trait with a default no-op implementation and a
  #[cfg(feature = "durability")] real implementation.

INTEGRATION WITH SEARCH PIPELINE:
  The TwoTierSearcher (bd-3un.24) should:
  1. Hold an optional Arc<FileProtector>
  2. On SearchPhase::RefinementFailed, check if failure was due to index corruption
  3. If so, attempt repair and retry the search once
  4. Log the entire sequence (corruption detected -> repair -> retry -> success/failure)

File: frankensearch-durability/src/file_protector.rs
acceptance_criteria:
1. Corruption detection pipeline scans supported artifact types and produces normalized health states.
2. Automated repair orchestration executes deterministic repair order with bounded retries and explicit fallback/degraded outcomes.
3. Unrecoverable cases surface clear incident records and safe failure semantics to callers.
4. Pipeline provides dry-run/diagnostic mode plus actionable execution mode.
5. Integration/e2e tests cover single-artifact, multi-artifact, concurrent-access, and unrecoverable corruption scenarios with replayable logs.

REVISION (review pass 7 - error type dependency):

ADDED bd-3un.2 (core error types) as a blocking dependency. The repair pipeline introduces new error variants:
- SearchError::IndexCorrupted { path, expected_crc, actual_crc }
- SearchError::RepairFailed { reason }
- SearchError::DurabilityDisabled

These must be defined in the shared error enum (bd-3un.2) so that consumers can pattern-match on them uniformly. The repair pipeline returns these errors through the standard SearchResult type.

NOTE: bd-3un.2's revision already includes feature-gated error variants for storage/durability. The dependency ensures the error types are implemented before the repair pipeline that uses them.

title: CRITICAL: federated min_indices is a STOP-QUOTA not a floor — default config cancels every shard after the first reply, and partial federation is invisible to the caller
description:
Found by user-directed semantic-path review (MossyPine, 2026-07-31); both halves personally re-verified at origin/main federated.rs.

HALF A — stop-quota (federated.rs:343-345 + default at :76): collect_shard_results drains its ready-batch loop then does 'if self.config.min_indices > 0 && shard_results.len() >= self.config.min_indices { break; }'. Dropping 'pending' on break CANCELS every still-in-flight shard. The same field is documented at :63-64 as 'Minimum number of indices that must respond successfully' and used that way as a post-hoc floor at :216-221. One knob does two contradictory jobs: floor AND ceiling. The Default impl sets min_indices: 1 (:76), so EVERY out-of-the-box FederatedSearcher breaks on the first shard completion. A 5-shard deployment returns results fused from whichever single shard replied first; recall silently drops to ~1/5 and is nondeterministic run-to-run (fastest shard wins).

HALF B — invisible partial federation (federated.rs:195-235, :323-339, :348-352): search returns SearchResult<Vec<FederatedHit>>. Shard failures and timeouts are swallowed into tracing::warn!, and first_shard_error is DISCARDED whenever shard_results is non-empty. FederatedHit carries per-doc appeared_in but there is no per-QUERY record of which shards were queried, answered, failed or timed out. A 10-shard deployment with 7 shards down returns Ok(hits) indistinguishable from a healthy response; dashboards show zero errors and appeared_in looks correct because it only lists shards that DID answer. Half A makes partial responses the NORMAL path rather than an incident path, so Half B hides the routine case.

FIX A: add a distinct wait_for_indices: usize (default usize::MAX) and gate the break on it; leave min_indices as the floor only. NOTE the existing test federated.rs:1175 scatter_gather_returns_early_when_min_indices_is_satisfied ASSERTS the current behavior and must be re-pointed at the new knob, or the fix will read as a regression.
FIX B: return (Vec<FederatedHit>, FederatedResponseStats) carrying queried/completed/failed/timed_out; even a usize pair unblocks caller-side alerting.
close_reason: Fixed at 2b1db60f: wait_for_indices gather ceiling (default wait-for-all), min_indices floor-only, FederatedResponse coverage record makes partial federation visible. Red-proofed at parent 40ebb6d9.

title: fsfs async retry loops must not block executor threads
description: Deadlock-finder audit found production std::thread::sleep calls inside async fsfs runtime paths. run_daemon_command and one-shot indexing retry backoffs accept &Cx and already await async operations, so blocking sleeps can pin executor threads and delay cancellation/progress under load. Acceptance: replace async-context blocking sleeps with asupersync wall-clock sleeps, leave synchronous daemon connect retry unchanged, add/keep a deterministic source-level proof that production async sleeps no longer use std::thread::sleep, and validate with scoped fsfs tests plus workspace check/clippy/fmt through rch.
close_reason: Fixed: async fsfs daemon polling and embedding retry backoffs now use asupersync wall-clock sleep instead of blocking std::thread::sleep, daemon observes Cx cancellation, synchronous daemon-connect retry remains intentionally blocking, regression test covers the source-level contract. title: Frozen ModelArtifactManifest and complete embedding-space provenance for every local/native backend
description:
FOUNDATIONAL IDENTITY AND LOCAL/NATIVE PROVENANCE. Create one versioned, digest-pinned ModelArtifactManifest contract shared by Model2Vec, native MiniLM safetensors, FastEmbed/ONNX, and explicit test/control models. For every artifact set record provider/backend, immutable upstream revision and credential-free URLs, file roles, exact sizes and SHA-256, license metadata, tokenizer/vocabulary identity, preprocessing/canonicalization/truncation, query/document instructions, pooling, normalization, output dimension, weights format, projection ancestry and conformance-vector digest. Runtime EmbeddingSpaceIdentity is derived from verified manifest plus implementation/protocol revision, never from a mutable directory name or display string. Detection rejects partial, symlinked, role-colliding, hash/size-drifted, unsupported or noncanonical artifacts. CI verifies vendored/embedded manifest bytes and forbids network in build.rs. Golden texts/vectors define when implementations may intentionally share an identity.

This bead also defines canonical producer-attestation envelopes, trust levels and validation primitives consumed by remote integrations, but it does not own concrete provider/daemon transport authentication, per-response admission, requested-mode policy, persistent FSVI enforcement or CASS lifecycle. Those terminal responsibilities are bd-remote-api-space-attestation-fcfj, bd-lk1g, bd-p6z6.2, bd-core-vector-space-search-guard-ctzo and bd-jbfg. Caller-supplied identity is never itself producer proof.
design: Use four deliberately separate versioned contracts rather than one overloaded revision: EmbeddingSpaceIdentityV1 for the mathematical input-to-vector map; EmbeddingProducerAttestationV1 for backend/protocol/numeric implementation plus a pinned golden-vector certificate; EmbeddingInputContractV1 for outer canonicalization, content selection, chunking, query/document instructions and doc-id semantics; and VectorStorageIdentityV1 for FSVI encoding and quantization. Canonically serialize fixed-tag, length-prefixed fields with domain-separated SHA-256; persist canonical bytes plus fingerprint; reject unknown schemas, duplicate or missing artifact roles, noncanonical encodings, and bytes/fingerprint disagreement. Space identity binds logical model, immutable revision, ordered role-tagged artifact digests, tokenizer/vocab/config, model preprocessing, sequence/truncation/padding, instructions, pooling, normalization, dimension and structured MRL/projection ancestry. HashControl binds algorithm/version, seed, feature/tokenization/signing/normalization rules and can never attest semantic availability. Embedder outputs become identity-bound values; wrappers forward or structurally derive identity. Compatible implementations require an explicit conformance certificate, never name or dimension inference. Define VerifiedLocal, VerifiedRemote and AssumedRemote vocabulary plus canonical remote attestation validation inputs; concrete response authentication/admission remains in the dependent terminal beads. Build scripts remain network-free and logs remain bounded/redacted.
acceptance_criteria: All production local/native embedders load only from a verified versioned manifest and expose complete canonical EmbeddingSpaceIdentityV1 plus producer attestation; every returned local/native vector is bound to both. Exact-byte manifest fixtures and streaming size/hash/license/schema tests cover every backend. A property matrix mutates every identity, producer, input and storage field and proves the fingerprint changes; role-order canonicalization, duplicate/missing roles, noncanonical encoding, unknown schema, bytes/digest disagreement, symlinks, altered tokenizer/preprocessing/pooling/normalization/instructions/dimension, hash seed/features/rules, wrapper forwarding and structured MRL derivation are tested. Golden-vector certificates define allowed compatible implementations. Remote envelope/trust DTOs and validators reject missing/malformed/noncanonical fingerprints, caller-only claims and trust-level confusion, and provide the exact primitives consumed by the dependent API/daemon beads; this foundation does not claim a concrete provider response is authenticated. No production compatibility inference remains from ID, dimension, filename or display revision. Build scripts are network-free and structured logs are bounded/redacted. Closure records the exact dependent bead split and does not close any terminal remote/index/CASS requirement by implication.
close_reason: Canonical local/native model manifest and identity foundation complete; bundled-model CI integration landed at ff346052 with full recorded remote proof and explicit downstream scope split.

title: Score-bit-parity ENVELOPE: Quill's fused per-term field expansion diverges from the oracle at ULP scale as query leaf count grows
description: Campaign findings 5-8 (bd-bsjw grammar extension, 2026-08-02), one coherent class after four discrimination rounds: with parenthesised groups inflating query leaf counts, Quill diverges from the oracle by 1-2 ULPs (RankMismatch on identical docs, e.g. 0x415583bd vs bc; 0x41673288 vs 87; 0x4121c1e0 vs de; 0x41addfb9 vs ba — all pinned in the discrimination log on this bead's thread). ROOT: Quill's Term scorer FUSES each term's [content, 2.0x title] expansion into one sum contributing a single float per term, while the pinned oracle expands every unfielded term into a two-clause boolean (content branch + Boost(title,2) branch) and accumulates 2N interleaved clause outputs — different summation ASSOCIATION, so rounding diverges once enough leaves accumulate (reproduced at 8 leaves, depth-1 grouping, no boosts, no negation, pure Should). SECONDARY members of the class, each independently pinned: (a) a single top-level leaf boost over the multi-field expansion diverges 1 ULP (multiply/rounding order); (b) mixed-occur nesting (AND/NOT inside groups) cannot flatten and diverges 1-2 ULPs; (c) the oracle DROPS all negations inside BOOSTED groups via lenient-parse fallback — a MEMBERSHIP change, pinned three ways in frankensearch-lexical stacked_negation_prefixes test. DOCTRINE IMPLICATION: the language contract's 'exact Tantivy score-bit parity' is UNACHIEVABLE for long/composite queries without either (1) restructuring Quill's term scorer to emit per-field contributions in the oracle's interleaved order (perf-relevant: that shape is what Quill's fused loop optimizes away), or (2) amending the contract with a ULP-scale tolerance class (ScoreEpsilon exists in the comparator taxonomy but ComparatorConfig::default is zero-tolerance). This is an OWNER decision between conformance strictness and the fused-scorer design. Until then the bsjw generator fences groups and boosts (pointer comments at the fence sites); landed value retained: the Should-of-Should flatten (oracle-association for spliceable shapes) and the bd-htcun nesting fix are correct and tested independently of this envelope.

title: CRITICAL: RefreshWorker merges old-generation vectors with newly-embedded ones and re-stamps the index — a same-dimension model upgrade silently corrupts the whole corpus
description:
Found by user-directed review sweep (MossyPine, 2026-07-31); merge path personally re-verified at origin/main refresh.rs:604-646.

DEFECT: RefreshWorker is the single writer for all vector indices. It calls RAW embed_batch (refresh.rs:415,447) and persists the result, stamping only embedder id() — despite core/traits.rs:212-218 stating explicitly that embed()/embed_batch() are raw inference primitives, that any caller PERSISTING vectors must use embed_bound(), and that id() never establishes vector-space compatibility. rebuild_index then reads untouched documents' vectors straight out of the existing index (refresh.rs:626 vector_at_f32) and adds them beside the freshly embedded ones, NEVER comparing fast_index.embedder_id() against self.fast_embedder.id() (nor the quality pair).

FAILURE (routine, not adversarial): the fast model is upgraded to a new revision with the SAME id() and SAME dimension — e.g. a pooling or normalization change. The next refresh cycle embeds queued docs in the NEW space, merges every other document's OLD-space vector at :626, and re-stamps the index with the current id(), erasing the evidence. Cosine similarity is then computed across two incompatible spaces: the majority of the corpus returns near-random rankings. SemanticReadiness::IdentityMismatch can never fire because the index self-reports as current. A dimension CHANGE fails closed; the same-dimension case — the common one — fails OPEN.

ROOT CAUSE: vector-space identity was enforced in the type system (BoundQueryEmbedding/embed_bound) but the single production writer bypasses it and asserts identity with a string that the trait contract says proves nothing.

FIX (minimal): in rebuild_index, compare fast_index.embedder_id() to self.fast_embedder.id() (and the quality pair) BEFORE the merge branch and return Err on mismatch, forcing a full rebuild rather than a mixed-space merge. Proper fix folds into bd-9xuj T2's write-side slice (create_v2 + space fingerprints), which makes this class unrepresentable.

CROSS-CUTTING: this is the same failure as the recovery-planner fail-open (see the semantic_available/coverage bead) at two layers — refresh writes an index whose space identity is asserted only by a meaningless string, and the planner then reads that same self-reported string, so the planner STRUCTURALLY CANNOT detect the mixed-space index this produces.
close_reason: Fixed at tip by 5386b39e (fix(fusion): refuse unsafe legacy refresh merges): rebuild_index no longer merges prior-generation vectors at all — ensure_no_existing_generation_for_merge() refuses any cycle over a non-empty generation (pre-drain + re-checked in rebuild_index to close the publisher race), with typed incremental_merge_refusal. The bead's exact failure (same id(), same dimension, changed space) is pinned red by test same_id_same_dimension_changed_space_cannot_bypass_identityless_refusal; refusal also proven not to mutate the active generation, not resurrect tombstones/WAL residents, and not exhaust retry budget. Verified 39/39 refresh tests green at 197ce19b (this session, 2026-08-03). Residual (re-enabling identity-BOUND incremental merge via embed_bound/create_v2 space fingerprints) is bd-9xuj T2 write-side scope, not this defect.

title: Implement off-policy evaluation for safe ranking changes
description:
Implement offline ranking evaluation infrastructure using Inverse Propensity Scoring (IPS) and Doubly Robust (DR) estimators. This enables estimating the impact of ranking algorithm changes (new K, new blend_factor, new reranker model) using historical search logs BEFORE deploying online.

Graveyard entry: §12.12 Off-Policy Evaluation (IPS/DR)
EV score: 6.0 (Impact=3, Confidence=3, Reuse=4, Effort=3, Friction=2)
Priority tier: B (requires evidence ledger from bd-3un.39 first)

Architecture:
pub struct OffPolicyEvaluator {
    logging_policy: Box<dyn RankingPolicy>,   // The policy that generated the logs
    target_policy: Box<dyn RankingPolicy>,    // The proposed new policy
    clipping_threshold: f64,                   // Max IPS weight (default 100.0)
}

pub trait RankingPolicy: Send + Sync {
    fn score(&self, query: &str, doc_id: &str) -> f64;
    fn propensity(&self, query: &str, doc_id: &str, rank: usize) -> f64;
}

Estimators:
1. IPS (Inverse Propensity Scoring):
   estimated_reward = (1/N) * sum(reward_i * target_propensity_i / logging_propensity_i)
   - Unbiased but high variance
   - Clipping: cap importance weight at threshold to reduce variance

2. DR (Doubly Robust):
   estimated_reward = IPS_term + control_variate_from_reward_model
   - Variance <= IPS variance (provable)
   - Requires reward model (can use NDCG@10 from golden corpus)

3. Effective Sample Size (ESS):
   ESS = (sum(w_i))^2 / sum(w_i^2)
   - Reject estimate if ESS < 100 (insufficient overlap)

Integration:
- Consumes evidence ledger (bd-3un.39) as log source
- Consumes test fixture corpus (bd-3un.38) for reward labels
- Produces: estimated NDCG@10 delta, confidence interval, ESS

Budgeted mode: Offline only (no runtime cost). Memory proportional to log size.

Fallback: Don't use OPE estimates; rely on golden-check corpus only.

File: frankensearch-fusion/src/ope.rs (offline evaluation module)

Reference: Dudik et al. (2011) "Doubly Robust Policy Evaluation", Swaminathan & Joachims (2015) "Batch Learning from Logged Bandit Feedback"
Baseline comparator: Golden-check-only validation (current bd-3un.38)
acceptance_criteria:
1. The feature is fully implemented according to this bead design, scope, and referenced files or modules.
2. Integration with dependent components is complete and behavior remains correct across normal and degraded flows.
3. Edge and error cases are explicitly handled with deterministic outcomes and clear reason codes or errors.
4. Unit and integration tests (and e2e where relevant) are added, passing, and include detailed structured logging assertions.
5. Performance and resource expectations in the bead are validated and documented with reproducible evidence.

REFINEMENT PASS 1 — Architecture clarifications and integration notes:

1. EVIDENCE LEDGER CLARIFICATION: This bead depends on bd-3un.39 (structured tracing) as the source of historical search logs. The evidence ledger is the structured tracing output (JSON spans) from the search pipeline. OPE reads these logs offline to evaluate proposed ranking changes.

3. OFFLINE-ONLY DESIGN: This is an analysis tool, not a runtime component. It lives in a separate binary (examples/ope_eval.rs or tools/ope_eval.rs) that reads serialized evidence logs and outputs a report. No impact on search latency or correctness.

4. PRACTICAL USAGE: An engineer would run this before deploying a ranking change:
   cargo run --example ope_eval -- --log-dir ./evidence/ --new-k 80 --new-blend 0.6
   Output: Estimated NDCG@10 delta: +0.03 (95% CI: [-0.01, +0.07]), ESS: 234, Recommendation: DEPLOY

5. TEST REQUIREMENTS (covered by bd-3un.31/32): Add tests for:

1. ADDED bd-3un.5 and bd-3un.2 DEPENDENCIES: The OPE evaluator works with ranked lists of ScoredResult and computes NDCG over FusedHit-style outputs (from bd-3un.5). Error handling for the offline evaluation binary needs SearchError (from bd-3un.2).

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
REVIEW FIX — Formula corrections and propensity clarification:

1. PROPENSITY CLARIFICATION: The RankingPolicy trait's propensity() method conflates two distinct concepts:
   - Policy propensity: P(doc placed at rank | query, policy) — probability the ranking policy places this document at this rank
   - Position bias: P(user examines rank) — probability the user looks at position `rank`

   For IPS in ranking evaluation, we need POLICY propensity (not position bias). Clarify:

   pub trait RankingPolicy {
       /// Probability that this policy places doc_id at the given rank for this query.
       /// For deterministic policies: 1.0 if doc is at that rank, 0.0 otherwise.
       /// For stochastic policies: the probability under the policy's randomization.
       fn rank_probability(&self, query: &str, doc_id: &str, rank: usize) -> f64;
   }

2. DOUBLY ROBUST FORMULA (complete):
   DR = (1/N) * Σᵢ [ r_hat(xᵢ) + wᵢ * (rᵢ - r_hat(xᵢ)) ]
   where:
     rᵢ = observed reward (e.g., NDCG@10 for query i)
     r_hat(xᵢ) = reward model prediction (e.g., predicted NDCG based on score features)
     wᵢ = π_target(aᵢ|xᵢ) / π_logging(aᵢ|xᵢ) = importance weight
     xᵢ = query features, aᵢ = ranking action (the full ranked list)

   Properties:
   - If reward model is perfect (r_hat = r): DR = E[r] regardless of weights (unbiased)
   - If weights are correct: DR is unbiased regardless of reward model
   - Variance(DR) <= Variance(IPS) (always, by construction)

3. CLIPPING DEFAULT: Change from 100.0 to 10.0. At w=100, a single observation gets 100x the influence of a normal observation — this is rarely desirable. With w=10, max influence ratio is 10:1, which provides meaningful variance reduction while preserving most of the bias correction.

4. ESS CONTEXT: Add note that the ESS < 100 threshold assumes at least 500 total queries in the log. For smaller logs, scale proportionally: ESS_threshold = max(20, total_queries / 5).

5. TEST REQUIREMENT ADDITIONS:
   - Known-answer test: create synthetic data where true policy value is computable, verify OPE estimate within CI
   - Propensity ratio: for identical policies (target = logging), all weights = 1.0, IPS = simple mean
   - Clipping effect: with clipping=10, max weight in output is 10.0

comments.text:
PERFORMANCE PROOF-LANE PROTOCOL (bd-bobf gate)

This bead is subject to the bd-bobf performance proof-lane gate. Before any performance-critical change in this bead's implementation may be considered release-ready, the following evidence artifacts must be produced and verified:

1. BASELINE BENCHMARK: Run criterion benchmarks (bd-3un.33) capturing p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (ops/sec), and peak memory (RSS delta) for the hot path this bead optimizes. Record results in data/perf-evidence/<bead-id>-baseline.json.

2. PROFILE HOTSPOT EVIDENCE: Profile the hot path using cargo flamegraph or perf. Identify top-5 hotspot functions by cumulative time. Record in data/perf-evidence/<bead-id>-hotspots.txt.

3. OPPORTUNITY SCORE: Compute opportunity_score = (baseline_p95 / optimized_p95). Must be >= 2.0 to justify the optimization complexity. If < 2.0, document why the optimization is still warranted (e.g., tail latency improvement, memory reduction).

4. ISOMORPHISM PROOF NOTE: Document that the optimization preserves result ordering, tie-breaking determinism, floating-point reproducibility, and RNG seed behavior. Specifically: "Given identical inputs and configuration, the optimized path produces bit-identical output rankings as the unoptimized path." If not bit-identical (e.g., FP reordering), document the acceptable divergence bound.

5. GOLDEN OUTPUT VERIFICATION: Run the fixture corpus queries (bd-3un.38) through both the baseline and optimized paths. Assert identical result sets (or document bounded divergence). Include rollback command: `git revert <commit>` or feature flag to disable.

STATUS: Evidence collection is deferred until the implementation is merged and benchmarks can be run against real workloads. This comment establishes the required evidence format for release-gate compliance (bd-ehuk).

title: Graduate SIMD unsafe from PERF_ONLY to REFACTORABLE: core::simd under target_feature emits identical AVX2 with zero unsafe

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
UNSAFE AUDIT of the whole workspace (rust-unsafe-code-exorcist, solo tier, audit-only) 2026-07-27 TealIsland. ~103 unsafe blocks enumerated by ast-grep per kind (not grep), classified A/B/C.

(A) STRICTLY_UNAVOIDABLE — 19 sites, all keep their unsafe:
- MEMORY MAPPING, 19 of them: durability/file_protector.rs (10), durability/fsvi_protector.rs (6), index/lib.rs (2), index/mapped_file.rs (1). Mmap::map / MmapMut::map_mut are unsafe because the OS lets another process truncate or rewrite the file while a live &[u8] points into it; that is a data race Rust's model cannot express away. FALSIFICATION: no crate offers a safe wrapper (memmap2, memmap, mmap-rs all expose it as unsafe) because none can — the invariant is external to the process. The only alternative is to stop mmapping and read into owned buffers, which forfeits zero-copy, lazy paging, and page-cache sharing across processes. That is a real performance loss, so it is explicitly out of scope for the user's "without hurting performance" constraint.
- RAW SYSCALL FFI, 2: fsfs/concurrency.rs libc::kill (liveness probe), fsfs/runtime.rs Command::pre_exec + libc::prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG). pre_exec is unsafe because the closure runs post-fork where only async-signal-safe calls are legal; the existing SAFETY comment already cites signal-safety(7) and is correct.

(B) PERF_ONLY — the SIMD bulk, ~80 sites: index/simd.rs (55), embed/simd.rs (3), core/simd.rs (2), embed/hash_embedder.rs (2), plus bench-only kernels. Hand-written AVX2 via core::arch intrinsics.

★★ THE KEY FINDING — MOST OF (B) SHOULD GRADUATE TO (C), AT ZERO PERFORMANCE COST.
The project is pinned to nightly (rust-toolchain.toml, nightly-2026-07-20), which makes core::simd (portable_simd) available. A portable-SIMD kernel written INSIDE a #[target_feature(enable="avx2,fma")] function needs NO unsafe at all — Simd::from_slice is a safe bounds-checked load and all arithmetic is safe operators — and it compiles to the same instructions.

CODEGEN EVIDENCE (rustc 1.99.0-nightly, --edition 2024 -O -C target-cpu=x86-64-v3, same file, both functions no_mangle so neither is DCE'd):
  dot_intrinsics (unsafe core::arch)  : 65 asm lines, vfmadd=9, vmovup=9
  dot_portable   (safe core::simd)    : 77 asm lines, vfmadd=9, vmovup=9
IDENTICAL hot loop — same 9 fused multiply-adds, same 9 unaligned vector loads. The 12 extra lines are the horizontal reduction tail (reduce_sum vs a hand-rolled hadd chain), which executes ONCE PER CALL rather than per element.

★ WHY THIS DOES NOT CONTRADICT OUR EXISTING EVIDENCE. PERF_LEDGER records AVX2 runtime-dispatch kernels beating portable SIMD 2.3-2.6x, and NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE records the wide::u32x8 banded-crossover result. Both of those measured the `wide` CRATE, which is stable-Rust portable SIMD compiled for the BASELINE target — it cannot emit AVX2/FMA at all unless the whole binary is built with -C target-cpu. That is precisely why it lost. core::simd inside an explicit #[target_feature] function is a different mechanism: the compiler is told avx2+fma are present for that function only, so it emits vfmadd. Do NOT dismiss this lever by analogy to the `wide` results — they are not the same experiment.

CAVEAT, STATED PLAINLY: this is a CODEGEN comparison, not a benchmark. Identical instruction counts predict no regression but do not prove one. Per the skill's own rubric a (B)->(C) graduation requires criterion + hyperfine + flamegraph numbers. Nothing should land on the strength of the asm diff alone. Second caveat: portable_simd is an UNSTABLE nightly feature, so adopting it accepts API-churn risk; the project already pins nightly and already references core::simd in an embed bench comment, so the exposure is bounded but real.

CONCRETE FIRST TARGET when this is picked up: embed/hash_embedder.rs jl_accumulate_lanes_avx2. It is ALREADY a #[target_feature] fn yet still needs unsafe purely for the intrinsic calls; with u64x4 the load becomes u64x4::from_array(*states) (safe), the xor/shift chain becomes safe operators, and the movemask becomes a safe mask op. It is small, self-contained, has an existing bench (embed/benches/hash_embed.rs), and would prove the technique end-to-end on real project code.

(C) REFACTORABLE, actionable today — NONE outside the SIMD bulk. Every non-SIMD site is either mmap or raw-syscall FFI, i.e. genuinely (A). So there is no free zero-cost unsafe removal sitting in the tree right now; the whole opportunity is the SIMD graduation above.

RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE: (1) convert jl_accumulate_lanes_avx2 as the pilot, bench before/after with the existing harness; (2) if neutral-or-better, convert index/simd.rs kernel by kernel, each with its own paired bench, never in bulk; (3) leave the 19 mmap sites and 2 FFI sites permanently (A) with their SAFETY comments hardened; (4) consider a safe-only cargo feature only if a kernel is found where portable SIMD genuinely regresses.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
EXECUTION OUTCOME 2026-07-27 (TealIsland): the SIMD conversion is REJECTED, and NOT on performance grounds. The (B)->(C) graduation recorded earlier is technically real but must not be acted on yet. Recording the reason so nobody re-runs this investigation.

★ THE BLOCKER IS PACKAGING, NOT SPEED. core::simd requires a crate-root #![feature(portable_simd)], which is an UNSTABLE nightly feature. Measured facts about this workspace:
- frankensearch uses ZERO #![feature(...)] attributes today (verified by rg across crates/ and frankensearch/).
- Neither sibling dependency does either: asupersync and frankensqlite both have no feature attributes at their lib roots.
- frankensearch-embed and frankensearch-index are BOTH in the documented crates.io publish sequence (README: core, embed, index, lexical, fusion, storage, frankensearch).
So the crates are, as far as LANGUAGE FEATURES go, stable-compatible today. The nightly pin in rust-toolchain.toml is a toolchain choice (edition 2024 has been stable since 1.85), not a language-feature dependency.

Adding #![feature(portable_simd)] would therefore PERMANENTLY force every downstream crates.io consumer onto nightly — for a library whose entire purpose is to be a drop-in dependency — in exchange for removing the `unsafe` keyword from SIMD kernels that are already runtime-dispatched behind is_x86_feature_detected, individually SAFETY-commented, benchmarked, and consciously classified (B) PERF_ONLY. That is a bad trade and I am not making it.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES, with reasons:
- Gate portable_simd behind a cargo feature (e.g. nightly-simd): doubles the kernel code paths and the test matrix permanently, for zero user-visible benefit. Strictly worse than either endpoint.
- Convert only non-published crates: the SIMD lives in embed/index/core, all published. Nothing meaningful is left.
- Build the whole binary with -C target-cpu=native so `wide` emits AVX2: forfeits the portable binary and the runtime dispatch that lets one build serve older CPUs. Contradicts the existing dispatch design.

★ TRIGGER TO REVISIT: portable_simd stabilization. When it lands on stable, this becomes a straightforward win with the codegen evidence already in hand — identical hot loop (vfmadd=9, vmovup=9 both ways). At that point the pilot is embed/hash_embedder.rs jl_accumulate_lanes_avx2: u64x4::from_array(*states) for the load, safe ^ and << >> operators for the xorshift chain, and a safe mask op replacing _mm256_movemask_pd. It is bit-exact BY CONSTRUCTION (xorshift and the odd-lane count are exact integer ops, and the per-dim contribution is a sum of +/-1) but MUST still be differentially tested, because hash-embedder determinism is a documented contract, not a nicety.

WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD — the (A) sites are now genuinely auditable. Commit 41d8531e hardens every Mmap::map site in the durability layer: file_protector.rs went 3 -> 6 SAFETY comments, fsvi_protector.rs 1 -> 3. Five sites had NO comment at all. Two more said "SAFETY: mmap is read-only", which actively misstates the invariant — our access mode is not what makes the call sound. The real hazard is that the kernel lets any other process truncate or rewrite the file while the mapping is live, mutating bytes behind a live &[u8]; that is an OS-level cross-process property Rust cannot express, which is exactly why no crate offers a safe wrapper. What upholds it here is the VERIFICATION CONTRACT rather than exclusion: bytes read through these mappings are checked against the trailer CRC32/xxh3 witnesses or a recorded digest before publication, so a concurrent writer produces a verification failure, never a silent bad repair. Gates: 139/139 durability lib tests, clippy --no-deps -D warnings clean, rustfmt clean; the diff is 100% comment lines (verified: zero non-comment added lines), so the file's 30 pre-existing UBS criticals (panic!/unwrap in test code) are untouched and none are mine.

REMAINING (A) GAP: crates/frankensearch-index/src/lib.rs has one uncommented mmap site (the MmapMut::map_mut path). Deliberately NOT touched — lib.rs is one of the six entangled index sources carrying BrownCoyote's bd-u3wt tranche plus my uncommitted bd-tqhc 2a hunks. Fold it into the 2a landing window.

title: Integrate franken_networkx for graph-aware ranking signal and result diversification
description:
When franken_networkx matures, add a structural/graph-based ranking signal as a third input to the RRF fusion pipeline alongside lexical (BM25) and semantic (cosine). Document collections often have implicit relationship structure — citations, cross-references, thread links, file-system adjacency, import graphs — and exploiting this structure improves search quality for navigational and exploratory queries.

PREREQUISITE — DOCUMENT GRAPH CONSTRUCTION:
Before graph algorithms can run, frankensearch needs a document graph. The graph is:
- Nodes: documents in the index (identified by doc_id)
- Edges: relationships between documents, with types and weights
- Edge sources (consumers provide these, frankensearch doesn't infer them):
  a. Explicit: consumer calls graph_builder.add_edge(doc_a, doc_b, EdgeType::Reference, weight=1.0)
  b. Batch: consumer provides adjacency list at index time
  c. File-system: fsfs (bd-2hz) can derive edges from directory co-location and import statements

New type in frankensearch-core:
  pub struct DocumentGraph {
      adjacency: HashMap<DocId, Vec<(DocId, EdgeType, f32)>>,  // neighbor, type, weight
      node_count: usize,
  }
  pub enum EdgeType { Reference, CoLocation, Import, ThreadReply, Similar, Custom(String) }

The DocumentGraph is optional — frankensearch works without it (current behavior). When provided, the graph ranking signal activates automatically.

THREE GRAPH RANKING APPLICATIONS (phased implementation):

PHASE 1 — Query-Biased PageRank (highest impact, implement first):
- Standard PageRank computes global importance. Query-biased (Personalized) PageRank seeds the random walk from query-matched documents, computing importance RELATIVE to the query.
- Algorithm: PPR with restart probability α=0.15, seeded at documents matching the query
- Output: per-document PPR score in [0, 1], feeds into RRF as a third ranking
- Why it helps: boosts documents that are structurally central NEAR the query topic, not just globally important
- Computational cost: O(|E| * iterations), typically 10-20 iterations, <10ms for 10K-node graphs
- franken_networkx dependency: PageRank with personalization vector

PHASE 2 — Result Diversification via Graph Clustering:
- After RRF fusion produces a ranked list, check if top-K results are concentrated in one graph cluster
- Use spectral clustering or community detection (Louvain/Leiden) to identify clusters
- If >60% of top-10 results are from the same cluster, replace some with representatives from other clusters
- This is a POST-FUSION re-ranking step, not a fusion input
- franken_networkx dependency: community detection (Louvain), spectral clustering

PHASE 3 — Document Expansion (query-time neighbor boosting):
- When a query strongly matches document A (high semantic + lexical score), also boost A's graph neighbors
- Boost factor: neighbor_score = original_score * edge_weight * expansion_factor (default 0.3)
- Limit: expand only from top-3 initial matches, only 1-hop neighbors
- This helps for sparse queries where the best result has strong neighbors the user would also want
- franken_networkx dependency: neighborhood queries, edge weight lookup

RRF INTEGRATION MODEL:
- Phase 1 (PPR scores) integrates as a THIRD input to RRF fusion alongside lexical and semantic:
  rrf_score = 1/(K+rank_lexical) + 1/(K+rank_semantic) + weight_graph * 1/(K+rank_graph)
- weight_graph is configurable in TwoTierConfig (default 0.5 — lower than lexical/semantic because graph signal is optional and may not be available)
- When no DocumentGraph is provided, weight_graph = 0 and RRF reduces to current 2-input formula
- Phase 2 runs AFTER RRF (post-fusion diversification)
- Phase 3 runs BEFORE RRF (pre-fusion score boosting)

FEATURE FLAG:
`graph = ['dep:franken_networkx']` in frankensearch-fusion/Cargo.toml
- Off by default
- The `full` meta-feature should include it when franken_networkx is mature

CRATE PLACEMENT:
- DocumentGraph, EdgeType: frankensearch-core/src/graph.rs (zero-dep types)
- GraphRanker (PPR): frankensearch-fusion/src/graph_rank.rs
- Diversifier (clustering): frankensearch-fusion/src/diversify.rs
- DocumentExpander: frankensearch-fusion/src/expand.rs
acceptance_criteria:
Phase 1 (PPR):
1. PPR scores sum to ~1.0 (valid probability distribution)
2. PPR with no seed documents returns uniform scores (degenerates to global PageRank)
3. PPR with seed documents returns higher scores for seed neighbors than distant nodes
4. RRF with 3 inputs (lexical + semantic + graph) produces valid rankings
5. RRF with graph weight=0 produces identical results to current 2-input RRF
6. PPR computation completes in <10ms for 10K-node graph
7. No DocumentGraph provided → graph signal silently disabled, no errors

Phase 2 (Diversification):
8. Top-10 results after diversification span at least 2 clusters (when graph has 3+ clusters)
9. Diversification does not remove highly relevant results (nDCG@10 drop < 5% vs undiversified)
10. Diversification is a no-op when results already span multiple clusters

Phase 3 (Expansion):
11. Expanded results include graph neighbors of top-3 matches
12. Expansion boost factor is correctly applied (neighbor_score = original * weight * factor)
13. Expansion is bounded (only 1-hop, only from top-3, max 10 expanded results)
14. Expansion with no graph → no-op
notes: Deferred by backlog harmonization pass. Re-entry criteria: (1) Sprint-1 keystone program bd-1zxn closed, (2) release gate bd-ehuk closed, (3) proof-lane contract bd-bobf has at least one completed exemplar, and (4) concrete EV score >= 2.0 with measured hotspot evidence.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: RATIONALE BACKFILL: Added concrete acceptance criteria so future graph-aware ranking integration is measurable, explainable, and reproducible.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
DESIGN CLARIFICATIONS:

1. DIVERSIFICATION ALGORITHM (Phase 2): When >60% of top-10 results are from the same cluster, the replacement algorithm is: (a) Compute cluster assignments for all top-K candidates (not just top-10), (b) Group results by cluster, (c) Greedily select: pick the highest-scoring result from the underrepresented cluster, swap it for the lowest-scoring same-cluster result in top-10, (d) Repeat until top-10 spans at least 2 clusters or no more candidates exist, (e) Never remove the top-1 result regardless of cluster distribution. This is essentially MMR (Maximal Marginal Relevance) with graph distance as the diversity metric.

2. MAGIC NUMBERS AND TUNABILITY: weight_graph (0.5), alpha (0.15 PPR restart probability), expansion_factor (0.3), diversification_threshold (0.6) are ALL configurable in GraphRankConfig. They should be added to the CMA-ES parameter space in bd-2hk9 when graph ranking is enabled.

3. GRAPH PERSISTENCE: DocumentGraph is not persisted by frankensearch — the consumer provides it at index time. For fsfs (bd-2hz): graph is rebuilt on each index refresh from file system adjacency.

4. SCALABILITY: HashMap adjacency is fine for <100K documents (frankensearch's target range). For larger graphs, use CSR (Compressed Sparse Row) representation from franken_networkx. franken_networkx should provide the graph data structure — this bead should NOT reimplement graph storage.

5. SCORE INFLATION IN PHASE 3 (EXPANSION): Expanded neighbor scores are capped: neighbor_score = min(original_score * weight * factor, original_top1_score * 0.9). This ensures expanded results never outrank the original top result. Expanded results are deduplicated: if a neighbor is already in results, keep max(existing_score, expanded_score).

title: Default-flip compatibility contract: feature matrix, typed blue-green reindex, and zero public-API loss
description:
USER-SAFETY CONTRACT AROUND THE LIBRARY FACADE LEXICAL FEATURE FLIP. Plain facade default remains the lightweight hash-only graph; the requested default means lexical and every aggregate that includes lexical select Quill. This bead is scoped to lexical backend compatibility and the effect of swapping that arm inside public hybrid search. It does not own semantic model acquisition, semantic FSVI migration, ANN binding, production semantic caches or CASS semantic recovery; those requirements remain in bd-q4rg, bd-2g2l and bd-a6zt.

IMPLEMENTATION CHILDREN. bd-8nqz.1 splits read-only search from mutation and pins candidate hydration to one immutable generation. bd-8nqz.2 owns total non-mutating layout inspection plus root-bound CURRENT refresh and cancel-safe blue-green lifecycle. bd-8nqz.3 makes lexical admission independent of embedding success, adds per-arm receipts/accounting and ensures high-level hybrid opens actually attach lexical search. bd-8nqz.4 owns stable engine-neutral result/serde/API contracts and the exact structural feature graph. bd-8nqz.5 is the hard downstream CASS Tantivy schema-v8 compatibility receipt. bd-8nqz.6 owns topological packaging/publication and clean external consumption. E7.6 depends on every child directly because parent-child hierarchy is not used as an implicit blocker.

FEATURE GRAPH. default=[hash] remains unchanged. lexical and aggregate hybrid/persistent/durable/full/full-fts5 select Quill and forward frankensearch-fusion/quill. lexical-tantivy remains independently selectable for the pinned oracle. cass-compat remains Tantivy-backed because it reads a foreign schema-v8 Tantivy index and is not a Quill fallback. Both/all-features may contain both engines but must serve Quill unless a caller explicitly selects a Tantivy-native path.

LEXICAL ON-DISK UPGRADE. Pure inspection detects empty, direct Quill, direct Tantivy, valid blue-green, corrupt, mixed and ambiguous layouts before any open or write. Typed ReindexRequired carries detected format/backend/revision/path/expected backend and an actionable rebuild plan. The library never downloads, discovers source data, adopts a generation or rebuilds implicitly. A caller-authorized capability accepts source documents and Cx, writes a fresh sibling generation, validates and fsyncs it, then publishes CURRENT atomically. Failure/cancellation preserves the old reader/generation; legacy bytes are never overwritten or deleted.

PUBLIC CONTRACT PARITY. Inventory traits, field names and ownership, serde, query syntax/leniency, snippets/highlights, metadata, explain, counts, errors, tie ordering and configuration. Stable engine-neutral facade DTOs prevent false Quill/Tantivy aliases; native types remain in explicit namespaces. Real-prose dual-backend and frozen-semantic hybrid-interchange lanes prove no public behavior is lost.

TESTS/LOGGING. Compile/dependency matrix for no-default, default hash-only, quill/lexical, lexical-tantivy, both/oracle, cass-compat without Quill, hybrid, persistent, durable, full and full-fts5; all-target benches/examples; migration/rollback/fault-injection; generation-race hydration; embedding-failure lexical fallback; CASS schema-v8; package and clean-consumer E2E. Structured bounded logs name backend/format/revision/generation/source hashes, candidate-batch identity, validation/fsync/switch/recovery stages and typed errors without document text, metadata values, full sensitive paths or credentials.
design: Treat feature selection, read authority, immutable generation ownership, public DTOs, migration, downstream compatibility and packaged consumption as separate contracts with explicit receipts. No source-tree compile result substitutes for a runtime, migration, package or downstream proof. Semantic lifecycle work remains separate and fully preserved.
acceptance_criteria: All six P0 implementation children close with immutable evidence. Plain default is hash-only; lexical and aggregates serve Quill; explicit Tantivy/CASS lanes serve Tantivy. Search requires no writer lease, hydration is snapshot-consistent, CURRENT refresh is atomic, mixed layouts fail closed, embedding failures retain lexical documents, public/serde contracts have no unreviewed gap, CASS schema-v8 behavior survives, and packaged artifacts work in a clean external consumer. Real-prose and bounded hybrid total observation, fault injection, rollback, all-target feature matrix and bounded redacted logging pass. Semantic lifecycle work remains open and is neither deleted nor falsely claimed.

title: Resolve Frankentorch registry graph for packaged native rerank
description: Cross-repository prerequisite for bd-8nqz.6. Determine and prove a crates.io-resolvable dependency graph for the native rerank feature currently using git-only ft-api, ft-autograd, and ft-core. Evaluate conflict-free renamed registry packages with Cargo package aliases, a publishable native-rerank dependency refactor, or an explicit facade/package boundary. Verify candidate names against crates.io. Do not publish crates or tags. Preserve source behavior and avoid local path/git patches in the final packaged-consumer graph.
design: Audit the exact Frankentorch package DAG and public API usage from frankensearch-rerank. Prefer a semver-versioned registry graph whose package names are globally available while retaining stable Rust import names through Cargo package aliases. Reject any design that requires git/path patches in a crates.io package, accidentally resolves the unrelated existing ft-api crate, duplicates tensor types across incompatible dependency universes, or publishes only a leaf while its normal dependency closure remains unavailable. A bounded implementation slice may change manifests and package metadata only when cargo package plus a clean registry-only consumer can resolve the graph without publishing.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Full Frankentorch guidance and package DAG are audited. 2. Candidate registry names are verified live against crates.io and documented with collision evidence. 3. The chosen design gives every normal dependency a versioned registry source and preserves one coherent tensor/autograd/API type universe. 4. cargo metadata/package dry-run and a clean no-path/no-git consumer prove resolution, or the bead records the exact cross-repo release sequence and blockers preventing such proof. 5. Frankensearch native rerank/default/full package boundaries are explicit and no feature silently loses behavior. 6. No crates or tags are published. 7. Any edits are reserved, tested, formatted, scanned, committed, and pushed only when they constitute a genuinely registry-resolvable bounded slice.
notes:
Decision receipt (2026-07-27 EDT; auditor WildChapel)

Chosen design: publish a collision-free six-package Frankentorch registry family and retain the current Rust import names through Cargo package aliases plus explicit library target names. A Frankensearch-only native-rerank refactor cannot remove the transitive package closure; a facade/package carve-out would silently change the current `rerank`/`native`/`full` behavior and is not the smallest correct fix.

Exact normal-dependency closure and topological publish order:
1. `frankentorch-core` (`[lib] name = "ft_core"`).
2. `frankentorch-kernel-cpu` (`ft_kernel_cpu`) depends on core; `frankentorch-runtime` (`ft_runtime`) depends on core. These two may publish after core and in either order.
3. `frankentorch-dispatch` (`ft_dispatch`) depends on core and kernel-cpu.
4. `frankentorch-autograd` (`ft_autograd`) depends on core, dispatch, and kernel-cpu.
5. `frankentorch-api` (`ft_api`) depends on autograd, core, dispatch, kernel-cpu, and runtime.
6. After all six registry artifacts exist and their archives verify, replace Frankensearch workspace git pins with versioned aliases such as `ft-core = { package = "frankentorch-core", version = "0.1.0" }`, keep `frankensearch-rerank` feature names/imports stable, and prove a fresh registry-only consumer with no path, git, or patch entries.

Live crates.io census (2026-07-27, crates.io v1 API): `ft-api` returned HTTP 200 and is an unrelated FifthTry 0.1.0 crate. `ft-autograd`, `ft-core`, `ft-dispatch`, `ft-kernel-cpu`, and `ft-runtime` returned 404. All chosen names also returned 404: `frankentorch-core`, `frankentorch-kernel-cpu`, `frankentorch-dispatch`, `frankentorch-autograd`, `frankentorch-runtime`, and `frankentorch-api`. HTTP 404 proves no current public crate record; it does not guarantee crates.io will accept a name that is reserved, deleted, or otherwise ownership-restricted.

Executable failure receipt at clean Frankentorch HEAD `5fdca1bfabaeecb3da004a3b68baab10209a8c70`:
`cargo package -p ft-api --allow-dirty --no-verify --locked`
exited 101 with: `all dependencies must have a version requirement specified when packaging. dependency ft-autograd does not specify a version. The packaged dependency will use the version from crates.io; the path specification will be removed.`
`cargo tree -p ft-api --edges normal` independently confirms the six-package closure above. `cargo package --list -p ft-api --allow-dirty` lists 551 files; the current ft-api tree is about 8.6 MiB raw, so release preparation must also audit package include/exclude policy and archive size.

Rejected alternatives:
- Using crates.io `ft-api` resolves to the wrong project.
- Renaming or versioning only ft-api/ft-autograd/ft-core leaves kernel-cpu, dispatch, and runtime unavailable.
- Removing direct `ft-autograd`/`ft-core` dependencies from Frankensearch does not remove the same packages from ft-api transitive dependencies.
- Git/path fallbacks or `[patch]` blocks are not allowed in the final crates.io consumer proof.
- Duplicating package identities risks two incompatible core/autograd type universes.
- Dropping native rerank from aggregate features changes documented behavior and does not by itself make the optional normal dependencies publishable.

External-authority blocker: no code-only change can create a genuinely crates.io-resolvable graph while all six candidate packages are unpublished. Manifest preparation and local package archives can be completed without external authority, but claiming the names and publishing each crate requires an authorized crates.io owner/token and explicit human authorization. This task expressly forbids publishing crates or tags, so the admissible closeout here is the exact release plan, not a false clean-consumer success claim. After authorization, publish and verify bottom-up, wait for index availability after each layer, then run the Frankensearch registry-only clean-consumer receipt.

Cross-repo tracking: Frankentorch local DB issue `frankentorch-registry-safe-core-graph-818va` records the release preparation plan and references this bead. Its JSONL export is currently blocked by a pre-existing duplicate `frankentorch-kgs4.150` at lines 917 and 919; therefore the Frankensearch bead remains the Git-durable source of truth until that unrelated tracker defect is repaired. No Frankentorch manifests or source were edited, and no crate or tag was published.

title: Split lexical read/write traits and pin candidate hydration to one immutable generation
description:
P0 FACADE SAFETY PREREQUISITE. The current LexicalSearch trait combines search, metadata hydration, indexing and commit, which forces read-only consumers and TwoTierSearcher to own a writer-capable backend. Quill fusion candidate search and later hydration can also reopen different snapshots, producing scores from generation N and metadata from generation N+1.

DESIGN: split the public contract into a read-only lexical search trait and a separate mutation/indexing trait. Make fusion candidate search return a typed candidate batch whose opaque backend-owned hydration context pins the exact immutable snapshot/generation used for scoring. Hydration consumes or borrows that batch context; callers cannot forge, relabel or mix it across engines/generations. TwoTierSearcher and the synchronous searcher depend only on the read trait. Implement adapters for QuillSearchIndex, QuillIndex, TantivyIndex, FTS5 and every shadow/oracle implementation without compatibility shims. Keep full public cancellation and typed-error behavior.

TESTS AND EVIDENCE: inline unit tests for empty/error/cancelled candidates, eager and deferred metadata, wrong-backend/wrong-generation batch rejection, repeated hydration, and no writer lease on read-only opens. Deterministic no-mock generation-race E2E: query and retain candidates from N; commit update/delete or swap CURRENT to N+1; hydrate the retained batch and prove ordered scores plus metadata remain from N; a subsequent query must observe N+1. Run the same behavioral contract against Quill reader, Quill writer, Tantivy, FTS5 and shadow adapters. Structured bounded logs include backend, immutable generation, candidate-batch identity, hydration outcome and cancellation phase, never document text or metadata values.
design: The hydration context is an opaque backend-owned capability tied to the exact immutable search snapshot. Search and mutation remain composable but separately permissioned. Adapters implement one canonical contract rather than exposing backend-specific lifetimes through the facade.
acceptance_criteria: TwoTierSearcher and sync searcher accept the read-only trait; no library search path requires a writer lease. Candidate batches carry an unforgeable backend/generation hydration context, and every adapter passes the same total public-result contract. The concurrent generation-swap E2E proves old candidates hydrate from their original snapshot while the next query sees the new generation. Wrong-context, cancellation and partial-error cases fail closed with typed errors and preserve the last valid reader. Workspace/all-feature gates and redacted logging assertions pass.
close_reason: Lexical read/write traits split and candidate hydration pinned to one immutable generation; the combined LexicalSearch trait is removed with no compatibility shim. Chain fb578c2d, 48b5952a, e126f1b0, 29eaefe1, 327d264a, af4f7ae9. Backends (Tantivy, FTS5, Quill) and every consumer (shadow, gauntlet, fsfs, facade, e2e, READMEs) ported directly. Pin test lexical_read_hydration_is_pinned_to_the_scoring_generation varies only the generation and goes red without the fix. Two silent deferred-metadata regressions found and fixed during the port. Workspace --all-targets, default-lane clippy -D warnings, perf-harness and shadow-oracle lanes all green; core 1087/0, lexical 117/0, storage 344/0. bd-uqae5 closed alongside. Two gauntlet perf::tests failures are pre-existing bd-jlvbv gates.toml fallout, not this chain.

- Generation pinning is REAL for Quill: quill_hydrate_candidates (quill/src/index.rs:9695) downcasts the context to Arc<QuillSearchSnapshot> and returns a typed SearchError for a foreign backend rather than a silent no-op.

MY SLICE (B2a), deliberately narrow to avoid colliding with live work: make the default hydrate_candidates FAIL CLOSED on a non-None context, and pin the behavioral contract for the eager-batch backends. A backend that never issues a context can never legitimately receive one, so accepting it is always a bug.

NOT touching the 180-reference LexicalSearch removal sweep in this slice — those files are live under bd-qwkq (BrownCoyote) and bd-fjpu (TealIsland), and a sweeping rename across them is the highest-collision, lowest-safety-value part of B2. It stays open on this bead with the evidence above.

comments.text:
STOPPING THE SWEEP BEFORE EDITING — it is not mechanical, and done naively it would permanently destroy a measured optimization. Evidence below; no files were modified. I am holding reservations on the 16 files pending a routing decision.

THE FINDING: the split traits have ALREADY silently regressed Tantivy hybrid search, and deleting the combined trait would make that permanent.

- TantivyIndex has a REAL deferred-metadata path on the combined trait: search_fusion_candidates (lexical/src/lib.rs:2248) returns hits with metadata: None from a cheap doc-id scan, fusion_metadata_is_deferred() returns true (:2274), and hydrate_fusion_metadata (:2279) restores metadata via hydrate_fusion_metadata_with_collector. That is the exact waste the lexical_candidate_metadata_waste_ab bench exists to measure.
- But TantivyIndex s LexicalRead impl (:2399) overrides ONLY search and doc_count. It does not override search_candidates or hydrate_candidates, so it inherits the EAGER defaults.
- B1b made TwoTierSearcher and open_hybrid depend on LexicalRead only. So since 0220d5c5, Tantivy hybrid search has been taking the eager path and paying full metadata materialization at scoring time. The deferred code on the combined trait is already dead for hybrid consumers.
- Same shape at storage/src/fts5_adapter.rs:467 and core/src/shadow.rs:1368 — both override only search and doc_count.

So "remove the combined trait" is not a rename. The method sets are not 1:1: search_fusion_candidates -> search_candidates changes return type to LexicalCandidateBatch, hydrate_fusion_metadata -> hydrate_candidates gains the context parameter, and fusion_metadata_is_deferred is subsumed by LexicalCandidateBatch::is_deferred. Deleting the combined trait without porting those bodies deletes the deferred path outright and locks in the eager regression.

THE CORRECT SEQUENCE IS PORT-THEN-REMOVE, and the port is the bead s actual headline applied to the remaining adapters: give each backend a real search_candidates that returns a DEFERRED batch pinned to its scoring snapshot, and a hydrate_candidates that reads from that pin. For Tantivy the pin is obvious and I verified it is feasible: self.reader.searcher() (lexical/src/lib.rs:1837 and elsewhere) returns an owned tantivy Searcher, which IS a pinned segment set — exactly the immutable-generation handle LexicalHydrationContext is designed to carry. Porting it both restores the lost optimization AND closes the "every adapter passes the same total public-result contract" acceptance criterion, instead of satisfying it vacuously by making everyone eager.

WHY I DID NOT JUST PROCEED: the two available readings diverge sharply. (A) port the three adapters onto pinned deferred candidates, then delete the combined trait — correct, restores the optimization, satisfies the contract, but it is B1-scale design work per backend, not a sweep. (B) delete the combined trait and accept eager-only — mechanical and quick, but it destroys a measured optimization and would make the regression permanent and invisible. I will not do (B) silently, and (A) is a materially larger commitment than the sweep as scoped.

Recommend routing (A) as its own slice, backend by backend, starting with Tantivy since its pin is already available. My earlier B2a (fb578c2d) is unaffected and stands.
