OPTION A, STEP 2 LANDED: e126f1b0 — ShadowLexical ported off the combined trait.

SAME CLASS OF BUG AS TANTIVY, found by porting rather than assumed: ShadowLexical is a decorator whose combined impl forwarded search_fusion_candidates / fusion_metadata_is_deferred / hydrate_fusion_metadata straight to the serving backend, but whose LexicalRead impl overrode only search and doc_count. So split consumers got the eager default and the serving backend s deferred path was dropped AT THE DECORATOR. An in-tree comment asserted that eager default was deliberate because threading the serving backend s private context through the shadow comparison was unsound; it is not needed, because the comparison consumes batch.results() — exactly the metadata-less rows the combined path already submitted. search_candidates now forwards the serving batch whole, context included, and hydrate_candidates forwards to the same backend, so the pin stays coherent end to end and the decorator never mints or inspects one. I replaced the stale comment with that reasoning rather than deleting it silently.

SHAPE: a type change, not method overrides. dyn LexicalRead + LexicalWrite is not expressible, and re-unifying them behind a private supertrait would be exactly the compat shim the split exists to remove — so a dual-capability backend is held as SplitLexical { read, write }, two handles coerced from one Arc, with generic constructors so callers still pass a single Arc. Every ShadowLexical construction site is inside shadow.rs, so the blast radius was contained. ShadowLexicalObserver narrowed to Arc<dyn LexicalRead> — it only ever queries its oracle, so it now cannot reach a mutation surface at all, which is precisely this bead s property. The shadow-side comparison drops the oracle s own pin with the batch (into_parts().0) because it ranks candidates and never reads their metadata. Test doubles StaticLexical and SlowShadow were split. shadow.rs now has zero LexicalSearch references including doc links.

title: Root-bound lexical reader, total layout inspection, and cancel-safe blue-green CURRENT refresh
description:
P0 LIBRARY LIFECYCLE PREREQUISITE. A long-lived QuillSearchIndex reopens its fixed child directory and therefore never observes a blue-green CURRENT switch. Direct IndexBuilder paths can also initialize Quill beside an existing Tantivy meta.json because MANIFEST absence is mistaken for an empty layout.

Implement one shared non-mutating lexical-layout inspector with typed states: empty, direct Quill, direct Tantivy, valid blue-green, corrupt Quill, corrupt Tantivy, mixed, and ambiguous. Inspection must never adopt a child, write CURRENT, acquire a writer lease, overwrite bytes, or infer safety from MANIFEST absence. Add a root-bound facade reader that explicitly resolves CURRENT, validates the selected backend and generation, atomically swaps path/backend/generation on refresh, pins in-flight searches to the old Arc, and preserves the old reader on cancellation or failed validation. Tantivy rollback is available only when lexical-tantivy is compiled. Factor the library-safe pieces from fsfs-private detection rather than duplicating policy.

TESTS/E2E/LOGGING: table-driven unit tests for every layout state and symlink/path boundary; no-mock direct-Tantivy, direct-Quill and blue-green fixtures; concurrent search plus CURRENT swap; corrupt target, missing target, cancellation at every open/validate/swap stage; restart and rollback; and explicit proof that all legacy bytes remain byte-identical. Logs are structured, bounded and redacted, recording root, backend, format revision, generation, CURRENT transition, validation stage and typed disposition without document content.
design: Layout inspection is pure and authoritative. Mutation is a separate explicit caller-authorized rebuild/publication API. Refresh follows resolve, open, validate, atomic swap; it never weakens the current reader before the replacement is proven.
acceptance_criteria: Every lexical layout maps to exactly one typed state, with mixed/ambiguous/corrupt layouts failing closed. Read-only open performs zero filesystem writes and acquires no writer lease. Root-bound refresh sees valid CURRENT switches, pins in-flight reads to the old generation, and retains the old reader on failure or cancellation. Migration/rollback E2E preserves old bytes, fault injection covers every publication boundary, and bounded redacted logs plus workspace/all-feature gates pass.

Its 03:44 comment says Quill closeout was blocked by "pre-existing peer-owned Argus test compile calls (has_validated_post_move_contract at argus.rs:5751/7134/7187/7217)". I fixed exactly those under bd-or1wl; quill compiles under --all-targets and the workspace clippy gate exits 0. The other noted blocker, workspace fmt on quill_perf_ratchet.rs, is filed as bd-t4z14 and still open.

THE DEFECT, precisely, so nobody re-derives it:
segment_old_enough is
    stat_old_enough(stat, now, grace) && unreachable_since.is_none_or(|t| now - t >= grace)
is_none_or means ABSENT PROVENANCE RETURNS TRUE, so with no witness the decision falls back entirely to the segment's own mtime plus grace. Absence of receipt currently means COLLECTABLE. The contract requires the opposite.

But a blanket is_none_or -> is_some_and flip is WRONG and I did not make it. Two reasons:
  (a) segment_unreachability_floor_at never returns Ok(None) on the manifest path -- both the recovery branch (:9521-9567) and the Current branch (:9569-9604) return Some(..) or Err. So the flip would not even fix the failing test.
  (b) collect_abandoned_genesis_garbage_at_platform (:9309) deliberately passes None to sweep_garbage_directory for the genesis case where BOTH manifest slots are absent and everything present really is garbage. A blanket flip would make genesis cleanup collect nothing.

WHY THE TEST STILL FAILS: on the Current path the floor is a MANIFEST-LEVEL timestamp -- max(MANIFEST ctime, manifest.last_publish_unix_s). It is the same value for every candidate segment and says nothing about when THIS segment became unreachable. In the fixture, segment 0xb is absent from BOTH MANIFEST and MANIFEST.prev, so nothing anywhere witnesses when it stopped being reachable, yet the manifest-level floor is older than grace and the segment's own mtime is older than grace, so it is collected. That is exactly what the test's assertion message calls out: "a missing first-unreachable receipt must fail closed rather than infer age from mtime".

DESIGN I INTEND, which needs no new durable state: the first-unreachable receipt already exists implicitly in the slot pair. A segment that was legitimately retired appears in MANIFEST.prev and not in MANIFEST, and MANIFEST.prev's publication is the durable witness of when it became unreachable. So:
  - segment present in MANIFEST                      -> live, never collectable (unchanged)
  - segment in MANIFEST.prev but not MANIFEST        -> collectable once prev-derived witness + grace has elapsed
  - segment in NEITHER slot                          -> NO PROVENANCE, NOT COLLECTABLE, regardless of mtime  <-- the fix
  - no manifest slots at all (genesis path)          -> unchanged, mtime+grace still governs
This makes the predicate three-valued instead of a boolean over an Option, which is why sweep_garbage_directory needs the previous-slot segment set threaded alongside live_segments.

PLANTED NEGATIVE I will add beside the committed-red test: a segment absent from both slots whose mtime is backdated well beyond grace -- i.e. the input a naive mtime-inferring implementation wrongly deletes -- asserting report.is_empty() and that the directory survives. That is distinct from the existing test, which relies on the ambient clock; the planted negative forces the stale-timestamp case explicitly so the fail-closed rule cannot be satisfied by accident of timing.

title: IndexBuilder lexical admission independent of embeddings, per-arm receipts, and ergonomic hybrid open
description:
P0 USER-VISIBLE CORRECTNESS DEFECT. IndexBuilder currently stages a document for lexical indexing only after embedding succeeds, so the documents most in need of lexical fallback disappear from lexical search too. Current reports and size accounting also hide the lexical arm, and advertised examples build lexical data but create TwoTierSearcher without attaching it.

Reorder admission so every valid source document independently attempts lexical indexing regardless of fast/quality embedding outcome. Preserve per-document identity and return explicit arm-specific receipts: source count, lexical indexed/errors, fast-vector indexed/errors, quality-vector indexed/errors, active lexical backend/path/generation, publication disposition, and bytes by lexical/vector/metadata arm. No aggregate success may hide a failed arm. Replace vector-only size accounting with total and per-arm values. Add a root-bound open_hybrid or equally ergonomic helper that attaches the active lexical reader and vectors correctly; migrate facade docs, examples and tests to it without losing lower-level composition APIs.

TESTS/E2E/LOGGING: unit matrix for lexical success plus embedding failure, embedding success plus lexical failure, both fail, empty documents, duplicate IDs, cancellation and partial publication. No-mock E2E indexes a corpus with deliberately failing embedders, proves failed-vector documents remain lexically searchable, restarts, refreshes CURRENT and verifies receipts/size accounting. Compile and execute every quickstart. Structured per-stage logs carry document-count deltas, arm, backend/generation, error class and publication receipt, never document text.
design: Lexical and vector admission are sibling arms driven from one validated source-document stream. Each arm produces its own durable receipt and errors; publication composes only validated arm outputs. High-level hybrid open consumes those receipts and the root-bound reader rather than silently omitting lexical search.

title: Stable engine-neutral lexical API and exact facade feature/dependency contract
description: P0 SOURCE-COMPATIBILITY, FEATURE-SELECTION, AND REPLACEMENT-AUTHORIZATION CONTRACT. Define stable engine-neutral facade DTOs/traits without pretending Quill and Tantivy native result types are field-identical. Plain default stays lightweight hash-only. lexical and aggregate hybrid/persistent/durable/full/full-fts5 select Quill; explicit lexical-tantivy and cass-compat select Tantivy; both/all-features compile both with deterministic documented selection. Prove ordinary Core Lexical V3, native enriched search, exact count/page, CASS compatibility, and complete feature/dependency structure before the library flip. QG-10 becomes structural evidence rather than timing noise.
design: Facade-owned stable DTOs expose exact reviewed semantics; native types remain under unambiguous quill and lexical_tantivy namespaces. Ordinary LexicalSearch evidence is method-bound and marks count/snippet/highlight NotExposed. A separate live native witness invokes QuillIndex and TantivyIndex search_with_snippets with identical corpus, query, limit, trusted tags, and window, compile-exhaustively observes order/rank, score bits, metadata presence/digest, query_type, rendered snippet presence/digest, empty/error shape, and custom-tag/UTF-8 behavior. Highlight spans are not claimed because no engine-neutral public result exposes them. Exact total and pagination use separate native methods independently of k/offset. Add a dedicated replacement-ready validator or signed manifest that requires exact Core V3 verified reload with admissible coverage, enriched/count/page receipts, CASS receipt, public API inventory, feature graph identity, and accepted divergence census; CampaignReport passed or rank-envelope-only coverage can never authorize the flip. QG-10 validates a versioned Cargo metadata/tree/backend-identity manifest across default, no-default, lexical, quill, lexical-tantivy, cass-compat, aggregates, all-features, benches, examples, and external clean consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Public field/serde inventory has no unreviewed Quill/Tantivy gap. Plain default is hash-only; lexical and aggregates serve Quill; explicit Tantivy/CASS lanes serve Tantivy; both/all-features compile and select deterministically. Every all-target feature lane, benchmark, example, clean packaged external consumer, and runtime backend identity assertion passes. The live enriched campaign detects independent mutations of rank/order, one-bit score, metadata None/empty/value, query_type, snippet None/empty/rendered, default/custom tags, UTF-8 boundaries, truncation, empty/no-match, phrase/boolean, long query, zero limit, typed errors, and unsupported stored schemas; versioned artifacts replay and reject tamper with fixture-only bounded diagnostics. Separate count/page witnesses prove exact totals independent of k/offset and never derive them from returned length. Quill cancellation correctness has a real method-bound witness without requiring Tantivy parity. The replacement-ready validator fails closed on rank-envelope-only/generic passed reports or any missing required receipt. QG-10 emits structural manifests with requested features, resolved backend, dependency/revision/toolchain hashes, public schema versions, and forbidden dependency assertions.

title: Native enriched Quill/Tantivy witness with independent semantic oracles and immutable provenance
description: P0 NATIVE RESULT-CONTRACT RECEIPT. Rebase the useful isolated enriched witness onto the exact accepted Core Lexical V3 candidate, but treat it only as one partial receipt. Invoke real QuillIndex and TantivyIndex native enriched search, exact-count, and pagination APIs over identical committed fixtures. Observe exact order, rank, score bits, metadata None versus empty versus value, query type, rendered snippets, exact totals, pages, typed errors, and empty shapes. Require the exact shipping-default Quill/Tantivy engine identity and reject CASS identities. Every artifact must bind clean production provenance, exact source candidate SHA, Cargo.lock, toolchain, schema/analyzer, corpus/query manifests, and independently derived engine identities. The witness must never issue replacement authorization; only the terminal release-gate aggregator may do so.

Use committed fixture expectations as an oracle independent of cross-engine equality: trusted custom/default tag rendering and HTML escaping, UTF-8 window boundaries, deterministic long-query truncation, metadata None/empty/value, exact total independent of k, pagination offsets, empty/no-match, zero limit, phrase/boolean, unsupported stored schemas, and positionless multi-term phrase QueryCapability. Run both real engines and compare to both the independent expectations and one another; inject common-mode mutations to prove equality alone cannot pass. The typed QueryCapability mapper gets a distinct stable enriched error class/code and positionful control. Canonical artifact loading recomputes semantics, verifies address/provenance, bounds and redacts diagnostics, and rejects synthetic from_body-only construction as release evidence. Use the Core CampaignReport report hash or a dedicated domain separator, never the enriched-body hash domain.

A real positionless stored-schema phrase returns the exact QueryCapability class/code/field/operator/capability; the positionful control succeeds. SLICE 3 LANDED (41a0c74e): UTF-8 window boundaries and deterministic long-query truncation, both
against BOTH engines. Bead stays IN_PROGRESS.

UTF-8 WINDOWS. A snippet is a window over document text, so it must consist of whole Unicode scalar
values. Rust's String already guarantees valid UTF-8, so validity proves NOTHING here -- the
assertions are that no U+FFFD appears (a byte-indexed window cutting mid-character would surface
one) and that a multi-byte token survives INTACT (a window that silently dropped the partial
character would lose text the document contains). Fixture gained a CJK/combining/emoji document.

TRUNCATION, AND MY FIRST VERSION WAS TOO WEAK TO KEEP -- recording it because the weak version
looked exactly as green as the strong one. The property is that an over-length query behaves
exactly like its first-10,000-character prefix: same page, same total, same score bits. My first
probe was all non-matching padding with one matching term at the HEAD. That proves DETERMINISM but
not the CUT POINT: an engine truncating at 5,000 characters would have passed it, because the head
term survives any prefix. The probe now STRADDLES the boundary -- "lexical" just inside the cap,
"escaping" just beyond -- so both failure directions are observable: cutting early drops doc-beta,
cutting late picks up doc-markup, and the test asserts both. A determinism test and a boundary test
are not the same test, and only one of them is worth having here.

A DIVERGENCE RECORDED RATHER THAN EQUATED AWAY: both engines cap at 10,000 characters, but Quill
exports MAX_QUERY_LENGTH and emits a QueryDiagnosticKind::Truncated diagnostic, while Tantivy keeps
the constant private and truncates SILENTLY. The value is all the independent expectation needs;
whether truncation is REPORTED is a contract difference that belongs in the divergence census, not
in an assertion that would force one engine's choice onto the other.

Both dimensions run through the same two oracle functions on both arms, so a divergence surfaces as
one engine failing the SHARED oracle rather than as a cross-engine diff.

title: QG-10 facade API, feature graph, dependency, runtime identity, and source-workspace manifest
description: P0 STRUCTURAL FACADE RECEIPT. QG-10 is not a timing or registry-publication gate. Produce a versioned, content-addressed source-workspace manifest for the exact candidate that inventories every facade public DTO, trait, re-export, schema version, feature selection, resolved backend, dependency tree, example, benchmark, and binary. Plain default remains hash-only. lexical and aggregates resolve Quill. lexical-tantivy and cass-compat resolve Tantivy. both/all-features compile both and select deterministically. The manifest must prove Tantivy and its transitive tree are absent wherever Quill is promised, while explicit compatibility lanes retain exactly the intended Tantivy graph. Registry topology, package contents, version propagation, and clean packaged external consumers are exclusively owned by bd-8nqz.6; the terminal flip composes both receipts.
design: Derive this receipt from cargo metadata, cargo tree, compile-time facade inventory, rustdoc/public-api inventory, runtime backend identity probes, examples, benches, binaries, and doc tests. Cover default, no-default, hash, quill, lexical, lexical-bench, lexical-tantivy, cass-compat, both-backends, semantic, hybrid, persistent, durable, full, full-fts5, and all-features. Record requested features separately from unified resolved features and execute isolated package graphs where feature unification would hide a defect. Bind git revision/clean state, Cargo.lock, rustc/target/profile, Cargo.toml hashes, public schema versions, resolved backend, and forbidden/required dependency assertions. Any new facade export, feature, binary, example, benchmark, or schema version must make the inventory test fail until reviewed. Do not duplicate the packaged-artifact and clean-consumer machinery in bd-8nqz.6.

title: Treasure Island base fixture, lexical-oracle, and real-semantic retrieval proof
description:
BASE REAL-PROSE RETRIEVAL PROOF over Project Gutenberg Treasure Island, ebook 120. This bead owns only fixture integrity, deterministic chunking, reviewed qrels, shared lexical proof and real semantic proof. Persisted explicit-path restart, facade hybrid orchestration and identity/topology negatives belong to bd-q4rg; CI execution/evidence policy belongs to bd-2g2l; CASS lifecycle proof remains separate.

FIXTURE: commit the exact public-domain UTF-8 source with Gutenberg URL, retrieval date, license, byte length and SHA-256; tests never fetch. Strip the wrapper and chunk deterministically into 34 chapters and stable passages. Golden manifest records chapter heading, byte span and content hash. Unit tests cover wrapper boundaries, every chapter, empty/malformed headings, UTF-8, deterministic IDs, overlap policy and manifest drift.

QRELS: frozen/versioned lexical name/place/phrase/negative queries and semantic paraphrases that avoid answer vocabulary, with graded multi-passage relevance where supported. Qrels are independently reviewed rather than derived from Quill or Tantivy output. Record query/corpus/qrels hashes and no-relevant-document policy.

LEXICAL BASE: run Quill and pinned Tantivy through the identical public lexical contract and total result observation. Rare names, places, phrases, negatives and parser edges must meet reviewed expectations; metadata/snippet/explain/order differences are compared through bd-qwkq.

SEMANTIC BASE: load the exact pinned real MiniLM artifact and assert semantic identity/dimension/revision/hash. Embed the fixture once per immutable identity. Paraphrase queries meet frozen nDCG/Recall/MRR bounds and beat FNV hash plus lexical-only controls on the same inputs. Missing, corrupt, hash or wrong-identity artifacts fail closed; no silent semantic success.

ENGINEERING: separate fixture, lexical, semantic and control tests; optimized inference; fresh roots; zero-network sentinel; scoped quiet logging; <=10000 lines and <=8MiB; structured query IDs/classes, passage IDs, ranks, hashes, stage times and metrics without unrestricted query/document text. Preserve exact commands, ELF/model/corpus hashes and failure artifacts.
design: Keep this bead runnable before persistence and provisioning work: immutable local model provisioning is an explicit prerequisite, but path publication, hybrid restart and CASS UX are not. Core100-style fast controls remain alongside the real semantic lane. The facade/hybrid bead consumes these exact fixture and qrels manifests rather than duplicating them.
acceptance_criteria: Exact source/chunk/qrels/model manifests validate and deterministic fixture unit tests pass. Quill and pinned Tantivy satisfy the same lexical expectations and total observation contract. Real MiniLM semantic metrics clear predeclared numeric bounds and beat hash/lexical controls on the identical query set; wrong or missing identity cannot skip or masquerade as semantic. Tests perform zero network, use optimized inference, enforce timeout/log/redaction ceilings, and emit checksum-addressed evidence. This bead does not claim persisted restart, hybrid contribution or CASS lifecycle coverage.
notes:
EVIDENCE 2026-07-26, commit d46a20d3 (local, not pushed).

LEXICAL LANE: test result ok, 1 passed 0 failed, 0.76s, 339 real passages in Quill.
  precision: every top-10 hit for all 8 terms genuinely contains the term (verified against an independent corpus copy; haystack includes the chapter title because titles are indexed and BM25-boosted)
  recall:    expected chapter within k=40 for the 4 concentrated terms (coracle, Gunn, stockade, Benbow)
  negative:  photosynthesis / cryptocurrency / zzzqqxvw -> exactly zero hits
  Deliberately NO chapter-recall assertion for Hispaniola/Livesey/Smollett/Flint: they recur throughout the novel, so their top-k is a term-density accident, not a retrieval property.

SEMANTIC LANE: test result ok, 3 passed 0 failed, 362.27s, real all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (tokenizer sha256 be50c3628f2bf5bb5e3a7f17b1f74611b2561a3a27eeab05e5aa30f411572037, pinned rev c9745ed1d9f207416be6d2e6f8de32d1f16199bf).
  semantic 13/16  vs  hash 4/16
  discordant: semantic-only 9, hash-only 0  ->  one-sided sign test p = 0.5^9 ~= 0.002
  Also green: a_hash_embedder_is_never_mistaken_for_a_semantic_one; semantically_close_passages_score_higher_than_unrelated_ones (paraphrase-vs-unrelated cosine gap > 0.15).

CRITERION HISTORY (important, do not silently 'simplify' this later): the first run was 6/8 vs 3/8 and FAILED the original max_hash_hits<=2 guard. The threshold was NOT raised. Root cause of the bad criterion: HashEmbedder is not noise -- it hashes TOKENS into dimensions and behaves as a degenerate bag-of-words matcher, so an absolute cap on it measures incidental vocabulary overlap rather than meaning. (That property is also the best available explanation for why the production degradation went unnoticed: the fallback returns plausible hits, not obvious garbage.) Replaced with a paired sign test over 16 queries; 8 could never reach significance since 3-0 gives p=0.125.

NOT DONE, explicitly not claimed: hybrid lane written and compiling but NEVER RUN (it is the only lane needing both run_test_with_cx and the embedder, which triggers bd-irb1's TRACE tax); still uses rrf_fuse rather than TwoTierSearcher; still uses InMemoryVectorIndex rather than a persisted/reopened FSVI. title: Persist HNSW fallback rebuilds so old or degraded sidecars self-heal
description:
Problem:
HnswIndex::load rebuilds in memory when it sees legacy v1/v2 metadata or degraded current-format graph state, but does not expose that disposition. The caller in crates/frankensearch-index/src/two_tier.rs treats the matching rebuilt index as a successful load and returns before the save path. Every cold open repeats the rebuild and missing or corrupt graph siblings never self-heal.

Acceptance:
- Distinguish native load from fallback rebuild, or otherwise persist every successful fallback rebuild.
- Legacy and degraded current-format rebuilds write current metadata plus valid graph and data siblings.
- Add deterministic second-load coverage proving the repaired sidecar uses the native path, without timing assertions.
- Persistence failure remains graceful: retain the rebuilt in-memory ANN, warn actionably, and do not fail startup.
- Config-mismatch and vector-change rebuild paths still persist correctly.

Evidence:
The fallback return is in hnsw.rs around lines 198 onward; the early-return and bypassed save path are in two_tier.rs around lines 867-929. Existing rebuild tests assert search correctness but not disk repair.

title: Umbrella: typed per-tier embeddings, direct quality retrieval, and independent candidate union
description:
P0 FRANKENSEARCH LIBRARY UMBRELLA. Coordinate the validated query identity and coverage foundation, retained immutable FSVI v2 tier ownership, and real sync or async typed search activation. The public FrankenSearch library and facade construction surfaces must consume those landed primitives: callers select FastOnly, QualityOnly, FullProgressive, PartialQuality, LexicalOnly or explicit nonsemantic HashControl; each fast and quality query value carries its independently validated complete identity; and no library path can use one vector in multiple spaces or infer compatibility from dimension.

QualityOnly retrieves the quality tier as its primary arm. FullProgressive independently embeds and retrieves fast and quality tiers, then deterministically unions candidates before fusion or blending. Partial coverage remains functional and truthful through requested and realized per-tier owner-backed coverage. Hash is test/control or declared lexical degradation, never semantic availability.

This is an umbrella and non-dormancy gate, not a schema-only implementation bead. It waits on C1, C2/C3 and ctzo and requires actual non-test public library and facade call sites plus a machine-readable consumer census. Persisted restart, fsfs staging/publication, CASS product integration, terminal Treasure Island lifecycle, recovery, cache/ANN/daemon terminal enforcement, and final raw API deletion belong to their dedicated downstream beads and are not acceptance criteria here.
design:
Treat C1, C2/C3 and ctzo as independently closable layers: validated types and coverage; owner-backed admitted v2 tiers; and sync or async retrieval activation. The umbrella verifies composition through public library and facade APIs and prevents a dormant-type close. It does not duplicate their implementation or absorb persisted product lifecycles.

The public facade may expose a typed fallible builder before full persisted migration, but every executed search must reach the ctzo validated capability. Consumer census distinguishes definitions, tests, examples and production call sites and fails when all non-test consumers are zero.
acceptance_criteria:
1. C1, C2/C3 and ctzo are closed with exact commits and their foundation_only versus production-activation receipts agree. Canonical public library and facade builders are fallible, accept independent typed fast and quality bindings, and execute through retained owner-backed tier capabilities.

2. Non-test library or facade call sites execute FastOnly, direct QualityOnly, FullProgressive independent retrieval plus deterministic union, truthful PartialQuality, LexicalOnly and explicit nonsemantic HashControl. The out-of-fast-pool fixture proves quality retrieval and union through the public library surface. Same-dimension wrong-space and swapped-tier mutations fail before semantic work.

3. A machine-readable repository and public-API census reports every definition, re-export, example, test and non-test consumer of the new identity, coverage, owner and topology types. Closure requires nonzero executed public-library/facade production consumers; core types, serde round trips, test-only create_v2 calls, comments or schema declarations cannot satisfy it.

4. No public library path applies one raw vector to both tiers, derives topology from dimension/name/id, labels hash as semantic, rescoring-only quality refinement as direct retrieval, or reports unknown coverage as complete. Requested/realized coverage and arm contribution come from retained owner witnesses and actual retrieval.

5. Library/facade unit, property, public API, interaction and no-mock in-process tests pass with bounded structured identity/topology/coverage logs, all aggregate feature builds, warnings-denied lint, formatting and changed-file scanning. This umbrella expressly does not close or require persisted restart, fsfs, CASS, terminal Treasure Island, recovery, cache/ANN/daemon or raw API retirement work.

title: Semantic search silently degrades to non-semantic hash embeddings (CASS: 'semantic search never works')
description:
REPRODUCED TERMINAL USER DEFECT: CASS reports semantic absent/needs_consent and real semantic retrieval is not reliably available. The umbrella tracks two distinct cross-repository defects without overstating either current call path.

CAUSE A1, GENERIC FRANKENSEARCH DEGRADATION: EmbedderStack auto-detection can return an infallible HashOnly stack when real model artifacts are absent. A consumer that builds vectors from it creates a fnv1a-identified nonsemantic generation; TwoTierSearcher correctly lexical-short-circuits shipped hash embedders. Installing a model later cannot repair that generation; compatible blue-green reindex is mandatory. Production callers must not silently inherit this generic default.

CAUSE A2, CURRENT CASS FORCING FUNCTION: current CASS does not call EmbedderStack::auto_detect in its ordinary registry path. It retains MiniLM as the requested default even when absent, so explicit semantic fails and hybrid falls back lexically. Hash is selected explicitly by --fast-only, an embedder override, or legacy state, but those states can still be mislabeled or lack an acquire/reindex/retry forcing function. CASS must truthfully distinguish missing model, explicit/legacy hash, missing/stale index and degraded hybrid, then offer policy-controlled recovery.

CAUSE B, SPLIT ARTIFACT AUTHORITY: CASS monolithic exact writer and reader both use vector_index/index-<embedder>.fsvi. The mismatch is specifically progressive/two-tier loading, readiness and ANN discovery, which still inspect vector.fast.idx/vector.idx/vector.quality.idx or directory conventions, can memoize progressive unavailable, and fall back to single-tier exact/lexical behavior. bd-07os supplies explicit paths, but safe serving additionally requires one immutable owned-byte authority so validation and search cannot be separated by path replacement. CASS ds7uy.1/.3 make a role-specific generation manifest plus retained owner the sole authority.

POLICY: requested mode and caller policy are explicit typed inputs. Explicit semantic fails closed with actionable ModelUnavailable/NeedsReindex. Hybrid may continue lexically only with machine-readable degradation and RecoveryPlan. Hash is reachable only through explicit constructor/test/control policy and is never semantic. Environment variables must not silently change library semantics. Every caller is audited by requested mode.

END-TO-END RECOVERY: empty cache request fails or offers policy-approved provisioning; acquire an immutable verified real-model generation; build a compatible nonzero semantic index generation at manifest-declared paths; validate the same owned bytes that will be searched; atomically publish the composite model/index selection; reclassify readiness; then retry the original request exactly once. Installing a model alone remains needs-reindex when the index is absent, hash-built or identity-incompatible.

DIAGNOSTICS: local actionable output may list bounded searched paths and exact commands; exported telemetry uses bounded hashes. Every selection/rejection records requested/realized mode, full vector-space identity hash, generation/topology, typed zero-signal reason and recovery without raw query/document/token/vector text.
design: This is the terminal cross-repo umbrella, not an auto-detect patch. It converges frozen identity, explicit paths, immutable owned-byte serving, role-specific model/vector/ANN generations, zero-signal semantics, provisioning/RecoveryPlan, real Treasure proof and CASS journal/readiness/reindex/query work. Foundational FrankenSearch APIs close on their own exact contracts; the final CASS receipt proves integration and avoids circular prerequisites.
acceptance_criteria: Both corrected causal families have executable regression tests. Generic auto-detect HashOnly, current CASS missing-MiniLM, explicit/legacy hash, progressive filename discovery, monolithic exact retrieval and ANN/readiness states all produce typed truthful outcomes. A fresh-process no-mock lifecycle proves empty cache -> actionable failure/policy -> immutable verified model acquisition -> source-consistent blue-green index at manifest paths -> same-owner validation/search -> composite publication -> readiness recheck -> one retry -> real semantic hits. Installing alone remains needs-reindex when appropriate. Explicit semantic fails closed; hybrid fallback is typed. Exact repository commits, model/corpus/docset/generation hashes, bounded diagnostics, redacted capped telemetry and zero-network warm restart evidence are retained.

comments.author: MossySpire
comments.text:
MossySpire: CAUSE A visibility fix LANDED (5097f545). CAUSE B refinement below -- the bead's model of it is slightly off in a way that changes where the fix belongs.

=== CAUSE A: what landed ===
The bead notes "Existing EmbedderStack degradation diagnostics were not wired to production callers." Confirmed and fixed. Three sites resolved a stack and immediately took fast_arc(), discarding availability(): index_builder.rs:209, and fsfs runtime.rs resolve_fast_embedder/resolve_quality_embedder (11181/11199).

Landed: IndexBuildStats::embedder_availability + is_degraded_generation(), plus a warn at BUILD time. Deliberately at the write boundary, because that is where the condition becomes permanent -- the vectors carry the embedder's identity, so a HashOnly build is an unrepairable generation and a later model install cannot fix it. Also covers a caller-supplied stack, since passing a hash stack explicitly is equally consequential. Three tests assert three DIFFERENT availabilities (HashOnly / FastOnly / Full) so a constant field cannot satisfy them.

CORRECTION to my own earlier claim that the read side had no signal: it already sets metrics.skip_reason = "non_semantic_fast_embedder_lexical_short_circuit" (searcher.rs:1255/1384). What it lacked was a log; TwoTierSearcher::new now warns once at construction (per-query logging would spam a hot path).

NOT fixed by this: retrieval itself. That needs acquisition + blue-green rebuild and is in flight elsewhere.

=== CAUSE B: the conventions do NOT silently mismatch -- the reader hard-errors ===
The bead says writer and reader naming "never intersect", implying silence. Within frankensearch that is not what happens. resolve_fast_path (two_tier.rs:1398) tries <dir>/vector.fast.idx, then <dir>/vector.idx, and on failure returns a TYPED error naming both attempted paths:

    Err(SearchError::IndexCandidatesNotFound { paths: vec![fast_path, fallback_path] })

That error is then handled well downstream: fsfs output_schema.rs maps IndexNotFound/IndexCandidatesNotFound to user-facing messages WITH the attempted paths and a remediation suggestion (743, 832, 837, 921). frankensearch's own writer uses the same constants (two_tier.rs:1376), so the library is internally consistent.

CONSEQUENCE: a CASS index at vector_index/index-<embedder>.fsvi does not silently produce lexical-only results at this layer -- it produces a typed, path-naming error. So the "semantic never participates, silently" symptom cannot originate in resolve_fast_path. It must come from the CASS integration boundary: either CASS constructs a searcher with no vector index at all (so the resolver is never reached), or it catches this error and continues degraded without surfacing it.

WHERE THE FIX BELONGS: bd-07os (explicit consumer-owned TwoTierIndex artifact paths) is exactly the right home, and the useful framing for it is "make the consumer declare its artifact paths" rather than "teach the reader more filename guesses". Adding index-<embedder>.fsvi as a third guess in resolve_fast_path would be the wrong fix: it makes discovery more magical, cannot disambiguate multiple embedders in one directory, and hides the very error that is currently doing its job.

RECOMMENDED NEXT DIAGNOSTIC for whoever owns it: instrument or trace the CASS path to determine which of the two applies -- resolver never reached, or typed error caught and discarded. That single fact decides whether the fix is path declaration (bd-07os) or error propagation, and it is cheap to obtain.

I did NOT edit any of this. crates/frankensearch-index/{lib,two_tier,search,hnsw}.rs and crates/frankensearch-embed/* are inside a live ~51-file uncommitted peer changeset whose design is still moving (RecoveryPlan appeared in the working tree and was then removed again). title: Fix TOCTOU race in PID file and lock sentinel acquisition
description: Both PidFile::acquire() in lifecycle.rs and try_acquire_sentinel() in concurrency.rs have TOCTOU races. They read the lock file, check if stale, then write a new one. Between check and write, another process can do the same. Fix: use OpenOptions::create_new(true) for atomic file creation with retry loop for stale lock cleanup.
close_reason: Already fixed in code (create_new + retry loops) and verified via rch-targeted fsfs tests

title: ArtifactStore v4 F1: immutable Source and Build byte snapshot
description: Implement an immutable byte-level Source plus Build snapshot that covers every compiler-visible input: tracked and untracked files, ignored-but-visible generated inputs, file kind and symlink target identity, workspace members, path dependencies, exact Cargo.lock, toolchain and target configuration, Cargo config, environment allowlist, build script and generated output identities, selected features/profile, and resulting executable hashes. Capture through descriptor-stable reads and reject any mutation or omission before execution authentication.
design: Build the snapshot from descriptor-stable byte reads and canonical relative paths. Bind file kind, mode where relevant, symlink link text and resolved target identity, inclusion reason, byte length and digest. Recursively include workspace and path-dependency manifests and sources, exact lock graph and registry/git checksums, rustup-selected compiler and linker identities, target specification, Cargo configs, environment allowlist, build script inputs/outputs, generated sources, feature/profile/rustflags, and the executable plus debug/build metadata needed to reproduce linkage.
acceptance_criteria: Mutation tests independently change a tracked file, untracked compiler-visible file, ignored generated input, symlink target, file kind, workspace member, path dependency, Cargo.lock entry, registry checksum, toolchain, linker, target config, Cargo config, feature, profile, rustflags, build script output, and executable; each mutation changes identity or rejects. Omitted compiler-visible inputs and ambiguous paths fail closed. Concurrent mutation during capture rejects rather than mixing generations. Verified reload reproduces the exact snapshot identity from canonical bytes. Strict-remote Linux and macOS builds bind their executing ELF or Mach-O to the admitted Source and Build objects.

title: ArtifactStore v4 F2: supervisor-issued execution and completion authentication
description: Add external supervisor-issued Execution and Completion authentication. The supervisor, not the measured child, owns a one-time nonce and signs the admitted source/build/run envelope and a final manifest after collecting terminal status, logs, artifacts, digests, resource/lifecycle receipts, and durability evidence. Every terminal outcome, including nonzero exit, signal, cancellation, timeout, overflow, and launch failure, receives an outcome-neutral authenticated completion or an explicit typed absence; the child cannot self-certify promotion eligibility.
design: A trusted external supervisor issues a single-use nonce after verifying F1, holds signing authority outside the child, launches the exact admitted executable, binds process tree, machine/profile, command, environment policy, corpus/query/fixture identities, and run window, then collects terminal artifacts through descriptor-stable paths. It signs completion only after validating exit/signal/cancel/timeout state, bounded logs, artifact digests, lifecycle/resource evidence, and required durability. The child may emit data but cannot sign or choose admission state.
acceptance_criteria: Real process tests cover launch success, nonzero exit, signal, cancellation, timeout, output overflow, exec failure, supervisor interruption, missing artifact, tampered log, cross-run artifact, nonce replay, expired nonce, wrong signer, child-held key, process-tree escape, source/ELF mismatch, and partial durability. Every terminal path yields either one signed completion bound to its issued nonce or a typed externally witnessed absence that is never promotable. A nonce is accepted once only. Completion signing is outcome-neutral and cannot change Pass/Miss/NoDecision. Linux and macOS mock-free supervisor runs verify the full chain.

title: ArtifactStore v4 F3: codec, ArtifactStore admission, and frozen v3 legacy path
description: Implement the v4 artifact codec and ArtifactStore admission boundary over F0 and F2. Preserve a frozen v3 reader labeled UnauthenticatedLegacy for reproducibility only. Add a pre-policy v4 rejecting canary so code cannot silently accept v4-shaped data through legacy defaults. Verified reload must bind content address, receipt chain, nonce, signer, terminal outcome, privacy policy, and source/build/execution/completion object graph before policy evaluation. Unknown versions, fields, algorithms, signers, partial writes, and downgrade attempts fail closed.
design: Use strict canonical v4 envelopes with create-new atomic publication, file and directory durability, content addressing over canonical bytes, and verified reload before policy. Keep the v3 parser frozen and tag every result UnauthenticatedLegacy. Dispatch on explicit version and object kind only. The v4 rejecting canary is evaluated before legacy/default policy so a new envelope cannot fall through to permissive handling.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip and golden tests cover every v4 object and terminal state. Unknown, missing, duplicated, reordered where prohibited, noncanonical, truncated, extended, partially written, digest-mismatched, signature-mismatched, wrong-nonce, wrong-signer, cross-object, and downgrade artifacts reject. The pre-policy rejecting canary proves v4 data cannot be admitted by a v3 reader or generic passed flag. Frozen v3 fixtures remain replayable but always UnauthenticatedLegacy and release-ineligible. Atomicity tests cover crash points through create, write, sync, rename/link, parent sync, and index publication.

title: ArtifactStore v4 F4: runner, QG, lexical, and privacy consumer wiring
description: Wire the authenticated v4 chain through the shared runner, QG evidence, perf ratchet, lexical gauntlet, CASS contract, H2 lifecycle receipts, and release validators using real consumer boundaries. FixturePublic remains the only CI and public-artifact mode; PrivateLocal policy remains independently governed and cannot block public fixture evidence. DiagnosticAttempt is always NoClaim, AdmittedCampaignEvidence may record Pass or Miss, and ReplacementQualified requires admitted Pass plus complete required coverage. No consumer may infer authenticity from content hashes alone or infer a win from authentication.
design: Consumers accept typed verified objects rather than paths, booleans, or caller-supplied hashes. Reconcile the shared runner with ScarletPelican-owned bd-e8h-p0-runner-verify-jr6w rather than duplicating runner source. H2 consumes authenticated lifecycle fields at evidence assembly. QG .15/.15.1 consume authenticated hashes only at promotion; diagnostic validation remains runnable without claiming authorization. Lexical and CASS artifacts replace stale ArtifactObject v2/V3/V5 promotion wording with explicit v4 authenticated coverage. Relate bd-fttb so FixturePublic can proceed independently while PrivateLocal remains opt-in and fail-closed.
acceptance_criteria: Mock-free E2E runs traverse supervisor -> ArtifactStore v4 -> runner or lexical producer -> verified consumer -> policy output. DiagnosticAttempt always yields NoClaim even when authentic. AdmittedCampaignEvidence records both Pass and Miss without relabeling. ReplacementQualified is possible only for VerifiedReceiptChain plus admitted Pass plus every required coverage witness and explicit release authority. Hash-only, v3 legacy, missing H2 lifecycle, missing coverage, private-policy mismatch, cross-worker mix, stale source/ELF, invalid null, and failed terminal completion reject promotion. FixturePublic CI evidence remains usable without PrivateLocal keys; no public-fixture dependency is blocked by bd-fttb.

title: ArtifactStore v4 F5: adversarial, mock-free, and cross-platform release review
description: Perform the terminal adversarial review of the full v4 chain on Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64 with mock-free supervisor and consumer executions. Attack source substitution, same-count and same-size artifacts, symlink and generated-input mutation, executable replacement, nonce replay, child self-signing, missing terminal receipts, outcome relabeling, v3/v4 downgrade, partial durability, privacy leakage, cross-worker mixing, and validator bypass. Preserve every invalidating receipt and require independent review before any promotion consumer treats v4 as release-capable.
design: Use an independent reviewer and red-team matrix against exact final source. Include same-count/same-size valid-object substitution, source and executable TOCTOU, path and symlink aliasing, build-cache poisoning, nonce and signature replay, child self-attestation, signer rotation, terminal receipt omission, authentic outcome relabeling, v3 downgrade, partial fsync, privacy canaries, cross-platform encoding, and direct consumer bypass. Preserve rejected artifacts with bounded diagnostics and replay commands.
acceptance_criteria: All declared attacks fail closed in deterministic unit/mutation tests and mock-free Linux x86_64 plus macOS arm64 E2E. At least one authentic Pass, authentic Miss, authentic failed execution, IntegrityOnly artifact, and UnauthenticatedLegacy artifact demonstrate distinct policy results. Review verifies no consumer relies on content hash, filename, passed boolean, exit zero, or schema version as authentication. Exact final-source strict-remote workspace check, clippy -D warnings, tests, formatting, UBS, source/build/supervisor/codec/consumer receipt hashes, and independent signoff are attached. title: ArtifactStore v4: authenticated provenance and outcome-neutral evidence admission
description: Restore the missing P0 ArtifactStore v4 program that binds immutable source and build inputs to supervisor-authenticated execution and completion receipts, then wires those receipts into evidence consumers without confusing authenticity with benchmark outcome. Artifact integrity, authenticated producer provenance, evidence admission, target decision, and release qualification are separate typed states. v4 must coexist with a frozen, explicitly unauthenticated v3 legacy reader; only authenticated v4 evidence may participate in new promotion paths. The umbrella closes only after F0 through F5 complete in dependency order.
design: Use a linear proof chain F0 -> F1 -> F2 -> F3 -> F4 -> F5. The umbrella has a blocking dependency only on terminal F5, which transitively waits for every earlier phase; the stable ArtifactStore v4 title prefix and labels provide hierarchy without reverse dependency edges or a parent-child cycle. Artifact authentication is outcome-neutral. Policy evaluates a verified object only after cryptographic and structural verification, and release qualification evaluates admission plus coverage and target decisions afterward.
acceptance_criteria: F0 through F5 are individually closed with implementing SHAs and exact proof. The dependency graph is acyclic and the umbrella is blocked transitively by all six phases. Machine-readable v4 states distinguish VerifiedReceiptChain, IntegrityOnly, and UnauthenticatedLegacy from AdmissionDecision and from Pass, Miss, NoDecision, Quarantine, and ReplacementQualified. No v3 or hash-only evidence can enter a new promotion path. Both valid losses and failed executions remain durable without becoming claims. Final strict-remote checks, cross-platform mock-free evidence, privacy canaries, adversarial review, and downstream consumer reconciliation are attached before closure.

title: int8 ADC two-pass vector scan (sidecar) — match Lucene/Meilisearch-class quantized retrieval
description:
RADICAL LEVER (from /extreme-software-optimization + /alien-graveyard dig). Context: the exact in-format dot kernels are now ~3x optimized (commits 72ac004/bca1374/c0e9c80) and the top-k path is already bounded-heap + rayon-parallel + merge. The dot scan is compute+bandwidth bound on f16. Further EXACT in-format speedup is exhausted (two ~0-gain reverts logged in NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE).

The incumbents we benchmark against (Lucene int8/HNSW, Meilisearch binary quantization, FAISS PQ/SQ) all win at scale via QUANTIZED first-pass + rescore. frankensearch does exact f16 brute force. The radical lever: int8 ADC (asymmetric distance computation) two-pass scan.

DESIGN (sidecar = NO FSVI format break):
- Build an additive int8 sidecar artifact next to the f16 FSVI: per-vector (or per-block) int8 quantization with a stored scale (and optional bias). Lazy/at-index-time build; absent => fall back to current exact f16 brute force.
- Pass 1: int8 dot over ALL N (SIMD i8->i16->i32 widening multiply-accumulate via wide; ~1 byte/elem => half the memory bandwidth of f16 + faster integer MAC). Produce approximate scores.
- Pass 2: take top-(k * rescore_mult) candidates, rescore with the exact f16 dot_product_f16_bytes_f32 (already optimized), return exact-ordered top-k of those.

WHY IT WINS: pass-1 int8 is ~2-4x faster than f16 (bandwidth + int MAC), and pass-2 full-precision runs on only k*mult candidates instead of N => net ~2-3x on the scan for 10k-100k corpora, while keeping near-exact recall.

PROOF OBLIGATIONS (hard, gate before landing):
1. RECALL eval: recall@10 vs exact brute force on the fixture corpus (and a realistic embedding corpus) MUST be >= a set threshold (e.g. 0.98) at the chosen rescore_mult. This is APPROXIMATE - it changes results, so it needs an IR-metrics gate (metrics_eval.rs has nDCG/Recall helpers), NOT a bit-exactness proof.
2. Determinism: pass-1 ordering + pass-2 rescore must be deterministic (tie-break by doc_id) so Tier-1 reproducibility holds for a fixed build.
3. Sidecar round-trip + absence fallback tests; existing FSVI round-trip unchanged.
4. Per-crate head-to-head bench: int8-two-pass vs exact f16 brute force on vector_search_topk-style workloads; record ratio + recall. Keep only if ratio < 0.97 AND recall >= threshold; else revert + NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.

Alien mapping: vectorized execution + quantized ADC (alien-graveyard), bounded-recall approximation with a measured guarantee (alien-artifact-coding: approximate with an error bound). Labels: perf, simd, vector-search, bold-verify, radical.
notes: Balanced 41-pair null control (8 full corpora/arm) on vmi1227854 was honest but undecidable: mult3 R=1.136852 inside [0.761654,1.306149], mult5 R=1.192786 inside [0.786578,1.198934]. Exact binary ffb2201d..., candidate leaf 23.36% self-time, recall/nDCG and bit parity pass. Production restored to ORIG; candidate retained bench-only. Retry only after external worker isolation/affinity materially narrows the per-function null floor.

title: quill: 1-byte vint decode fast path (read_vint/read_u32_vint — 33% of query self-time)
description: PROFILE-DIRECTED (local perf flat self-time on segment_fanout_ab query path, 2026-07-23): variable-length integer decode is ~33% of query self-time — read_vint (grimoire) 16.3%, PositionByteReader::read_u32_vint (quiver) 11.3%, PayloadReader::read_vint 3.6%, decode_vint_payload 1.8%. title: Quill Basic-field scoring must clamp term frequency to presence like Tantivy
description:
LIVE CASS-PROFILE RANK DIVERGENCE WITH EXACT NUMERICAL ROOT CAUSE. On a Basic-record-option field containing repeated edge-ngram terms, Tantivy stores no term frequency and therefore scores presence with effective tf=1. Quill currently feeds raw repeated-token tf into BM25 (observed tf=7), producing a stable RankMismatch. The predicted score delta is 0.756431132 and the observed delta is 0.756431579, residual 4.47e-7, which identifies record-option handling rather than floating-point noise.

Carry the schema posting record option into the scorer. Clamp Basic/Doc-only fields to presence tf=1 while preserving raw tf for fields that explicitly record frequencies or positions. The fix must apply consistently to exhaustive scoring, MaxScore/WAND/grouped execution, block maxima and every CASS compatibility path; bounds must remain sound. Do not normalize scores post hoc, loosen the comparator, reorder ties, or special-case the fixture.

Add an exact unit witness for repeated edge ngrams on a Basic field, an end-to-end Basic-versus-positioned schema regression, and the minimized real CASS campaign fixture. Run the full exact clean-provenance 40-path CASS differential campaign and join the mismatch/fix to the append-only Divergence Register. Preserve the pre-fix numerical evidence and fixing commit.
design: Make posting-record semantics explicit scorer input rather than inferring from token multiplicity. Basic fields use binary presence tf=1 for score and upper-bound computation. Frequency and position-bearing fields retain their recorded raw tf. One shared helper or typed scorer policy must feed exhaustive BM25, block-max bounds, WAND/MaxScore and grouped paths so pruning cannot disagree with exhaustive scoring. The patch remains limited to argus/index scorer plumbing and tests, with no query-parser, codec, comparator or post-ranking workaround.
acceptance_criteria: Focused strict-remote tests prove: repeated Basic edge-ngram tokens score exactly as presence tf=1; frequency/position-bearing controls retain tf>1 behavior; Basic and positioned end-to-end indexes match pinned Tantivy ordered IDs and f32 score bits within the registered exact contract; exhaustive, MaxScore/WAND, grouped and block-bound paths agree and prune soundly; empty, single occurrence, maximum frequency, multiple segments and reopen cases pass. The exact minimized CASS witness no longer produces RankMismatch, and the complete clean-provenance 40-path campaign passes or records every remaining independent mismatch. Workspace/quill check and clippy -D warnings, rustfmt, changed-file UBS, exact source/binary/corpus/query hashes and bounded logs are attached. The append-only Divergence Register retains first-seen numerical evidence, fixing commit and regression IDs.

title: Structure-aware differential fuzzing over query ASTs (Quill vs pinned tantivy oracle)
description:
The fixed gauntlet query set can find only divergences someone anticipated. Build structure-aware fuzzing that generates typed query trees, not random parser bytes, over the complete grammar supported by the ordinary public lexical contract: terms, phrases and slop, nested boolean AND/OR/NOT, required/prohibited/should combinations, field scope, numeric/string ranges, glob/prefix, boosts including invalid non-finite values, negation-only queries, oversized tokens, same-position alternatives, and empty/whitespace cases. Generate unsupported capability combinations in a distinct typed-error lane.

Comparison consumes the live method-bound Core Lexical V3 observation from bd-live-total-lexical-contract-gxwy and covers every field actually exposed by each invoked ordinary method. It must not fabricate snippets, highlights, counts, or other NotExposed values from a different call. Native enriched/count/page/CASS receipts remain independently required by bd-qwkq and the terminal release gate; they do not serialize ordinary AST fuzzing.

Shrinking is mandatory: minimize the query AST, schema, and corpus while preserving the exact mismatch class, then emit a Divergence Register candidate with seed and immutable evidence hashes. A deterministic PR corpus replays every prior failure, and a longer nightly campaign records grammar/depth/interaction coverage. Passing output is quiet. Failure output records bounded seed, canonical AST/schema/corpus hashes, both method-bound observations, first diff, shrink trace, and register ID without unrestricted query/document/metadata text.
design: Generate typed query ASTs constrained by a generated schema/capability model, with invalid combinations classified separately. Compare through the live ordinary total observation and exhaustively destructure each method-bound field. Shrink AST, schema and minimal corpus together while preserving mismatch class. Persist canonical bounded structures plus hashes and redacted excerpts. Coverage counters include every public AST variant, depth, interaction and capability; new variants fail the census until classified.
acceptance_criteria: Seeded PR and nightly campaigns cover every supported AST node, required interaction/depth/capability class and deliberate invalid class against both real engines. The same seed reproduces byte-identically. Every mismatch shrinks to a bounded AST/schema/corpus replay, receives a Divergence Register ID, and joins the regression corpus. Every value exposed by the invoked ordinary public method, including order/rank, score bits, metadata/explanation state, empty shape, cancellation and typed errors, is compared; NotExposed values are never synthesized from another call. Coverage thresholds and time budgets fail closed. Passing logs remain quiet; failure artifacts are bounded, redacted, immutable and replayable. The terminal release gate still separately requires enriched/count/page/CASS receipts, so no public modality is lost.

title: Grouped MaxScore prunes ZERO windows — 1b5a1018's pruning proof fails on main
close_reason:
FIXED in 73c61d74 (main+master). Root cause was NOT the merge/CheckpointPostingCursor hypothesis in the first comment -- that delegation is intact. It is structural: BufferedUnionScorer::new fills its first window at construction and fill_exhaustive_window swap_removes exhausted children, so a group whose postings all land inside one UNION_HORIZON window has an EMPTY active immediately, with its scores in score_window. group_upper_bound returned None on empty active => not groupable => exhaustive every window.

SageCardinal's correctness trap confirmed and avoided: caching the ceiling alone makes a drained group eligible while group_competitive_docs still enumerates only active, returning Ok(true) with ZERO docs pushed -- the root reads 'no documents in this window' and silently drops them from the top-k. All three parts landed together: (1) group_competitive_docs enumerates current + buffered residue at offsets >= scan_offset + live children's competitive cursors (provably non-overlapping: advance_buffered take()s the current score, and an active child was already advanced to at least the group's own horizon); (2) group_ceiling captured in new() from the original children before the first refill, None unless every original child is a bounded direct term; (3) group_upper_bound reads the cache. Scoring needed no change -- fill_candidate_window drives real child scorers via advance()/score()/next() and a Union's advance already consumes residue, so only candidate DISCOVERY was broken.

KEY FINDING -- THE EXISTING FIXTURE COULD NOT HAVE CERTIFIED THE FIX. At k=1 the dropped doc ties the incumbent at exactly 2e8 (its ~1.0 contribution is below the f32 ULP of ~16 at that magnitude) and loses the ascending-docid tie-break regardless, so deleting it changes nothing observable: the naive broken fix goes FULLY GREEN, prune assertion included. Proven empirically, not argued -- with only part 1 disabled behind a temporary probe, grouped_max_score_matches_exhaustive_and_prunes PASSES while the new test FAILS with 'docid differs at rank 1: 0 vs 5001'. Probe then removed; zero trace in the diff.

New pin: grouped_max_score_drained_essential_group_keeps_its_documents -- essential group drained to empty active with residue {5001,5002}, at k=3, where its docs must WIN the top-k so loss changes both ranking and hit count.

VERIFICATION: 465/465 quill lib tests pass (2 remote-only ignored); cargo check -p frankensearch-quill --all-targets green on DEFAULT features; clippy --no-deps -p frankensearch-quill --all-targets --features bench-internals exit 0; rustfmt clean. All on rch.

GROUPED_MAX_SCORE_ENABLED remains false. This UNBLOCKS bd-quill-e8-perf-doctrine-x4e4.5.1; it does not activate it. The flip still requires benches/grouped_maxscore_ab.rs decidable against its own A/A null -- and now it is finally meaningful to run, since the lever provably prunes.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND (SageCardinal) — and it is NOT the CheckpointPostingCursor/merge hypothesis in my earlier comment. Correcting that: the merge timeline is real but incidental; the defect is structural and would fail with or without ae5baa0d.

THE BUG: group_upper_bound() reads union.active, but a BufferedUnionScorer DRAINS active as soon as it fills a window.

argus.rs:3684 BufferedUnionScorer::new ends with 'if scorer.refill()? { scorer.advance_buffered(); }' — every union fills its first window AT CONSTRUCTION. fill_exhaustive_window (argus.rs:3800) advances each child through the window and SWAP_REMOVES any child whose doc() becomes None:

    self.active[index].next()?;
    if self.active[index].doc().is_none() { self.active.swap_remove(index); break; }

So a group whose postings all fall inside one 4096-doc window has an EMPTY active vector immediately after construction — its scores live in score_window, not in active.

group_upper_bound (argus.rs:3751) opens with 'if self.active.is_empty() { return None; }' => None => competitive_is_groupable == false => the all-groupable branch in competitive_candidates is skipped => control falls to '2..=MAX_SCORE_MAX_CLAUSES => return Ok(None)' => fill_exhaustive_window => max_score_windows stays 0. Exactly the observed stats.

WALK THE FIXTURE (rows_by_term = [[0,5000],[0,5000],[5000],[6000]], groups [2,2]):
- group0 terms [0,5000]: its window is [0,4096); after scoring doc 0, next() -> 5000 which is >= horizon, so 'index += 1' — NOT removed. group0.active stays 2.
- group1 terms [5000] and [6000]: group1's own first window starts at min(5000,6000)=5000, horizon [5000,9096) — BOTH postings are inside, so both terms exhaust and are swap_removed. group1.active == EMPTY.
=> competitive_is_groupable(group1) == false => no grouped pruning, ever.

WHY THE TERM PATH IS UNAFFECTED (the asymmetry I flagged): a direct Term child's competitive_score_upper_bound reads term.term_score_upper_bound, a value captured once in TermScorer::new (argus.rs:1332). It is independent of cursor drain state. Only the GROUP ceiling was made to depend on live active membership.

FIX DIRECTION: make the whole-group ceiling independent of drain state — compute it once at group construction (sum of all children's ceilings before any refill) and retain it. That stays rank-SAFE: a ceiling over all original children is still a valid upper bound for any remaining subset, merely looser as the group drains. Do NOT try to reconstruct it from active; active is not the group's remaining-work set.

Then re-run grouped_max_score_matches_exhaustive_and_prunes and require max_score_windows >= 1 WITH the existing bit-parity assertions still green, before unblocking bd-quill-e8-perf-doctrine-x4e4.5.1.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SECOND FINDING — THE OBVIOUS FIX IS A CORRECTNESS TRAP. Do not apply it. (SageCardinal)

I implemented the fix from my previous comment (cache the whole-group ceiling at construction, before the constructor's refill drains active), then checked the consumer before landing it. REVERTED — it converts 'prunes nothing' into 'silently returns wrong results'.

WHY: group_competitive_docs (argus.rs:2511) enumerates the group's candidate docs ONLY from union.active:

    for child in &union.active {
        let Some(mut cursor) = child.competitive_term_cursor() else { return Ok(false); };
        while let Some(doc) = cursor.doc() { ...; docs.push(doc); cursor.next()?; }
    }
    Ok(true)

If active is EMPTY (drained into score_window at construction — the very condition my ceiling fix makes eligible), the loop body never executes and the function returns Ok(TRUE) having pushed ZERO docs. The caller reads that as 'this essential group has no documents in the window', so the root never visits them => DOCUMENTS SILENTLY DROPPED FROM THE TOP-K.

Today that path is unreachable precisely BECAUSE group_upper_bound returns None for a drained group. So the current None-on-empty-active is LOAD-BEARING FOR CORRECTNESS, not merely a conservative default. I have added exactly that warning as a comment on group_upper_bound so the next agent does not repeat my near-miss.

WHAT THE REAL FIX REQUIRES: a group's remaining-doc set is NOT union.active. It is
  {current} UNION {window_start + off : off >= scan_offset, score_window[off].is_some()} UNION {docs reachable from active children's competitive cursors}
i.e. buffered residue PLUS live cursors. group_competitive_docs must enumerate all three, or fail closed (Ok(false)) whenever it cannot. Only once THAT is correct may group_upper_bound stop depending on active.

Sequencing for whoever takes this:
  1. Fix group_competitive_docs to enumerate buffered residue + live cursors, or fail closed.
  2. Add a fixture that puts a group ENTIRELY inside one 4096-doc window (the drained case — the existing fixture's group1, terms [5000] and [6000], is exactly this) and assert bit-parity vs exhaustive, so the doc-dropping path is pinned BEFORE it becomes reachable.
  3. Only then cache the ceiling at construction (that part is sound: a sum over all original children remains a valid upper bound for any surviving subset).
  4. Require max_score_windows >= 1 AND all bit-parity green.

I deliberately did NOT land steps 1-3 in a single pass at the end of a long session with one verification cycle available on a contended fleet. Rushing a rank-safety change under exactly those conditions is what produced this bead in the first place.

comments.author: MossySpire
comments.text:
MossySpire (cc/opus-5): CONFIRMED SageCardinal's root cause by independent code read, and found a THIRD problem that invalidates the proposed verification step. Read this before writing the fix.

=== CONFIRMED ===
(1) group_upper_bound (argus.rs:3757) returns None on empty active => competitive_is_groupable false => competitive_candidates falls to '2..=MAX_SCORE_MAX_CLAUSES => return Ok(None)' => fill_exhaustive_window. Zero pruning. Verified by reading, not by trusting the bead.
(2) group_competitive_docs (argus.rs:2511) iterates ONLY union.active and returns Ok(true) with zero docs pushed when active is drained. Confirmed load-bearing: the None in (1) is the only thing keeping that state unreachable.
(3) Fixture walk confirmed. group1 (terms [5000] and [6000]) has its own first window [5000, 9096) at construction, both postings fall inside, both children swap_remove => active EMPTY, scores in score_window. group0 keeps active=2 in window [0,4096) because its second posting (5000) is beyond the horizon and hits the 'index += 1' branch instead.

=== NEW FINDING: THE EXISTING TEST CANNOT CERTIFY THE FIX ===
The current fixture uses k=1, and at k=1 the doc-dropping bug is INVISIBLE -- so the naive ceiling-cache fix (the one SageCardinal correctly reverted) would make grouped_max_score_matches_exhaustive_and_prunes GO FULLY GREEN, prune assertion included, while silently dropping documents. The existing test would certify the broken fix.

Mechanism, traced through root window 2 ([5000, 9096), cutoff 2e8):
- By then group0 has refilled onto its own window at 5000; both its children exhaust inside it, so group0.active is ALSO empty. group0 is the ESSENTIAL group.
- Naive fix => group0 groupable => group_competitive_docs(group0) returns Ok(true) with ZERO docs => candidates == [].
- fill_candidate_window with an empty candidate slice: partition_point returns 0, candidates.get(0) is None, so every child takes the advance_scorer_to_horizon branch. NOTHING in window 2 is ever scored. Docs 5000 and 6000 both vanish.
- Top-1 is still doc 0, so assert_hits_bit_exact passes and max_score_windows becomes 1. Green, and wrong.

WHY k=1 HIDES IT (worth confirming when you run it): doc 5000 carries terms 0,1 (boost 1e8) PLUS term 2 (boost 1.0), so it should outscore doc 0. It does not, because the sum is computed in f32 where the ULP at 2e8 is ~16 -- the ~1.0 contribution rounds away and doc 5000 TIES doc 0 at exactly 2e8, losing the tie-break on ascending docid. That tie is why 'the true top-1 (doc 0)' in the fixture comment holds, and it is also why deleting doc 5000 from the candidate set changes nothing observable at k=1.

CONSEQUENCE: at k=2 the same drop turns top-2 [doc 0, doc 5000] into [doc 0] alone, and assert_hits_bit_exact fails on the length check first. So the drained-group fixture from step 2 of the plan MUST use k>=2, and should assert hit COUNT explicitly. A k=1 fixture is not a pin.

=== SCORING SIDE IS ALREADY CORRECT -- ONLY DISCOVERY IS BROKEN ===
fill_candidate_window (argus.rs:4234) drives the real child scorers via advance()/score()/next(), and ReferenceScorer::advance on a Union consumes that union's buffered residue correctly. So a drained group SCORES fine; it is only CANDIDATE DISCOVERY that cannot see it. That narrows the fix and means no change is needed on the scoring path.

=== FIX (revised from SageCardinal's sequencing) ===
A group's remaining doc set is exactly: {union.current} + {union.window_start + off : off >= union.scan_offset, score_window[off].is_some()} + {docs from active children's competitive cursors}. Three parts, all needed:
  - residue covers [group.window_start, group.horizon)
  - live cursors cover [group.horizon, root horizon_end) -- an active child was advanced to >= the GROUP's horizon during its own fill, so parts 2 and 3 do not overlap
  - filter to < horizon_end; all three parts are already >= root window_start because the root recomputes window_start as the min over children's current, so no doc can escape the window check at argus.rs:4093.
Then, and only then, cache the ceiling at construction (sum over ALL original children, computed in new() after the retain but BEFORE the first refill, and None unless every original child is a bounded direct term). A sum over all original children stays a valid upper bound for any surviving subset -- looser, still rank-safe.

Sequencing unchanged and still correct: enumeration first, k>=2 drained-group fixture second, ceiling cache third, then require max_score_windows >= 1 with bit-parity green.

title: Unstaged test vector_component_close_rejects_nan will fail: to_bits() fast-path catches identical NaN
description:
In hnsw.rs, the unstaged test assert!(!vector_component_close(f32::NAN, f32::NAN)) will fail because the to_bits() fast-path (line 474) returns true before reaching the is_finite() guard (line 476). f32::NAN.to_bits() == f32::NAN.to_bits() is true for canonical NaN.

Fix: move is_finite() check BEFORE to_bits() comparison, so NaN is rejected regardless of bit pattern. This is more defensive since NaN in vectors indicates data corruption.
close_reason: Handled in bd-1zyz fix. NaN-with-same-bits is correctly accepted by to_bits() fast path — this is benign since NaN vectors are rejected at construction time in build_from_parts(). Added 6 regression tests covering all Inf/NaN edge cases including vector_component_close_identical_nan_bits_accepted.

title: Total CASS-profile lexical result contract in live Quill/Tantivy gauntlet
description: The CASS-profile campaign adapters still emit only ranks, score bits, snippets and counts. They cannot use the ScoredResult-only LexicalObservation schema and are blind to CASS consumer-visible stored fields, filter realization, diagnostics and typed failures. design: First freeze the actual CASS consumer boundary by tracing coding_agent_session_search query/result/robot output and the frankensearch CASS compatibility APIs; list every observable field and behavior before coding. Define a versioned exhaustively typed CassLexicalObservation rather than a string map. It must bind raw/normalized query and parser diagnostics; structured filters and their realized lowering; ordered hits/native ties; exact score bits; document identity; every returned stored field and presence state such as agent/workspace/source path/message index/timestamp/title/content or preview/source identity/origin/conversation data as actually exposed; snippet/highlight/explain; count/empty shape; pagination; and typed errors. Content-bearing values persist only canonical digest, length and absent/empty/value state. Both CassQuillSubject and CassTantivyOracle must materialize this observation through their normal consumer boundary or an exhaustively destructured dev adapter over the same implementation, not by echoing the input corpus. Add the profile bundle beside the legacy EngineObservation so rank/tie/count/AST evidence is preserved. Integrate comparison, artifact v2, campaign disposition, divergence registry, replay/shrink and redaction exactly like the core total bundle. Any field the two backends cannot expose symmetrically must be explicitly NotExposed with a reviewed contract decision, never silently omitted.
acceptance_criteria: A checked field inventory links every CASS public result, CLI JSON and robot field to one exhaustively typed observation member and test. Adding or changing a public field breaks compilation or a schema-exhaustiveness golden. Independent per-field mutations, None-versus-empty presence, filters, diagnostics, typed errors, pagination, counts, empty shape, equal-score ordering, snippets and stored-field digests fail the live comparator. A bounded deterministic campaign proves real CASS Quill and Tantivy adapters persist, reload, compare, replay, shrink and redact ArtifactObject v2 without echoing the source corpus. Unknown-version, omitted-field, tamper and redaction canaries pass. Legacy rank, tie, count and AST suites remain green. The mandatory 10K PR, 250K-plus nightly, repository-snapshot and CASS-profile executions are owned by bd-y7vz, which depends on terminal bd-qwkq; no scale requirement is removed or duplicated.
