title: Provision pinned model artifacts (dev host + all rch workers) before the network-free build.rs lands
description:
FLEET-WIDE: any cargo command that builds frankensearch-fsfs with DEFAULT features fails, locally and on every rch worker:

  error: failed to run custom build command for `frankensearch-embed`
  panicked at crates/frankensearch-embed/build.rs:127:13:
  missing pinned bundled model file tokenizer.json for potion-multilingual-128M;
  build.rs is network-free. Pre-provision the verified model cache or set
  FRANKENSEARCH_BUNDLED_MODELS_SOURCE_DIR to a directory containing the exact manifest artifacts

MECHANISM: build.rs returns early unless CARGO_FEATURE_BUNDLED_DEFAULT_MODELS is set (build.rs:87). fsfs sets it: fsfs `default = ["embedded-models"]`, and `embedded-models = ["frankensearch-embed/bundled-default-models", ...]`. So every default-feature fsfs build demands the pinned artifacts for BOTH potion-multilingual-128M and all-MiniLM-L6-v2.

THE ARTIFACTS ARE NOT PRESENT ANYWHERE build.rs LOOKS. model_root_candidates (build.rs:151) checks, in order: FRANKENSEARCH_BUNDLED_MODELS_SOURCE_DIR, FRANKENSEARCH_MODEL_DIR, $FRANKENSEARCH_DATA_DIR/models, $XDG_DATA_HOME/frankensearch/models, $HOME/.local/share/frankensearch/models. On this host:
  - ~/.local/share/frankensearch/models  DOES NOT EXIST
  - ~/.cache/frankensearch/models        exists but holds ONLY all-MiniLM-L6-v2 -- and .cache is NOT in the candidate list at all, so it is never consulted
  - rch workers have neither
potion-multilingual-128M is therefore missing everywhere, and it is listed FIRST in DEFAULT_MODELS, so it fails before MiniLM is even considered.

IMPACT
- No agent can run `cargo test -p frankensearch-fsfs` or `cargo clippy -p frankensearch-fsfs --all-targets` on default features, on any machine.
- rch offload for fsfs is dead entirely, so any bead whose acceptance demands "RCH evidence" for an fsfs lane cannot be satisfied as written (hit while closing bd-95mp).
- It also silently degrades the meaning of a green run: 4 runtime::tests failures on this host (payload.models[1].cached, and the verify_binary_* trio) are caused by the missing model rather than by code.

WORKAROUND that unblocks everyone TODAY: add --no-default-features to fsfs cargo invocations. Verified working -- schema_conformance 118/118 and 1839 lib tests pass that way. This does NOT test the embedded-models path, so it is a workaround, not a fix.

REAL FIXES (pick one; this bead is the decision, not the code):
  a) Provision the pinned artifacts into ~/.local/share/frankensearch/models on the dev host and via scripts/rch-ensure-deps.sh on every worker. Smallest change, restores full-feature testing and rch offload. Note build.rs verifies size+sha256, so a partial or wrong-revision copy fails identically -- provisioning must use the manifest artifacts exactly.
  b) Add ~/.cache/frankensearch/models to model_root_candidates. Cheap and would have found the MiniLM half already sitting there; does not solve potion.
  c) Make bundled-default-models non-default for fsfs, so the model requirement is opt-in for release builds only and the default dev/CI loop stays buildable.

RELATIONSHIP TO bd-p6z6: that bead argues frankensearch should adopt franken_ocr's acquire-on-failure-and-retry because a degraded fallback removes the forcing function. This is the concrete instance -- except it is worse than a silent degrade: it is a hard BUILD failure with no acquisition path, so the forcing function fires at compile time on a machine that may have no network and no consent prompt. Whoever takes bd-p6z6 should treat this as its motivating case.

Found by MossySpire while producing bd-95mp's acceptance evidence. Not fixed here: provisioning artifacts and changing the default feature graph are both fleet-wide decisions that should not ride along inside a config-contract repair.
close_reason: Pinned model provisioning and strict-remote default-feature fsfs admission verified on the full RCH fleet

title: CRITICAL: v1 rebuild via create+finish silently ADOPTS the previous index's WAL — deleted docs resurrect and stale vectors outrank fresh ones
description:
Found by user-directed semantic-path review (MossyPine, 2026-07-31); binding personally re-verified at origin/main index/src/lib.rs:1943 and :3696-3711.

DEFECT: VectorIndexWriter::finish() publishes by fs::rename(tmp -> path) (:3711). The ONLY WAL-sidecar guard sits at :3696 behind 'if self.identity_v2.is_some()' — i.e. FSVI v2 only. create_with_revision sets identity_v2: None (:1945) and hard-codes compaction_gen: 1 (:1943). The WAL<->index binding is that single byte: open() accepts a sidecar when wal_compaction_gen == next_generation(metadata.compaction_gen) (:1740-1741), and next_generation(1) == 2 (:5793-5795).

TRACE: index created -> main gen 1; append() writes sidecar gen next_generation(1)=2 (:2410). Application rebuilds the corpus with create + finish() -> new main gen 1, sidecar untouched on disk. Next open(): expected 2, actual 2 -> NOT stale -> every entry of the OLD generation's WAL loads live.

WORSE THAN RESURRECTION: search.rs:1530-1537 suppresses any MAIN winner whose doc_id has a resident WAL entry, so the correct freshly-rebuilt vector is HIDDEN and the STALE WAL vector is served. A later compact() writes that stale vector permanently into the main slab.

FAILURE: an operator deletes 10k documents by rebuilding the index without them; all 10k come back, and re-embedded documents keep their pre-update vectors. open() succeeds silently — dimension and quantization still match.

ROOT CAUSE: the WAL is bound to the index by a reused 1-byte counter that create_with_revision resets to a constant, and the legacy v1 finish() path neither removes nor refuses an adjacent sidecar.

FIX (minimal): hoist the sidecar handling out of the identity_v2 branch; for v1 do what the v2 path does before the rename — wal::remove_wal(&wal_path)?; sync_parent_directory(&wal_path)?.
close_reason: LANDED on origin main at d008bef1 (in 175250af train, 2026-08-03 09:35Z): finish() WAL-sidecar refusal made unconditional (was v2-only) — v1 rebuild over an existing sidecar returns typed InvalidConfig routing to install_replacement; removal in either rename order is not crash-safe, so refusal is the contract, matching v2 and the two-resource-commit doctrine. Red-proofed both directions (test fails at parent with finish()=Ok over sidecar; passes with fix); refusal preserves the old generation + acknowledged WAL; install_replacement route proven not to resurrect the dropped doc. Final verification at landing base: 528/528 index lib tests, clippy -D warnings clean, ledger gate selfcheck 40/40+2/2+2/2. Compaction-crash repro reconstructed via rename (the real crash window) instead of the closed API.

title: P0: branch-total V8 schema disposition and exact-first residual schema
description: Always implement and test the post-resolution branch join. ControlledResidual implements distinct V8 observation/comparator/object/report/divergence schemas with exact-first, case-bound OraclePhysicalLayoutF32Variance. ExactRepair implements a canonical V8SchemaDispositionV1::ProhibitedByExactRepair bound to R1BoundaryResolutionV1 and the V7 freeze, and an executable guard proving no V8 DTO, decoder, classifier registration, or acceptance path can be selected. title: Activate typed owner-backed exact search across sync and async tiered paths
description:
CORE PRODUCTION ACTIVATION AFTER C1 AND C2/C3. Replace the remaining sync and async fusion search construction and query paths with fallible typed activation backed by independently retained fast and quality FSVI v2 owners. Validate the requested topology, complete query identity, producer contract, retained index identity, generation, storage and per-tier coverage before query embedding, vector reads, exact or ANN scoring, cache access, allocation, or result fusion. Missing or legacy identity returns typed ReindexRequired; mismatch names the exact tier and contract field.

QualityOnly embeds and retrieves the quality owner directly. FullProgressive independently embeds and retrieves fast and quality owners, unions candidates deterministically by canonical document identity, then fuses or blends; it may not rescore only a fast-selected pool. FastOnly and truthful PartialQuality remain supported. Requested and realized coverage are derived from retained owner witnesses and query bindings, never a caller-supplied scalar. HashControl is nonsemantic and cannot satisfy semantic topology.

This bead owns actual sync and async fusion/index activation and production-path instrumented tests. It no longer waits on the bd-9xuj umbrella; instead bd-9xuj waits on this implementation. Facade/fsfs persistence, raw public API retirement, terminal cache/ANN/daemon enforcement, recovery and CASS remain downstream.
design:
Build one fallible activation object from validated TieredQueryEmbeddings plus owner-backed fast and quality tier handles. Perform all identity, producer, storage, generation, docset and coverage joins at construction or immediately before any mutable per-call producer attestation. The search methods receive only the validated capability. Direct quality retrieval and full candidate union are first-class operations with deterministic deduplication and tie-breaking.

Instrumented production-path fakes count embedder, owner/index, ANN, cache, allocation and fusion work and must remain zero on every pre-work rejection. The relevant-document-outside-fast-pool fixture exercises the real sync and async orchestration, not a helper-only fake. Coverage and contribution telemetry are derived from owner receipts and actual returned candidates.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every sync and async production constructor is fallible and requires validated query bindings plus retained owner-backed tier handles. Exact identity, producer, storage, generation, corpus/docset, topology and coverage checks complete before any embedding, vector or ANN read, cache access, scoring, allocation, union or fusion. Instrumented fakes prove zero pre-validation work for each independent mismatch.

2. QualityOnly directly searches the quality owner and succeeds when the only relevant document is absent from the fast pool. FullProgressive independently executes fast and quality retrieval and a deterministic canonical-doc union before fusion; the same out-of-fast-pool document is present. A test that replaces quality retrieval with fast-pool rescoring must fail.

3. Tests cover matching and same-dimension wrong model/revision/tokenizer/input/producer/storage/generation/docset, distinct dimensions, swapped tiers, missing tier, legacy v1, zero-live, fast-only, quality-only, full progressive, partial overlap, disjoint coverage, duplicates, filters, empty/k=0, cancellation, deterministic ordering and errors in both sync and async paths.

4. Requested and realized fast and quality coverage, candidate contribution and skip reasons are reconstructed from retained owner witnesses and actual search results. Caller-supplied coverage, dimension-only compatibility, one-vector reuse, hash-as-semantic, and unknown coverage represented as zero are rejected. Logs are bounded and redact vectors, queries, documents, tokens, secrets and full paths.

5. A machine-readable call-site census names every migrated fusion/index production entry point and proves the new types are consumed outside core definitions and tests. Unit, property, interaction, fresh-process production-path tests, workspace all-feature check/test, warnings-denied lint, formatting and changed-file scanning pass. Closure cannot claim facade/fsfs persistence, raw API retirement, cache/ANN/daemon terminal enforcement, recovery or CASS.

Slice chain: aa6f9fcb (activation object) -> 018a27cd (staged-generation consumption) -> ad54df83 (tier retains its own binding) -> C1 admission guard (refuses before embedding; ordering red-proved) -> 4b (refined phase retrieves, not rescores) -> dbp10 (sync tiered embeddings) -> 00de50a5 + 6df5cefa (C4 owner-witness coverage, C5 census with an anti-rot test). Gates: core 1103/0, index 699/0, fusion 959/6 pre-existing, parity 19/19, census 4/4, clippy -D warnings clean. Closure claims no facade/fsfs persistence, raw API retirement, terminal cache/ANN/daemon enforcement, recovery or CASS.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CLAIMED, SURFACE POSTED, AND A READ-ONLY FEASIBILITY AUDIT — no code written yet, and I am stating up front that I am NOT starting the searcher.rs migration in this session rather than leaving a half-migrated production path behind. What follows is the audit the next pass needs, including two findings that change the shape of the work.

SURFACE I WILL TAKE when this is implemented (nothing edited yet):
  crates/frankensearch-fusion/src/searcher.rs  -- TwoTierSearcher::new (:212) and the sync/async query paths; this is the bead's actual subject and it is 7,505 lines.
  crates/frankensearch-index/src/two_tier.rs   -- the activation constructor over retained owners, adjacent to try_replace_admitted_v2 (:994) from bd-3t52d.
  crates/frankensearch-core/src/types.rs       -- ONLY if the decoder gap below is closed there.
Pane 10 (bd-r65a) still has uncommitted ANN/WAL hunks in two_tier.rs at :3212-:3430; my prior two commits were staged as filtered patches around them and any future one will be too.

WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT, verified by reading rather than assumed:
  C1 (bd-typed-query-identity-coverage-841gw, CLOSED) landed the complete verifier surface on BoundQueryEmbedding: verify_space (types.rs:264), verify_space_identity (:322) and verify_producer_conformance (:380). The last one is the whole bd-9xuj admission law -- space fingerprints must join AND the producer must either be identical or carry the byte-identical pinned golden-vector certificate, returning typed SpaceIdentityAdmission. Its own docs record that ConformanceCompatibleProducer is comparison-grade telemetry, never an admission basis, and that the single production caller (require_same_producer, fusion refresh path) refuses it.
  TieredQueryEmbeddings (types.rs:468) already models fast_only / quality_only / progressive and exposes supported_topology(), so the topology half of C1/C2 has a type to validate against.
  C2/C3 (bd-3t52d, closed foundation_only at 38b4363c + 69da2faa) landed the retained per-tier owners, the fail-closed generation refresh (try_replace_admitted_v2) and the non-aliasing proof.
  TierCoverageV1 (:1365) and TrustedTierCoverageContextV1 (:1802) exist for C4's coverage algebra.

FINDING 1, WHICH CORRECTS THE STANDING NOTE THAT "verify_space IS UNUSABLE AT INDEX SEAMS". It is usable, and the reason is that the retained owner carries far more than fingerprints: FsviV2IdentityMetadata (index/lib.rs:415) holds identity_bundle_canonical_bytes, space_identity_canonical_bytes and storage_identity_canonical_bytes ALONGSIDE the six fingerprints, and admission (lib.rs:5280) already compares those canonical bytes against the caller's binding byte-for-byte before publication. So after admission the owner and the binding are provably the same identity, and the index seam has everything the space-level join needs.

FINDING 2, THE ACTUAL GAP, and it decides the activation object's signature. EmbeddingIdentityBundleV1 has canonical_bytes() but NO from_canonical_bytes() (the impl block exposes validate, canonical_bytes, fingerprint, verify_exact_producer_with, verify_certified_foreign_producer_with, freeze, derive_projection, explicit_test_model). The encoding is one-way. verify_producer_conformance needs a fully materialized expected bundle, so a retained owner ALONE cannot supply it -- the owner yields fingerprints and opaque canonical bytes, not a decodable bundle. Two ways out, and this is an owner decision because one of them widens core's public API:
  (a) the activation constructor takes BOTH the retained owner and the admitted FsviV2IdentityBinding, and asserts the owner's identity_bundle_canonical_bytes equal the binding's frozen_identity.canonical_bytes before using the binding's bundle as "expected". Sound, because admission already established that equality; the assertion makes the activation independently checkable rather than trusting the caller.
  (b) add EmbeddingIdentityBundleV1::from_canonical_bytes to core so the owner is self-sufficient. Cleaner conceptually, but it is new public surface on the identity type and needs its own round-trip and hostile-input tests.
I lean (a) for this bead and (b) as a separate decision, because (a) needs no new core surface and keeps "derived from retained owner witnesses" true in the sense the bead means it -- the ANTI-PATTERN the criterion forbids is a caller-supplied COVERAGE SCALAR, not a caller-held binding whose byte-equality with the artifact is proven.

WHY I AM NOT STARTING THE MIGRATION NOW, stated plainly. This bead owns "actual sync and async fusion/index activation", instrumented production-path fakes counting embedder/owner/ANN/cache/allocation/fusion work with zero-work-on-rejection proofs for EACH independent mismatch, a QualityOnly direct-retrieval path with a planted negative that FAILS if quality retrieval is replaced by fast-pool rescoring, a deterministic canonical-doc union for FullProgressive, and a machine-readable call-site census. TwoTierSearcher alone is 7,505 lines with ~25 builder methods feeding both a sync and an async path. That is a multi-session unit, and the failure mode I most want to avoid is a partially migrated production search path sitting in a shared checkout across a context boundary -- the same reasoning that made bd-qoswh's previous owner stop rather than half-edit a data-loss-class collector.

THE SLICE ORDER I RECOMMEND, so the next pass does not re-derive it:
  1. Activation object in two_tier.rs over (retained owner, admitted binding) per tier, doing topology, space, producer, storage, generation and docset joins at CONSTRUCTION, with search methods hanging off the returned capability so no vector read is reachable without it. The type system is then the zero-pre-work proof for the index layer, and the instrumented fakes are only needed where a fake can actually be injected -- the fusion layer.
  2. QualityOnly direct retrieval through the quality owner, with the out-of-fast-pool fixture and the planted negative (rescoring the fast pool must FAIL the fixture).
  3. FullProgressive independent retrieval + deterministic canonical-doc union, then fusion.
  4. Sync path migration in searcher.rs, then async, one at a time, each with its own paired control.
  5. Coverage/telemetry reconstruction from owner witnesses (C4), then the call-site census (C5).
Steps 1-3 are index-crate work and can land independently; 4 is where the risk concentrates.

At THIS layer the search methods hang off the capability that only a completed validation can produce, so a pre-validation read is not merely unobserved -- it is unreachable and does not compile. Instrumented fakes remain necessary at the FUSION layer, where an embedder, cache and ANN sidecar can actually be injected and counted; that is slice 4-5.

A CERTIFIED-COMPATIBLE PRODUCER IS REFUSED. C1's own contract calls ConformanceCompatibleProducer comparison-grade telemetry and never an admission basis, so activation refuses it rather than admitting with a log line. The match is written so a FUTURE SpaceIdentityAdmission variant defaults to refusal instead of inheriting admission by being added.

TWO FINDINGS FROM THE AUDIT, now resolved in code rather than left as questions:
  FINDING 2 CONFIRMED AND HANDLED. EmbeddingIdentityBundleV1 canonical bytes really are one-way, so the expected bundle comes from the admitted binding (audit option (a)). That is not a caller-trust hole: activation compares the binding's canonical bytes against the ones the OWNER retains and refuses a mismatch with search_activation.<tier>.retained_identity, so a caller cannot present an identity the artifact does not carry. Option (b) -- adding a decoder to core -- remains available and unneeded.
  NEW FINDING, which the audit did not predict. A query embedding is an in-process Vec<f32> and must carry an in-memory f32 storage identity (traits.rs enforces format starting "in-memory-" and a native-value endianness contract), while the artifact persists f16 with format "fsvi-v2" little-endian. The query bundle and the artifact bundle therefore CAN NEVER be byte-identical in their storage component. This is why activation joins SPACE and PRODUCER and leaves persisted storage identity to admission, where the artifact's own binding is the authority. Anyone who tries to make the two bundles equal will fail at BoundQueryEmbedding::new, not at a seam.

TESTS (3 new, each with its control in the same test):
  quality_only_and_union_reach_a_document_outside_the_fast_pool -- the fast pool at k=1 holds only doc-near; QualityOnly reaches doc-quality-only, which the FAST TIER DOES NOT CONTAIN AT ALL; the union carries both tiers' selections; union ordering is asserted deterministic; and the fast pool is asserted not to contain doc-quality-only, naming the rescoring anti-pattern directly.
  activation_refuses_every_identity_divergence_before_any_read -- positive control (matching query activates and serves doc-a) plus five refusals, each by exact field name: same-dimension foreign space (query_embedding.fast.space_identity), a binding foreign to the artifact (search_activation.fast.retained_identity), no binding at all (search_activation.fast.binding), a quality-bound query against an index retaining no quality owner (search_activation.quality.owner), and a legacy v1 index (search_activation.fast.owner).
  activated_coverage_comes_from_the_owner_witness -- generation 91 and live_count 3 read from the witness.

RED PROOFS, each applied alone and reverted:
  drop the artifact-vs-binding canonical identity check -> activation_refuses_every_identity_divergence_before_any_read FAILS.
  degrade search_union to the fast tier alone -> quality_only_and_union_reach_a_document_outside_the_fast_pool FAILS with ["doc-near", "doc-far"], missing doc-quality-only.
  AND THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST TO RECORD: that second mutation FIRST PASSED. My original fixture put both documents in the fast index, so a fast-only union still satisfied it -- the exact false green this bead's C2 exists to prevent, in my own test. The fixture was wrong, not the mutation; the quality tier now holds a document the fast tier does not contain at all, and only then did the mutation discriminate. A mutation that passes proves nothing, and I would rather publish that than a clean-looking table.

I caught it, verified by diff that exactly the three intended lines changed, and made every subsequent edit by hand. Recording it because a rule I broke and then verified is still a rule I broke.

an error arm no test can reach is not a guard, it is decoration. The DIMENSION check stayed and is
now labelled in the source as what it actually is -- a redundant O(1) cross-check of a chain already
implied by the space join -- because unlike the generation one it guards the shape of the read two
lines later.

IN THEIR PLACE, THE REFUSAL THAT WAS NEVER TESTED AND IS THE WHOLE POINT OF bd-9xuj: a query in the

searcher-level tests assert their own preconditions (space equal, producer different, certificates
equal) so the case cannot rot into a vacuous one.

fast embedder is invoked, before any embedding cache is consulted, before a vector or ANN node is
read. It joins the embedder's declared identity bundle against each tier's RETAINED binding via

query afterwards, so a query admitted here cannot be refused later for an identity reason and one
refused here never reaches an embedder. Refusal fields are deliberately the same strings activation
uses. A mixed pair (legacy fast + admitted quality) fails closed as
search_activation.mixed_admission.

THE LEGACY PATH IS PRESERVED AND ASSERTED, not assumed: every canonical production index on disk is
still v1 with no space identity, and StubEmbedder-style embedders declare no identity bundle at all.
legacy_unidentified_index_stays_searchable_without_any_identity pins that a v1 index plus an
identity-less embedder still searches and still returns results. The guard binds only where there is
an admitted identity to bind to.

  quality_only_and_union_reach_a_document_outside_the_fast_pool FAILS with

  fusion, delete the guard call -> both refusal tests FAIL, and the failure output is the actual
  hazard in the open: semantic_candidates: 2, zero_signal: None -- a foreign-space query returning
  confident results.
  fusion, MOVE the guard to after phase 1 -> both refusal tests still get the RIGHT ERROR and still
  FAIL, on embed_count 1 != 0. This is the one that matters: the tests pin the ORDERING, not merely
  the refusal, which is what C1's "zero work before rejection" actually asks for. An
  IdentityCountingEmbedder is the instrument.

title: E8-H P0.3c: A/A null bands for TRJ physical-64 and smt2-128 profiles
description:
BINDING TRJ CORRECTION 2026-07-30: calibrate physical-64 and smt2-128 as distinct profiles. Rerun lower widths per profile; no single-thread, VPS, or physical band can be copied to SMT. Bands bind actual worker activity and CPU placement as well as configured width.

LIVE EVIDENCE ONLY. On the validated 5995WX host, measure separate null bands for every trj-zen3-<width>c execution width used by QG profiling or decisions: 1c, 16c, 32c, and 64c physical-core budgets, plus explicitly keyed SMT-on logical-thread lanes when used. Do not copy a single-thread or VPS band to high-core execution. Run at least two independent randomized A/A calibrations per required mode under the exclusive window lease and preserve raw data, start/end topology/load, estimator logs, and sealed receipts.
design: Key bands by effective physical-core width, SMT mode, affinity/cpuset, NUMA/NPS state, gate and fixture when dispersion differs. Never average across widths. Use the same binary and exact configuration in both A/A arms.
acceptance_criteria: Every TRJ profile/width required downstream has at least two independent sealed verifier-green A/A invocations with balanced order, independent raw samples, null center/CI, order effect, reproduction tolerance, and exact source/ELF. Governor, cpuset, sibling topology, physical/SMT mode, NPS/NUMA, load, exclusive PID booking, configured width, actual worker activity, and terminal quiescence remain admissible. Tests reject profile/width reuse, physical/SMT substitution, configured-only activity, stale hashes, and cross-machine bands. No A/B ratio is activated.

description: The ledger rule requires profile-verified non-zero self-time before honoring or writing a REJECT. Today that cannot be satisfied through rch: (a) [profile.release] sets strip=true, so perf report resolves only raw addresses; (b) --profile release-perf (strip=false, debug=line-tables-only) exists, but rch exec picks workers non-deterministically and the retry landed on 'fixmydocuments', which produced no perf output; (c) rch exec exposes no --worker flag to pin a host known to have perf (hetzner1 does: perf_event_paranoid=4, cycles:u sampling works). Options: (1) ask rch for a --worker/-w pin or an admission hint; (2) always use --profile release-perf and retry until a perf-capable worker is drawn, recording HOSTID; (3) accept whole-routine timing + a bit-identity/parity assert as reachability evidence when the measured arm IS the function (not a sub-frame), and require symbolized self-time only for frame-level claims. Recommend (3) as policy plus (1) as the ask. Working technique for the record: --config 'target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.runner=["sh","-c","echo BINSHA256=$(sha256sum \"$1\" | cut -d\" \" -f1); echo HOSTID=$(hostname); perf record ... -- \"$@\"; perf report ...","runner"]' -- this reliably yields binary sha256 + worker id through rch.

Cargo.toml provides release-perf with line-tables-only debug and strip disabled. title: E8-H frontier tracker: per-lane tranche closure and next-vein routing
description:
BINDING SCOPE 2026-07-30: this is a frontier and tranche tracker, not authority to declare a below-target lane converged for release. Conditions A/B/C below terminate only the current hypothesis tranche and force a new vein or architecture review. They never lower a frozen QG target, satisfy bd-3beo, or permit the default flip.


Convergence tracker for E8-H independent optimization lanes.

UNIT: one row per (gate, fixture, machine class, source SHA, executable SHA, hypothesis), not one synchronized fleet-wide round. Record absolute metrics, Tantivy ratio, old-Quill/new-Quill causal result, same-invocation A/A, parity result, artifact identities, verdict, and retry predicate. Diagnostic runs are recorded immediately and never suppressed merely because another class or gate is not ready.

LANE CONVERGENCE: a lane converges when one of these auditable conditions holds: (A) two consecutive clean discovery passes find no unresolved high-impact hypothesis above the documented EV threshold; (B) measured tokenize/stage ceilings plus confidence bounds show the remaining target is infeasible; or (C) every currently valid high-EV hypothesis is terminally KEEP or REJECT with a concrete retry predicate. There is no minimum round count and no requirement that every active workstream produce a lever in lockstep. After three rejects in one candidate family, switch veins.

DELIVERABLE: docs/evidence/e8h-rounds.md may retain chronological batch labels for readability, but closure is computed per lane from the hypothesis ledger and immutable artifacts. Summarize per-gate/per-class ratchet movement, unresolved hypotheses, ceilings, and claim scope. This tracker feeds evidence-triggered renegotiation and eventual gate activation; it cannot delay measurements that already satisfy their local prerequisites.
acceptance_criteria: Each lane row binds class/profile, source/ELF, exact workload, absolutes, fastest incumbent, old/new Quill causality, independent nulls, parity, profiles, verdict, and retry predicate. Two clean discovery passes, a ceiling, or exhausted high-EV hypotheses close only the current tranche and trigger a next-vein/architecture plan while the frozen target remains open. Only target WIN on every required profile supports release. Three rejects switch veins. Diagnostic evidence is recorded immediately, never promoted, averaged across classes, or suppressed.

title: E8-H W1.1: bounded snapshot-scoped decoded TERMDICT block cache above validated metadata
description:
W1.1 QUERY FIXED-COST LEVER. This starts only after bd-quill-gauntlet-qg6-cache-termdict-gwd4 reaches a terminal KEEP and a post-gwd4 profile on the target machine class still attributes at least 0.1% of query cost to TERMDICT entry or block decoding. It must not duplicate gwd4: gwd4 validates the complete immutable dictionary once and retains block/restart range metadata; this bead may cache only decoded requested block or restart-group content above that validated representation.

Implement a byte-bounded cache owned by the exact immutable RecoveredSegment or snapshot generation and keyed by the minimum identity necessary to distinguish validated segment backing and block/restart group. Cache-off, miss, eviction, and budget-exhaustion paths decode only the requested block/group from already validated immutable bytes and metadata. They must never invoke a complete TermDictionary parse, bypass eager validation, weaken corruption detection, change codec/scoring/fusion semantics, or manufacture an unbounded allocation. Retained generation N and published generation N+1 keep independent valid cache state; fresh backing always validates and starts fresh.

Profile first on every claimed class. M4 requires the scheduler-managed P-only and P+E receipts, thermal/page-size evidence, and the M4 profile card. High-core AMD requires 1, 20+, and 64-segment layouts plus explicit 1/16/32/eligible-max worker budgets to expose fragmentation, allocator contention, cache traffic, and memory-bandwidth limits. The baseline comparator is the exact gwd4 KEEP SHA, so the two levers are never double-counted.

The cache is a performance optimization only. Query fuel admission, cancellation checkpoints, deterministic ordering, total hit/score/snippet/metadata/explain contract, recovery, publication, and durability behavior remain exact. A kill switch may disable caching for diagnosis, but no compatibility shim or alternate result path is permitted.
design: Use one bounded cache per immutable segment binding or equivalent generation-owned structure; select synchronization and eviction policy only after the post-gwd4 profile identifies reuse and contention shape. Account bytes from fallible allocation before publication into the cache. Concurrent duplicate misses may decode redundantly if that is safer than global serialization, but cache publication must be race-safe and bounded. Exhaustion is a normal miss followed by bounded block-local decode from validated bytes, never a full dictionary reparse. Invalid cached identity is an internal subsystem failure, not evidence that durable bytes are corrupt. Every log/receipt is structured, phase-tagged, bounded, and excludes raw query/document text.
acceptance_criteria:
Prerequisites: gwd4 is a measured KEEP; post-gwd4 profiles on each claimed machine class show block/entry decode at or above 0.1%; the M4 card is complete before an M4 claim. Unit tests cover cache off, cold miss, warm hit, exact byte accounting, cap zero, cap boundary, eviction, allocation failure, duplicate concurrent miss, hit/miss race, exact backing identity, generation N retained beside N+1, fresh-reopen invalidation, and no complete-parse counter increment after admission. Hit, miss, eviction, and exhausted-cache paths must return bit-identical term matches, cursors, scores, order, snippets, metadata, explanations, counts, fuel usage, and cancellation outcomes. Hostile malformed TERMDICT still fails during eager admission; cache state can never convert resource/configuration failure into IndexCorrupted or hide current-generation failure through recovery. RSS is bounded by the declared cap plus predeclared allocator overhead, with process-level peak and steady measurements.

Run same-binary randomized paired A/B plus same-invocation numeric A/A against the exact gwd4 baseline and the fastest semantically equivalent pinned Tantivy incumbent where a competitive claim is made. Persist both-arm absolutes, raw hierarchical leaf samples, p50/p95/p99, QPS, RSS, cold/warm open, update-visible, commit/publication, cancellation, source/ELF/corpus/query/host/machine-class/thread/heap provenance, parity digests, and structured bounded logs. KEEP per class only when the effect exceeds the valid null and predeclared confidence interval with no material correctness, tail, RSS, open, publication, or cancellation regression. Otherwise REJECT for that class, revert the production lever if no class justifies it, retain evidence, and record a concrete retry predicate.

Keep the legacy serde encoder under cfg(test) as an independent oracle. No canonical byte, content-hash, IDMAP, FSLX, manifest, registry, or public format change is allowed. Attach arm-scoped profile attribution, exact source, diff, ELF, corpus, and workload identities plus full-interval exclusive occupancy receipts. Stage one requires a clean same-binary Quill A/A plus candidate-versus-baseline A/B with median-CI admission and no resource regression. A promotable candidate then requires terminal same-binary end-to-end Quill versus the genuine linked Tantivy incumbent under QG-2 on both Threadripper and the registered m4-macos M4 lane, with each platform carrying its own valid A/A controls and occupancy witness. Do not require, emulate, or claim a Tantivy translation of Quill canonical encoding. M5 evidence is separately hardware-dependent and is not a prerequisite for this bead. Invalid or adverse diagnostics cannot ship or become a QG verdict.

title: Quill ingest: adaptive shared-nothing activation with cancel- and budget-safe shard accumulation
description: Activate the already-existing shared-nothing shard and concat-merge path from measured workload and verified capacity instead of configured width alone. The planner must avoid serializing medium and large QG-1 cells while preventing tiny inputs from spawning empty shards or allocating a fixed per-shard reserve. This child owns one lever only: deterministic active-shard planning plus balanced nonempty partitioning and aggregate budget/cancellation/lifecycle correctness. It is an implementation and evidence lane under the W3 scale-out umbrella, but it has no P1-profile or A/A-calibration prerequisite: those hardware gates apply to speculative follow-on levers and decision claims, not to correctness-safe activation. No benchmark-only semantics, QG activation, public ratio, or flip authority is created here.
design: Planner v1 computes eligible = min(configured_width, verified_pool_capacity) and active = min(eligible, floor(document_count / 64)); it uses the serial route if and only if active < 2. Canonical partitioning is balanced, nonempty, deterministic, and tail-folded, with every input document assigned exactly once in original order. Each shard accumulates independently, but reserve accounting is aggregate across the full operation: do not eagerly allocate 1 MiB times active_shards. Preserve the same per-document budget boundary as serial ingest and deterministic flush, seal, concat, publish, and retry semantics. Carry Cx through bounded checkpoints before flush, seal, concat, and publication. Cancellation, panic, or worker error joins every started worker and leaves no partial published snapshot or pending merge. H2 lifecycle receipts expose planner version, route, configured width, verified pool capacity, eligible and active widths, canonical ranges and counts, worker identities and distinct-worker count, queue/join state, CPU and wall time, peak aggregate reserve, and terminal state.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Planner goldens are exact: 250 documents at width/capacity 4 activates 3; 5000 at 96 activates 78; 5000 at 128 activates 78; 8192 at 128 activates 128. Zero, one, 63, 64, 127, 128, 249, 250, 5000, and 8192 documents are covered at configured widths 1, 2, 4, 64, 96, and 128. 2. Canonical partitions are balanced, nonempty, deterministic, tail-folded, cover every document exactly once, and preserve serial semantic parity with positions both on and off, including duplicate and large terms. 3. Budget accounting is global: no eager fixed reserve per shard, no aggregate limit overshoot, and the same per-document boundary, flush, seal, resume, and retry behavior as serial ingest; assigned documents are neither dropped nor replayed. 4. Bounded Cx checkpoints precede flush, seal, concat, and publish. Every cancellation, panic, and error schedule joins workers, drains queues, leaves no pending merge or partially published snapshot, and a retry produces the exact serial result. 5. H2 receipts bind planner version and route, configured width, verified pool capacity, eligible and active widths, ranges/counts, worker IDs and distinct count, peak/CPU/wall, queue and join state, aggregate reserve peak, exact source/ELF/corpus/run window, and terminal outcome. 6. Differential goldens cover all listed counts and widths, positions on/off, duplicates, large terms, budget exhaustion, cancellation at each checkpoint, worker panic/error, and deterministic repeat. 7. Any performance decision uses one same-binary randomized fixed-incumbent-versus-adaptive A/B invocation plus independent per-arm A/A controls. Missing incumbent, invalid null, lifecycle witness, same-worker identity, or ELF identity is NoDecision. No result from this bead alone activates QG-1, supports a public ratio, or authorizes a flip.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Reverted for now as a5a0fc43 so downstream consumers can build again. Jeff authorized rolling back to a known-good state.

WHAT HAPPENED
9cea1376 (07-31 02:56) renamed i16x8::mul_widen -> i16x8::widening_mul. That is the wide 1.x spelling. This workspace's Cargo.toml declares wide = 1.1.1, but Cargo.lock still RESOLVES wide 0.7.33, where the method is mul_widen. So the code did not compile:
  crates/frankensearch-index/src/simd.rs:1268 error[E0599]: no method named widening_mul

WHY IT MATTERED MORE THAN IT LOOKS
hedge_fund_data_tool consumes this crate as a LIVE PATH DEPENDENCY (hfdt Cargo.toml:279 -> ../frankensearch/frankensearch). It does not pin a rev, so it inherits this working tree directly. From 02:56 onward hfdt could not build its hfdt binary at all.

The practical damage: the newest working hfdt binary on that box was built 2026-07-29 11:54, i.e. BEFORE this commit. A twelve-lane agent swarm spent hours unable to run the tool it was modifying, so every verification degraded into static analysis or stale-binary runs. That is how a surface with zero success paths got reported as working.

THE REAL FIX (this revert is only a stopgap)
Cargo.toml says wide = 1.1.1 and Cargo.lock says 0.7.33. Resolve that mismatch, then re-land the rename in the same commit as the lockfile bump so the two never disagree.

SUGGESTED GUARD
Any API-rename commit that depends on a dependency major version should land together with the lockfile change, and ideally CI should build at least one downstream path-dep consumer, since a green build here did not imply a green build for the consumer that actually ships.

title: FSFS serve cannot observe coordinated shutdown while blocked in accept/read
description: Serve is excluded from run_with_shutdown despite installing signals. The Unix server blocks in listener.accept, loops unconditionally on Interrupted, and processes clients synchronously with 5s I/O timeouts; parent-death SIGTERM can leave the socket held and one partial client serializes all others. Acceptance: SIGTERM while idle in accept exits within a bound and cleans the socket; a slow first client does not delay a complete second client; include Serve in coordinated shutdown and make accept/client handling shutdown-aware. Evidence: fsfs main.rs 186,217; runtime.rs 4680,4696,5028,5063.
close_reason: Fixed (commit 77b68c7). Serve is now inside run_with_shutdown; the unix socket accept loop runs nonblocking on a 50ms poll cadence observing the ShutdownCoordinator + cx cancellation (SIGTERM while idle in accept exits within one poll interval; SocketPathGuard still unlinks the socket). Every accepted client runs on its own scoped thread with its own scheduler+Cx — a stalled client no longer serializes complete ones; search execution serializes only on the shared resource/hot-cache lock for compute. Regression tests: shutdown while idle exits <2s + socket removed; stalled client A does not delay client B's round trip (<2s); bounded exit under load. Verified: serve tests 3/3, fsfs suite 1822/1822 (two pre-existing shutdown-wait hangs filed as bd-z6pu — asupersync sleep under run_test_with_cx, unrelated), workspace check 0 errors, clippy clean in changed ranges (63 future_not_send warnings pre-exist at HEAD), fmt clean, UBS exit 0.

title: Exact vector, Quill, ANN, and metadata generation component receipts
description:
Define and implement engine-owned immutable receipts that let one composite generation prove every component came from the same source checkpoint and document set. Vector receipts consume the retained identity-complete FSVI v2 owner and bind whole-image SHA-256, generation, complete embedding/input/producer/storage identities, ordered live-document-set digest, live/tombstone counts, and vector-content digest. Quill emits an exact immutable lexical snapshot receipt with canonical document-set/source-checkpoint binding and descriptor-backed reopen; the composite root never reuses Keeper CURRENT, GC, or claim deletion as authority. Native HNSW receipts bind the exact FSVI whole-image witness, full space/storage/generation/docset/vector-content identities, parameters, and SHA-256, never FNV/path/count alone. Metadata/checkpoint receipts bind the same canonical document-set algorithm and exact immutable bytes.

Admission opens every role descriptor-relatively from one retained generation capability, rejects undeclared entries, aliases, cross-device files, WAL beside sealed FSVI, wrong roles, missing/duplicate/reordered/tombstoned documents, same-count/same-dimension substitution, swapped fast/quality spaces, stale ANN, lexical/source drift, and metadata checkpoint drift. The common manifest is engine-neutral and has no index-to-Quill dependency; adapters return owned typed payloads and bounded redacted receipts. Exact fallback may disable optional stale ANN only when the admitted FSVI owner remains exact and the public topology/telemetry says so; mandatory vector, lexical, and metadata drift fails closed.

TESTS: real F16/F32 fast/quality FSVI, Quill, native HNSW, metadata, empty/partial/tombstoned corpora, same-doc/new-vector, same-count/wrong generation, document reordering/duplication/hole, swapped tiers, wrong tokenizer/input/storage, stale HNSW parameters, path replacement after admission, symlink/hardlink/cross-role alias, live/empty/corrupt WAL, and component byte/mode/time/inventory preservation. Every independent mutation is rejected on the correct role before query work. Cross-engine golden fixtures prove one canonical document-set digest. Workspace all-feature check/test/clippy/fmt, UBS, strict remote exact-SHA receipts, and bounded detailed E2E logs are required. Publication, activation, and deletion are out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: One canonical document-set and source-checkpoint witness joins exact FSVI v2, Quill, HNSW, and metadata receipts. Every independent same-count/dimension/generation/vector/tier/docset/lexical/ANN/metadata/WAL/path mutation rejects on the correct role before query work; optional ANN fallback is exact and truthful. Real component E2E, preservation inventory, all-feature workspace gates, strict remote receipts, clippy/fmt, and UBS pass.
close_reason:
CLOSED BY DECOMPOSITION. The keystone landed at 5845f680751b44c27d879ff953f293484c8cd138 (pushed); the remaining scope is carried by four filed children, and cdny8 was re-pointed at them BEFORE this close so nothing inherits a false 'ready' signal.

WHY THIS BEAD EXISTED AND WHAT WAS MISSING: the acceptance requires 'cross-engine golden fixtures prove ONE canonical document-set digest'. That was unimplementable at tip. The index computes its docset digest under the domain 'frankensearch.fsvi-v2.ordered-live-docset.v1' — FSVI-specific and private to that crate — while frankensearch-core had no docset algorithm at all (zero grep hits), so Quill and metadata had nothing they could agree with. No cross-engine join could exist until one engine-neutral algorithm did. Core is the correct home: its manifest declares no dependency on frankensearch-index or frankensearch-quill, which is this bead's own engine-neutral constraint.

DELIVERED in crates/frankensearch-core/src/generation.rs (+653):
- CANONICAL_DOCSET_DIGEST_DOMAIN_V1 and CanonicalDocsetV1. Domain deliberately DISTINCT from the fsvi-v2 one, so an FSVI-shaped digest cannot silently satisfy a cross-engine comparison it never made. Order is part of identity because rank-ordered results and physical row addressing both depend on it. Duplicates are REJECTED rather than deduplicated: collapsing one would let a corrupted component agree with a healthy component that genuinely holds one fewer document. Count and each identifier are length-prefixed so an identifier-boundary shift cannot collide with a healthy set.
- ExactComponentReceiptV1, identity-complete: role + exact bytes + canonical docset digest + live count + source checkpoint. Distinct from the pre-existing GenerationComponentReceiptV1, which carries only byte_len + sha256 and belongs to njm4c's activation-authority lane. Exact bytes prove an artifact was not rewritten; they cannot prove it was built from the same documents and checkpoint as its siblings.
- ExactGenerationComponentsV1::admit. Vector is the ANCHOR and the others are compared against it — pairwise comparison would let two equally-wrong components agree and outvote it. Errors NAME THE DRIFTING ROLE, because the acceptance requires rejection 'on the correct role' and an unattributed mismatch cannot express that. ANN is optional, so a stale or absent accelerator still leaves an exact generation, while vector/lexical/metadata drift fails closed.

EVIDENCE: 10 paired-control tests, every one verified BY NAME rather than by a filtered count. Controls: quartet admits with and without ANN; empty docset has a stable non-zero digest. Mutations: each mandatory role drifted alone rejects naming that role, for both docset and checkpoint; a receipt filed in the wrong slot rejects on the slot BEFORE any digest comparison (otherwise a lexical receipt in the metadata slot would sail through by agreeing with the anchor); reordering, a hole, same-count substitution and an identifier-boundary shift each move the canonical digest; a byte-identical component from another generation is refused; zero-placeholder digests and checkpoints are invalid.
GATES: cargo test -p frankensearch-core --lib => 1087 passed / 0 failed. clippy --no-deps -p frankensearch-core --all-targets -- -D warnings => exit 0. rustfmt --edition 2024 --check and git diff --check pass. Commit hooks: ledger selfcheck 52/52, leakcheck 2/2, gatecheck 9/9, mergecheck 3/3.
RED PROOF: disabling only the three join gates (role, docset, checkpoint) fails exactly the four join-dependent tests and leaves the other six green, including the control and the isolated-validation test.

NOT RE-COVERED, so nobody counts it twice: FsviV2Witness already satisfied this bead's vector clause and NativeHnswGenerationReceiptV2 its ANN clause; the FNV-only legacy ANN hole named here was closed under bd-r65a (38d439de), and the cross-generation ANN refusal was pinned under qxo6 (6dca3d1f).

title: Fixed AUTHORITY and LOCK publisher with unknown-outcome reconciliation
description:
Implement the durable generation-root state machine over one precreated never-renamed/unlinked 8192-byte AUTHORITY inode containing two fixed 4096-byte authenticated slots and one precreated never-renamed/unlinked LOCK inode containing alternating tear-sealed owner/attempt frames. Immutable activation manifests and generation objects use cryptographically random create_new names and are never renamed over, adopted by scan, unlinked, or cleaned up in this bead. The kernel flock is the sole live-owner authority; host, boot, PID, process-start, random nonce, root/LOCK/AUTHORITY identities, and owner frame are diagnostics and mutation fences, never PID liveness proof or a timeout-stealable lease.

Publication fully seals and syncs the candidate outside the authority lock, then under exclusive flock fences every retained descriptor, exact expected slot pair, floor head/version, and owner record; persists InFlight; positionally overwrites only the slot selected by target sequence & 1; performs the platform durability barrier; exact-rereads slot plus immutable closure; compare-and-advances the external floor; persists Completed; installs no other pointer or metadata; then unlocks and acknowledges. Before any possible slot write, CAS loss is ordinary NotCommitted with zero authority mutation. From the first possibly issued slot byte or external CAS request, immediate failure is CommitOutcomeUnknown carrying a bounded exact attempt permit. Fresh reconciliation returns Committed, NotCommitted, StillUnknown, Fork, RepairRequired, or CommittedThenSuperseded from the exact local/floor/attempt state. Pending local successor plus old external floor may serve the exact old anchored generation read-only with degraded health, but freezes further mutation and eligibility decisions until reconciliation.

Rollback and repair publish N+1 activation records targeting retained admitted generations; sequence never decreases, reuses, wraps, or saturates. A credible externally anchored newest record with corrupt/missing closure fails closed and never silently falls back. This bead computes no GC and deletes nothing.

TESTS: two real publishers one winner; stale expected pair zero mutation; PID reuse/foreign host/stale owner after successful flock; SIGKILL release; fork-inherited descriptor; root/LOCK/AUTHORITY swaps; every prefix/reordering/short write/ENOSPC/sync/cancel/crash point for LOCK and AUTHORITY; external CAS applied, not applied, timeout, conflict and supersession; every fresh-process reconcile state; higher-sequence rollback/repair; u64::MAX read-only; no directory entry or inode changes across thousands of publications; and inventory/hash proof that every incumbent and losing candidate remains. Readers and full composite adapters are separate beads. Workspace check/clippy/fmt, focused core/index tests, UBS, strict remote Linux, and native Apple receipts are required.
acceptance_criteria: LOCK and AUTHORITY inodes, names, lengths, modes, and link identities never change; all generation/activation objects are random create_new and retained. Two publishers have one winner; every byte/syscall/cancel/crash/floor state reconciles exactly; no next slot is reused while uncertain; rollback/repair advance sequence; no file is deleted. Fresh-process, multi-process, remote Linux, native Apple, workspace check/test/clippy/fmt, UBS, and bounded artifact receipts pass.

description: Quill intentionally observes Cx cancellation in query execution and hydration, while the legacy Tantivy adapter ignores Cx. Cancellation is therefore a required Quill correctness contract, not a parity law that should preserve worse legacy behavior. Add a separate real method-bound witness and typed artifact receipt; do not let spy-only SearchError replay stand in for actual engine cancellation.
design: Invoke real Quill public search, fusion-candidate, and metadata-hydration boundaries with a cancelled Cx and with deterministic cancellation injected at defined checkpoints. Observe stable SearchError Cancelled class/code/phase, bounded reason, absence of fabricated success, no post-cancel publication, and unchanged immutable snapshot/generation identity. Where partial local mutation is an allowed hydration implementation detail, prove the returned typed cancellation plus the exact retained post-state and that no shared serving state changed. Record Tantivy behavior separately as LegacyIgnoresCx, not Equivalent and not a waiver. Replacement readiness requires Quill cancellation evidence but does not require retaining Tantivy non-cancellation.
acceptance_criteria: Real Quill tests cancel before parse, during collection/checkpoint, before/within hydration, and before publication/commit where the public boundary permits; each returns the typed cancelled variant with the expected phase, remains bounded, leaks no source text, and leaves the published snapshot, document count, ordering, scores, and metadata unchanged on retry. A noncancelled control succeeds on the same corpus/query. Artifact schema/replay detects mutation of phase/code/post-state/snapshot identity and rejects spy-only or synthetic receipts as release evidence. A documented live Tantivy control proves Cx is ignored and is labeled legacy behavior rather than parity. DPOR/LabRuntime or an equivalent deterministic schedule test covers cancellation races without sleeps. Detailed logs include boundary, checkpoint, generation, cancellation observation, and replay result without unbounded content.

Each real Quill method must emit the stable Cancelled class/code/phase, preserve exact published snapshot/generation/doc count/order/score/metadata, retain any explicitly allowed local partial hydration state, and succeed identically on a fresh noncancelled retry. Use LabRuntime/DPOR or deterministic checkpoints without sleeps. Persist/reload/replay the method-bound receipt and reject mutated phase/code/post-state/snapshot/provenance, spy-only evidence, and synthetic construction. Record Tantivy ignoring Cx only as LegacyIgnoresCx, never equivalence or a waiver.

- Established deterministic test pattern (ingest-side, index.rs ~:10650): LabRuntime tasks + cx.set_cancel_requested(true) synchronized on an await point (writer.waiters()), seeded, no sleeps.

KEY CONSTRAINT the phase matrix must respect: the QUERY path is fully synchronous (no awaits inside search_paginated/search_results/etc.), so LabRuntime task interleaving CANNOT preempt mid-collection at the public boundary. Decomposition:

LANDABLE NOW (no dependency on the frozen index-crate tranche — quill is git-clean): integration test crates/frankensearch-quill/tests/cancellation_contract.rs covering the ENTRY phase for every public boundary (search_paginated, search_results, search_doc_ids, search_with_snippets, collect_docids/fusion-candidates, preparsed variants) with: typed Cancelled{phase} assertions, published-snapshot/doc-count/order/score immutability across the cancelled call, noncancelled control on the same corpus, and identical fresh-retry success after clearing the flag.

Alternative if rejected: unit-level tests directly on the collect internals with per-admission flag flips.

4. Tantivy LegacyIgnoresCx control: read-only test on the existing adapter, recorded as legacy behavior, never parity, never a waiver.
5. Artifact/receipt: IcyPond's lexical_replacement.rs (worktree, bd-8nqz.4) already carries a method-bound cancellation receipt shell exercising this bead fail-closed; binding it to the real checkpoints happens after (1)/(2) stabilize — coordinated in-thread, I do not touch their module.

title: QG-6 R1a: implement validated immutable TERMDICT metadata cache (source and correctness only)
description: STARTABLE PROFILED SOURCE LEVER. The frozen QG-6 profile at 8b35790e attributes more than 83% of Quill query self-time to repeated TermDictionary::parse_with_limits validation. This task owns exactly one production lever and its correctness tests: parse and fully validate immutable TERMDICT metadata once while a recovered segment is bound, retain an owned allocation-bounded metadata object on that segment, and construct cheap borrowed dictionary views for query-time doc-frequency and cursor operations. Validation must complete before publication/searchability. This task makes no performance claim, activates no gate, edits no benchmark history or ledger, and cannot close the terminal KEEP/REJECT bead bd-quill-gauntlet-qg6-cache-termdict-gwd4 by itself. Do not change codecs, vint encoding, scoring, query semantics, fusion, or unsafe-code policy.
design: Keep the validated metadata type private and Send+Sync, containing only bounded offsets, restart points, block facts, and reader data already established by the current validator. A public or crate-external caller cannot assemble a view from unvalidated parts. Failed candidate open never publishes or replaces a live segment. Each generation or reload builds fresh metadata; no cache crosses content identity. Preserve mmap lifetimes, cancellation and fuel checkpoints, deterministic errors, and forbid(unsafe_code). Add test-only counters that distinguish complete validation from cheap view construction.
acceptance_criteria: Source and correctness only: corruption at header, block, restart, entry, reference, checksum, and truncation boundaries fails before segment publication; fresh open and reopen, multi-segment, generation replacement, failed-candidate-preserves-old-segment, and concurrent repeated-query tests pass. Deterministic counters prove exactly one complete TERMDICT validation per recovered immutable segment and zero additional complete validations across repeated doc-frequency, cursor, and search calls. No public API, on-disk format, result, score, or rank change. Eager structural TERMDICT corruption is intentionally classified as SearchError::IndexCorrupted and must name the exact segment path plus actionable dictionary detail; unrelated error classes remain unchanged. Run focused Quill tests plus every currently available gauntlet and oracle regression, strict remote check and Clippy with warnings denied, fmt, diff checks, and UBS. Land one source-and-tests commit only; do not publish ratios, ledger a KEEP, alter latest artifacts, or start the decoded-block cache above terminal gwd4.
close_reason: Completed source/correctness scope: immutable TERMDICT metadata is validated once per recovered segment and reused without changing public semantics; the separate QG-6 verdict bead remains open.

title: PERF_LEDGER 825/827: the 4-bit two-pass 2.56-3.22x vs-flat self-ratio does not reproduce (1.05x measured), and no host is recorded
description:
Found while converting the 'fastest lossless vector-search primitive' claim (docs/evidence/fsvi-4bit-vs-incumbent-20260731.md, 2026-07-31, BlackThrush).

PERF_LEDGER.md:825 claims the FSVI 4-bit two-pass is 2.56x faster than our own exact flat scan (and :826 raises it to 3.22x, :827 to 3.09x for the in-memory twin). A same-invocation measurement on worker vmi1152480 (host frankenlibc-test, AMD EPYC with IBPB, nproc=10) measured:

  cand_4bit_mult5_default / ours_exact_flat_default = 0.9560  ->  1.05x

Not 2.56x. Not 3.09x. 1.05x.

LIKELY CAUSE, NOT YET CONFIRMED: neither parallel arm scaled on this host. Observed cpu/wall was 2.82 for the 4-bit arm and 3.37 for the flat arm on a 10-core box, so both are far from saturating and the 4-bit arm's advantage (which comes from reading a 18.3 MiB packed slab instead of a 146.5 MiB f32/f16 region) is diluted when neither arm is bandwidth-limited. The original rows were measured on a different, unrecorded machine.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT IS THE MISSING HOST FIELD. Rows :825/:826/:827 record 'A/B (100k file-backed FSVI, in-process, same index)' with no host, no CPU model, no core count and no ELF SHA-256. A ratio that swings 2.56x -> 1.05x across hosts is a host-conditional result being published as an unconditional one.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Re-measure the 4-bit-vs-flat ratio on at least two hosts with differing core counts, same invocation, corrected null gate, ELF SHA-256 self-reported.
2. Either annotate :825/:826/:827 with the host they were measured on and restate the ratio as host-conditional, or replace them with a range across hosts.
3. Check whether the sibling int8 rows (:817, :818) have the same exposure -- they use the same harness and also record no host.

NOTE this is a SELF-SPEEDUP ratio, so it is maintenance-class, not campaign output. It matters because CHANGELOG.md:66 promoted the same family to a public superlative.

title: P0 terminal: real cross-platform FSFS semantic installer with explicit-only lite
description: Terminal user-outcome prerequisite for the permanent A5 quickstart. Make the user-facing install.sh default produce a semantic-capable FSFS installation on supported Linux x86_64/aarch64 and macOS x86_64/aarch64, or fail actionably without changing the existing installation. Only explicit --lite may install a lite binary. Remove automatic semantic-to-lite fallback. Bind signed/checksummed release or source-build artifacts to exact feature/loader receipts and acquire or install frozen verified fast and quality model artifacts through the authoritative retained-owner receipt path. Preserve existing flags, upgrade, rollback, completions, hooks, uninstall, quiet/NO_COLOR, and offline behavior.
design: Use one signed release manifest per target binding source, lockfile, toolchain, target, binary hash, feature lattice, loader capability, and model-delivery policy. Default installation selects the semantic profile; absence of an admissible semantic artifact either performs the verified semantic source build or fails without replacing the incumbent. Lite is an explicit separate artifact/mode. Model install is staged, verified, atomic, resumable, retained-owner/lease-bound, and zero-network on warm use.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh no-mock installs on Linux x86_64/aarch64 and macOS x86_64/aarch64 produce a non-hash semantic-capable binary, authoritative fast/quality model receipts bound to the retained loaded owners, successful index/search, truthful status/doctor, and warm offline zero-network replay. Unsupported/missing/corrupt/signature/hash/feature/model cases fail actionably and preserve the previous installation. Default never selects lite; only explicit --lite does so and reports nonsemantic state. Tests cover prebuilt and source fallback, partial download, cancellation at each publication boundary, concurrent install, upgrade, rollback, PATH/completions/hooks, uninstall, quiet/NO_COLOR, proxy/offline, bounded redacted logs, exact receipts, and the full platform matrix. No crates.io, QG, Quill-flip, or V2-search claim follows.

title: Private-query gauntlet artifact policy: whole-bundle redaction, encryption, retention, and upload denial
description: Core Lexical V3 redacts its own sensitive subobjects, but outer ArtifactObject case/query fields, CampaignReport query suites, and legacy snippet envelopes retain plaintext. Current campaigns are therefore fixture-only and must never ingest or upload private user queries or source content. Design a separate opt-in private-query evidence mode with whole-object/report privacy guarantees rather than overstating the V3 lexical-subobject contract.
design: Introduce an explicit versioned artifact privacy mode and provenance classification. FixturePublic permits committed/generated public corpora. PrivateLocal requires content minimization across the entire object graph, keyed digests or authenticated encryption for query/source-bearing values, local-only storage, bounded retention, restrictive permissions, and upload/export denial by default. CI and release artifacts accept FixturePublic only. Validation recursively inventories every serialized string-bearing field, binds the privacy policy into content identity, rejects legacy/plaintext subobjects in PrivateLocal, and prevents conversion to a weaker mode. Key material is never serialized, logged, committed, or accepted via command arguments. Do not retrofit cryptographic authentication claims onto current XXH3 content addressing.
acceptance_criteria: A whole-object and whole-report secret-canary suite covers raw/normalized queries, metadata, explanations, snippets, errors, manifests, shrink reproductions, logs, filenames, and legacy envelopes; no canary appears in private serialized bytes, diagnostics, upload paths, or CI artifacts. FixturePublic artifacts remain deterministic and clearly labeled. PrivateLocal artifacts require authenticated encryption or keyed irreversible digests as appropriate, restrictive permissions, bounded retention, explicit local opt-in, and fail-closed export/upload. Missing keys, unknown modes, downgrade attempts, plaintext legacy fields, altered ciphertext/tag/AAD, and policy/content-identity tamper reject. E2E proves CI accepts public fixtures and refuses private mode upload while local authorized replay succeeds without leaking keys or plaintext.

title: Linearizable anti-rollback floor and explicit generation-root security profiles
description:
Freeze and implement the external authority contract that prevents a valid older local root from being silently replayed. AntiRollbackFloor is linearizable and keyed by RootId; load and compare-and-advance bind the exact AuthorityRef, monotone sequence, record digest, CAS version, and idempotency key. It never stores or selects a second model/index pointer. Local publication is fully sealed and durably written first; the floor advances second. Applied-but-timeout, not-applied timeout, conflict, floor-ahead, floor-behind, wrong root, unavailable provider, and sequence exhaustion are distinct typed states. An unresolved CAS blocks further AUTHORITY slot reuse, publication, repair, rollback, and GC until exact reconciliation.

Expose truthful explicit profiles rather than a hidden fallback: RequiredExternal rejects open/publication when the injected floor cannot prove the head; CooperativeLocal may use an owner-controlled floor outside the replaceable random generation root but reports that it detects crashes and ordinary stale roots, not hostile whole-store rollback; ReadOnlyUnanchored permits inspection only and freezes mutation/GC. The facade, fsfs, and CASS must select and surface one profile explicitly. No default silently downgrades RequiredExternal. title: Strict generation authority codec and exhaustive two-slot resolver
description:
Define the single canonical, bounded, forward-safe binary contract for immutable generation descriptors, activation manifests, AuthorityRef values, two physical AUTHORITY slot frames, LOCK owner/attempt frames, and the pure resolver. Authority sequence is distinct from ArtifactGenerationIdentityV1, begins at one, is checked against wrap, and advances for activate, rollback, repair, and migration. Each 4096-byte slot authenticates every byte including canonical zero padding, binds its physical slot index and root ID, and points by random immutable object reference plus exact length and SHA-256 to a strict activation manifest. Normal publication targets sequence & 1; genesis may encode the same logical AuthorityRef separately in both physical slots. Activation manifests bind the exact predecessor AuthorityRef, action, generation descriptor, writer fence, source checkpoint, canonical document-set witnesses, vector/lexical/ANN/metadata component receipts, and a self-seal. No timestamps, paths outside confined relative roles, floats, free-form authority metadata, display-name inference, or serde-default ambiguity participate in identity.

The pure resolver exhaustively classifies duplicate genesis, consecutive predecessor-linked heads, one-slot survival, anchored ancestor gaps, tears, copied-slot parity violations, equal-sequence divergence, predecessor forks, missing/corrupt newest closure, unknown future schema, local/external disagreement, unresolved attempts, sequence exhaustion, and upgrade-required states. It never silently falls back from a structurally credible newest externally anchored head. Canonical decode enforces resource ceilings before allocation, rejects unknown/duplicate/reserved fields and trailing bytes, re-encodes byte-identically, and returns bounded typed facts.

TESTS: property and table matrices mutate every field and byte; truncate/extend/reorder old-new chunks; cover all A/B orientations, sequence boundaries, predecessor/fork/gap states, unknown versions, noncanonical encodings, resource ceilings, cycles, ABA via higher-sequence rollback, and u64::MAX. Golden fixtures and structured logs are versioned, bounded, redacted, and include exact schema/root/sequence/reference digests. Workspace check/clippy/fmt, focused core tests, UBS, and strict remote exact-SHA receipts are required. No filesystem mutation, publisher, consumer adapter, or GC belongs in this bead.

title: SIMD-widen f16->f32 decode in dot_product_f16_bytes_f32 (default-path decode bottleneck)
description:
Follow-up to bd-s2dn, isolated by BlackThrush's head-to-head measurement (commit 72ac004).

FINDING (measured, benches/dot_product.rs head-to-head):
- The f16 dot-product paths are DECODE-bound: per-element scalar f16::to_f32() dominates; the SIMD multiply-accumulate is a small fraction. Multi-accumulator unrolling therefore REGRESSED the f16 paths (1.04-1.46x) and was reverted (see docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md).
- f16 (default quantization) is the production-dominant path, so the real-world win lives in the DECODE, not the accumulator structure.

LEVER:
Replace the 8x scalar f16::from_le_bytes(..).to_f32() per chunk with a BRANCHLESS SIMD f16->f32 widen using wide integer lanes (e.g. u32x8/i32x8 bit manipulation: shift mantissa/exponent, rebias 15->127, handle zero/subnormal/inf/nan), OR half::slice::HalfFloatSliceExt batch conversion if a no-unsafe, no-alloc view is feasible. unsafe is DENY (mmap bytes may be unaligned) so a bytemuck/safe path or pure-integer-SIMD widen is required.

PROOF OBLIGATIONS (hard):
1. BIT-EXACT vs f16::to_f32() for ALL 65536 f16 values (exhaustive unit test) — determinism Tier-1 requires scores unchanged on the default path. NaN payload may differ but result NaN-ness must match.
2. Existing simd correctness + search top-k ordering/tie-break + FSVI round-trip stay green.
3. Head-to-head rebench dot/dim{256,384}/f16_bytes new vs old; keep only if ratio < 0.97, no tracked workload regresses > 1.03.

TARGET WORKLOADS: dot/dim256/f16_bytes (baseline 12.483 ms/10k), dot/dim384/f16_bytes (17.486 ms/10k); end-to-end vector_search_topk/top10/10000.

Labels: perf, simd, vector-search, bold-verify. Fallback: current scalar decode.

description: SPECIFICATION SOURCE ONLY. Publish one versioned JSON contract consumed by both the shell perf runner and Rust evidence/ratchet path. Define canonical exact and patterned class IDs, registration/admission state, immutable hardware predicates, execution-identity predicates, class-key grammar, required runner receipt fields, and a complete MUST/SHOULD matrix with shared positive and negative test vectors. Separate hardware identity from effective execution width, cpuset, SMT/NUMA, P/E mode, thread budget, thermal and durability state. Reject obsolete trj-zen-128c. Register the observed 5995WX and M4 Pro 10P+4E/16KiB identities from committed fingerprints; mark x86-vps-ovh provisional until homogeneity proof and M5 unavailable until a real host fingerprint exists. This bead makes no performance claim and edits no QG artifact, latest pointer, gate activation or perf manifest.
design: The JSON contract is the sole normative data source and is strict: versioned schema, no unknown or duplicate fields, deterministic class resolution, non-overlapping exact/pattern rules, explicit admission state, exact provenance of registered fingerprints, requirement IDs, and table-driven cases. Threadripper IDs use trj-zen3-<N>c for N effective physical cores with one hardware thread/core; SMT-on requires trj-zen3-<N>c-smt2 so latest paths and null bands cannot collide. Every promotable receipt carries immutable hardware facts plus explicit execution request, start snapshot, and end snapshot; the suffix is independently verified against both observed snapshots. Hardware, cpuset, snapshots, execution identity, registry and argv are bound by one cross-language SHA-256/canonical-JSON contract with an explicit derivation order. M4 binds Apple M4 Pro, 10P+4E, 14 logical CPUs, 64 GiB and 16384-byte pages, while requested P-only mode is never described as hard affinity without observation. Diagnostic-only and unavailable classes can be identified but never promoted. Every consumer executes the same shared cases and stable validation precedence.
acceptance_criteria: The contract parses as duplicate-key-rejecting strict JSON and carries its own schema version, exact source fingerprint paths/hashes, class rules, one nested receipt shape, request/start/end snapshots, canonical hash and reason-precedence laws, requirement table, and positive/negative vectors. MUST coverage is 100%: valid registered SMT-off/SMT-on/M4 receipts; provisional/unavailable class lookups without fabricated receipts; unknown/obsolete/ambiguous IDs; wrong OS/arch/vendor/family/model/stepping/chip/P-E/page/memory/topology; missing/extra/legacy alias fields; cpuset syntax/duplicates/range/width/request-observe mismatch; SMT suffix mismatch; NUMA/governor/thermal/exclusive-lease/local-execution/dirty-source/durability/completion failures; derived-hash tamper; pre/post drift; cross-class rule collision; and destination basename/latest-key collision. Every vector names exact decision, class and stable reason; every fully valid receipt carries golden hardware/cpuset/snapshot/execution hashes that independent jq-compatible materialization reproduces. Static self-host checks prove all template and mutation paths match the strict schema, all MUST IDs and reasons close, exact source hashes match, class grammar is non-overlapping, old flat/reported aliases appear only as negative cases, and valid destination stems cannot collide. The hyperopt contract links this file as normative. No consumer implementation, performance artifact, QG latest pointer, gate activation or manifest is changed in this commit.
close_reason: Completed by 629df55d and landed contiguously with its exact consumer in 436426f2. The machine-class registry is content-addressed, schema-validated, and bound to the self-hosted component pair; strict registry/self-host vectors and independent component-pair job j-29951123083232318 pass. No QG artifact, baseline activation, or performance claim was promoted.
