title: QG gate activation: run QG-1/2/3/5/6 vs Tantivy oracle and flip activated=true with real baselines
description:
ANTI-PARALYSIS EXECUTION AND EVIDENCE-ASSEMBLY TASK for QG-1, QG-2, QG-3, QG-5, and QG-6. Run every affordable independent slice immediately; never wait for a full matrix, gate activation, another platform, or a perfect harness before attempting unaffected cells. This bead coordinates execution only: the canonical QG validity beads own workload semantics, the executable QG validator owns admissibility, bd-3beo owns the bounded flip decision, and E8.5 owns profile-first optimization after any credible loss.

Each slice must link a genuine Tantivy 0.26.1 incumbent and Quill candidate in the same binary; use identical inputs, operation scope, heap/thread/positions/durability/query options; alternate arm order; emit both-engine absolute measurements, raw independent samples, paired effects, uncertainty, and a same-invocation A/A null where meaningful. Corpus/setup work outside the claimed metric must be separately measured or excluded symmetrically. Record exact source, dirty-state, Cargo.lock, toolchain, features/profile, corpus/query/config, worker/storage, executing ELF hash, command/environment, timeout/resource receipt, and the runtime incumbent-identity line.

Timeouts, truncation, missing required cells, invalid/null-unstable comparisons, and unsupported lanes are retained as diagnostics but are never baselines and never activate a gate. Narrow fixture slices are first-class execution units; an assembler must prove disjoint complete coverage, identical immutable provenance, stable schema, and no duplicate or omitted cell before producing a gate artifact. Completed valid cells may be reported immediately with their precise provisional/decision status. A statistically credible Quill loss, even if non-material for the flip, must immediately create or join a lane under bd-quill-e8-perf-doctrine-x4e4.5; a noisy or invalid result creates a measurement-repair owner while other cells continue.
design: Use a scale ladder and resumable gate assembler rather than one monolithic 30-minute job. Smoke validates dispatch and schema only. Decision slices run optimized on an isolated reference worker, one canonical cell or bounded homogeneous shard per invocation, with compile and measurement receipts separated in the artifact. The assembler accepts a shard only when the canonical gate validator accepts every contained cell and all shard provenance fields match; it rejects overlap, holes, mixed binaries/workers/configs, stale source, or partial terminal status. Publish per-cell evidence as soon as valid, but change activated=true only after the canonical required-cell set is complete. Route QG-1 through .6, QG-2 through .12, QG-3 through .7, QG-5 through .13, and QG-6 through .9 plus the four-arm admission lane. Every credible loss attaches its immutable artifact to E8.5 before optimization; every invalid run records a bounded retry predicate and owner.
acceptance_criteria: 1. QG-1, QG-2, QG-3, QG-5, and QG-6 each have a complete machine-validated artifact assembled from one run or proven disjoint shards; no required cell remains unmeasured, duplicated, truncated, or silently skipped. 2. Every cell records genuine runtime Tantivy identity, both-arm absolutes, raw samples, paired effect and confidence interval, A/A null where meaningful, exact immutable provenance, command/environment, wall/CPU/RSS or applicable resource facts, and terminal status. 3. Canonical validity contracts pass: .6 for QG-1, .12 for QG-2, .7 for QG-3, .13 for QG-5, and .9 plus the four-arm admission contract for QG-6. 4. The executable estimator/validator rejects synthetic corruptions for missing cells, mixed provenance, invalid nulls, aggregation masks, unsupported claims, and partial terminal status. 5. Each gate remains inactive until its complete artifact validates; then and only then activated=true and the immutable baseline/history artifact are committed. 6. Every valid Quill loss is linked to an active E8.5 optimization child with profile-first evidence; every invalid/noisy cell has a repair owner and retry predicate while unrelated cells continue. 7. Bounded logs, redaction canaries, artifact hashes, format/clippy/tests, UBS, and strict remote receipts pass. Closure is not permitted merely because a monolithic run timed out or a subset produced interesting numbers.

THE ONE BLOCKER: rch relinks the whole dependency graph on EVERY exec (~25 min of a 30-min window), and QG-5's xlarge fixture is a 1,000,000-document compaction run 10 times per arm across two arms. Measurement cannot fit in the ~5 minutes that remain.

I verified the relink is unconditional rather than assuming it: attempt 3 ran immediately after attempt 2 finished, on the same worker, with a byte-identical cargo invocation, and still emitted 270 Compiling lines. This is the SAME root fact behind quill-perf-ratchet's rerun_elf_mismatch — two invocations can never share a bench ELF because each one produces a fresh binary.

THREE WAYS TO CLEAR IT, any one suffices (orchestrator's call, not mine):
  (a) a longer rch window for this specific job (build_timeout_sec is global and shared by 11 repos, so I will not raise it unilaterally);
  (b) a warm or persistent per-project target pool so compile is amortised;
  (c) permission to score QG-5 at the medium corpus instead of xlarge — this changes what the gate certifies, so it needs an explicit decision rather than me quietly redefining the fixture.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: QG-5 is the last untested leg of the concat-merge thesis. QG-1 already answered the parallel half — the ratio is FLAT across thread counts (0.113/0.107/0.118/0.173 at 1/4/8/16), so multi-core ingest supplies none of the needed 25x. Compaction remains the one place the merge-path bet could still pay, and it is precisely the gate the instrument cannot currently reach.

title: Embedding Batch Coalescing with Deadline Scheduling
description:
Implement batch coalescing for embedding requests with deadline-aware scheduling. When multiple concurrent callers request embeddings (e.g., during index building), coalesce their requests into optimal batches rather than processing one-at-a-time.

## Design

```rust
pub struct BatchCoalescer {
    pending: Mutex<Vec<PendingRequest>>,
    config: CoalescerConfig,
    notify: Condvar,
}

pub struct CoalescerConfig {
    pub max_batch_size: usize,       // Maximum texts per batch (default: 32)
    pub max_wait_ms: u64,            // Maximum time to wait for batch fill (default: 10ms)
    pub min_batch_size: usize,       // Minimum batch before early dispatch (default: 4)
    pub priority_lanes: usize,       // Number of priority levels (default: 2: interactive vs background)
}

pub struct PendingRequest {
    pub text: String,
    pub deadline: Instant,           // When this request MUST be processed
    pub priority: Priority,          // Interactive (high) vs Background (low)
    pub result_tx: oneshot::Sender<Vec<f32>>,
}

pub enum Priority {
    Interactive,  // Search query — tight deadline (~15ms budget)
    Background,   // Index building — can wait for full batch
}
```

## Scheduling Algorithm

1. Requests arrive with deadlines and priorities
2. Interactive requests: dispatch immediately if batch has >= 1 interactive request and wait time > max_wait_ms / 2
3. Background requests: accumulate until max_batch_size or max_wait_ms
4. Mixed batches: interactive requests set the deadline for the whole batch
5. Batch dispatched to Embedder::embed_batch() (if available, else sequential)

## Key Optimization

ONNX model inference (FastEmbed, Model2Vec) has near-fixed overhead per batch. Processing 1 text vs 32 texts takes similar GPU/CPU setup time. Batching amortizes this overhead.

## Performance Model

- FastEmbed (MiniLM-L6-v2): 128ms for 1 text, ~140ms for 32 texts = 4.4ms/text batched vs 128ms/text unbatched = 29x throughput improvement
- Model2Vec (potion): 0.57ms for 1 text, ~2ms for 32 texts = 0.06ms/text batched

## Why This Matters

During index building, frankensearch processes thousands of documents. Without batching, each document is embedded individually, wasting 95%+ of the model inference overhead. Batch coalescing is the single highest-impact optimization for index build time.

The deadline scheduling ensures that interactive search queries are never delayed by background batch accumulation — a critical UX property.

## Testing

- Unit: single request dispatched within max_wait_ms
- Unit: full batch dispatched immediately
- Unit: interactive priority triggers early dispatch
- Unit: deadline enforcement (no request waits past deadline)
- Unit: mixed priority batch scheduling
- Integration: concurrent callers receive correct results
- Integration: throughput improvement vs sequential
- Benchmark: batch coalescing overhead, throughput scaling with batch size
acceptance_criteria:
1. The feature is fully implemented according to this bead design, scope, and referenced files or modules.
2. Integration with dependent components is complete and behavior remains correct across normal and degraded flows.
3. Edge and error cases are explicitly handled with deterministic outcomes and clear reason codes or errors.
4. Unit and integration tests (and e2e where relevant) are added, passing, and include detailed structured logging assertions.
5. Performance and resource expectations in the bead are validated and documented with reproducible evidence.

title: CRITICAL: daemon rerank pads missing scores with 0.0 and has no attested mode — a batch-capping daemon silently sinks every candidate past its limit
description:
Found by user-directed semantic-path review (MossyPine, 2026-07-31). CONFIRMED at origin/main daemon_fallback.rs:1134-1144; trait at core/daemon.rs:643-648; the control it lacks is core/daemon.rs:696-719 validate_response_shape.

HALF A — arity: rerank_sync zips positionally and pads: 'score: scores.get(index).copied().unwrap_or(0.0)' (:1140). A daemon returning FEWER scores than documents silently assigns 0.0 to every document past the returned prefix; extra scores are silently dropped; no finiteness check, so a NaN from the daemon propagates into RerankScore.score. FAILURE: a daemon that caps rerank batches at 32 (or truncates on a partial read) is handed 100 candidates; candidates 33-100 all get 0.0, sink to the bottom of the reranked list, and the search returns confidently-wrong top-k. No error, no warning, and the local-reranker fallback at :1156-1164 is only reached on Err.

HALF B — trust: DaemonClient::rerank is a raw unverified primitive with NO rerank_attested sibling, and DaemonFallbackReranker::new (:1017-1030) takes no DaemonConnectionIdentityV1 — there is no verified constructor at all. Meanwhile DaemonFallbackEmbedder::new_verified (:342) runs challenge/attestation and validate_response_shape enforces exact count, dimension, finiteness and non-all-zero. So a deployment that believes it is in 'verified daemon mode' because the EMBEDDER is new_verified is running an UNAUTHENTICATED reranker against the same socket: any process that can bind that endpoint controls final result ordering.

ROOT CAUSE: the rerank surface was added alongside embed but never enrolled in the attestation regime, and Vec<f32> was chosen as the wire type without a length invariant.

FIX (part 1, cheap, do now): in rerank_sync immediately after Ok(scores), reject scores.len() != documents.len() or any non-finite score by converting to DaemonError::InvalidInput and routing through the existing Err(failure) fallback arm. FIX (part 2, separate bead): add rerank_attested to DaemonClient and a verified constructor; short term expose trust_level() -> Assumed on the reranker so the asymmetry is loud.
close_reason: Part 1 landed eef00358: rerank_sync validates arity+finiteness immediately after Ok(scores); violations convert to DaemonError::InvalidInput and take the existing fallback arm (local reranker or typed RerankFailed). comments.text:
GreenCat: the cited lever is REFUTED, and the prior review's own escape hatch turns out to name a different, unexamined site. Verified independently rather than inherited.

1) THE CITED COPY CANNOT BE REMOVED — it is a compile-time necessity, not a missed optimization. StoredFieldValue<'a> (scribe.rs:1768-1773) carries `bytes: &'a [u8]`, borrowed from the caller's document. StoredFieldColumns::blob is a Vec<u8> that must outlive that borrow across document boundaries and be handed to the sealer. append_document's `self.blob.extend_from_slice(bytes)` (scribe.rs:2194 — the bead's scribe.rs:2382 is line drift; 2382 is now `.iter()` inside ColumnarAccumulator::new) is therefore the single point where borrowed input becomes owned persistent bytes. No representation change removes it; handing ownership in from callers relocates the allocation to the caller rather than eliminating a copy, and the bytes originate in user input Quill does not own. Confirms TanShore's mechanism read.

2) A reserve-only change is even weaker than the 0.45% card suggests: reset() (scribe.rs:2218-2224) does clear(), not shrink, so blob/offsets/present retain capacity across segments and only the FIRST segment pays growth. After warmup that family is ~0.

3) THE SECOND COPY IS REAL AND WAS NOT EXAMINED. TanShore wrote that 'the sealed STOREDMETA encoder must materialize the same bytes again' and treated it as immovable. It is a distinct site: EncodedStoredMetaSection::encode_accumulator_with_limits does `bytes.extend_from_slice(field.blob())` at quiver.rs:10419, copying the ENTIRE accumulated blob a second time into the section buffer. So each stored byte is copied twice per seal, and only the first copy is forced by ownership. Note the Delta path does NOT have this shape — build_delta_stored_meta (scribe.rs:3785-3843) assembles Vec<Option<&[u8]>> of borrowed slices, so the accumulator path is the asymmetric one (classic sibling-path gap).

DISPOSITION: closing this bead as a REJECT of its named lever. I am NOT smuggling the seal-side copy into it — that is a different site with a different risk profile (EncodedStoredMetaSection owns one contiguous `bytes` buffer that is checksummed and passed around; eliding the copy needs a segmented/borrowing section representation plus byte-identical FSLX proof plus same-invocation A/A + live-incumbent A/B at 200k docs). Per the single-writer rule on graph structure I have NOT created a bead for it; flagging it here for the structure owner. No performance claim is made — no measurement was run, and none is needed to establish (1), which is a type-level fact.

title: Migrate activation, history, time travel, and repair to immutable generation authority
description:
Migrate the existing core GenerationController, ActiveGeneration, GenerationHistory, time-travel, and RepairProvider semantics in place to the durable composite authority; do not create compatibility wrappers or a second generation model. Activation consumes SealedCandidate plus exact expected AuthorityCas and returns the retained composite snapshot or CommitOutcomeUnknown. History retains snapshot Arcs keyed by RootId, AuthorityRef, authority sequence, ArtifactGenerationIdentity, manifest reference, and commit range; overlapping ranges are never resolved by first match. Dropping an in-process history lease only drops an Arc and never deletes bytes.

Rollback publishes a new N+1 Rollback activation targeting an admitted retained generation and advances the external floor; it never restores an old activation number or moves a pathname pointer backward. Repair never backs up and overwrites the damaged artifact. It builds a new immutable component/generation, admits it, and publishes a higher-sequence Repair activation through the same state machine. Resetting counters or health cannot manufacture authority. Time travel resolves an explicit unique authority/generation key, returns a retained snapshot, and reports ambiguity, missing retention root, corrupt closure, or unsupported history distinctly. Existing activation invariants become mandatory profile checks that consumers may tighten but never omit.

TESTS: existing happy paths preserved through new APIs; overlapping commit ranges; concurrent activation/history lookup; old Arc after new activation; ABA activate/rollback/stale CAS; higher-sequence rollback and repair; destructive-rewrite canaries; repair failure at every build/admit/publish boundary; sequence exhaustion; corrupt active with valid retained rollback; corrupt rollback target; history limit/age changes without deletion; and fresh-process restart/time-travel/repair with real components. Structural tests prove no production caller retains path-backed ActiveGeneration, local-only activation counters, pointer-moving rollback, or destructive RepairProvider writes. Logs are bounded and redacted. Workspace all-feature tests/check/clippy/fmt, UBS, strict remote receipts, and no-mock lifecycle E2E are required.
acceptance_criteria: All production core activation/history/time-travel/repair callers use retained immutable authority/snapshot types; no local-only sequence, path-backed active state, ambiguous range selection, backward rollback, destructive repair, or health reset can manufacture authority. Higher-sequence rollback/repair and retained-history E2E pass every fault/restart case. Workspace all-feature gates, strict remote receipts, clippy/fmt, and UBS pass.

title: CRITICAL: no cross-process publication lease on any fsfs mutating path — daemon compaction can silently discard WAL appends inside a generation marked complete
description:
Found by user-directed review sweep (MossyPine, 2026-07-31, mail #7365). CONFIRMED against origin/main.

DEFECT: the only cross-process exclusion in fsfs is Quill's per-engine-dir flock acquired INSIDE QuillIndex::create (runtime.rs:10245 -> keeper.rs:3528). The one-shot pipeline mutates shared index_root state BEFORE that point: shared checkpoint overwrite (10150-10176), VectorIndex::replace_with_empty on the shared FSVI (10211-10216), soft-delete of live vectors (10318-10320). Four command surfaces mutate FSVI/WAL with NO lock at all: run_delete_command (8251), run_compact_command (8345 - rewrites main FSVI and unlinks the WAL), run_daemon_command (8417 - compacts whenever the WAL grows, i.e. exactly while another process appends), watch-mode live pipeline (12131).

FAILURE: 'fsfs index' appends fsynced WAL batches while the daemon compacts; appends landing between the daemon's WAL read and its WAL unlink are discarded; the indexer nonetheless writes generation_complete: true (10922). Semantic search then admits a generation with silently missing vectors - undetectable at query time. Companion HIGH: two concurrent 'fsfs index' runs each get a fresh engine dir (9497-9516), both complete, then CURRENT/manifests/FSVI/sentinel interleave last-writer-wins, baking an at-rest cross-generation mix that the fingerprint machinery then pins as legitimate. The migration rebuild is reachable from a SEARCH (11772 -> 11131), so two concurrent read-only searches over a legacy root become two racing writers.

ROOT CAUSE: writer exclusion implemented one layer down (engine dir) and never at the index_root where FSVI/checkpoint/sentinel/CURRENT live.

FIX: index_root-level flock + owner record (reuse keeper.rs's proven dev+ino-fenced design, keeper.rs ~6100-6540) acquired at the top of EVERY mutating entry point - one-shot index, watch build, delete, compact, each daemon iteration, migration rebuild - before the first shared write. Tests: two concurrent publishers (exactly one proceeds, loser performs zero shared mutations); index-vs-daemon-compaction WAL append preservation; concurrent-search-triggered rebuild.

NOTE: three previously-reported defects in this rewrite VERIFIED FIXED (generation-mix admission pin, replay source-independence, sentinel-last+fsync ordering). This is the fourth, and matches the 'production wiring remains explicitly tracked' concession in 549a9469.
close_reason: Adopted after 40h dormancy (tracker unassigned; announced on-record). PublicationLease flock at index_root acquired by all 5 mutating entry points incl. daemon-lifetime hold; typed busy refusal with holder pid; fail-closed non-flock. Deterministic in-process conflict tests; 1888 fsfs tests, zero new failures vs baseline flake set.

title: Native HNSW: own the ANN graph engine in-tree and drop the hnsw_rs dependency entirely

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
USER DIRECTIVE 2026-07-27, verbatim: 'for a trivial repo like this, we are ALWAYS better off just rewriting it all ourselves properly as part of THIS project' and 'we can never be in a position of waiting and hoping that someone else updates a repo that we could trivially implement ourselves'. This bead supersedes the DEPENDENCE strategy of bd-mczj/bd-u3wt; it does not discard their evidence, it INHERITS it as the spec.

WHY THIS IS TRACTABLE — measured, not assumed. hnsw_rs appears in exactly THREE files: crates/frankensearch-index/src/hnsw.rs (adapter), src/bin/hnsw_patch_ab.rs (A/B bench), build.rs. The consumed API surface is tiny: types Hnsw, HnswIo, PointId, Neighbour, DistDot, AnnT, ReloadOptions; operations insert, parallel_insert, search, file_dump, get_point_indexation, load_hnsw. That is a handful of entry points, not a framework.

WHAT WE ALREADY OWN (so this is assembly, not invention): SIMD/AVX2 distance kernels far better than DistDot (dot_i8_i8, f16 4-accumulator ILP, int8 two-pass); FSVI storage + WAL + tombstones; EXACT brute-force top-k as a ground-truth oracle for differential recall testing; the bd-uh2f perf-evidence layer and hnsw_patch_ab A/B harness for honest before/after; recall_certificate.rs.

★ THE SPEC IS ALREADY WRITTEN — bd-u3wt catalogued the FOUR coupled defects upstream got wrong, each with a deterministic regression: (a) upper greedy descent must not attach a lower-level new point above its sampled level; (b) connection descent must begin at min(new_level, previous_max_level), or new-only upper layers are left empty; (c) reverse edges must be stored at the LOOP layer l, not at the new point's top layer (this is the asymmetric-underfill bug); (d) search_layer must treat every point whose sampled level is >= the logical layer as participating — an empty exact-top-level bucket does not mean the logical layer is empty (exposed by a deterministic high,high,zero sampled-level sequence). Plus the parallel_insert initial-entry-point race. We write these as tests FIRST; they are the acceptance criteria of the algorithm.

★ AND THE UB CLASS DISAPPEARS BY CONSTRUCTION: the workspace is #![forbid(unsafe_code)], so the reload UB I fixed today in bd-mczj (misaligned *const T cast + OOB read driven by a header field) is not merely fixed but UNREPRESENTABLE in a native implementation.

STRATEGIC PAYOFF: dissolves bd-mczj entirely. Cargo cannot publish a git-only dependency, which is why frankensearch-index/-fusion/frankensearch are currently UNPUBLISHABLE to crates.io. Owning the engine removes that blocker without waiting on an external maintainer's release timing, and removes a supply-chain dependency from the shipped stack. Precedent is established in this project: Quill replaced Tantivy for the same reasons.

SCOPE: new self-contained module (no edits to the frozen/entangled index sources while BrownCoyote's bd-u3wt tranche is uncommitted), serial-correct build first with parallel build behind attestation second, own serialization (no foreign format), differential recall vs exact search, then wire behind the existing ann feature and retire the adapter + the hnsw_rs dependency. NOT claimed until recall/latency are measured against the current pinned engine with the honest paired harness.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CORE ENGINE LANDED 0b59e600 on origin/main+master — crates/frankensearch-index/src/native_hnsw.rs, 1451 lines, 12/12 tests green, rustfmt clean, ubs criticals are the known panic-in-cfg(test) false-positive family. Self-contained: registered in no lib.rs yet, so it collides with ZERO in-flight index work (BrownCoyote's bd-u3wt tranche and my bd-tqhc 2a remain untouched and uncommitted).

WHAT EXISTS: HnswParams (validated), deterministic SplitMix64 LevelSampler (pure function of seed+id, so topology is reproducible), VectorDistance trait (the graph stores NO vectors — it indexes rows of a caller-owned store, so there is one copy of the data and we reuse the existing SIMD kernels), serial build/insert, beam search with NaN-safe total_cmp ordering, RNG neighbour-selection heuristic, degree pruning, and verify() returning a typed GraphDefect enum (11 variants) rather than a string so an attestation gate can branch on defect class.

BD-U3WT INVARIANTS IMPLEMENTED + FIXTURED: (1) descent never links above the sampled level; (2) connection starts at min(new_level, previous_max_level); (3) reciprocal edges stored at the LOOP layer, never the new point's top layer; (4) participation is level >= layer, never ==. Fixtures: two-orthogonal-points mutual reachability (the original bd-u3wt reproduction), high/high/zero level sequence, n=0/1/2/3/8/9/17 boundaries, determinism, out-of-order insert rejection, degenerate params. ★ verify_rejects_an_edge_above_a_neighbours_level FORGES a violation and asserts the exact defect variant — the gate is proven non-vacuous rather than passing trivially.

MEASURED (50 queries, ef=100, LCG-random 32-dim corpus): recall@10 = 1.0000 at n=1000 AND n=5000; structure verifies at both; layer-0 avg degree 31.1 of 32 budget; 4 layers. Work: 885 dist/query at n=1000 (1.1x vs exact) and 1814 at n=5000 (2.8x vs exact) — speedup is modest at these sizes because ANN pays off with scale and ef is untuned; the recall/latency curve and larger n are the next measurement, NOT a claim.

★★ TWO FINDINGS THAT COST REAL TIME, both now documented IN the code so nobody repeats them:
(a) A LATTICE TEST CORPUS IS A TRAP. My first fixture used (i*31 + d*17) % 101 — a plausible-looking deterministic corpus. It is tie-heavy enough to BOTH depress apparent recall to 0.64 AND genuinely fragment the graph (verify reported 33 of 5000 points reachable). I nearly 'fixed' a correct algorithm against a broken benchmark, and made two algorithm changes on that false signal before switching to an LCG corpus, where the SAME build scores recall 1.0 and verifies clean. Generalization: before treating a quality number as a defect signal, confirm the FIXTURE is representative — a deterministic corpus is not automatically a valid one.
(b) PRUNING MUST DROP BOTH DIRECTIONS AND PROTECT THE NEW EDGE. Trimming only one side silently makes the graph directed (traversal enters regions it cannot leave — the same asymmetry class bd-u3wt found upstream), and pruning the edge just created orphans the new point since nothing else links to it yet. Both are enforced and commented at the site.
Also measured and recorded: removing the heuristic top-up starves the graph (recall 0.66 -> 0.54, degree 32 -> 11.6), so the top-up stays.

NOT CLAIMED / REMAINING: persistence (own format, no foreign serialization), tombstone + WAL integration, parallel build behind structural attestation, wiring behind the ann feature, retiring the hnsw.rs adapter and DROPPING the hnsw_rs dependency (the actual bd-mczj dissolution), and honest paired latency/recall A/B against the pinned engine on a real manifested corpus before any performance statement.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FRESH-EYES REVIEW 2026-07-27, commit a1437cfb — four defects found by re-reading today's work, all fixed and verified.

★ (1) QUADRATIC BUILD (native_hnsw, severity: would have made the engine unusable at its target scale). beam_search allocated and zeroed vec![false; adjacency.len()] on EVERY call, and construction runs one beam search per layer per point => an n-point build wrote O(n^2 * layers) bytes of bookkeeping before any useful work. At the 100k scale hnsw_threshold targets that is ~4e10 byte-writes. Replaced with an epoch-stamped VisitedSet allocated once and reused (clearing = counter bump; wraparound handled by a single fill(0)); insert borrows it out of the struct via mem::take so &mut self and the buffer coexist, and it is restored on the error path too; search uses one buffer per query instead of one per layer. MEASURED AFTER: build n=5000 1.64s, n=20000 9.47s — 4x the data for 5.8x the time, not the ~16x quadratic scaling would give. recall@10 unchanged: 1.0000 @ n=5000, 0.9980 @ n=20000; speedup over exact scan rises 2.8x -> 8.4x, confirming the ANN value proposition grows with n as it should.

★ (2) prune() EVICTED THE WRONG NEIGHBOUR (native_hnsw, quality). When reinstating the protected edge it called kept.pop(), but kept is NOT distance-ordered: select_neighbours appends its top-up fill AFTER the heuristic's picks, so the list interleaves (e.g. [c0,c5,c9,c1,c2]) and popping usually evicted a NEAR neighbour rather than the farthest. Now locates the genuinely farthest kept entry by scanning the distance-sorted candidate list in reverse. (The related ordering worry was checked and is fine:  is computed AFTER the protected reinstatement, so the protected node is never also removed from the counterpart.)

★ (3) EMPTY LANE COULD CARRY NO REASON (sync_searcher, contract violation — this is bd-tqhc's whole point). classify_fast_empty ran a SECOND full search and returned classified.zero_signal, which is None when that lane finds hits. The production fast lane is the int8 two-pass while the classified lane is the exact scan, so they can disagree about emptiness — leaving an empty result with zero_signal = None. Now reads the index census (zero_signal_state().empty_result_reason(had_filter)) instead: cheaper than a re-scan, cannot disagree with itself, and ALWAYS yields a reason; request-scoped conditions (k=0 / non-finite / zero-norm) are checked first in the documented precedence. The async searcher has the same narrow gap but TwoTierIndex exposes no public census and two_tier.rs is frozen under BrownCoyote's tranche, so it is precisely documented in place instead — FOLLOW-UP: add a public census accessor on TwoTierIndex (mirroring InMemoryVectorIndex) and switch searcher.rs to it once the ANN tranche lands.

★ (4) TWO TESTS ASSERTED LESS THAN THEIR NAMES CLAIMED. (a) zero_signal_lifecycle accepted AllTombstoned OR NewlyCreatedEmpty after delete-all — and was actually producing NewlyCreatedEmpty every run, so the tombstone classification the test is NAMED for was never exercised: appended records live in the WAL, where deletion REMOVES rather than tombstones. Fixture now compacts WAL into main first, so deletion produces real tombstones, and both the initial and post-restart assertions are exact equality. (b) cancellation_contract's degenerate-request case accepted 'either a typed cancellation or a benign empty result', which passes whichever way precedence runs and therefore pinned nothing. Probed the real behavior — cancellation DOES dominate, a zero limit returns Cancelled{phase:"search"} because the entry checkpoint precedes the limit==0 short circuit — so that is now asserted exactly, and the offset-past-the-end case the comment promised but never tested was added.
GENERALIZATION for this campaign: an either/or assertion over a DETERMINISTIC input is a smell — it cannot distinguish 'the behavior I want' from 'the fallback', and in case (a) it hid a completely untested code path for the life of the test. Probe the actual value, then pin it.

GATES: index lib clippy --no-deps --all-targets -D warnings clean; fusion 909 passed / 1 failed (the failure is CyanPine's in-flight daemon_fallback.rs rewrite, +337/-1396, staged AND modified — not mine, and the federated min_indices red I filed as bd-6bgp is now GONE, fixed in 39a644dc); quill cancellation_contract 3/3; lexical legacy_ignores_cx 1/1; index zero_signal_lifecycle 3/3; native_hnsw 12/12; rustfmt clean on all touched files; ubs criticals are the known panic-in-cfg(test) family.

SECOND FRESH-EYES PASS 2026-07-27, commit 12e75b69. Four findings, one of which is a CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER CLAIMS ON THIS BEAD.

★★ (1) CORRECTION — 'the workspace forbids unsafe' IS FALSE. I asserted this in the module header, in commit 0b59e600's message, in my earlier comment on this bead, and in mail 4291 to BrownCoyote. The workspace lints unsafe_code = "deny" (NOT forbid), with an explicit comment that deny is used precisely so crates can opt in — and frankensearch-index itself opts in TWICE for memory-mapping (mapped_file.rs:103 and lib.rs:224, both Mmap/MmapMut). The substantive claim survives in narrowed form: native_hnsw.rs contains no unsafe and needs none (it stores ids and distances, never reinterpreted bytes), so the bd-mczj reload UB class cannot occur IN THIS MODULE. But it is a module property, not a crate guarantee. ★★ (2) THE MODULE WAS NEVER LINTED, AND MY 'clippy clean' CLAIM WAS VACUOUS. native_hnsw.rs is declared in NO lib.rs —  matches only the file itself. Nothing compiles it: cargo test -p frankensearch-index runs 0 of its 12 tests, CI does not build it, and my previously reported 'index lib clippy --no-deps --all-targets -D warnings clean' never saw the module at all. Fixed the verification by replicating the workspace's EXACT lint policy (pedantic + nursery + its 21 named allows, e.g. cast_precision_loss and missing_const_for_fn are already allowed) in the shadow harness. First real run: 6 lib errors + 22 with tests. All six fixed on their merits rather than silenced — HnswParams derives Eq (all-usize, so equality is exact); LevelSampler now WALKS UP to the sampled level instead of casting an f64, making the MAX_LEVEL ceiling structural rather than a clamp-then-cast whose out-of-range behaviour would saturate a corrupt value into a plausible-looking level; select_neighbours never touched self and became an associated function; plus map_or, Vec clone, and literal-separator fixes. Lib clippy is now genuinely clean under the real policy.
   ★ REGISTRATION IS STILL OPEN AND IS A REAL RISK: until  is added to lib.rs, the file is dead weight that CI cannot protect from rot. I did NOT add it, because lib.rs carries my uncommitted tqhc-2a hunks plus BrownCoyote's, so a path-limited commit would sweep 2a in. It must be registered in the same window as the 2a landing (or via an index-only checkpoint with Brown's OK, the ce66fc7f method).

(3) A FULL GRAPH SATURATED SILENTLY. insert computed  via u32::try_from(len).unwrap_or(u32::MAX), so once a graph exceeded u32 addressing, an insert of id=u32::MAX would read as validly in-order. Now returns a typed capacity error naming the row count.

A failed insert therefore invalidates the graph: discard and rebuild. build() already does the right thing by dropping the partial graph. Rollback was considered and rejected as disproportionate — it would have to undo links AND the prunes those links triggered on other points, for a failure mode that means the vector store cannot read its own rows.

title: Implement S3-FIFO lock-free cache eviction
description:
Implement S3-FIFO (Yang et al. 2023) three-queue cache eviction for embedding vectors, search results, and index segments. S3-FIFO uses Small/Main/Ghost FIFO queues with no per-access list manipulation (unlike LRU), achieving higher hit rates and lock-free operation.

Graveyard entry: §15.1 S3-FIFO Cache Eviction
EV score: 50 (Impact=4, Confidence=5, Reuse=5, Effort=2, Friction=1)
Priority tier: A

Architecture:
pub struct S3FifoCache<K, V> {
    small: FifoQueue<K, V>,    // New entries land here (10% capacity)
    main: FifoQueue<K, V>,     // Promoted entries (90% capacity)
    ghost: GhostQueue<K>,      // Evicted keys (metadata only, 2x main capacity)
    max_bytes: usize,          // Configurable memory budget (default 256MB)
    freq_threshold: u8,        // Promotion threshold (default 1)
}

Eviction policy:
1. New items enter Small queue
2. On Small eviction: if accessed >= freq_threshold times, promote to Main; else evict
3. On Main eviction: evict (FIFO order)
4. Ghost tracks recently evicted keys (metadata only); re-access of ghost key → direct Main insert
5. All queues are FIFO (no list manipulation per access)

Cache targets in frankensearch:
- Embedding vectors: Key=(doc_id, embedder_id), Value=Vec<f32> (256-768 bytes)
- Quality model inference: Key=content_hash, Value=Vec<f32> (avoids re-embedding)
- Tantivy search results: Key=(query_hash, k), Value=Vec<ScoredResult>

Trait interface:
pub trait CachePolicy<K: Hash + Eq, V>: Send + Sync {
    fn get(&self, key: &K) -> Option<&V>;
    fn insert(&self, key: K, value: V, size_bytes: usize);
    fn hit_rate(&self) -> f64;
    fn memory_used(&self) -> usize;
}

Implementations: S3Fifo (default), Unbounded (HashMap, for tests), NoCache (passthrough).

Budgeted mode: max_bytes configurable via FRANKENSEARCH_CACHE_MB env var. On exhaustion: evict Small first. Hit rate < 30% for 100 queries → bypass cache + log WARN.

Fallback: CachePolicy::noop() returns None for all gets (zero-cost passthrough).

Isomorphism proof: Cache is transparent — same query produces identical rankings with/without cache. Verify via golden-check corpus (bd-3un.38).

File: frankensearch-core/src/cache.rs (trait + S3Fifo impl)

Reference: Yang et al. "FIFO Queues are All You Need for Cache Eviction" (SOSP 2023)
Baseline comparator: OnceLock (never evicts), HashMap (unbounded growth), LRU (lock per access)

1. The feature is fully implemented according to this bead design, scope, and referenced files or modules.
2. Integration with dependent components is complete and behavior remains correct across normal and degraded flows.
3. Edge and error cases are explicitly handled with deterministic outcomes and clear reason codes or errors.
4. Unit and integration tests (and e2e where relevant) are added, passing, and include detailed structured logging assertions.
5. Performance and resource expectations in the bead are validated and documented with reproducible evidence.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
REFINEMENT PASS 1 — Architecture clarifications and integration notes:

1. SCOPE CLARIFICATION: This bead (S3-FIFO cache) is for EMBEDDING-LEVEL caching (vectors, model inference results, search result sets). It is ORTHOGONAL to bd-3un.41 (IndexCache for index-level caching with OnceLock). They operate at different layers:
   - bd-l7v: Per-query/per-document embedding cache (hot path, high churn)
   - bd-3un.41: Per-index file cache (cold path, loaded once, invalidated on staleness)
   Both should use CachePolicy trait from this bead, but bd-3un.41's OnceLock pattern is appropriate for index segments (loaded once, held for lifetime).

2. FILE PLACEMENT CORRECTION: The CachePolicy trait should live in frankensearch-core/src/cache.rs (as stated). The S3Fifo implementation should ALSO live there since it's a zero-dep data structure. The NoCache and Unbounded impls go alongside. No external crate dependency needed — S3-FIFO is ~150 lines of safe Rust.

3. THREAD SAFETY: S3FifoCache must be Send + Sync. Use DashMap for concurrent access or wrap with RwLock. For the FIFO queues, use crossbeam-queue::ArrayQueue (bounded, lock-free) or a simple VecDeque behind Mutex (simpler, still fast since queue operations are O(1)).

4. INTEGRATION HOOK: The TwoTierSearcher (bd-3un.24) should accept an optional Arc<dyn CachePolicy> parameter. When present, check cache before embedding and store results after embedding. This means the cache is injected, not hardcoded.

5. TEST REQUIREMENTS (covered by bd-3un.31): Add tests for:
   - Cache hit/miss counting accuracy
   - Small→Main promotion on freq_threshold
   - Ghost queue re-admission to Main
   - Memory budget enforcement (insert beyond max_bytes triggers eviction)
   - Concurrent get/insert from multiple threads
   - Isomorphism: same query produces identical results with/without cache

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
REFINEMENT PASS 3 — Composition with bd-qtx (quantization ladder):

The S3-FIFO cache stores embedding vectors keyed by (doc_id, embedder_id). When bd-qtx is implemented, the cache key should also include the quantization level to avoid serving f16-quantized vectors when f32 was requested (or vice versa). Updated key: (doc_id, embedder_id, quant_level).

This is a soft composition concern — no dependency needed since the cache stores whatever Vec<f32> the embedder produces (always f32 at query time, quantization only affects storage). The cache correctly caches the COMPUTED embeddings, not the STORED ones. No action needed — just documenting that the cache is quantization-transparent.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
ASUPERSYNC MIGRATION — MODERATE REVISION (sync primitives for cache):

Replace std sync primitives with asupersync equivalents for the S3-FIFO cache:

BEFORE:
  - DashMap or RwLock for concurrent cache access
  - crossbeam-queue::ArrayQueue for FIFO queues

AFTER:
  - asupersync::sync::RwLock for concurrent cache access (cancel-aware)
  - VecDeque behind asupersync::sync::Mutex for FIFO queues (simpler, cancel-aware)
  - OR: keep lock-free ArrayQueue from crossbeam if benchmarks show it's needed (crossbeam-queue is a small, focused crate without tokio deps — acceptable to keep)

REVISED CachePolicy trait:
  pub trait CachePolicy<K: Hash + Eq, V>: Send + Sync {
      async fn get(&self, cx: &Cx, key: &K) -> Option<V>;
      async fn insert(&self, cx: &Cx, key: K, value: V, size_bytes: usize);
      fn hit_rate(&self) -> f64;
      fn memory_used(&self) -> usize;
  }

Note: get() and insert() are now async because they acquire cancel-aware locks. The Cx parameter enables:
1. Cancel-aware lock acquisition (don't deadlock if task is cancelled while waiting for lock)
2. Budget enforcement (cache operations respect the task's deadline)
3. Tracing integration (cache hit/miss events in structured trace)

TESTING: Use LabRuntime for deterministic cache behavior testing:
  - Deterministic scheduling means cache hit/miss patterns are reproducible
  - ContendedMutex variant for measuring lock contention under load

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
PERFORMANCE PROOF-LANE PROTOCOL (bd-bobf gate)

This bead is subject to the bd-bobf performance proof-lane gate. Before any performance-critical change in this bead's implementation may be considered release-ready, the following evidence artifacts must be produced and verified:

1. BASELINE BENCHMARK: Run criterion benchmarks (bd-3un.33) capturing p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (ops/sec), and peak memory (RSS delta) for the hot path this bead optimizes. Record results in data/perf-evidence/<bead-id>-baseline.json.

2. PROFILE HOTSPOT EVIDENCE: Profile the hot path using cargo flamegraph or perf. Identify top-5 hotspot functions by cumulative time. Record in data/perf-evidence/<bead-id>-hotspots.txt.

3. OPPORTUNITY SCORE: Compute opportunity_score = (baseline_p95 / optimized_p95). Must be >= 2.0 to justify the optimization complexity. If < 2.0, document why the optimization is still warranted (e.g., tail latency improvement, memory reduction).

4. ISOMORPHISM PROOF NOTE: Document that the optimization preserves result ordering, tie-breaking determinism, floating-point reproducibility, and RNG seed behavior. Specifically: "Given identical inputs and configuration, the optimized path produces bit-identical output rankings as the unoptimized path." If not bit-identical (e.g., FP reordering), document the acceptable divergence bound.

5. GOLDEN OUTPUT VERIFICATION: Run the fixture corpus queries (bd-3un.38) through both the baseline and optimized paths. Assert identical result sets (or document bounded divergence). Include rollback command: `git revert <commit>` or feature flag to disable.

STATUS: Evidence collection is deferred until the implementation is merged and benchmarks can be run against real workloads. This comment establishes the required evidence format for release-gate compliance (bd-ehuk).

title: Re-measure multi-accumulator on f16 dot kernels NOW that decode is SIMD (was decode-bound)
description:
Context: bd-gfzk landed branchless SIMD f16->f32 widen (commit 8c2862f/bca1374), making dot_product_f16_bytes_f32 ~3x faster. The f16 paths were previously decode-bound, so multi-accumulator unrolling REGRESSED them (docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md). Now that decode is SIMD and no longer dominant, accumulation latency may have become a meaningful fraction again.

LEVER: re-try 4 independent f32x8 accumulators on the (now SIMD-decoded) f16 kernels; head-to-head rebench dot/dim{256,384}/f16_bytes & f16_slice.

CAVEAT (important): multi-accumulator REORDERS the f32 summation -> dot scores change by ~1e-7 -> NO LONGER bit-identical to the current kernel (unlike the bit-exact SIMD-decode win). Must re-run full index lib tests + any score-sensitive goldens to confirm determinism/Tier-1 ordering holds (the f32_bytes/f32_f32 reorder already on main passed goldens, so likely OK, but verify). Keep only if ratio < 0.97 with no tracked regression > 1.03; else revert + NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE row.

Bench infra already exists: crates/frankensearch-index/benches/dot_product.rs (f16_*_new vs f16_*_old). Labels: perf, simd, vector-search, bold-verify.
close_reason: Refuted + measured: f16 dot is bandwidth-bound (5-7.7MB slab out of cache), so 4-accumulator gives only within-noise ~0.95 with overlapping CIs; doesn't transfer to the larger limit_all slab and would break default-f16 cross-host bit-identity. See docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md 2026-06-29 (commit 89bbddf).

title: Wire total lexical contracts through live Quill/Tantivy adapters and immutable gauntlet artifacts
description: P0 ORDINARY CORE LEXICAL CONTRACT V3. Production differential campaigns must persist and replay a method-bound, engine-neutral witness for ordinary LexicalSearch boundaries without dropping the legacy rank, tie, snippet, count, AST, or registered-divergence evidence. Core V3 covers full search, fusion candidates, all-lexical hydration, strict-hybrid subset hydration, semantic-only no-op hydration, and mixed-winner hydration. Ordinary method evidence may expose only values returned by the actual call; count, snippets, and highlights remain NotExposed here and are proven separately by bd-8nqz.4. CASS profile remains a separate typed contract under bd-cass-total-lexical-contract-jxyq.
design: Artifact object schema V3 and campaign report schema V5 retain both legacy rich rank-envelope evidence and Core Lexical V3 inputs. Real Quill and pinned-Tantivy adapters invoke the same ordinary LexicalSearch methods and bind every observation to engine role, immutable snapshot SHA-256, corpus/query-contract identity, classified raw query, limit, seed, boundary, exposure, capability, and normalized-transform provenance. Stable SearchError class/code/canonical fixed-width payload is equivalence evidence; bounded redacted Display/source-chain diagnostics are retained but are not equivalence. Hydration evidence includes exact selection ranks/origins, input, post-state, canonical NotRun, success/error including partial mutation, and scoped deferred-metadata waivers only after the exact shape proves restoration. Validation replay-recomputes all derived comparison, waiver, mismatch, coverage, and disposition fields. Campaign admission requires nonempty and explicit-empty full/candidate successes on each engine; every hydration shape must succeed; and deferred engines must independently restore metadata for all-lexical, strict-hybrid, and mixed-winner shapes. V1/V2 objects and V3/V4 reports are decode-only nonadmissible. Evidence redaction is lexical-subobject and fixture-only; outer raw fixture queries and legacy snippets are not private-query-safe.
acceptance_criteria: Live same-corpus Quill/Tantivy adapters emit and persist every named Core V3 lane; verified reload and replay are exact. Independent mutations of every observed context, hit, rank/order, one-bit score, source/component, metadata presence/digest, explanation, count state, empty shape, typed error class/code/payload, hydration selection/origin/input/post-state/result, capability, and provenance fail the actual artifact/campaign. Regressions cover the historical None versus empty metadata bug, forged NotRun thresholds, independent full and candidate Cancelled/Error outcomes, partial hydration errors, successful empty searches, all eager/deferred pairings, and all three deferred restoration shapes. A frozen known-miss query proves full/candidate explicit empty semantics in persisted real artifacts. Core V3 admission is unavailable to rank-envelope-only profiles and may not authorize replacement through generic CampaignReport passed. Unknown schema, omitted lane, valid-but-altered field, content-address tamper, and derived-field tamper reject. Full current-source gauntlet default and tantivy-oracle suites, fmt, clippy, UBS, and clean strict-RCH evidence pass before closure; implementing SHA and exact commands are attached. Native enriched snippets/query_type/count/page compatibility and a dedicated replacement-ready join remain required under bd-8nqz.4.
notes: SCOPE BOUNDARY (2026-07-26): this task owns the ordinary public LexicalSearch/ScoredResult QuillSubject versus TantivyOracle lanes only. CASS-profile result types are not ScoredResult and must not be coerced into this schema or silently marked NotApplicable; sibling P0 bd-cass-total-lexical-contract-jxyq owns their exhaustively typed live adapter/artifact integration. Terminal bd-qwkq depends on both tasks, so the release gate cannot pass with either profile blind.

title: Tantivy full and fusion-candidate collectors diverge under exact-score ties
description: P0 SAME-ENGINE PUBLIC-CONTRACT DEFECT exposed by the live Core Lexical V3 campaign. TantivyIndex::search always executes TopDocs alone, while search_doc_ids/search_fusion_candidates executes the tuple (TopDocs, Count) for queries rejected by use_count_free_top_k. On the committed 120-document default corpus, query 'how to sear a steak properly' (100 matches, k=20) returns a different first doc_id/rank ordering between the two ordinary methods before metadata hydration. This is not a Quill/Tantivy divergence and must not be waived: the same Tantivy index disagrees with itself. Canonical repair should make the non-counting fusion-candidate path use the same native TopDocs collector semantics for every parsed query shape, retaining counted execution only where total_count is actually part of the API or as an explicit benchmark baseline. Do not repair by sorting doc IDs, expanding k, loosening rank envelopes, or teaching the comparator to ignore order. Recheck ord-table materialization independently so collector parity is not confused with ID mapping.
acceptance_criteria: A real same-index regression with enough identical-score matches to cross k proves TantivyIndex::search, search_doc_ids, search_fusion_candidates, and post-hydration results have identical ordered doc_id, rank, f32 score bits, source/components/explanation and final metadata for (a) >2 plain terms, (b) phrase/boolean/fielded structured syntax, (c) one/two plain terms, (d) k=0, empty and no-match, and (e) limit below/at/above the cutoff tie group. A separate assertion proves fast ord-table ID materialization equals docstore materialization, so parity is not obtained through stale/misaligned ordinals. execute_query_with_offset still returns exact total_count independent of k; search_doc_ids performs no Count collection for any query and retains the counted helper only as an explicit benchmark control. Same-binary benchmark/negative evidence records the performance effect without making a speed claim. Full lexical default+all-feature tests, full gauntlet default+Tantivy-oracle live campaign with exact clean provenance, strict RCH check/clippy -D warnings, fmt, UBS, bounded logs and verified persisted replay pass. No comparator waiver or post-hoc tie sort is admissible.
close_reason: Completed: Tantivy ordinary and fusion-candidate collectors now preserve the same ordered public contract under exact-score ties, with a clean-provenance live campaign and verified persisted reload.

title: Attest daemon-produced embeddings with full vector-space identity; never label them as local fallback vectors
description: DaemonClient returns raw vectors without producer-authenticated identity, and DaemonFallbackEmbedder can report caller/local fallback metadata even when bytes came from a daemon. CASS UDS checks only a model ID, so same-name new weights/tokenizer/preprocessing or a same-dimension wrong space can poison queries and indexes. Extend daemon handshake/health and every embed response with a producer-authenticated envelope binding request nonce, exact response payload digest, canonical EmbeddingSpaceIdentity and EmbeddingProducerAttestation fingerprints, provider/backend, immutable weights and tokenizer digests, preprocessing/pooling/normalization/dimension, protocol revision and daemon generation. A caller-supplied immutable epoch is expected state, not proof from the responder. Validate the responding daemon per connection and response before accepting a vector; reconnect or fail typed on drift. A compatible verified live daemon may satisfy readiness without local model files or eager load. An explicitly assumed daemon may support only labeled transient exploration and is forbidden for persistent/verified paths. Mismatch recovery is restart/upgrade daemon or select a compatible index, not blind install/reindex. Never attest fallback identity for unverified daemon bytes.
design: Consume bd-4v5n canonical contracts and use a challenge-response protocol. A pinned daemon launch/public-key receipt or equivalently authenticated local transport establishes producer authority; each response binds the challenge/request nonce, daemon generation, space and producer fingerprints, ordered batch shape and body digest. UDS peer credentials alone are insufficient to prove model bytes. Reject absent/malformed/replayed/stale envelopes, caller-only metadata, mid-connection key/generation/identity drift and payload tamper before returning any identity-bound vector. Cancellation never publishes a partial batch or updates the accepted generation. Trust level is explicit; AssumedDaemon is nonpersistent and cannot satisfy verified semantic readiness.
acceptance_criteria: Every accepted verified daemon vector carries producer-authenticated per-response proof and matches the complete expected identity at handshake, health, connection and response boundaries. Same-name or same-dimension changed spaces, wrong executable/key, caller-only epoch, absent/malformed identity, replayed nonce, payload tamper and midstream drift fail typed before search/index/cache work. A compatible verified daemon-only configuration is truthfully ready without local artifacts; assumed daemon is visibly degraded and cannot persist. Unit, protocol, reconnect/cancel, key-rotation, batch-order, wrong-space same-dimension, lexical-fallback-zero-semantic, and no-mock fresh-process FrankenSearch daemon/FSFS lifecycle tests pass with bounded redacted logs. One terminal event asserts stable code/category/exit 78/non-retry. Logs include endpoint, protocol, key and identity hashes, never vectors, query text, credentials, raw bodies, or sensitive paths. Closure records the exact FrankenSearch commit plus an explicit handoff to bd-cass-semantic-cross-repo-receipt-91k2; terminal CASS product integration is a downstream receipt and is not a prerequisite for this foundational protocol bead.
notes: 2026-07-27 CyanPine: landed frankensearch protocol foundation e580d460. title: Write unit and integration tests for typed filter predicates
description:

10. filter_chain_empty: Empty FilterChain matches everything (no filters = no restriction).
11. filter_name: Each filter returns descriptive name() string.

Integration Tests:
12. vector_search_with_filter: 100 vectors, 50 type=tweet, 50 type=dm. Search with DocTypeFilter('tweet'), verify all results are tweets.
13. vector_search_early_exit: Measure that filtered search with highly selective filter is faster than unfiltered + post-filter (early exit optimization).

title: Cross-tier publication binding: fast/quality FSVI pair lacks a shared publication identity (bd-zhjv8 finding 3)
description: Split from bd-zhjv8 (findings 1+2 fixed: generation-authority install_replacement + staged two_tier publish). Remaining window: TwoTierIndexBuilder::finish publishes fast then quality as two independent install_replacement renames; a crash between them yields a mixed-generation pair (new fast + old quality) that opens cleanly and that refresh merges can launder. Design direction: stamp BOTH tiers with one shared publication nonce in the FSVI header's two unused reserved bytes (reserved[1..3], currently zero — legacy pairs read as 0==0 so compatibility is free); choose the nonce != the destination pair's current nonce so successive generations can never collide; TwoTierIndex::open compares nonces when both tiers exist and on mismatch degrades to fast-only with a warn (graceful degradation instead of silent mixed-generation results). Red proof: build pair A, replace only the fast tier with a nonce-B build (simulated crash between renames), open, assert quality tier is refused/degraded rather than blended.
close_reason: Landed: reserved-bytes publication nonce stamped identically on both tiers by finish() (successor of destination pair's nonce); open() degrades mixed pairs to fast-only with warn; legacy 0==0 pairs unaffected; vacuum/compact preserve the stamp. Red-proofed both detection and stamping; workspace check/clippy/fmt green.

title: P0: authoritative immutable model verification receipts for FSFS defaults
description: Prerequisite 1 for A5. Repair bundled-model verification receipt authority in frankensearch-embed before any default loader or quickstart trusts cached state. Freeze the receipt schema and complete manifest fingerprint; keep the receipt writer private and atomically publish only after full artifact hashing. Cached verification and status/doctor observation are read-only. Reject crafted same-model-ID legacy receipts, missing schema or fingerprint, stale receipts, partial artifacts, same-size substitutions, symlinks, and mutation races. No receipt may attest bytes it did not hash.
design: Derive an opaque, non-Serde verified capability solely from the frozen manifest and verified bytes. The capability retains the same immutable generation/file owner whose bytes were verified; a verified token followed by mutable path re-resolution is forbidden. Path-only backends require an immutable generation lease plus before/after file identity and digest binding through loader construction and first use. Stage, fsync, hash, and atomically publish canonical bounded receipt bytes only after complete verification. Non-test detection or concrete Model2Vec/FastEmbed constructors must require and consume the capability; a bool, public DTO, marker filename, model ID, size/mtime tuple, or status observation cannot substitute. Caches accelerate observation but never mint, refresh, repair, or mutate authority.
acceptance_criteria: A crafted same-ID legacy receipt fails before model load. Missing/future schema, wrong manifest fingerprint, role omission/duplication, same-size byte substitution, partial directory, symlink, stale receipt, and receipt/content mismatch fail closed. The consumed loader retains the exact verified immutable owner; mutation, rename, replacement, or path retargeting between verification, capability handoff, loader construction, and first embedding rejects. Path-only backends prove an immutable generation lease and matching before/after identity+digest. Hash-to-publish, cache-to-execution, and two-process mutation races cannot yield trusted stale authority. Cached observation changes no receipt/artifact bytes, mtimes, or directory entries. Interrupted publication preserves prior authority. A per-symbol census proves at least one executed non-test loader consumer; deleting or bypassing capability consumption fails compile or a real-loader mutation canary. Unit/property/fresh-process race tests, default/all-feature embed tests, strict workspace checks, bounded redacted logs, and exact source/receipt/artifact hashes pass.
close_reason: Implemented in A4, landed 7903e4b8 (WhiteGrove; reviews GrayThrush + CreamCoast). Receipt schema frozen with manifest fingerprint; minter private behind full-SHA verify_dir_and_record with atomic publish; status/doctor/auto-detect are observers only (repeated-observer tests freeze entry set/kind/len/bytes/mtime/mode). Crafted same-model-ID legacy receipt rejection PROVEN executing on the landed tree: default_build_quickstart E2E stage=doctor-failure stale_same_id_receipt_rejected=true, then explicit CLI verify refreshes receipts (receipt_refreshed=true) before indexing. Strict-remote embed receipt/golden/race suite green (vmi1227854 2/2, per freeze receipts mails 8749/8770).

title: Explicit, verified model provisioning with CLI acquire-and-retry; no silent hash or hidden library/build network
description:
TERMINAL SEMANTIC PROVISIONING INTEGRATION. Silent hash fallback removes the forcing function: semantic requests never fail, prompt or reindex, and a hash-built FSVI remains incompatible after model installation. HashEmbedder remains an explicit test/control implementation and is never reported as semantic. Explicit semantic fails closed with typed RecoveryPlan; hybrid lexical fallback is explicit and actionable.

Implementation is deliberately split: bd-p6z6.1 owns streamed verified atomic acquisition; .2 owns library/TTY/non-TTY/offline requested-mode policy; .3 owns blue-green compatible reindex, atomic publication, rollback and one original-command retry; .4 owns doctor and no-mock lifecycle E2E. This umbrella reconciles their public API, CLI, fsfs, facade and documentation surfaces. QualityOnly MiniLM must be independently usable; ordinary builds and build.rs never download models; acquired alone never means searchable.
design: Keep acquisition, policy, execution and terminal E2E independently reviewable and dependency-ordered. The umbrella closes only after all children integrate through one versioned RecoveryPlan and no duplicated hidden fallback/network/runtime authority remains.
acceptance_criteria: All four children close with exact commits and evidence. Library, TTY, non-TTY and offline behavior is explicit; acquisition is atomic/cancel-correct; blue-green reindex/publish/rollback and exactly-one retry preserve old generations; doctor and no-mock Treasure/CASS lifecycle pass. Hash is never semantic, quality-only works, warm/offline is zero-network, build scripts are network-free, and bounded structured evidence covers every failure state.
notes:
TEST + LOGGING REQUIREMENTS (added per user directive; do not close without these).
UNIT: (1) manifest embedded via include_str! matches the published bytes -- assert exact size and sha256 per file, mirroring franken_ocr's builtin_manifest_publishes_the_zoo_and_lints_clean regression test, so a silent manifest edit cannot retarget an installed binary. (2) sha256 mismatch during acquisition -> typed error, partial file NOT installed. (3) size mismatch mid-stream -> abort before overrun. (4) cache-hit path verifies without allocating the whole artifact (assert bounded memory / streaming). (5) atomic install: interrupt between staging and rename leaves the previous verified file intact. (6) concurrent acquisition from two processes -> advisory lock serialises; exactly one download; both succeed.
E2E SCRIPT: start from an empty cache; run a real semantic query; assert the acquire-then-RETRY path returns actual results without the user issuing a second command; re-run and assert zero network calls on the warm path. Then corrupt one byte of the cached weights and assert the next run detects it and re-acquires rather than producing garbage embeddings.
OFFLINE MUST KEEP WORKING -- DO NOT LOSE FUNCTIONALITY: with FRANKENSEARCH_OFFLINE=1 (or no network) and no model present, the failure must be immediate and actionable, never a hang and never a silent hash fallback. Add an explicit offline test asserting the message names every searched directory AND the exact install command, enforced by a regression test the way franken_ocr does it (tests/agent_ergonomics_regression.rs:141 model_not_found_error_is_actionable).
LOGGING: log acquisition start/end with URL host, bytes, elapsed, and verification outcome; log the warm-path decision at debug! with the reason it was considered valid. A user must be able to answer 'did it download, and did it verify?' from one run's logs.

title: Semantic model acquisition: stream-verify and atomically publish frozen artifacts
description: Implement the explicit cancel-correct library acquisition primitive for frozen semantic model manifests. No prompts, private runtime, hidden network or build.rs download. Stream into a unique staging artifact under an advisory cross-process lock; enforce declared byte budget, content length, SHA-256, revision/license/source manifest and vector-space identity; load-self-test; fsync file; atomically rename; fsync parent. A failed, cancelled, truncated, oversized, hash-mismatched, corrupt or concurrent attempt preserves every prior verified generation and leaves a typed recovery state. Support identical hash-verified --from-file installation and warm-cache zero-network lookup. Structured progress records model/revision, URL host only, bounded bytes/duration/cache reason and verification result without sensitive paths or content.
design: One versioned ModelArtifactManifest is the authority. Acquisition returns typed stage receipts and never marks semantic ready; readiness remains a separate compatible-index decision. Verification precedes atomic publication. No cleanup operation may delete a prior generation; orphan staging is diagnosed and later GC requires explicit policy.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest revision/size/hash/license/vector-space invariants pass. Network and --from-file paths share streaming verification and atomic publication. Tests cover exact success, truncation, overrun, size/hash mismatch, corrupt cache, interrupted rename/fsync, cancellation at every stage, permission/no-space/TLS/HTTP failures, two-process races, warm zero-network and prior-generation preservation. Load self-test is required but reports acquired-needs-reindex, not searchable. Ordinary builds and build.rs perform no model network access. Logs are bounded/redacted and carry exact hashes and stage outcomes.

title: Semantic readiness policy: explicit library, TTY, non-TTY and offline behavior
description: Define exhaustive requested-mode policy around typed model, producer-attestation, and readiness failures. Library APIs never prompt or network and return RecoveryPlan plus caller-authorized operations. Explicit semantic fails closed when no real compatible model/index exists. Explicit remote configuration is intent, so a present API key/endpoint/identity setting that is missing, malformed, unverifiable, or producer-unattested returns the typed failure or a durable non-indexable UnverifiedRemote state; detection must never convert it to None or silently continue as HashOnly/local fallback. Hybrid may return lexical results only with stable requested/realized mode, coverage, degradation code, zero admitted semantic scores, and exact recovery action. CLI interactive TTY may offer one consent prompt showing exact model/revision/license/source, byte budget, destination class, document count and estimated reindex cost. Non-TTY requires an explicit ensure/provision flag or emits stable machine-readable argv; offline fails immediately with local --from-file plan. QualityOnly MiniLM must not force the larger fast model. Environment variables cannot silently change library semantics.
design: RequestedMode and caller policy are explicit function inputs. Refactor auto-detection so discovery is SearchResult<Option<...>> or an equivalent typed outcome: absence of all remote intent is None, but invalid explicit intent is an error. VerifiedRemote, AssumedRemote, verified local, hash control, missing, and degraded are distinct exhaustive states. Hash remains a supported explicit test/control constructor but cannot satisfy semantic availability. AssumedRemote cannot index or query a verified persistent vector generation. Consent is scoped to the exact manifest revision, destination and byte budget and cannot silently authorize a different model or reindex. Human rendering and machine RecoveryPlan derive from the same typed decision.
acceptance_criteria: Exhaustive unit/integration matrix covers library explicit semantic/hybrid/hash-control, TTY accept/decline, non-TTY with and without explicit flag, offline, quality-only, fast-only, progressive, verified remote and assumed remote requests. Missing or incompatible real models never become semantic via hash. Explicit API key/endpoint plus missing identity, malformed JSON, invalid epoch, unattested provider, or typed UnverifiableRemoteSpace never becomes HashOnly or another backend; assertions cover selected stack, writes, logs, terminal event, code/category/exit 78/non-retry, and recovery. Hybrid lexical fallback preserves lexical results while admitting zero semantic scores and includes stable reason/coverage/recovery metadata. Consent binds exact revision/destination/bytes. Offline emits local plan and performs zero network. Environment cannot alter library semantics implicitly. Structured logs preserve first-party decision points without credentials, paths, query text, vectors, or raw provider errors.

title: Semantic recovery execution: blue-green reindex, validate, publish and retry once
description:
EXECUTE THE TYPED RECOVERY PLAN after exact model acquisition through migrated composite generation and the bd-9xuj typed per-tier umbrella. This must be a real production consumer of RecoveryPlan, not a schema, display-only message or parallel string state machine. Resolve one immutable readiness snapshot, derive the exact plan, acquire authorization once, and carry its identity/topology/coverage predicates through build, validation, expected-old publication, reconciliation, one exact original-command replay and typed terminal reporting.

Build a random inactive generation without mutating the selected closure. Persist independent fast and quality bound model/vector/input/producer/storage identities, retained FSVI owners, source checkpoint, ordered shard/docset coverage, Quill, optional ANN and metadata receipts. Validate compatible nonzero requested coverage plus real direct QualityOnly or FullProgressive behavior as requested, seal and publish one higher-sequence authority activation, then replay the exact command once preserving query, filters, limits, output and replayable flags. Non-replayable stdin is bounded or rejected. There are no split current pointers or raw vector shortcuts.

Failure after acknowledged publication creates a higher-sequence rollback activation to the retained prior generation; it never rewrites or deletes generations. CommitOutcomeUnknown is reconciled before retry. Concurrent acquisition, reindex, watch, replay and restart converge on one winner. Hash-built, legacy, partial or wrong-identity indexes remain NeedsReindex until a complete source rebuild; model installation alone never relabels them. The direct ctzo edge is removed as redundant because bd-9xuj now waits on ctzo and owner foundations.
design:
Consume xomn.3 composite authority, p6z6.2 policy and the bd-9xuj typed umbrella. Production orchestration accepts and executes the canonical RecoveryPlan object; presentation adapters render that same object. Generic cancel-correct capabilities expose source sequence, build intent, catch-up, coverage, validation, expected authority, reconciliation, rollback and one bounded replay and return immutable receipts plus typed unknown outcomes.

CASS owns its journal and UI orchestration downstream. This primitive supplies the real reference consumer and cannot close on unused RecoveryPlan types.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A machine-readable production call-site census proves RecoveryPlan is constructed, authorized, executed and reported by real recovery orchestration; zero consumers, display-only consumers, test-only types or duplicated string decision logic fail closure. Every state transition preserves the same plan identity and readiness snapshot or returns typed drift and recomputes before mutation.

2. Exact source, independent fast/quality identity and retained owner, requested topology, actual shard/docset coverage and real semantic validation precede one expected-old authority publication and one exact replay. QualityOnly validates direct quality retrieval; FullProgressive validates independent fast/quality retrieval plus union. No raw vector, split pointer, hash fallback, relabel, mutation or deletion exists.

3. Crash/cancel/permission/ENOSPC/sync/floor faults at every build, seal, validation, attempt, authority, external CAS, snapshot install and replay boundary leave exact old/new/pending classification. Unknown outcomes reconcile before retry. Post-publication failure creates monotone rollback; concurrent callers and watcher-versus-recovery have one winner.

4. Replay preserves query, filters, limit, output, requested topology and flags exactly; non-replayable stdin is rejected or explicitly bounded before mutation. Human, JSON and stream reporting derive from the executed plan and agree on bounded recovery argv and identity/topology/coverage facts.

5. A real no-mock reference consumer and downstream CASS receipt prove acquire -> rebuild -> validate -> publish -> replay -> restart -> drift -> recover with bounded redacted logs and exact hashes. Deterministic fault tests, strict remote/native gates, workspace check/test, warnings-denied lint, formatting, changed-file scanning and artifact validation pass.
