title: Semantic recovery doctor and no-mock fresh-process lifecycle E2E
description: Finish product integration and no-mock proof. Doctor classifies missing, partial, corrupt, unresolvable, incompatible, stale-index, zero-live, ANN/cache drift and orphan staging states and prints the exact safe next command. A committed fresh-process E2E begins with empty HOME/XDG/model/index roots; proves requested-mode policy; installs exact MiniLM under explicit consent; performs blue-green reindex; validates and publishes one composite generation; retries the original command once; restarts; detects drift; performs higher-sequence rollback; proves already-retained readers remain exact; then computes retention eligibility as a dry run while deleting zero files. Include noninteractive, offline, no-space, permission, TLS/HTTP, timeout, cancellation and concurrent-process cases. A network-denial sentinel proves warm/offline runs perform zero network. Evidence and logs are bounded, redacted, checksum-addressed and uploaded on every exit path. Destructive collection requires a separate user-authorized task and is out of scope.
design: This child owns product-facing diagnosis and the terminal executable lifecycle, not acquisition primitives. The driver must be committed, reproducible, fresh-root, offline-verifiable and capable of preserving artifacts on every pass/failure/timeout. Human and JSON doctor output share typed RecoveryPlan data.
acceptance_criteria: Doctor exhaustively identifies every listed state and exact safe recovery. Fresh-process no-mock E2E proves empty-cache request -> policy -> acquire -> reindex -> validate/publish -> one retry -> restart -> drift -> higher-sequence rollback -> retained old-reader readability -> retention eligibility dry-run with zero deletion. Noninteractive/offline/failure/concurrency matrices pass. Network denial proves warm/offline zero network. Artifacts include commands, environment, ELF/model/corpus/document-set/generation/authority hashes, CPU/wall/RSS, timeout/signal status and bounded redacted logs on pass and failure; upload/retention failure fails the lane. Destructive collection is separately authorized and out of scope.

title: CLI E2E envelope admission: validate RFC3339 UTC timestamps and config-hash shape
description: The CLI E2E provenance contract promises a canonical RFC3339 UTC timestamp and a typed configuration identity, but current load boundaries accept arbitrary timestamp strings and do not validate ManifestBody.config_hash. Repair both executable admission boundaries in place: E2eEnvelope.ts must use one canonical UTC parser, and ManifestBody.config_hash must be exactly sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits. Inventory and migrate every ManifestBody producer, including privacy and deluxe-TUI paths, so no producer emits labels, bare digests, or other prefixed forms. No compatibility shim is allowed.
design: Separate generic envelope validation from manifest-body validation. Route E2eEnvelope.ts through one core RFC3339 parser, require UTC Z, and require the canonical formatter to round-trip to the exact admitted string. Invoke that same parser at every envelope load boundary. In validate_manifest_envelope and every ManifestBody load path, validate config_hash as the typed sha256: plus exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits identity. Inventory all ManifestBody constructors and fixture or golden producers, migrate each to the canonical typed identity, and keep deterministic field-specific errors. Do not retain a second parser, alternate accepted spelling, or compatibility path.
acceptance_criteria: Accept E2eEnvelope.ts only when the shared parser recognizes a real RFC3339 calendar instant, the offset is UTC Z, and canonical formatting round-trips to the identical string. Reject invalid calendar dates, leap and range errors, unsupported or noncanonical fractions, numeric offsets including equivalent +00:00, lowercase z, missing components, whitespace, and trailing data. Accept ManifestBody.config_hash only as sha256: plus exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits; reject bare, uppercase, nonhex, short, long, empty, mislabeled, and trailing forms with deterministic errors naming ts or config_hash. Inventory and migrate every ManifestBody producer, explicitly including privacy and deluxe-TUI, with no compatibility shim. Add hostile unit tests at every load boundary, update affected fixtures and goldens deliberately, run every active CLI scenario plus deterministic replay and no-mock E2E, and pass fmt, workspace check, and Clippy with warnings denied.

title: CLI E2E bundle: bind replay.jsonl bytes into the artifact manifest
description: The fsfs CLI E2E bundle validates an in-memory replay vector, but ArtifactEntry omits replay.jsonl. A standalone manifest therefore cannot attest the replay stream that the public bundle contract names. Bind replay.jsonl into the existing manifest and artifacts-index derivation with its exact SHA-256 checksum and line_count, using the ArtifactEntry schema that actually exists. The admitted bytes must be the same bytes materialized and replayed.
design: Define one canonical replay.jsonl filename constant. Serialize the deterministic replay records exactly once with a pinned no-trailing-newline policy, then feed that single byte buffer into manifest and artifacts-index derivation before writing it to disk. Materialize replay.jsonl, read it back, and validate that the read bytes, exact SHA-256, and exact line_count match the sealed ArtifactEntry before golden comparison or replay admission. Do not add a byte-count field or a second serializer. Keep reconstruction driven from primary scenario, config, and exit-status inputs so all derived artifacts agree by construction.
acceptance_criteria: A valid nonempty bundle contains replay.jsonl under the canonical filename constant, with the exact SHA-256 of the materialized bytes and exact ArtifactEntry.line_count; canonical output has no trailing newline. Materialization followed by readback must reproduce the one serialized byte buffer exactly. Admission must fail closed for empty, missing, extra, reordered, duplicate, truncated, mutated, substituted, checksum-altered, line-count-altered, and leading or trailing newline variants, including a same-line-count payload substitution. Reconstruction from scenario, config, and exit status must produce the identical replay bytes and complete artifact set. Add hostile unit cases, run every active CLI scenario, deterministic replay twice, deliberate golden resealing, no-mock embedded-model E2E, fmt, workspace check, and Clippy with warnings denied.

title: Performance-run PID-tree booking, ownership, and quiescence receipt
description: Implement atomic booking and ownership for every benchmark and profile invocation. Bind worker, cpuset, storage and fixture slot, command, source, executable, root PID plus birth identity, and the complete descendant process tree. Prevent overlapping bookings. Cleanup revalidates identity and signals only the owned tree—never ambiguous pgrep matches or unrelated agents. Release only after the root and descendants terminate, queues drain, work reaches zero, terminal artifacts and bounded logs seal, and the reservation receipt is published. Queue and build time remain outside docs/s while submit, lease, start, timed-work, terminal, upload, and release timestamps remain auditable.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Booking is atomic and collision-safe across every declared exclusive resource and machine profile. 2. Fork, exec, reparenting, PID reuse, disconnect, stale lease, timeout, cancellation, and crash recovery are handled explicitly with birth-identity checks. 3. Cleanup cannot affect unrelated-process canaries and never uses ambiguous name matching as authority. 4. Completion requires sealed exit, descendant-terminal, queue-drained, pending-zero, artifact-upload, and release receipts; missing state yields NoDecision and a retry predicate. 5. Unit, deterministic fault, and hostile interleaving tests cover every lifecycle transition and ownership race. 6. Real-process-tree mock-free E2E tests exercise success, failure, cancellation, disconnect, collision, stale lease, PID reuse, recovery, and canary survival with detailed bounded structured ownership logs and redaction canaries.

title: MEDIUM: ratchet has no anti-rollback memory — replacing an activated gate's measured history with the bootstrap sentinel re-enters the first-measurement concession
description:
Found and personally re-verified by MossyPine (user-directed review sweep, 2026-07-31, mail #7365). CONFIRMED at origin/main perf_ratchet.rs:2665-2678.

DEFECT: GateTargetEvaluator::target() evaluates 'if self.observe_only { note } else if self.activated { block } else { quarantine }'. observe_only is passed as baseline_is_bootstrap (1140-1147, 1184-1191). Therefore whenever the committed baseline is the legal unmeasured bootstrap sentinel (is_explicit_bootstrap, 2398-2410), EVERY gate-target miss degrades to perf.ratchet.bootstrap_target_missed as a note - including when gate_activated == true.

FAILURE: an activated gate whose committed history object is replaced by the bootstrap sentinel (itself a legal artifact the ratchet accepts as baseline) evaluates a target-missing candidate as Allow rather than Block, establishing a fresh worse baseline and resetting the ratchet. All other checks (receipts, evidence, reruns, provenance) can be honestly satisfied by a genuinely slower candidate. This is the one identified path by which a MISS can pass promotion, which conflicts with the binding user rule that the flip requires wins across the board and that no MISS may authorize progress.

ROOT CAUSE: the legitimate 'first baseline may be established despite a MISS' concession was keyed off the baseline's identity alone, never intersected with gate activation state.

FIX (minimal): 'if self.observe_only && !self.activated { note } else if self.activated { block } else { quarantine }'. Regression test: activated gate + explicit bootstrap baseline + target miss must produce Block (perf.ratchet.gate_target_missed), and the existing non-activated bootstrap note behavior must be preserved. RED-proof the test against the current ordering before landing.
close_reason: Completed: activated bootstrap target misses now block, with red and green regression proof in a32403dc.

comments.author: MossyPine
comments.text:
CORRECTION by the reporter (MossyPine), mail #7385. My original framing ('activated gates can note-not-block a MISS' + a one-line ordering fix) is WITHDRAWN as WRONG. I implemented the ordering change and it turned the pre-existing test activated_bootstrap_records_target_miss_and_establishes_measured_baseline RED: that test deliberately asserts activated + explicit bootstrap baseline + missed target => Allow with bootstrap_target_missed RETAINED ('initial activation must retain the target MISS verdict'). That is the mechanism by which an activated-but-never-measured gate banks its first honest baseline — exactly how QG-2's honest MISS was recorded. Blocking there would make the first measurement of any activated gate unbankable. Source reverted byte-identical to origin/main (sha 4897bc87...); nothing pushed; reservation released; I am unassigned.

WHAT SURVIVES (downgraded HIGH -> MEDIUM-low): the concession is keyed on the baseline artifact's identity alone and the ratchet keeps no memory that a measured baseline ever existed. Residual risk is a BASELINE DOWNGRADE / ratchet rollback: replacing an activated gate's measured history object with the sentinel re-enters the concession and lets a slower candidate install a worse baseline, detectable only by reviewing .bench-history diffs. It is NOT a path by which a MISS passes as a win (the MISS is recorded, bootstrap_promotion is stamped, and the flip decision is user-owned). title: A/A null straddle veto is a latent gate defect in 3 layers — dormant only because our nulls are loose
description:
Fleet-wide primitive transfer from frankenlibc (2026-07-29). The A/A null 'CI must contain 1.0' clause couples the verdict to the NULL'S PRECISION in the wrong direction: a tighter null has a narrower CI, so it is MORE likely to exclude 1.0 and veto its own row regardless of effect size.

frankensearch CARRIES the defect in three layers:
1. crates/frankensearch-core/src/bench_support.rs:106-107 — PairedRatio::is_admissible_null() requires median_ci95_low <= 1.0 && 1.0 <= median_ci95_high. This is the SHARED helper.
2. ~20+ bench harnesses each with 'self.p5 <= 1.0 && 1.0 <= self.p95' (frankensearch-ops/*_ab.rs, fusion/negation_normalize_ab.rs, rerank/*, index/wal_append_dedup_ab.rs, quill/postings_decode_ab.rs, durability/durability_bench.rs). On failure they emit verdict BIASED_NULL_UNDECIDABLE, which vetoes the row outright.
3. crates/frankensearch-quill-gauntlet/src/perf_ratchet.rs::validate_null_control (origin/main:1699) — routes to state.quarantine('perf.ratchet.invalid_null_control'), making the row non-ratchet_admissible.

EVIDENCE THAT IT HAS NEVER FIRED (so per the fleet instruction the gate is NOT to be changed yet):
- BIASED_NULL_UNDECIDABLE and invalid_null_control appear ZERO times across all of docs/. 36 recorded verdicts: 17 CANDIDATE_FASTER, 12 INSIDE_NULL_FLOOR, 5 INCONCLUSIVE, 2 CANDIDATE_SLOWER.
- All 5 recorded A/A null CIs straddle 1.0 with room: half-widths 3.45%, 4.10%, 7.27%, 11.06%, 16.60%. frankenlibc's were 0.04%-0.5%, i.e. 7x-400x TIGHTER. We are in the opposite precision regime; a CI that wide straddles 1.0 almost unconditionally.
- Independent corroboration: the v2 six-class ledger audit found VOID-CV is ZERO and 93% of the 220 VOID reject rows were VOID-NONULL (nulls absent entirely), not straddle vetoes.
- All recorded null medians (0.9945, 1.0032, 1.0166, 0.9988) are within 2% of 1.0, so they would also pass the CORRECTED rule's clause 3.

WHY IT IS STILL A TRAP: the campaign is actively pursuing tighter nulls (more pairs, CPU pinning, governor=performance, interleaved paired sampling). Every one of those improvements shrinks the null half-width toward frankenlibc's regime and starts tripping this veto. The clause punishes exactly the measurement quality we are trying to buy.

NOTE bench_support.rs ALREADY implements the correct clause (null_half_width() plus a documented 'clears the admissible A/A median-CI floor by 2x' method), so the straddle test is a redundant EXTRA veto layered on top of a correct margin test. The fix is therefore mostly deletion plus adding clause 3 (null median within 2% of 1.0), keeping null CIs as reported telemetry.

DO NOT FIX BLIND. Required first: reproduce frankenlibc's protocol — same ELF, different core, lower load, confirm ratios reproduce within ~2.5%, and show a DIFFERENT subset of cases passes the null gate. A reproducible effect with a moving gate verdict is the proof. Integrity check: if correcting the gate turns losses into wins, distrust it (frankenlibc's 7 wordexp cases all became decidable and ALL 7 LOST, triple-replicated).

QualityOnly directly embeds and retrieves the retained quality tier. FullProgressive independently embeds and retrieves fast and quality tiers and deterministically unions candidates before fusion. The persisted fixture must include a relevant quality document outside the fast candidate pool and prove both direct quality retrieval and FullProgressive union find it after restart. design:
This is the persisted public facade layer between base retrieval and CI. Build through real facade builders and production create_v2 or admitted-owner paths; forbid test-only construction from satisfying positive call-site checks. Each backend-qualified run publishes exactly one immutable closure and reopens one retained snapshot. Use one frozen query manifest with an explicit out-of-fast-pool semantic target and evidence of lexical and semantic arm contribution.

Cache replacement is validate-then-swap. Coverage receipts bind exact fast and quality indexed/live docsets or ordered shards and are compared with source truth before search. It does not own CI workflow policy or CASS acquisition.

3. Real QualityOnly directly retrieves quality after restart. FullProgressive independently retrieves both tier owners and unions candidates. A persisted relevant document outside the fast candidate pool is returned by both modes; replacing quality retrieval with fast-only rescoring fails. comments.text:
UPSTREAM BASELINE NOW GREEN 2026-07-26 (TealIsland) — what this bead can build on, and what it explicitly still owns.

Per the 8w6e/q4rg split agreed with BrownCoyote (Agent Mail thread bd-8w6e), bd-8w6e now has a fully green 7-test binary you can consume rather than re-derive:
  test result: ok. 7 passed; 0 failed; finished in 728.09s (exit 0, 14:13 wall)
  semantic 13/16 vs hash 4/16; discordant semantic-only 9, hash-only 0
  frankensearch/tests/treasure_island_e2e.rs, features quill,native

AVAILABLE TO YOU: the immutable Treasure Island fixture (34 chapters -> 339 passages), the reviewed qrels (16 semantic + lexical/negative sets, now verified free of answer-vocabulary leakage), a real Quill lexical baseline, and a real MiniLM semantic-vs-hash baseline with predeclared bounds.

WHAT THE HYBRID LANE DOES AND DOES NOT PROVE. hybrid::rrf_fuses_both_arms_over_real_prose passes and is genuine evidence that both arms feed fusion over real prose: it asserts in_both_sources > 0, and separately that a proper-noun-free concept query yields hits with semantic_rank.is_some() && lexical_rank.is_none() -- so the semantic arm demonstrably contributes what BM25 alone cannot. It also asserts descending rrf_score ordering and that the true Ben Gunn chapter is in the fused set.

IT PROVES NOTHING THIS BEAD NEEDS BEYOND THAT. By design it uses rrf_fuse directly, NOT TwoTierSearcher, and InMemoryVectorIndex, NOT a persisted explicit-path FSVI. There is no commit/fsync, no drop, no fresh-process reopen, no identity/topology negative, no quality-only or progressive-phase coverage. Treat it as a fusion sanity lane, not a facade proof.

TWO THINGS THAT WILL BITE THIS BEAD, LEARNED THE HARD WAY:

(1) MODEL PROVISIONING IS NOT "tokenizer + weights". NativeEmbedder::load verifies the COMPLETE frozen artifact set; minilm_native_frankentorch() requires five files. This host had two and every real-model lane died inside the loader. resolve_model_dir now derives its required list from the frozen manifest (single source of truth) -- reuse that helper rather than writing a third list.

(2) RUN THE FULL BINARY, NOT FILTERED SUBSETS. Both fixture-hygiene tests had apparently never executed because every prior invocation filtered to `lexical` or `semantic`, and one of them was RED the whole time (a real qrels leak). Any per-module filter you adopt here will hide the same class of defect.

Also relevant: bd-irb1 does NOT prevent these lanes from running (measured; see my comment there) -- the quiet_logging containment is sufficient today. And per bd-tqhy all timing here is opt-level=0, so do not cite these numbers as performance evidence.

title: C0 RELEASE BLOCKER: machine-bound QG-1 applicability plans without shrinking the canonical 74-cell matrix
description:
Exact-source audit of protected commit a61456eca99c2a19394e37fe5d826094989982d6, whose QG sources are byte-identical at protected tip 5a0468a700a88afdf5baff85a0b1fcfd1cca76e3, found that QG-1 admission is impossible on every machine profile whose verified execution capacity is below 128. PerfMatrixSpec::complete() correctly defines one immutable global QG-1 universe, currently 72 bulk-indexing cells over four corpora, nine literal widths, and positions on/off, plus two tokenizer diagnostics. However, scripts/perf-runner.sh hardcodes QG-1 thread_budget=128; LocalPerfRunConfig and validate_bounded_inputs require the caller budget to equal the global matrix maximum; validate_execution_projection_binding requires the widest measured row, receipt budget, and global maximum all to equal 128; and the ratchet expects every global cell. This makes physical Threadripper and Apple evidence structurally inadmissible even when every cell the admitted machine can execute has been measured correctly.

Repair the contract without shrinking, rewriting, or conditionally redefining PerfMatrixSpec::complete(). Introduce a versioned, hash-sealed QG-1 applicability plan that projects every canonical cell for one registry-admitted execution profile as exactly one of Applicable { role: Required | Diagnostic } or NotApplicable { typed bounded reason bound to canonical class, execution profile, required width, and verified profile capacity }.

NotApplicable is applicability metadata, never an EvidenceRole, measured sample, terminal benchmark result, WIN, MISS, or substitute for a Required cell. Every applicable bulk-indexing cell in a promotion-eligible profile is Required. The two tokenize_only cells remain Applicable/Diagnostic. Diagnostic-only machine classes retain Applicable/Diagnostic bulk rows; they never obtain an empty-required-set Allow. A class that is unavailable or cannot establish its topology does not receive an all-NotApplicable plan: plan construction fails and the gate remains NoDecision.

Execution capacity is derived from the canonical machine-class registry and verified runtime topology, never from a caller-selected thread budget and never through min(requested, available) shrinking. Keep separate fields for execution_capacity and max_exercised_cell_width. A runtime with less capacity than the frozen profile rejects before spawning measurement; a profile may deliberately cap a larger host only when the registry defines and verifies that exact profile.

Required QG-1 profile semantics:
- trj physical-64: 56 Required bulk cells, 2 Diagnostic tokenizer cells, 16 NotApplicable width-96/128 cells; execution_capacity=64, max_exercised_cell_width=64.
- trj smt2-128: 72 Required bulk cells, 2 Diagnostic tokenizer cells, 0 NotApplicable; execution_capacity=128, max_exercised_cell_width=128. Lower-width rows must be rerun in the SMT profile and cannot be borrowed from physical-64.
- Apple scheduler-10 and scheduler-14: 32 Required bulk cells at literal widths 1/2/4/8, 2 Diagnostic tokenizer cells, 40 NotApplicable width-16+ cells; execution_capacity=10 or 14 and max_exercised_cell_width=8. Do not invent width-10 or width-14 QG-1 cells. These profiles describe worker-pool and scheduler envelopes and are not evidence of P-core, E-core, or residency attribution.
- Every promotion-eligible TRJ, M4, and eventually M5 profile must represent the exact QG-1 primary target cells bulk/medium/8/positions_on and bulk/xlarge/8/positions_on as Applicable/Required. Capacity below 8 cannot produce a promotion plan.
- M5 remains unavailable until its real fingerprint and execution profiles are frozen. Do not copy M4 capacities or turn M5 unavailability into per-cell NotApplicable entries.
- x86-vps-ovh remains diagnostic-only. Applicable cells are Diagnostic and wider cells are NotApplicable; the required-cell fold returns NoClaim, never Allow.

The plan hash binds the canonical global matrix schema/hash, normalized quill-perf-gates manifest hash, canonical machine-registry hash, gate, class, execution-profile ID, capacity semantics, execution capacity, maximum exercised width, primary target width, and every ordered projection including each canonical cell-contract hash, role, or typed NotApplicable reason. Threshold artifacts, evidence artifacts, runner receipts, artifact manifests, shard manifests, assembly receipts, and candidate/rerun ratchet inputs carry and exactly reconcile this plan hash.

Remove caller authority over QG-1 thread_budget from perf-runner.sh and quill_perf_finalize. The typed Rust registry resolves the profile and derives capacity. The runner derives the plan before spawning the benchmark, passes only controlled class, profile, capacity, and plan identity to the child, requires the benchmark to independently derive the identical plan, and verifies the same registry/execution identity again after exit. Topology drift is rejection/NoDecision, never a smaller regenerated plan.

Full decision execution selects exactly the Applicable cells. Arbitrary QUILL_PERF_FIXTURE filtering or smoke truncation may persist a partial diagnostic shard but forces NoClaim. A benchmark never executes or emits measured evidence for a NotApplicable cell.

Make completeness and ratchet logic plan-relative while preserving the full global projection: final threshold/evidence rows equal the exact Applicable set; every Required applicable row is present exactly once; no NotApplicable row has samples or satisfies completeness; missing, extra, duplicate, wrong-role, wrong-plan, wrong-class, wrong-profile, capacity/topology mismatch, or configured-width mismatch rejects; candidate and rerun require identical plan, class, profile, source, lockfile, executable, corpus, estimator, and run-window identities; profiles cannot substitute for or average with one another; evaluate_qg1 rejects before target evaluation unless both width-8 primary cells are Applicable/Required; and a per-profile WIN is not a fleet WIN. The release finalizer still requires every separately frozen required profile and every frozen performance target. No target waiver or AllowWithOptimizationDebt path is introduced.

For shard execution, every shard carries the same full plan and only a subset of Applicable terminal cells. Assembly accepts immutable terminal shards only when all plan and execution identities match, rejects overlaps and cross-profile substitution, and forms the exact union of Applicable cells in canonical order. NotApplicable entries come only from the common plan, never from shards. Assembly is input-order independent and retains every source runner-receipt hash and per-cell provenance under a separate offline assembly receipt; it must not manufacture one synthetic runner receipt. Crash/timeout shards remain durable nonclaim evidence with a concrete retry predicate, and an incomplete assembly cannot advance latest or activate QG-1.

Bump strict schemas and retain deny_unknown_fields. Existing pre-plan artifacts remain immutable historical or diagnostic inputs and are rejected for promotion with a precise schema/applicability reason; do not rewrite attempt history or reinterpret old evidence as current-schema evidence.

This bead owns QG-1 applicability semantics and its direct producer, runner, ratchet, and assembly wiring. It does not redefine estimator math, the generic terminal-status taxonomy owned by x4e4.15, live QG-1 measurement owned by x4e4.6, fleet class membership, or performance targets. It produces no performance claim. Semantic foundation receipt F is explicitly excluded and remains post-Batch4. QG-10 component receipts must keep flip_authorized=false; exact-SHA crate publication and library flip remain blocked on bd-3beo plus all required target WINs.
acceptance_criteria:
1. PerfMatrixSpec::complete() still expands QG-1 to the exact same canonical cells and has a checked-in golden canonical matrix hash. Activation toggles remain excluded only from perf_manifest_contract_sha256; every semantic manifest or matrix change changes the relevant hash.

2. A strict deny-unknown-fields PerfApplicabilityPlan represents every canonical cell exactly once. CellApplicability remains separate from EvidenceRole. NotApplicable uses a closed typed reason carrying class, profile, required-width, and capacity facts; artifact-provided free text cannot create applicability.

3. Plan construction is independently recomputed from the embedded canonical matrix, manifest, machine registry, and verified execution profile. An artifact cannot self-declare a cell NotApplicable. Unavailable classes, unknown profiles, malformed topology, capacity below a promotion target, or runtime capacity below the frozen profile fail plan/admission rather than shrinking it.

4. Golden plan tests prove: trj physical-64 = 56 Required + 2 Diagnostic + 16 NotApplicable; trj smt2-128 = 72 Required + 2 Diagnostic + 0 NotApplicable; Apple scheduler-10 = 32 Required + 2 Diagnostic + 40 NotApplicable with capacity 10 and max exercised 8; Apple scheduler-14 = 32 Required + 2 Diagnostic + 40 NotApplicable with capacity 14 and max exercised 8; scheduler-10 and scheduler-14 have different plan hashes despite identical applicable literal widths; x86 diagnostic profiles cannot fold to Allow; M5 cannot produce a plan before real registration; and both width-8 primary cells are Required in every promotion plan.

5. LocalPerfRunConfig and quill_perf_finalize no longer accept a caller-authoritative QG-1 thread budget. scripts/perf-runner.sh contains no QG-1=128 policy. Capacity is registry-derived, persisted in the receipt, and checked against pre-spawn and post-exit topology. No silent min or capacity downgrade is possible.

6. PerfExecutionProvenance distinguishes execution_capacity from max_exercised_cell_width. configured_engine_thread_widths equals the distinct literal widths of selected Applicable measured cells; on Apple scheduler-10/14 it is exactly [1,2,4,8], max exercised is 8, and capacity is 10/14. The ratchet no longer compares these fields to the global width 128.

7. Full benchmark selection is derived solely from the applicability plan. Decision runs execute every Applicable cell and no NotApplicable cell. Fixture or smoke filters persist as partial NoClaim shards. Attempting to select a NotApplicable cell, omit an applicable width-8 target, or label an applicable bulk row Diagnostic in a promotion profile rejects before timing.

8. PerfGateArtifact, PerfEvidenceArtifact, RunnerArtifactManifest, sealed runner receipt, and assembly receipt bind the same matrix, manifest, registry, class, profile, capacity, and plan hashes. Tampering any projection, reason, role, capacity, profile, cell spec, or hash fails verified reload.

9. Plan-relative validator and ratchet tests reject missing, extra, duplicate, measured-NotApplicable, wrong-role, omitted-plan-entry, fake-128-on-M4, runtime-topology shrink, configured-width mismatch, physical/SMT substitution, scheduler-10/14 substitution, M4/M5 substitution, candidate/rerun plan mismatch, and NotApplicable satisfying a Required target.

10. Deterministic assembly accepts any permutation of valid same-plan terminal shards and produces byte-identical canonical output. It rejects missing or overlapping cells; mixed source, lock, ELF, corpus, estimator, run-window, class, profile, or plan identity; a shard for a NotApplicable cell; and a fabricated aggregate runner receipt. Output retains every source shard and runner receipt hash. Partial or crashed assemblies are durable NoClaim and never advance latest.

11. Destination identity includes both canonical class and execution profile, for example QG-1.m4-macos.scheduler-10.latest.json versus QG-1.m4-macos.scheduler-14.latest.json. Destination derivation is centralized and ratchet-verified; class-only filenames cannot collide or promote.

12. Existing pre-plan history is not rewritten. Current promotion loading rejects it precisely. No C0 test, artifact, documentation edit, or closeout claims that Quill meets QG-1, authorizes the flip, or weakens a target.

13. Comprehensive proof includes plan/hash/schema/round-trip and hostile mutation unit suites; registry admission and topology mutation suites; benchmark selection and role suites; local runner/finalizer pre-spawn failure suites; evidence/ratchet completeness and candidate-rerun suites; deterministic shard assembly suites; a real-binary no-mock contract E2E script with bounded structured JSONL logging; scheduled live smoke execution on registered TRJ physical/SMT and Apple scheduler-10/14 before QG-1 activation; cargo fmt --check; cargo check --workspace --all-targets; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; targeted and workspace tests through RCH where applicable; and UBS over every changed Rust, TOML, and shell file.

14. Structured logs include run ID/window, matrix/manifest/registry/plan hashes, class/profile, capacity/max-exercised widths, Applicable/Required/Diagnostic/NotApplicable counts, every cell terminal state, shard and receipt hashes, assembly set differences, and bounded retry predicates, while excluding document/query text and secrets.

15. QG-10 machine output remains flip_authorized=false until bd-3beo and exact-source-SHA all-required-target WIN authorization pass. M5 unavailability never fabricates a plan or WIN; semantic F remains excluded for post-Batch4.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 5 (no invalid artifact can activate or become latest) IS MET AT THE DECISION POINT, proven by name under flock /data/tmp/frankensearch-build.lock:
  perf_ratchet::tests::evidence_measured_at_a_quarantined_revision_blocks_promotion ... ok
  perf_ratchet::tests::evidence_from_an_unquarantined_revision_is_not_blocked_by_the_quarantine_screen ... ok
  perf_ratchet::tests::the_embedded_quarantine_register_covers_every_named_sweep_revision ... ok
  perf_evidence::tests -- 64 passed, 0 failed (60 pre-existing unaffected, 4 new green by name)
  cargo clippy --no-deps -p frankensearch-quill-gauntlet --lib --all-features -- -D warnings => exit 0
  cargo fmt --check => clean; pre-commit ledger gate green on every commit (selfcheck 52/52, gatecheck 9/9, mergecheck 3/3, leakcheck 2/2).

THREE DESIGN DECISIONS A REVIEWER SHOULD CHECK RATHER THAN ASSUME.
 (1) OUT OF BAND, not admission_no_claim. The artifact already carries an in-band non-admissibility field and using it was the obvious move -- but setting it on a historical artifact means REWRITING SEALED, PUBLISHED EVIDENCE, exactly the deletion-and-reinterpretation this bead forbids. Keying the quarantine on immutable git_revision leaves every historical byte identical and still stops the sweep supporting claims.
 (2) fatal, NOT quarantine, despite the name matching. PerfGateDecision documents Quarantine as "noisy, incomplete, incompatible, or still provisional" -- a state a rerun can leave. A structurally invalid sweep never leaves it; re-measuring reproduces the same invalid shape, so Quarantine would invite a retry that cannot succeed. fatal yields Block and matches this file's convention (fatal = contract violations, 72 uses; block = measurement outcomes).
 (3) THE REFUSAL IS A DISTINCT ERROR VARIANT from every broken-artifact case, because these bytes verify, the seal matches, and the summaries recompute. Integrity is not admissibility. Reporting it as corruption would invite an operator to "fix" it by re-measuring the same invalid shape.

FAIL-CLOSED THROUGHOUT: a MISSING register is empty (a checkout with nothing quarantined is legitimate) but a present-and-malformed one is an ERROR, so a corrupted file can never read as "nothing is quarantined". Prefixes under 7 hex characters are rejected at parse time rather than over-matching unrelated revisions at screen time. The register is embedded via include_str! so it travels with the binary -- a refusal that can be sidestepped by pointing the tool at another .bench-history directory is not a refusal.

THE DISCRIMINATOR TEST IS THE ONE THAT KEEPS THIS HONEST. Asserting only that a quarantined revision blocks would still pass if the screen degenerated into refusing EVERYTHING, which would take the whole ratchet offline while looking like coverage. The unquarantined-revision test is what distinguishes a working screen from a broken one, and the same reasoning drove the planted negative in f2cd18de, which asserts BOTH that the naive loader admits the intact-but-invalid artifact and that the admissible loader refuses it.

Resolve the repository root and every ancestor as descriptor-admitted directories. Resolve only leaf source and sentinel objects as regular files. Use no-follow bounded reads; cap path, argv, file, selector, and diagnostic sizes; reject symlinks, hostile nodes, path escape, topology drift, duplicate selectors, invalid UTF-8, case-folded aliases, and pre/post identity changes. title: QG-6 H1: decode phrase positions once per candidate posting
description: Profile-led H1 lever for the dominant phrase-query gap. The current sealed posting cursor clones its positions reader to decode the current candidate run for phrase matching, then the owned reader decodes that same run again only to advance. Add a cursor-local consumed-run state and a mutable decode-once path so the phrase scorer reads positions from the owned cursor and subsequent advance skips only that already-consumed run. Preserve the immutable position-handle contract for non-phrase callers, Delta encoding behavior, typed codec failures, fuel and cancellation checkpoints, deterministic ranking, and every supported phrase/slop/alternative behavior. This is a narrow self-speedup candidate, not QG activation evidence. Any performance verdict requires same-binary old/new Quill evidence, cache-miss attestation, parity, and the genuine Tantivy incumbent in the same invocation where campaign rules require it.
design: Keep the public Argus PostingCursor contract unchanged. Add a crate-private transactional decode_current_positions_into operation to Quiver PositionCursor. title: QG-6 R1 residual: current-source diagnostic TERMDICT profile
description:
DIAGNOSTIC NOCLAIM PROFILE. Begin only after bd-qg6-r1-train-disposition-446ne has a verified AcceptedForDiagnosticProfile receipt; RejectedAtConformance terminates as NoProfileBecauseRejected without timing. The causal timing lineage is frozen: OldA and OldB are independently constructed instances of exact control 40238f9cd87b756c53b1ce4cddf45ee976969089; CurrentA and CurrentB are independent instances of the reviewed train tip whose lever begins at 25ab76e3036a71648319876235269b47854f2a29; TantivyA and TantivyB are independent instances of the genuine pinned incumbent with a runtime oracle-revision assertion. c08b8fc2 and 3b0ead9b are historical provenance/equivalence references only and may not be causal arms.

The untouched timing ELF must contain all six physical arms in one invocation, with no shared Arc, cache, path, backing, or mutable fixture between instances. Every physical observation is stored and timed exactly once. A complete estimable meta-block is six Williams-design sweeps of six calls each, using base row [0,1,5,2,4,3] and cyclic role mapping (base[col] + row) mod 6. A meta-block therefore has exactly 36 unique leaves; no prefix, truncated schedule, or repeated leaf is admissible. Role mapping may be randomized once per meta-block and row order may be randomized, but columns may not be arbitrarily permuted. Admission proves each role occupies every ordinal once, each ordered role pair is before/after 3/3, every directed immediate predecessor occurs once, leaf intervals do not overlap, latency arithmetic is valid, and inter-sweep boundary identities/effects satisfy a predeclared bound or symmetric excluded-boundary probe.

Each leaf records stratum, query class and local query ID, meta-block, sweep/design row/ordinal/role, independent-instance receipt hash, monotonic start/end/latency, work units, result-envelope digest, cache disposition, generation, backing hash, source/Cargo.lock/timing-ELF/fixture/query-contract/host provenance, and typed outcome. Meta-block role-mean log latency yields a five-dimensional contrast vector: OldB-OldA, CurrentB-CurrentA, TantivyB-TantivyA, mean(Current)-mean(Old), and mean(Current)-mean(Tantivy). A single joint hierarchical bootstrap resamples the same query/meta-block draws for all contrasts. The three A/A nulls must each pass predeclared center, CI-width, log-MAD, order-effect, and drift bounds; any null failure is terminal NoDecision. Current/Old is a maintenance self-speedup only. Current/Tantivy is Diagnostic and NoClaim here. Raw leaves are retained for absolute p50/p95/p99; p99 is reported only when the predeclared minimum leaf count is met.

Steady ranked-cache-miss queries use a fixed-length, semantics-preserving raw-query nonce (space/tab encoding) that makes exact cache keys unique while tests prove identical parsed AST, result envelope, work/fuel/cancellation behavior, and constant raw length. Do not disable the cache via a controller in the timing path. Segment topology is exact, not nominal: configure fanout above the requested segment count, assert 1, at least 20, and 64 sealed segments, and use Tantivy NoMergePolicy with matching assertions. First-touch, steady ranked-cache-miss, and generation-rebind are separate strata and artifacts. First-touch creates a fresh matched six-arm set for every sweep. Rebind applies the same generation mutation/delete schedule and proves post-operation parity and generation/backing witnesses before timing.

Mechanism profiling is physically separate from timing. The exact 40238f9c control, reviewed current tip, and Tantivy timing arms remain untouched. Counters, allocation/copy/RSS, CPU frames, snapshot document-frequency calls, global-DF probes, TERMDICT borrowed views/validation/reuse, reader fanout, fuel/work, and cancellation are collected only by profile sidecar ELFs. If source instrumentation is required because the exact control lacks the feature, use control and current diagnostic descendants carrying an identical instrumentation patch; bind parent SHAs, patch IDs, feature sets, and sidecar ELF hashes. Profiled-ELF latency is never QG evidence. The timing crate must fail compilation if profile instrumentation is enabled, cargo feature proof must show no activation, symbol inspection must find no profile symbols in the timing ELF, and normalized hot-function object/disassembly bytes must match the uninstrumented source.

Run current-source cards first on TRJ physical-64 and Apple Silicon M4 scheduler-10 at 100K documents for 1, at least 20, and 64 exact segment layouts, then at 1M when the 100K contract is stable. Cover identifier, short keyword, natural language, phrase, boolean, first-touch, steady miss, and rebind. Artifacts use the unique QG-6-R1-residual-* stem and may not overwrite, promote, or masquerade as formal QG-6 gate artifacts. Terminal disposition is exactly NoProfileBecauseRejected, NoDecision with one fixed retry predicate, NoR2, or R2Required. R2Required needs two independent signals attributing at least 0.1 percent and material Amdahl headroom to the same checkpointed_snapshot_doc_freq or dictionary family, and must create separate one-lever R2 plus post-R2 profile beads as blockers of gwd4.
design:
PROFILE SIDECAR DESIGN. Add an independent Quill profile-internals feature, never aliased to bench-internals, conformance-internals, pruning-conformance, or the gauntlet perf-harness feature. Feature-gated APIs return an invocation-bound receipt with the ordinary outcome even on cancellation or fuel exhaustion. The receipt records snapshot epoch, keeper generation, sealed/delta segment counts; ranked cache Unsupported, NotChecked, Hit, Miss, or Disabled; snapshot document-frequency calls; global-DF sealed and delta probes; TERMDICT borrowed views; fanout eligibility and selected Serial or Rayon execution; sealed and delta lowerings; work upper bound and shipping fuel-metering state; attempted, admitted, and refused segment, dictionary-block, posting-block, and position-document units; checkpoint cancellation observations; typed Completed, Cancelled, FuelExhausted, or OtherError outcome; and overflow. Overflow saturates, sets counter_overflowed, and rejects evidence.

Use an invocation-local Arc profile session with relaxed increments and acquire loads only after Rayon joins. Cache and execution states are single-assignment atomics that reject conflicting observations. No globals and no reset API. Do not use pruning traces and do not force fuel metering because both alter shipping execution. Recovered-segment snapshots record segment ID, Owned or Mapped backing, source and TERMDICT bytes, FullValidation or MetadataReuse, validation/view/reuse counts, cumulative validation input bytes, and the existing honest payload estimate. Transition receipts expose same segment, reader Arc identity, metadata Arc identity, schema/file length/file hash/live TERMDICT binding equality, and payload-copy classification ProvenZeroSharedArc or NotObserved; never infer allocation or copy bytes from payload length.

Minimum red-test matrix: all Williams-design invariants; a cyclic-Latin negative control; truncated, forged, duplicate, overlapped, or arithmetically inconsistent schedules reject; 36 leaves produce exactly one contrast vector with no duplicated physical sample; synthetic carryover cancels under the Williams estimator; known ln(0.8) effect is recovered; each individual A/A bias forces NoDecision; duplicate IDs and shared instance/backing/path receipts reject; source, incumbent revision, fixture, executable, and provenance mismatches reject; joint bootstrap is deterministic and retains covariance under unequal query-group counts; raw tail samples survive aggregation; label swaps invert the expected contrast; first-touch reuse, warm cache hits, rebind generation skew, work mismatch, and cross-stratum mixing reject; recomputation verifies every admitted artifact.

Counter-specific tests: for S sealed segments and one exact term, first miss reports S snapshot-DF calls, S squared global sealed probes, S squared plus S TERMDICT views, S sealed lowerings, and identical results. Repeat hit reports zero query work. Disabled-cache fixture proceeds without cancellation. Below-threshold fragmentation reports Serial; at least eight segments reports Rayon and exactly S lowerings. Unmetered high-budget queries still report profile work. Low budget returns typed fuel exhaustion plus attempted/refused counts. Deterministic QueryCollection cancellation reports its exact admitted prefix. Control rebind shares reader backing but has a different metadata Arc, FullValidation, and nonzero validation bytes; R1 shares reader and metadata Arc, reports MetadataReuse, and has zero successor validation bytes; both prove zero backing-payload copy. Fresh, mismatched, mapped, cold-reopen, and concurrent-isolation cases are explicit. RED switches remove the reuse handoff, one DF event, or one TERMDICT-view event and must fail the corresponding algebra/identity assertion.

Timing-exclusion proof: profile types are unavailable without the feature; cargo tree proves perf-harness does not activate it; the timing crate has compile_error when profile instrumentation is active; nm finds no profile symbols; normalized object/disassembly bytes match for cache lookup, DF scan, checkpoint admission, fanout, TERMDICT view, and rebind; ordinary A/A is only the final sanity check.
acceptance_criteria:
Predecessor is closed with a verified AcceptedForDiagnosticProfile receipt before any build or timing; otherwise close NoProfileBecauseRejected. Exact control 40238f9c, reviewed current tip, and genuine pinned Tantivy are provenance-bound, and OldA, OldB, CurrentA, CurrentB, TantivyA, and TantivyB are six independently constructed physical instances. Historical c08b8fc2 and 3b0ead9b never enter causal contrasts. Every timed leaf is observed and stored once.

A validator admits only complete 36-leaf Williams meta-blocks and proves role-per-ordinal balance, ordered-pair 3/3 balance, directed immediate-predecessor balance, unique leaf IDs, nonoverlap, correct latency arithmetic, bounded boundary effect, stable instance receipts, and identical result, fuel, cancellation, lifecycle, generation, backing, fixture, executable, query-contract, and source provenance. Raw JSONL carries the full leaf schema and is bounded to 10000 lines and 8 MiB per fresh process, with phase, typed status/reason, hashes, timeout, and artifact references but no raw query, document, term, vector, filesystem path, credential, or secret.

The estimator forms exactly one five-contrast vector per query/meta-block and runs one joint hierarchical bootstrap. All three A/A nulls pass fixed center, CI-width, log-MAD, order-effect, and drift limits; any failure is NoDecision. Absolute p50/p95/p99 come from raw leaves, and p99 is typed insufficient_samples below its frozen minimum. Current/Old is labeled SELF-SPEEDUP maintenance; Current/Tantivy is labeled Diagnostic NoClaim.

Fixed-length space/tab nonces prove unique cache keys plus constant raw length and identical parse tree, result envelope, work, fuel, and cancellation. Exact segment counts are asserted for both engines. First-touch uses fresh six-arm instances for every sweep; steady queries prove ranked-cache miss; rebind uses an identical mutation/delete schedule and validates post-operation generation and backing witnesses. Cross-stratum sample mixing is rejected.

Timing and profiling use different ELFs. Exact causal timing sources are uninstrumented. Control/current profile descendants carry patch-identical instrumentation with parent SHA, instrumentation patch ID, features, and profile ELF hashes. Profile counters are invocation-local and overflow-rejecting. Compile-fail, cargo-tree, compile_error, symbol, and normalized object/disassembly checks prove that the timing ELF contains no profile instrumentation. No profiled-ELF latency enters timing evidence.

TRJ physical-64 and Apple Silicon M4 scheduler-10 each produce 100K-document cards for exact 1, at least 20, and 64 segment layouts over identifier, short keyword, natural language, phrase, boolean, first-touch, steady miss, and rebind; 1M follows only after all 100K validators are stable. Cards bind host, machine class, scheduler, affinity, SMT, NUMA, heap, actual thread count, source, Cargo.lock, all ELF hashes, corpus, query contract, snapshot, generation, and backing, and retain frames, allocation/copy/RSS, counter receipts, CPU-equivalent, and raw tails.

Tests include the complete schedule/negative-control/estimator/provenance/cache/topology/stratum matrix and the S, S-squared, S-squared-plus-S counter algebra, cache hit/miss/disabled, Serial/Rayon, unmetered/fuel/cancel, control-versus-R1 rebind, fresh/mapped/cold reopen, concurrent isolation, and explicit RED switches. Verification includes formatting, focused default/full-feature Quill and gauntlet tests, strict remote workspace check, strict remote workspace Clippy with warnings denied, relevant integration tests, diff review, and literal changed-file UBS disposition. UBS exit greater than zero remains HOLD and may not be described as green.

Artifacts use only QG-6-R1-residual-* names and cannot activate or overwrite a formal QG artifact. Terminal state is exactly NoProfileBecauseRejected, NoDecision with one concrete retry predicate, NoR2, or R2Required. R2Required needs two independent attributions of at least 0.1 percent plus material Amdahl headroom to the same eligible family, creates separate one-lever R2 and post-R2 profile beads, and adds both as blockers of gwd4. Nothing in this bead grants QG activation, KEEP, latest promotion, release, default flip, or public performance authority.

title: Implement quantization ladder (f32/f16/int8/int4) with formal quality bounds
description:
Implement a quantization ladder (f32/f16/int8/int4) with formal quality-memory tradeoff characterization for vector indices. Enables extreme memory savings for large-scale deployments.

OPTIMIZATION RATIONALE:

Current FSVI format supports f32 and f16. For large indices (100K+ docs), memory is the bottleneck:
- 100K docs x 384 dims x f32 = 147 MB
- 100K docs x 384 dims x f16 = 73 MB   (current default)
- 100K docs x 384 dims x int8 = 37 MB   (THIS BEAD)
- 100K docs x 384 dims x int4 = 18 MB   (THIS BEAD)

Opportunity Matrix:
| Quantization | Memory | Quality Loss | Effort | Score (Impact x Conf / Effort) |
|-------------|--------|-------------|--------|-------------------------------|
| int8 scalar | 4x vs f32 | ~1-2%  | 2      | 10.0                          |
| int4 packed | 8x vs f32 | ~3-5%  | 4      | 5.0                           |

IMPLEMENTATION:

1. Scalar Quantization (int8):
   - Per-dimension min/max computed during indexing
   - Quantize: q = round((x - min) / (max - min) * 255)
   - Dequantize: x' = q / 255 * (max - min) + min
   - Store quantization parameters in FSVI header (2 floats per dimension)
   - SIMD dot product on int8: use i16 multiply-accumulate via wide crate

pub struct ScalarQuantizer {
    mins: Vec<f32>,     // Per-dimension minimum
    scales: Vec<f32>,   // Per-dimension (max - min) / 255
}

impl ScalarQuantizer {
    pub fn fit(vectors: &[Vec<f32>]) -> Self;
    pub fn quantize(&self, vector: &[f32]) -> Vec<u8>;
    pub fn dot_product_quantized(&self, stored: &[u8], query: &[f32]) -> f32;
}

2. Product Quantization (optional, for int4-equivalent compression):
   - Split 384-dim vector into 48 sub-vectors of 8 dims each
   - K-means cluster each sub-space into 256 centroids
   - Store 1 byte per sub-vector (centroid index)
   - Asymmetric distance computation (ADC): query in full precision, database quantized
   - Compression: 384 dims -> 48 bytes (8x vs f32, 4x vs f16)

3. FSVI Format Extension:
   - quantization field in header: 0=f32, 1=f16, 2=int8, 3=int4/PQ
   - For int8: append quantization parameters after header (mins + scales)
   - For PQ: append codebook after header

4. Quality Characterization (Alien-Artifact):
   - For each quantization level, compute NDCG@10 on the test fixture corpus
   - Provide formal bounds on maximum quality loss:
     For int8: |cos_sim(q, x) - cos_sim(q, x')| <= epsilon
     where epsilon = max_dim(scale_i / 255) * sqrt(d) / ||q|| / ||x||
   - This is a PROVABLE bound on the worst-case quality degradation

5. Automatic Selection:
   pub fn recommended_quantization(index_size: usize, available_memory: usize) -> Quantization {
       let f16_size = index_size * dimension * 2;
       let int8_size = index_size * dimension;
       if f16_size <= available_memory { Quantization::F16 }
       else if int8_size <= available_memory { Quantization::Int8 }
       else { Quantization::PQ }
   }

File: frankensearch-index/src/quantization.rs
Dependencies: bd-3un.13 (FSVI format), bd-3un.14 (SIMD dot product)

Isomorphism: Rankings may change slightly due to quantization error. Provide formal epsilon bounds and NDCG regression test: NDCG@10(int8) >= 0.95 * NDCG@10(f16) on test corpus.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Quantization ladder support is implemented and versioned in index metadata/format for `f32`, `f16`, `int8`, and PQ/int4-equivalent mode, with backward-compatible read behavior for older indices.
2. Int8 quantization path includes fit/quantize/dequantize and quantized dot-product scoring with numerically validated tolerance against full-precision reference.
3. Quality guardrails are enforced with benchmark corpus checks (for example NDCG/Recall thresholds) and formalized error-bound documentation tied to implemented math.
4. Runtime selection policy chooses quantization level by memory budget/index size and is covered by deterministic unit tests.
5. Comprehensive unit, integration, and benchmark coverage includes edge cases (zero/constant vectors, tiny dims, malformed parameters), with detailed performance and quality logs suitable for CI regression gating.

     where epsilon = max_dim(scale_i / 255) * sqrt(d) / ||q|| / ||x||
   - This is a PROVABLE bound on the worst-case quality degradation

5. Automatic Selection:
   pub fn recommended_quantization(index_size: usize, available_memory: usize) -> Quantization {
       let f16_size = index_size * dimension * 2;
       let int8_size = index_size * dimension;
       if f16_size <= available_memory { Quantization::F16 }
       else if int8_size <= available_memory { Quantization::Int8 }
       else { Quantization::PQ }
   }

File: frankensearch-index/src/quantization.rs
Dependencies: bd-3un.13 (FSVI format), bd-3un.14 (SIMD dot product)

Isomorphism: Rankings may change slightly due to quantization error. Provide formal epsilon bounds and NDCG regression test: NDCG@10(int8) >= 0.95 * NDCG@10(f16) on test corpus.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
REVIEW FIX — Quality bound formula correction, naming, and missing deps:

1. QUALITY BOUND FORMULA CORRECTION: The body states:
   |cos_sim(q, x) - cos_sim(q, x')| <= epsilon
   where epsilon = max_dim(scale_i / 255) * sqrt(d) / ||q|| / ||x||

   This is INCORRECT. The correct bound:
   - Quantization error per dimension: |x_i - x'_i| <= scale_i / 255
   - Vector error: ||x - x'|| <= sqrt(sum((scale_i/255)²))
   - Dot product error: |dot(q, x) - dot(q, x')| <= ||q|| * ||x - x'||
   - Cosine similarity error:
     |cos_sim(q, x) - cos_sim(q, x')| <= ||x - x'|| / ||x|| ≈ sqrt(sum((scale_i/255)²)) / ||x||

   For unit-normalized vectors (||x|| = 1, typical for embeddings):
     epsilon ≈ sqrt(sum((scale_i/255)²))

   For uniform scale across dimensions (scale = max - min):
     epsilon ≈ (scale / 255) * sqrt(d)

   For 384-dim unit vectors with typical scale ~2: epsilon ≈ (2/255) * sqrt(384) ≈ 0.154
   This means int8 quantization introduces at most ~15% cosine similarity error — verifiable empirically.

2. NAMING FIX: "int4-equivalent" for Product Quantization is MISLEADING. PQ stores 1 byte per sub-vector (centroid index), not 4-bit integers. Rename:

   pub enum QuantizationLevel {
       F32,                        // Full precision (4 bytes/dim)
       F16,                        // Half precision (2 bytes/dim) — current default
       Int8 { scale: f32, zero: f32 },  // Scalar quantization (1 byte/dim)
       ProductQuantization {       // PQ: sub-vector centroid indices
           n_subvectors: usize,    // Default: 48 (for 384-dim)
           n_centroids: usize,     // Default: 256 (1 byte per index)
       },
   }

3. WIDE CRATE INT SIMD: The `wide` crate supports f32x8 and i32x8 but NOT i16 or i8 multiply-accumulate. For int8 dot product with accumulation into i32:
   - Option A: Use i32x8 from `wide` (widen i8 to i32, then multiply-accumulate) — safe, portable
   - Option B: Use Rust nightly std::simd for native i8 operations — nightly-only
   - DECISION: Use Option A (i32x8 widening) for V1. It's 4x slower than native i8 SIMD but safe and portable. Profile before optimizing.

4. MISSING DEPENDENCIES — Add:
   - bd-3un.38 (test corpus for NDCG evaluation)
   - bd-3un.5 (VectorHit result types)
   - bd-3un.2 (SearchError for error handling)

5. DEPENDENCY TYPE FIX: bd-3un should be parent-child, not blocks.

6. TEST REQUIREMENTS:
   - Int8 round-trip: quantize f32 → int8 → dequantize, max error within bound
   - NDCG regression: NDCG@10(int8) >= 0.95 * NDCG@10(f16) on test corpus
   - PQ round-trip: train centroids, quantize, dequantize, max error within expected range
   - FSVI format: write/read int8 quantized index (format version check)
   - Auto-selection: given memory budget, correct quantization level chosen
   - Edge cases: zero vectors, constant vectors, single-dimension vectors
   - Int8 dot product: matches f32 reference within quantization tolerance
   - Memory savings: verify 4x reduction for int8 vs f32, 2x vs f16

title: Qualified capability-root admission for Linux and Apple Silicon macOS
description:
Build the safe platform substrate required before generation-root source work. APIs accept an explicit trusted directory capability or unambiguous route and walk every component descriptor-relatively with NOFOLLOW; they reject empty, dot, dot-dot, prefix, NUL, symlink, non-directory ancestor, nested mount, hardlink alias, special file, path replacement, and root/LOCK/AUTHORITY descriptor mismatch. Every admitted file is a same-device single-link regular file with expected owner/mode, bounded exact read, retained descriptor plus Arc-owned bytes, and stable dev/inode/mode/nlink/uid/gid/size/mtime/ctime witnesses before and after validation. Atime alone is excluded on macOS and is never restored.

Qualify Linux local filesystems with explicit file and directory durability barriers. Qualify Apple Silicon macOS only on descriptor-confirmed local writable APFS with known ownership semantics, ACL-aware owner-private root validation, safe rustix component opens/flock/stat/fstatfs, and successful retained-fd regular-file plus directory F_FULLFSYNC capability receipts. Rustix has no safe ACL API, so admission must consume an audited safe ACL provider or an explicit caller-issued TrustedPrivateRoot capability; no local unsafe code or mode-bit-only privacy claim is allowed. Do not silently downgrade Apple durability to fsync. Unsupported/network/read-only/unknown-permissions filesystems and every unqualified target return typed UnsupportedFilesystem or DurabilityUnavailable before shared mutation. x86_64 macOS, Windows, and other targets compile typed zero-I/O unsupported stubs until their separate native beads are green.

TESTS: symlink or replacement at every ancestor/final component; decoy trees unchanged; wrong owner/mode/granting ACL; hardlink/nlink races; FIFO/device/directory; same-size rewrite; grow/shrink; inode/path/root swaps; cross-device subtree; atime-only advancement; Apple Silicon APFS case-sensitive/case-insensitive, internal/external capability probes, F_FULLFSYNC success/failure; Linux filesystem matrix; unsupported/network mounts; and bounded fault injection for every open/read/sync boundary. Physical M4 receipts identify exact OS/filesystem/media/binary and never generalize beyond observed capability; Intel Mac qualification is bd-macos-x86-generation-root-qualification-bb39t and does not block arm64 delivery. Workspace check/clippy/fmt, focused platform tests, UBS, strict remote Linux, and physical M4 receipts are required. Candidate 0daac945 is evidence only and must not be cherry-picked: it follows ancestor symlinks, replaces canonical vectors, deletes WAL, and lacks this lease/authority contract.

Because rustix does not expose macOS ACL inspection, require an audited safe ACL provider or caller-established trusted private-root capability and fail closed otherwise. Qualification is per architecture and filesystem capability: this P0 closes Linux plus Apple Silicon; x86_64 macOS is independently gated so absent hardware cannot stall the primary Apple target.

title: quill-duel: query AST canonicalization/dedup (score-neutral scope only)
description: From the duel's blind-spot probe (Gemini) with an ORCHESTRATOR-ADDED CORRECTNESS CAVEAT neither wizard caught. Agents paste redundant queries (repeated terms, duplicated clauses); the engine currently would probe/decode/score duplicates repeatedly. Add a canonicalization pass between parse (e4.1/e4.2) and planning: sort boolean children by (field, term) for deterministic plans, deduplicate clauses, cap adversarial repetition. THE CAVEAT: naive dedup CHANGES SCORES — in a BM25 sum-union, (A OR A) scores A twice, and tantivy/Lucene do NOT dedup, so deduping Should-clauses breaks oracle conformance on duplicate-term queries. SCOPE: (1) always-safe: dedup MustNot clauses (exclusion is idempotent), dedup identical Must FILTER clauses (match-only, no score), dedup within phrase-candidate prefilters, cap glob expansion duplicates; (2) score-affecting dedup (Should/scoring-Must): EITHER off by default with the oracle-matching behavior pinned by duplicate-term fixtures, OR enabled post-flip behind config with a Divergence Register entry (class QueryCanonicalization, consumer impact documented). Plan-cost savings (single dict probe per unique term, shared cursors) accrue even without score-affecting dedup via cursor sharing: duplicate scoring clauses can SHARE one cursor + multiply the contribution — score-identical AND cheap (implement this form first; it needs no divergence entry). Tests: duplicate-term conformance fixtures vs oracle; plan-cost assertions (dict probes == unique terms); deterministic plan ordering. Deps: e4.1, e4.3.
close_reason: Two-layer contract landed (commit 26dbfa8). (1) Parse layer: only idempotent occurrences merge (MustNot + negation wrappers); scoring clauses never merged — oracle sum-union scores (A OR A) twice, tantivy/Lucene do not dedup (peer parser work, completed/tested here). (2) Post-parse canonicalize_query: deterministic Boolean child ordering by (occur, structural key), exact-duplicate MustNot removal, exact-duplicate match-only Must filter removal (Range/Set/Glob/All, factor-1 boosts), duplicate (field_id,boost) expansion cleanup, Glob field sort+dedup; scoring Term/Phrase/Should never removed; idempotent; returns QueryCanonicalizationReport. (3) Score-affecting dedup deliberately NOT shipped: cursor sharing for duplicate scoring clauses is the planner's (e4.4/index.rs) — score-identical and probe-cheap, no divergence entry needed. (4) Conformance surfaces: language contract 4.2 updated, fixture query-default-recursive-dedup now oracle-true Boolean-of-2, unit pins for retained scoring duplicates vs merged exclusions. Tests: 8 canonicalization tests + updated contract tests; quill suite 342/342 green; clippy/fmt clean; UBS exit 0. Adversarial repetition cap: redundant — MAX_QUERY_LENGTH bounds the source.

title: quill-duel: shadow-oracle dark-launch dual-run mode (gate G2.5)
description: CONSENSUS #2 — INDEPENDENTLY CONVERGENT: both wizards proposed this unprompted (Fable idea 3, Gemini idea 4; cross-scores 920 and 800) — the strongest validation signal the dueling methodology produces. WHAT: during G2, opted-in fsfs deployments index into BOTH engines and serve queries from tantivy while asynchronously running the same query against Quill and logging classified divergences — converting real fleet dogfooding (chaotic agent queries, real monorepos) into flip evidence at zero user risk; synthetic gauntlet corpora (E6) cannot cover this distribution. MERGED DESIGN (post-reveal consensus): (1) placement behind the Arc<dyn LexicalSearch> seam as a wrapping ShadowLexical adapter — NOT inside TwoTierSearcher/fusion (preserves plan §13.1 'fusion needs zero changes'; Gemini conceded Fable's placement critique); (2) shadow query runs in a bounded asupersync background task (never blocks the serving path; poll_immediate contract untouched); (3) divergence artifacts as JSONL under the index dir (.quill-shadow/divergences.jsonl) stamped with the manifest GENERATION that produced them (enables exact replay; adopted from Gemini's shrinker refinement) — NOT direct writes into ops SQLite (dependency direction); (4) sampling + load-shedding: sample rate config, auto-shed when CPU/IO pressure crosses thresholds (Gemini's refinement, adopted); (5) opt-in config flag, default off; doubles lexical indexing cost only for opted-in machines. Divergences feed the Divergence Register + shrinker (see quill-duel-shrinker). Blocks e7.6: the flip commit cites shadow-mode divergence-clean evidence alongside gauntlet scorecards.
notes: POLISH PASS: explicit test + logging spec (every feature cluster ships tests with detailed logging): (1) NON-INTERFERENCE — property/e2e test that the serving path's latency and results are bit-identical with shadow on vs off (shadow task must never block or backpressure the serving query; assert via LabRuntime schedules + a wall-clock guard bench); (2) ARTIFACT WELL-FORMEDNESS — every divergence JSONL line validates against a schema (query, both top-k lists, classification, manifest generation, corpus hash) and round-trips into the shrinker (quill-duel-shrinker) and the exact-generation replay; (3) LOAD-SHED — synthetic CPU/IO pressure triggers shedding (sampled-out queries logged as shed, never silently dropped); sampling rate honored within tolerance (counted over N queries); (4) LIFECYCLE — shadow index build failure NEVER fails the serving path (typed degradation event + doctor surfacing); enabling/disabling the flag mid-session is clean (region cancel-correct, LabRuntime leak oracle); (5) STRUCTURED LOGGING — tracing spans per shadow query (serve latency, shadow latency, divergence class, shed decisions) since this doubles as the G2.5 evidence stream. All tests print seeds/generation ids for replay.
close_reason: Implemented default-off shadow oracle with bounded asupersync execution, schema-validated divergence/degradation/observation JSONL, load shedding, doctor visibility, gauntlet shrinker ingestion, mock-free lifecycle/E2E tests, and strict remote-only green gates. title: quill-duel: auto-minimizing divergence shrinker + BM25-factor auto-triage
description: From the duel (Fable idea 4, Gemini score 890). The E6 gauntlet's operational bottleneck will be diagnosing nightly divergences on 1M-doc corpora. Build into the gauntlet crate: (1) ddmin-style shrinker — given a (corpus, query, divergence), delta-debug the corpus down to a minimal reproducer (~3 docs) and the query to minimal form, exploiting the engine's determinism (§1.5); every shrunk case is committed as a PERMANENT regression fixture; (2) PRESERVE THE ORIGINAL: the artifact keeps the original query AST + corpus manifest hash alongside the minimal repro (Gemini's refinement, adopted post-reveal — over-minimization loses the semantic context of parser edge cases); (3) explanation-driven auto-triage: for score divergences, diff the BM25 factor breakdown (idf inputs: N, doc_freq; tf inputs: freq, fieldnorm byte, avgdl; boosts; accumulation order) between engines and auto-bucket into Divergence Register classes (stats-mismatch / fieldnorm / parser / tie-order / pruning) — turning multi-hour manual triage into minutes; (4) shadow-mode integration: .quill-shadow/divergences.jsonl entries (see quill-duel-shadow-oracle) feed the same shrinker via the stamped generation for exact-snapshot replay. Deps: e6.2 (differential runner + comparator + MismatchSignature dedup).
notes: POLISH PASS: the shrinker itself needs tests, not just outputs: (1) MINIMALITY+DETERMINISM — same (corpus, query, seed) shrinks to the byte-identical minimal repro (ddmin is deterministic given fixed probe order; pin it); shrunk case still exhibits the SAME divergence class as the original (guard against shrink-drift: re-classify after shrink, assert class equality, else keep the larger repro); (2) TRIAGE ACCURACY — seeded synthetic divergences with KNOWN causes (inject a wrong fieldnorm byte, a stats offset, a tie-order flip) must bucket into the correct register class >= high threshold; misclassifications logged with full factor diffs; (3) HARNESS SAFETY — shrinker runs against a COPY of the fixture corpus (never mutates originals), bounded iterations (budgeted mode + on-exhaustion keep-best); (4) E2E — one full pipeline test: gauntlet divergence -> shrink -> committed fixture file -> fixture replays red on the buggy build and green post-fix (use a deliberately-introduced scoring bug on a scratch branch of the scalar kernel via cfg(test) hook, not a real regression). Detailed tracing at each ddmin probe (kept/dropped doc ids, class checks).
close_reason: Landed (commit cc78425). (1) ddmin-style ShrinkDriver over the DifferentialCampaignEngine boundary: Zeller delta-debugging on documents (chunk-drop while divergence persists, escalating granularity) + greedy token-level query minimization, exploiting engine determinism; fuel-bounded with typed FuelExhausted. (2) ShrunkReproduction preserves the ORIGINAL (query text, corpus manifest hash, doc count) beside the minimal repro per Gemini's anti-over-minimization amendment; persist_shrunk_reproduction writes content-addressed permanent fixtures under <root>/shrunk/ with temp+rename+dir-fsync. (3) Explanation-driven auto-triage: comparator evidence (AST diffs, tie groups, set identity, score deltas) maps divergences to SuspectedLayer (FieldNormArithmetic/ParserLowering/TieOrder/Pruning/Indexing) with High/Medium/Low confidence; factor-level decomposition noted for when observations carry idf/tf/norm breakdowns. (4) Shadow integration: ShadowDivergenceRecord schema for .quill-shadow/divergences.jsonl; shrink_shadow_line parses + shrinks with stamped generation preserved for exact-snapshot replay. Tests: ddmin convergence (12→<=4 docs containing trigger + query minimized to trigger token), fuel exhaustion typed error, shadow schema fail-closed + generation stamping, triage verdicts per class, fixture persist/roundtrip. Gauntlet suite 83/83 green; clippy/fmt clean; UBS exit 0.

title: quill-duel: G1a skeleton-first resequencing — scalar reference engine end-to-end first
description: From the duel (Fable idea 2, Gemini score 850). RESEQUENCE the build order so a complete SCALAR, delta-free, single-shard reference engine (exhaustive kernel, scalar codecs, no pruning, no SIMD) runs end-to-end (ingest->seal->open->query) as gate G1a, BEFORE any optimization lever lands. WHY: the gauntlet (e6.2 differential runner) gets a real subject months earlier, so the highest-risk items (rank parity, parser corners, fieldnorm/stats semantics) accumulate conformance evidence from the start; every leapfrog bet (SIMD tokenizer e1.1, radix flush e1.5, MaxScore/BMW e4.4, delta e5.x, concat-merge e3.5) then lands as a ledgered one-lever A/B against a GREEN scalar baseline — the plan already mandates scalar reference implementations for differentials (§15.2), this makes them arrive FIRST instead of alongside. ANTI-THRASH GUARD (Gemini's sharpest-flaw objection, Fable's accepted answer): the skeleton MUST implement the final trait boundaries from day one — PostingCursor trait per e4.3/e2.2 (already specified), the accumulator seam per e1.7's A/B (already forced), and the byte-source-generic reader per e3.1 notes — so later kernels swap implementations, not interfaces. title: quill-duel: cross-process visibility contract + max_visibility_lag_ms + QG-3 two-topology amendment
description: From the duel's blind-spot probe (Fable; orchestrator-verified structural). Bet Q3's 'searchable immediately' (plan §6.3) is true IN-PROCESS ONLY: the delta segment is process-local memory, so the flagship topology — 'fsfs index --watch' daemon + separate 'fsfs search' CLI invocations — sees only sealed+published segments, i.e. commit-cadence freshness, same as tantivy today. Nothing in the plan/contracts states this; worse, in-process metrics (e7.2 debounce retune, QG-3's '>=4x update->searchable headroom') can 'improve' while the cross-process agent experience stays flat or degrades. WORK: (1) contract row in the Language/behavior contract (amend quill-e0.1 deliverable): visibility classes pinned — InProcess (delta, immediate) vs CrossProcess (published, commit-cadence); (2) Keeper policy max_visibility_lag_ms in QuillConfig: force seal-and-publish when the oldest unpublished delta entry exceeds the bound (piggyback existing seal triggers), making cross-process staleness a CONFIGURED GUARANTEE; add 'fsfs flush' as an explicit barrier command; (3) freshness surfacing: segment_stats() gains published_generation, last_publish_unix, live_writer (from the D1 LOCK); fsfs status + --format json search responses carry index_freshness; (4) QG-3 bench manifests (quill-e0.6 artifacts) measure update->searchable in BOTH topologies (in-process reader AND fresh-process reader) so the leapfrog claim is honest per topology. title: quill-duel: cross-process writer lock + readers-never-GC + publish CAS
description: CONSENSUS #1 from the 2026-07-16 dueling-idea-wizards session (DUELING_WIZARDS_REPORT.md; Fable self-rank 1, Gemini score 980, steelman 1000). FIXES A REAL DATA-LOSS HOLE in plan §11: crash-only open (§11.4) GCs unreferenced segment files, and writer serialization is an IN-PROCESS asupersync Mutex only — so an 'fsfs search' (reader process) opening the index concurrently with an 'fsfs index --watch' daemon (writer process) can GC the writer's sealed-but-not-yet-published segment, permanently corrupting the index on publish. The incumbent tantivy has a directory lockfile; Quill's plan had NOTHING cross-process (missed by three fresh-eyes passes; the single-process crash matrix e3.9 can never catch it). MERGED DESIGN (both wizards' refinements): (1) split the API — QuillIndex::open() = reader: NEVER GC, touch nothing; QuillIndex::open_writer() = acquire lock THEN recover/GC; (2) LOCK file stores owning PID + start-time nonce; takeover requires kill(pid,0)==ESRCH (OS-verified process death) — NEVER mtime/heartbeat-staleness alone (Gemini's SIGSTOP false-takeover objection: this repo's process-triage tooling really does SIGSTOP agents); (3) publish-time CAS via O_EXCL generation-claim file (Fable's post-reveal upgrade fixing the TOCTOU it found in its own mtime design): creating 'gen-<N+1>.claim' with O_CREAT|O_EXCL atomically claims the generation before the MANIFEST rename; a stale writer that lost the lock fails the claim with a typed error, never clobbers; (4) GC additionally never deletes files younger than a grace window (belt+braces). Tests: multi-PROCESS crash matrix (spawn real subprocesses: reader-during-unpublished-seal, two writers racing takeover, SIGSTOP'd writer + takeover + wake), LabRuntime in-process analogues, lock-file corruption/staleness cases. Amends plan §11.4 + e3.3's GC discipline. Blocks the flip (e7.6): shipping without this loses user data in the documented fleet topology.
close_reason: Completed cross-process writer admission, touchless readers, publish CAS, grace GC, durable writer recovery, and multiprocess/LabRuntime regressions

title: Quill E0: Contracts & gauntlet skeleton (gate G0)
description: EPIC. Gate G0 of COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_THE_QUILL_LEXICAL_ENGINE.md: no Quill engine code merges before the contracts land. Quill is the ground-up, zero-new-external-dep, memory-safe lexical BM25 engine that fully replaces tantivy as frankensearch's default lexical path, with tantivy 0.26.1 retained as a pinned conformance oracle. This epic produces the paper contracts (language/scoring/format/invariants), the conformance-harness skeleton with the oracle wired, and the pinned perf-gate manifests. Rationale: the entire replacement is de-risked by the narrow used-surface census (plan §3) — Term/Boolean/Phrase/Range(i64)/glob-derived-Regex/All queries, default BM25, one FAST column, custom analyzers, TopDocs/Count/DocSet collectors.
