title: quill-e0.1: Language Contract doc + fixture corpora
description: Write docs/contracts/quill-language-contract.md pinning exactly what 'same results as tantivy' means (plan §5, §8). Contents: (a) analyzer contract — token-stream equality (text/position/offset) vs the SHIPPING implementations: FrankensearchTokenizer (crates/frankensearch-lexical/src/lib.rs:466, fused simple+lowercase) and the CASS family (CassTokenizer, HyphenDecompose, CjkBigramDecompose, CassNormalizeAndLimit 256B, edge n-grams, preview — cass_compat.rs:58-1674); the shipping scalar code is the spec. (b) query grammar contract — default lenient parser (fields [content, title boost 2.0], quoted phrases, 10k-char truncation at char boundary, lenient drop-with-warn) + CASS boolean grammar (AND '&&'/OR '||' with OR binding TIGHTER than AND, NOT/'-' = Must(AllQuery)+MustNot, phrases, CassWildcardPattern globs Exact/Prefix/Suffix/Substring/Complex, i64 created_at range filters, CJK bigram expansion). (c) scoring contract — BM25 k1=1.2 b=0.75, idf=ln(1+(N-n+0.5)/(n+0.5)), tantivy fieldnorm 1-byte quantization, multi-field weighted sum, f32 accumulation in parse order, tie-break (score desc via total_cmp, docid asc). (d) conformance classes: RankExact (gate for equal-stats configs) and ScoreEpsilon (|rel dscore|<=1e-4, identical result sets, rank flips only inside epsilon-tied groups). Deliverables: the doc + committed fixture corpora: golden parse trees per query class, token-stream goldens per analyzer, harvested query-class corpus (identifier/short_keyword/natural_language/phrase/boolean/glob/range) seeded from tests/fixtures/{corpus,queries}.json and fsfs search_quality_harness slices. Success: doc reviewed; fixtures load in a test; every §3.1 surface row has at least one fixture.
notes: FRESH-EYES AMENDMENTS — three more contract rows to pin with fixtures: (1) OVERSIZED TERMS — RESOLVED against tantivy 0.26.1 source: MAX_TOKEN_LEN = u16::MAX - 5 = 65530 bytes (src/tokenizer/mod.rs:168); tokens exceeding it are DROPPED with a warning at indexing time (src/postings/postings_writer.rs:141-146). Contract row: Quill drops tokens > 65530 bytes identically (warn + drop, doc + query side symmetric); fixture with a >65530-byte token asserts both engines return identical results. (2) BOOLEAN SEMANTICS: Lucene/tantivy Occur semantics — when Must clauses are present, Should clauses become optional (contribute score, don't gate matching); MustNot never contributes score; pin with fixtures per shape. (3) DELETES vs STATS: tantivy does NOT discount deleted docs from doc_freq/N used in BM25 weights (deletes affect matching only, until merge) — pin the oracle's exact behavior; Quill snapshot stats mirror it (tombstones excluded from MATCHING; sealed-segment stats include tombstoned docs until compaction). (4) PARSER DEFAULT — RESOLVED against source: QueryParser conjunction_by_default = false (src/query/query_parser/query_parser.rs:263) and frankensearch never calls set_conjunction_by_default, so multi-term default = DISJUNCTION (OR of per-field Should clauses); cite in the grammar contract and still pin by fixtures.
close_reason: Language/scoring contract, executable fixture corpus, and oracle-parity regression coverage completed and reviewed

title: quill-e0.2: FSLX on-disk format spec v1 + format registry
description: Write docs/contracts/fslx-format-registry.md: the normative FSLX v1 spec (plan §10) + a registry table where EVERY future format change lands a row (version, change, migration note, gauntlet fixture id). Spec must pin: segment file layout (magic FSLXSEG\0, format_version u32, header{segment_id, schema_id, docid_lo/hi u64, doc_count, section table with per-section xxh3-64}, header_crc32, 64-byte aligned sections TERMDICT/POSTINGS/POSITIONS/BLOCKMAX/DOCLEN/IDMAP/IDHASH/NUMERIC/STOREDMETA/STATS, file xxh3 + crc32 trailer); MANIFEST v1 (magic FSLXMAN\0, generation, docid_high_watermark, segment entries incl. roaring-style tombstone bytes, stats rollup, crc32; two-slot MANIFEST/MANIFEST.prev publish); posting encoding (128-doc FOR blocks: first_doc absolute u32 + bitpacked deltas, 4-bit width descriptor, freq blocks w/ all-ones flag, vint final partial block, dense bitmap hybrid when span<512); IDHASH uses xxh3-64 of DocId bytes (NEVER ahash — not stable across versions/platforms); docids u32 in postings, u64 header fields; little-endian everywhere; no serde in durable bytes (hand-rolled only). Constraints: conventions must match the FSVI house style (frankensearch-index/src/lib.rs:6-113) and durability repair-trailer expectations (xxh3 fast path). title: quill-e0.3: Q1 merge=concat invariant doc + obligations
description: Write the Q1 invariant spec (plan §7) as docs/contracts/quill-q1-docid-discipline.md. Invariant: every segment carries a half-open global docid interval [lo,hi); live segments have pairwise-disjoint ranges; all postings/tombstones/doclens/idmap entries refer only to in-range docids. Allocation: Keeper-owned monotone allocator (high-watermark persisted in MANIFEST); per-shard SESSION leases (64k blocks, reused across watch-mode batches, tail BURNED at session end, never reused); upsert = new docid + tombstone old; docids never reused; u32 posting width with reserved renumbering deep-compaction escape hatch. Theorem: for disjoint ordered ranges, merged postings per term = concatenation, already docid-sorted — merge needs NO posting decode (k-way dict merge by term bytes; verbatim block copy; only seam blocks (<=1 per segment boundary per term) re-encode; stats re-aggregate; doclen/idmap concat; tombstones union). Obligations to encode as fixtures: Q1-OB1 manifest validation rejects overlapping ranges; Q1-OB2 merge(S1..Sn) bit-identical to single-segment indexing with same docid assignments; Q1-OB3 query results invariant under any merge schedule (BM25 stats are snapshot-level); Q1-OB4 compaction drops tombstoned docs PRESERVING surviving docids (gaps fine, FOR deltas absorb them), triggered by density threshold (default 20%), A/B'd at realistic densities (bd-6m8p lesson: never benchmark tombstone machinery at 0% density). Success: doc reviewed; each obligation has a named test-fixture stub in the gauntlet skeleton.
notes: FRESH-EYES AMENDMENT (plan §7 updated, commit follows): shard-lease interleaving breaks naive interval disjointness — a shard's later leases interleave with other shards' blocks, so a segment spanning two leases (or a same-shard merge skipping an interleaved foreign segment) would overlap another live segment's covering interval. The spec MUST pin two rules: (R1) SEAL-AT-LEASE-BOUNDARY — a sealed segment's docid range is a subinterval of ONE lease block; lease exhaustion forces a segment cut even below arena budget. (R2) MERGE ONLY BOUND-CONSECUTIVE RUNS — tier policy sorts live segments by lo and merges only consecutive runs; cross-shard merges are the normal case (concat is concat, equally cheap). R1+R2 preserve strict pairwise-disjoint covering intervals forever; burned lease tails are unused docids INSIDE an interval (always legal). Q1-OB1 gains two assertions: merge precondition = bound-consecutive inputs; seal invariant = single-lease span.
close_reason: Q1 spec landed at docs/contracts/quill-q1-docid-discipline.md: invariant Q1-a..d, session-lease allocation w/ 64k blocks + burn-on-end + u32 width & reserved deep-compaction escape hatch, R1 seal-at-lease-boundary + R2 bound-consecutive merges with induction rationale, merge=concat theorem + proof sketch + streaming merge procedure, §4.1 run-gap holes + merge_max_hole_ratio knob (new precision), obligations Q1-OB1..OB6 mapped to enforcing beads/fixtures (fixture STUBS land with the gauntlet skeleton e0.5 which depends on this doc), interactions incl. resumable-bulk + writer-lock, foreclosed-failure-modes rationale

title: Quill E1: Scribe — SIMD ingest pipeline
description: EPIC. The ingest front-end and the indexing-throughput headline (plan §6.1, bets Q2+Q4). Share-nothing shard-per-worker ingest: SIMD/SWAR tokenization + case folding -> local term interning (arena-backed, local u32 ids) -> columnar (term_id, doc_ord, pos) SoA accumulation in bump arenas -> radix-partition flush by term_id -> sealed FSLX mini-segments. Rationale: tantivy's write path routes every token through a term-keyed hashmap arena (cache-hostile random access) and generic schema dispatch; Quill confines the hashmap school to the small delta segment (E5) and makes bulk flush a sequence of cache-shaped sequential passes (the radix-hash-join lesson: histogram -> prefix-sum -> disjoint writes parallelizes with zero contention). Workers hold disjoint docid-range leases (Q1) so nothing shared-mutable exists on the hot path; work-stealing at the batch level handles Apple Silicon P/E asymmetry; disjoint ranges keep 16-96 core x86 contention-free. Positions recorded only for position-indexed fields. No per-token String allocs (CompactString only at dictionary insert). Epic closes when children close.

title: quill-e1.4: Columnar accumulator (SoA triples + fieldnorms)

Overflow discipline: doc_ord is shard-lease-relative until seal (rebased to global docid at segment build — cheap because leases are contiguous). title: quill-e1.5: Radix flush kernel (histogram -> prefix-sum -> partition -> build)
description: Flush = turn a shard's columnar arenas into one sealed FSLX mini-segment (plan §6.1). Kernel: histogram term_ids -> prefix-sum -> scatter triples into disjoint per-term ranges (1-pass LSD at <=2^16 local terms, 2-pass MSD beyond; per-thread local histograms + prefix-sum for parallel scatter with zero contention — the radix-hash-join pattern, graveyard 8.14); then per-partition strictly sequential posting-block build (delta+FOR bitpack via E2 codecs, block-max computation), term dict build (sort local ids by term bytes, prefix-block encode via E2), doc-length column, IDMAP/IDHASH, STATS. Triples within a term partition must be emitted docid-ascending (stable scatter preserves per-term append order; doc_ords are assigned ascending within a shard batch — assert this invariant). Skew handling: heavy terms (stopword-class) get their partition built with a streaming path (no extra copy). Output goes through the E3 segment writer. Property tests: flush(fixed corpus) is byte-identical run-to-run (determinism); posting lists docid-sorted; per-term doc_freq == distinct docs.
close_reason: Completed deterministic radix flush with stable parallel scatter, bounded metadata fallback, complete segment sections, and remote correctness proof

title: quill-e1.6: Shard router + docid-range leases (Q1 allocation)
description: Implement the Q1 allocation discipline (plan §7, spec from quill-e0.3): Keeper-side monotone docid allocator (high-watermark persisted in MANIFEST via E3); per-shard SESSION leases of contiguous 64k blocks; leases reused across watch-mode batches within a session; lease tail BURNED at session end (never reused); docids never reused; upsert = allocate new docid + tombstone old (old found via IDHASH probe). Shard router: fan IndexableDocument batches across W shard workers (default: physical cores, config clamp); routing is round-robin by batch (NOT by doc hash — batches keep locality and doc_ord contiguity). deterministic_ingest mode: single shard OR round-robin-with-barrier so docid assignment is a pure function of ingest order (used by LabRuntime suites and replay). Tests: lease disjointness under concurrent sessions (property test), burn-on-end accounting, deterministic mode replay produces byte-identical segments (with logging of lease grants).
notes: FRESH-EYES AMENDMENT: implement R1 from the Q1 spec — lease exhaustion forces a segment cut (flush) so no segment ever spans two lease blocks; mini-segments are therefore <=64k docs, which the arena budget usually enforces earlier anyway. Watch-mode sessions use a SINGLE shard (LiveIngestPipeline applies batches sequentially; single-shard keeps delta-overlay upsert/delete probes trivially correct and the session deterministic); multi-shard is the bulk-build configuration. Add a lease-boundary-cut unit test (index >64k docs through one shard, assert every sealed segment's range fits one lease block) with logging of cut reasons (budget vs lease-exhaustion).
close_reason: Implemented in scribe.rs: DocIdAllocator (monotone, watermark-aligned, 64k per-shard session leases, grant-time watermark advance = crash-safe burn, burn-on-end accounting, u32-space exhaustion typed) + ShardRouter (round-robin-by-batch, config clamp, deterministic_ingest -> single shard). 12 new tests incl. 8-session lease-disjointness property, burn accounting, and deterministic replay producing byte-identical segments + grant logs. clippy/fmt green on touched files.

title: quill-e2.2: FOR/bitpacked posting blocks + SIMD unpack (scalar-parity gate)
description: POSTINGS section per FSLX section 5.2 and registry 1.0.3: every block is independently self-delimiting with block_kind u8, posting_count u8, and payload_len u16 LE. FOR and BITMAP counts are exactly 128; VINT counts are 1..=127. Fresh writers select BITMAP iff inclusive span is below 512 and FOR otherwise; readers accept structurally canonical FOR at any span so width-0 FOR remains in the decoder domain. FOR stores absolute first_doc u32 plus 127 delta-minus-one values at minimal doc_width u8 0..=32. Frequencies use kind 0 iff all one, otherwise kind 1 plus minimal width 1..=32 and bitpacked freq-minus-one. VINT stores first doc absolute, later delta-minus-one, and positive freqs as canonical u32 LEB128; preserved VINT partials are legal at interior concat seams. Readers consume exact TERMDICT postings_len, reject invalid counts, nonminimal widths/vints, padding, arithmetic overflow, truncation/trailing bytes, and require summed counts equal doc_freq. Production decode uses the canonical scalar reservoir. A portable wide u32x8 candidate with bit-identical decoded output is retained behind test and bench-internals; the 2026-07-17 same-binary gate rejected a global wide-for-all route, and any future per-width dispatcher requires a fresh admissible gate. Mandatory scalar/wide differential covers widths 0..=32, 127-value doc-delta and 128-value frequency shapes, slice alignments, FOR/BITMAP payloads, and is registered as unit plus executable gauntlet fixture quiver-postings-bitpack-scalar-wide-v1. Cursor starts on first posting, exposes current doc/freq/posting ordinal, next, and advance target via validated block last-doc skips; u32::MAX is a valid docid, never an EOF sentinel. Encode validates strictly ascending docids and positive freqs. Tests include independent wire goldens, randomized roundtrip, corruption/no-panic matrix, explicit resource budgets, owned-list shape-derived validation limits, advance equivalence, every partial size 1..127 at interior seams, bitmap spans 511/512, and df=100 + df=300 proving decoded equivalence plus byte preservation/order and no new fragments. IDMAP: docid -> DocId (CompactString bytes): u32 offset array + blob, direct slice materialization (two-phase top-k materializes winners only, house pattern). IDHASH: open-addressed table keyed by xxh3-64 of DocId bytes -> docid, for upsert/delete probes; DURABLE hashing MUST be xxh3 (stable, versioned) — NEVER ahash (unstable across versions/platforms; this is a pinned format decision from plan §10.2). Collision discipline: probe verifies against IDMAP bytes before returning. Tests: roundtrip 1M synthetic DocIds incl. >24-byte ids (CompactString heap spill), hash-collision injection (craft two ids with same 64-bit xxh3 truncation via brute force on short ids, or simulate), reopen-and-probe correctness. Bench: id materialization vs the old reopen_id_materialize class — expected flat/trivial.

title: quill-e3.1: FSLX segment writer/reader (header/sections/checksums/mmap)
description: Implement the FSLX v1 segment container per the pinned spec (quill-e0.2): writer (assemble sections 64-byte aligned, per-section xxh3-64, header + header_crc32, file xxh3 + trailer crc32; write to .tmp- prefixed file, fsync, rename by Keeper) and reader (validate magic/version/header CRC eagerly; per-section checksums LAZILY on first touch + an eager verify() for doctor flows; typed corruption errors — SearchError-style IndexCorrupted, never panic). Read path: mmap via the FSVI precedent — PREFER a shared safe facade in frankensearch-index if extractable; else one module-scoped #![allow(unsafe_code)] with ledger comment, exactly like frankensearch-index does (workspace lint deny(unsafe_code); every other quill module forbid). Sections wired to E2 codecs. Tests: write->read roundtrip on fixture segments; alignment assertions; torn-file (truncate at every 1KiB boundary) -> typed error; the committed v1 golden segment from e2.8 must parse.
notes:
FRESH-EYES PASS 2: the reader is generic over its byte source from day one. Sealed segments use mmap-backed bytes on disk, while in-memory indexes may retain owned bytes; both use the same &[u8] parser and validation path.

E3.1 implementation decisions (2026-07-17, BeigeHorse): the normative registry overrides the stale plan header sketch. Section payloads remain opaque because E2.8 owns the future committed cross-version codec fixture. Canonical readers require H=56+28*N, the exact schema-derived known-section set, zero flags for known kinds, only OPTIONAL_SKIPPABLE on unknown kinds, strictly increasing minimally aligned nonoverlapping sections, zero padding, and a trailer immediately after the final payload. Structural validation plus header CRC and trailer CRC are eager; section xxh3 is verified lazily on first touch; verify() freshly hashes every section including unknown-skippable and recomputes file_xxh3. CRC is crc32fast IEEE CRC-32. Quill retains #![forbid(unsafe_code)] by using a localized safe read-only mmap facade in frankensearch-index under the immutable published-artifact lifecycle. The writer uses create_new for .tmp-segment-<hex16>, writes exact bytes, flushes and sync_all; E3.3 Keeper owns rename, manifest publication, and directory fsync. Published opens require canonical lowercase seg-<hex16>.fslx regular non-symlink paths and require the filename ID to equal header.segment_id. NUMERIC presence covers indexed I64 and U64; the registry preserves the full u64 value_bits domain. Quill corruption converts to SearchError::IndexCorrupted.

Three concurrently launched RCH attempts routed away from ovh-a despite the pin and were aborted immediately; their outputs are discarded and not cited.

Acceptance coverage includes independent manual assembly of a complete pinned v1 reader fixture without production encoder or checksum helpers, writer determinism, owned/borrowed/mmap parity, canonical alignment and padding, conditional section sets including explicit indexed-U64 omission rejection, unknown optional extension handling, lazy cached section checks, fresh eager verify, file/trailer corruption, hostile resource bounds, canonical published names, filename/header identity, temp collision safety, every 1 KiB torn boundary, and no-panic hostile prefixes. title: quill-e3.2: MANIFEST format + two-slot atomic publish protocol
description: MANIFEST v1 per spec (quill-e0.2 / plan §10.6, §11.3): magic FSLXMAN\0, format_version, generation u64, docid_high_watermark, schema_id, engine_version, segment entries {segment_id, file_len, file_xxh3, docid_lo/hi, doc_count, tombstone roaring bytes}, stats rollup, crc32. Publish protocol (plan §11.3): write MANIFEST(gen+1) to temp -> fsync file -> atomic rename over MANIFEST (previous kept as MANIFEST.prev) -> fsync directory. Publishes serialized behind a cancel-aware asupersync::sync::Mutex (the ONLY writer-side lock); readers never touch it (epoch snapshots, e5.2/12.1). commit(cx) choreography: seal deltas (E5) -> fsync new segment files -> publish manifest -> optional FileProtector .fec emission (e3.8). Hand-rolled bytes, no serde (house durable-format rule). Tests: publish/reopen generation monotonicity; MANIFEST corrupted -> fallback to MANIFEST.prev; concurrent publish attempts serialize (LabRuntime); high-watermark persistence round-trip (feeds e1.6 leases).
notes: FRESH-EYES PASS 2: pin the two-rename publish order and its crash window — publish = (1) write+fsync temp; (2) rename MANIFEST -> MANIFEST.prev; (3) rename temp -> MANIFEST; (4) fsync dir. A crash between (2) and (3) leaves NO MANIFEST but a valid .prev: open() must treat missing-MANIFEST-with-valid-prev as recover-from-prev (not IndexNotFound — distinguish 'directory has no index' from 'index mid-publish'). Kill-point tests must cover between-renames explicitly (extend e3.3/e3.9 matrices). Also pin: generation in .prev must be exactly current-1 or equal (idempotent republish), else typed corruption error.

title: quill-e3.3: Crash-only open/recovery + GC
description: open() = recover (plan §11.4, crash-only doctrine): read MANIFEST (fallback MANIFEST.prev on checksum failure); validate Q1-OB1 (pairwise-disjoint docid ranges — reject overlaps with a typed error); lazily checksum sections; GC unreferenced files. GC SAFETY (this repo's RULE 1 posture): deletes ONLY files matching Quill's own naming schema (seg-<hex16>.fslx, .tmp-*, orphaned .fec sidecars for quill files) INSIDE the index dir, with the durability crate's path-safety guard pattern (reject .. / absolute paths); never touches anything else. IndexNotFound on open-missing (matching TantivyIndex::open semantics, lexical/src/lib.rs:675). in_memory() constructor for tests (no files, delta-only). Tests: recovery matrix — kill-point fixtures at every arrow of the commit choreography (temp written / file fsynced / renamed / dir fsynced / .fec emitted) via fault-injection hooks; after each: committed docs durable + queryable, uncommitted invisible, GC removes exactly the garbage (assert file inventory), reopen idempotent (open->open byte-stable). LabRuntime-driven kill-point suite lands fully in quill-e3.9; here: the deterministic single-thread matrix.
notes: FRESH-EYES PASS 2: in_memory() is NOT delta-only — commit() on an in-memory index seals deltas into owned-buffer FSLX segments and publishes an in-memory manifest (same choreography, no fsync/files), so behavior matches on-disk exactly minus durability. Recovery/GC paths are no-ops for in-memory. Also (from e3.2 notes): open() distinguishes missing-MANIFEST-with-valid-.prev (mid-publish crash -> recover from prev) from truly-absent index (-> IndexNotFound). PASS 3: create() semantics must match the incumbent exactly — TantivyIndex::create is create_in_dir ELSE open_in_dir (lexical/src/lib.rs:642), i.e. CREATE-OR-OPEN, not fail-if-exists; Quill create(path, schema) = genesis manifest write if absent, else open-and-validate (schema_id mismatch -> typed error, NOT silent rebuild — rebuild policy belongs to fsfs, e7.5). Port the existing create/open/reopen tests in the harvest. DUEL RIPPLE (bd-quill-duel-writer-lock): GC OWNERSHIP MOVES — reader open() NEVER GCs (readers touch nothing); recovery+GC runs only under open_writer() holding the cross-process LOCK. This bead implements the recovery/GC MACHINERY; the lock/CAS/liveness protocol and the open/open_writer split live in the duel bead — coordinate the seam so GC has exactly one owner. The single-process crash matrix here remains valid; multi-process rows live in the duel bead.

title: quill-e3.4: Tombstone sets in MANIFEST (roaring-style)
description: Deletes against sealed segments (plan §10.5): per-segment tombstone sets stored in the MANIFEST generation (segments stay immutable). In-house roaring-style serialization: per-64k-chunk containers, array (<=4096 sparse u16s) or bitmap, hysteresis on promote/demote (graveyard 7.14 pattern) — small, since only the delete path touches it. Snapshot construction pairs segment + current tombstones; cursors filter tombstoned docids (branch-light: check only when a candidate is emitted, not per-advance). doc_count() = manifest live counts minus tombstone cardinalities (O(1) from rollup). delete_document flow: IDHASH probe (e2.6) -> tombstone add -> manifest publish on commit; delete_all = new empty generation (all segments dropped, files GC'd after snapshot drain). Tests: delete->search invisibility pre- and post-commit; upsert tombstones old docid; container promote/demote edges (4095/4096/4097 entries); serialization roundtrip; doc_count accuracy under interleaved add/delete (log per-op state transitions).
notes: FRESH-EYES AMENDMENT: DocId->docid resolution with upserts — multiple segments may contain the same DocId (older tombstoned + newest live). IDHASH probe order is NEWEST segment first (manifest order), skipping tombstoned docids; invariant: at most ONE live docid per DocId (upsert discipline). Add a repeated-upsert test (same DocId upserted N times across multiple seals) asserting single-live resolution and correct tombstone accumulation, with per-probe logging.

title: quill-e3.5: Concat-merge (Q1-OB2a/OB2b/OB3 fixtures)
description: THE structural win per plan section 7: merge bound-consecutive segments by k-way term-dictionary merge and, per term, copy every self-delimiting posting block verbatim and in source order. Absolute first_doc means no posting rebase. Preserved partial VINT blocks remain legal at interior seams; ordinary merge never fills tails, re-encodes seam blocks, or shifts later 128-posting boundaries. Re-emit BLOCKMAX/skip entries one-for-one in posting-block order, adjusting only offsets relative to the merged term stream while preserving first_doc and bound fields; synthesize no seam entry. Re-aggregate doc_freq/stats; concatenate positional sections with holes; rebuild IDHASH linearly; union tombstones without folding. Each freshly sealed leaf contributes at most one partial per term; merge products may contain multiple preserved leaf partials but merge creates none. Optional reblocking is explicit deep compaction only. Run as a region-scoped blocking task; output remains unreferenced until manifest publish. Q1-OB2a requires decoded postings, aggregate stats, and query results equal monolithic indexing with identical docid assignments. Q1-OB2b requires each input block appear byte-identically and in order under arbitrary merge schedules, with no new fragments. Q1-OB3 requires query invariance under arbitrary merge schedules. Mandatory fixture df=100 + df=300 plus interior partial sizes 1..127, term-in-subset cases, stats recount, and reversed/overlapping input rejection. Bench verifies I/O-shaped cost and approximately flat CPU per byte as segment count grows.
notes: FRESH-EYES AMENDMENT: merge() asserts its inputs are bound-consecutive under the manifest's lo-sorted order (R2 precondition, typed error otherwise) — the tier policy (e3.7) guarantees it, but the assertion keeps the invariant local and testable. Q1-OB1's validation additionally covers this precondition.

title: quill-e3.7: Tier policy + bulk-load mode

Bulk-load mode: suppress merging during initial build, one final concat pass at finish — replaces LogMergePolicy::set_min_num_segments(256) AND the entire force_merge_bounded/cooldown apparatus (cass_compat.rs:1025-1228), whose memory-pressure motivation evaporates when merge stops decoding postings. Config surface: fanout, tier boundaries, bulk mode toggle — all in a QuillConfig with documented defaults, no env vars (explicit config per house README guidance). Tests: segment-count bound holds under sustained watch-mode churn (simulated 10k batches); bulk mode produces exactly 1 final segment per shard set; policy decisions logged via tracing (ops surface).
notes: FRESH-EYES AMENDMENT: implement R2 from the Q1 spec — the tier policy sorts live segments by docid lo-bound and merges ONLY bound-consecutive runs in that order; cross-shard merges are the expected common case. Add property test: after arbitrary interleaved multi-shard ingest + random policy-driven merges, the manifest's covering intervals remain pairwise disjoint (the invariant that would break without R2). comments.author: cc
comments.text:
DEFER (correct, workload-gated) — shared cross-task rank cutoff (the E8 follow-up flagged in collect_sealed_segments' doc-comment).

MECHANISM: today each fan-out task prunes only against its OWN per-segment local cutoff (argus.rs collect -> competitive_cutoff_score -> refill_with_cutoff -> MaxScore/BMW block-skip at ~3896). A shared atomic floor = max over tasks of their local k-th-best score would let every task prune more aggressively.

RANK-SAFETY (proven, so it CAN be built safely): for any task i with >=k collected, its local k-th-best L_i <= the GLOBAL k-th-best, because a subset's k-th-largest is always <= the superset's k-th-largest. Therefore max_i(L_i) <= global k-th-best, so using max_i(L_i) as the pruning floor never drops a true global winner, and it is >= every local L_i so it prunes at least as much. Implement as an AtomicU64 packed-key initialized to u64::MAX, fetch_min on each task's heap peek, read as min(local_key, shared.load()) at the argus.rs:~3896 cutoff site.

WHY DEFERRED, NOT IMPLEMENTED NOW: the benefit requires cross-segment score SKEW (some segments hold systematically better docs so their local floor lifts the others). The realistic fan-out bench segment_fanout_ab draws vocabulary UNIFORMLY across all segments (xorshift % 24), so every segment's score distribution is statistically identical -> shared floor ~= each local floor -> ~zero extra pruning. Same shape as the just-rejected e5.6 expansion memo (correct but marginal on uniform workloads). Measuring it would require an artificial skewed corpus.

RETRY PREDICATE: implement when a real/representative workload has cross-segment score skew (e.g. recency-weighted or tiered segments where newer/one tier dominates the top-k), OR to reduce concurrent-fan-out CPU under throughput load. Then gate a KEEP on a skewed-corpus two-binary instruction A/B with the rank-safety invariant asserted (fanned page == serial page) and no regression on the uniform corpus.

So the accumulated Vec is already strictly-ascending + duplicate-free, and finish()'s unconditional sort_unstable + dedup is redundant. Tried: 'if self.docs.is_sorted_by(|l,r| l<r) { return self.docs } else { sort_unstable; dedup }' — byte-identical (runtime check + identical fallback; bench serial==fanned docid parity held) and the fast-path IS taken (NEW < OLD confirms).

MEASURED (two-binary instruction A/B, segment_fanout_ab smoke rounds=5, RAYON=1): OLD 37,643,480,019 vs NEW 37,640,709,445 = -0.0074% (noise floor). WASH: at smoke the docid result sets are ~1000 ids so finish() is a negligible fraction of the decode-dominated unscored scan; and because segments are docid-ordered the input is already globally sorted, so sort_unstable (pdqsort) short-circuits to O(n) anyway — the only real saving is the O(n) dedup pass. Reverted.

The engine is decode-bound everywhere and the decode is floored (bd-b6tc/bd-udz8, cod's SIMD lane); every architectural fan-out lever touches a small non-decode fraction. title: quill-e5.2: Epoch/Arc-swap snapshot publication
description: Lock-free read visibility (plan §6.3, §12.1): each applied batch atomically swaps the shard's published delta snapshot (Arc swap; readers clone the Arc, never lock); a search Snapshot = current MANIFEST generation's sealed segments + tombstones + all shards' delta snapshots + aggregated snapshot-level BM25 stats (N/avgdl/doc_freq adjustments from delta contents — delta terms contribute to doc_freq/N so scores stay consistent pre/post seal; pin with a fixture: score(doc) identical the instant before and after its segment seals, within RankExact). Generation retirement: old snapshots drop when Arc count drains; segment file deletion deferred until then (drop-guard, tested in e3.9). Tests: read-during-write consistency (LabRuntime schedules), snapshot immutability (a held snapshot never sees later writes), stats-consistency fixture above.
notes: FRESH-EYES PASS 3: delta stats must EXCLUDE delta-tombstoned docids (a doc upserted/deleted while still delta-resident never existed durably — e5.4 does not emit it at seal), so per-term delta doc_freq counts LIVE delta docs only. Rationale: this makes seal a stats no-op (score(doc) identical the instant before/after seal — the existing fixture), whereas sealed-then-deleted docs stay IN stats until compaction (mirroring tantivy, e4.3 notes). Add a repeated-upsert-in-delta stats test: upsert the same DocId 3x within one delta, assert doc_freq contribution is exactly 1 and scores match the post-seal state. Also: snapshot composition = current MANIFEST generation (e3.2) + shard delta snapshots — dep edge added. DUEL RIPPLE (bd-quill-duel-visibility-contract): the epoch-published delta snapshot is PROCESS-LOCAL — 'searchable immediately' holds in-process only; cross-process readers see published generations. title: quill-e5.4: Seal path (drain -> radix build -> FSLX)

comments.author: cc
comments.text:
REJECT (measured, marginal) — string Range/Glob term-expansion snapshot memoization. This bead-comment is the ledger-of-record (docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md has another agent's uncommitted rows I won't entangle).

FINDING: Implemented the snapshot-scoped lazy memo (std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<(field,bounds/pattern,limit)->Arc<Vec<Vec<u8>>>>>) on the immutable QuillSearchSnapshot; compute-under-lock so the first fan-out leaf fills and the rest reuse. Byte-identical: full quill lib 473/473 pass incl. tantivy-oracle differential + range/glob; clippy clean. Cache verified HITTING via instrumented counters: per distinct string-range probe, 1 COMPUTE + 7 HIT across the 8 leaves (exactly the intended O(M^2)->O(M)).

MEASUREMENT (deterministic perf stat -e instructions, two-binary OLD@HEAD vs NEW, isolated targets, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1, 8 sealed segments, 32 distinct 64-term content:[lo TO hi] probes once each = honest within-query M->1, build-only baseline subtracted):
  OLD sweep 53,158,025,682  vs  NEW sweep 52,467,454,424  =>  NEW -1.30% (decidable, but marginal).

WHY MARGINAL: perf profile of the range query is ~82% term-DICTIONARY DECODE that is the expanded-term-set SCORING (lower_leaf_string_predicate -> 64x lower_leaf_term dictionary lookups per leaf x 8 leaves: decode_entry 41% + read_vint_multibyte 20% + validate_block 15%), which is per-leaf-INHERENT and NOT cacheable. The snapshot expansion itself (range_cursor enumerate + open_dictionary) is only ~0.2% of the query, so removing its (M-1)x redundancy nets ~1.3% at M=8. Scales with segment count M, but large indexes cross the fan-out gate where the redundancy is parallel-overlapped CPU waste, not wall-clock.

NOTE: the DefaultQueryParser does NOT lower bare '*sub*' globs to a content Query::Glob (that is CASS-parser behavior via regex_fields); glob only reaches snapshot_glob_terms through the CASS/shadow path. Verified by instrumentation (0 GLOBCOMPUTE for '*2000*').

DECISION: reverted the cache (byte-identical but below the perf bar); no code shipped. RETRY PREDICATE: only if (a) a real workload profiles snapshot_string_range_terms/snapshot_glob_terms as a >=1% hotspot (e.g. very high segment count on the serial path, or leading-star CASS globs that full-scan huge dictionaries with few matches), or (b) pursued as throughput/CPU-waste reduction under concurrent fan-out load rather than single-query latency. The OTHER e5.6 part (persist numeric fast columns) is untouched and remains the substantive architectural work.

title: quill-e6.3: Metamorphic suites
description: Implement qualified metamorphic laws at both Quill-internal and Quill-versus-pinned-Tantivy boundaries. Each law declares preconditions, observable projection, equivalence relation, allowed divergence/tie law, corpus/query generator, shrinker, and whether it applies cross-engine. Required document/index transforms: input-order permutation with stable external doc IDs; duplicate ingest under declared upsert/dedup semantics; duplicate-then-delete where that sequence is contractually never-added; upsert versus delete+add; flush-budget and segment-geometry perturbation; merge schedule and reopen/recovery perturbation; tombstone/compaction schedule. Query transforms: analyzer-declared whitespace/case normalization, Boolean associativity/commutativity only where scores/order are semantically invariant, single-term quote equivalence only on position-capable fields, and positionless capability errors. Do not label a transform semantics-preserving merely because it is convenient. Every failing seed shrinks to a bounded fixture and emits a redacted replay artifact registered as fixed, accepted with rationale, or blocking.
design: Represent laws as data plus typed runner hooks. Precondition failures are SkipWithReason, not passes. Compare through the total LexicalObservation contract and use field-specific equivalence laws. Run each applicable law against Quill, Tantivy, and cross-engine compositions to distinguish engine defects from invalid laws.
acceptance_criteria: Every required law has explicit preconditions, observable projection, equivalence relation, positive fixture, intentionally invalid negative fixture, seeded property campaign, shrink/replay test, and applicability matrix. CI PR and nightly campaigns have fixed budgets and upload bounded replay artifacts on failure. Positionless and tie cases are qualified correctly. No skip is counted as a pass. All unexplained divergences enter the versioned Divergence Register.

  (a) duplicate the harness in my file -- I am not doing this. A second, independently drifting copy of the observation harness is precisely what makes cross-engine differential results untrustworthy, and it would be a silent fork of the total-lexical contract.

Those are pure functions over a seed and a corpus size. ## The gap I am proposing to own: BOOLEAN ASSOCIATIVITY
`rg -i associativ` over crates/frankensearch-quill-gauntlet/src returns ZERO hits. The registry's
required-law set (runner.rs:9151) has no associativity entry. The bead's acceptance text requires
"Boolean associativity/commutativity only where scores/order are semantically invariant" -- so
commutativity alone does not satisfy it.

This is not an oversight I am second-guessing: it was a deliberate deferral. The OR law's own doc
comment says the law "excludes association, boosts, and mixed occurrences because those shapes can
expose parser or score-accumulation behavior." Two-term commutativity structurally CANNOT express
associativity, which needs three operands. It belongs to neither existing partition: not an
index-maintenance family (pane 11), and not in the ten-family list pane 3 reconciled as 8/8.

Proposed law IDs:
  e6.3-three-term-and-associativity-v1   -- (A AND B) AND C  ==  A AND (B AND C)
  e6.3-three-term-or-associativity-v1    -- (A OR B) OR C    ==  A OR (B OR C)

## How I will qualify it -- the part that matters
I will NOT declare associativity score-invariant because it is convenient. The existing doc comment
warns precisely that nested grouping can change score accumulation, and the bead says "Do not label
a transform semantics-preserving merely because it is convenient."

So the equivalence relation is an OUTPUT of measurement, not an input:
  1. Measure both groupings live on Quill and Tantivy across a seed matrix.
  2. If the total lexical observation diverges only by TieOrder, the law is "rank exact or tie order

     scores excluded -- stated in the descriptor's preconditions, or (b) if the engines disagree
     with each other, a Divergence Register entry per the acceptance criteria, and the law lands
     qualified rather than green.
  Whichever of those the measurement supports is what I will land, and I will report the measured
  result either way. A law that turns out to be weaker than hoped is a result, not a failure.

Planted-invalid negative: re-associating across MIXED operators -- (A AND B) OR C vs A AND (B OR C)
-- which is genuinely not equivalent and must fail. That is the counterexample that proves the
positive law is not vacuous.

observable projection binding, equivalence relation, positive fixture, planted-invalid negative,
seeded property campaign, shrink/replay, applicability matrix. One commit per law.

  a_planted_corpus_mutation_makes_the_reopen_recovery_law_fail

e6.3-tombstone-compaction-v1 -- 8/8

  the_tombstone_capability_flip_is_earned_by_a_witnessed_compaction
  a_failing_tombstone_fixture_shrinks_and_still_reproduces_live
  compaction_restores_never_added_statistics
  without_the_compaction_step_the_total_projection_diverges

TWO FINDINGS THAT CHANGED MY OWN EARLIER POSITION, both stated because they revise things I wrote on this bead.

1. REOPEN SCOPE, NARROWED AND MEASURED. My generator let the seed decide whether to flush before a reopen, on the reasoning that an unflushed reopen "exercises recovery of buffered state". That was wrong about the contract. Uncommitted ingest is not durable, so such a reopen returns an index missing those documents and the law would fail for a durability reason it does not name. Reopen is now qualified to committed boundaries; the exclusion is MEASURED (an_uncommitted_reopen_loses_the_buffered_documents: the reopened instance reports 0 documents), pinned structurally (every_reopen_follows_a_flush_of_the_batch_before_it), and enforced during shrinking (an out-of-scope reduction is refused before it is executed, so a replay artifact cannot reproduce a different bug than the one being shrunk). What this LOSES is the uncommitted-reopen case, which this law never had standing to judge; what it KEEPS is every reopen the law is actually about.

2. THE TOMBSTONE BLOCKER IS DISCHARGED BY COMPACTION, so the law does NOT need the narrowed projection I proposed. The ScoreSensitiveCorpusStatistics skip was well founded for a bare delete -- the earlier probe on this bead saw a survivor's score bits move from 402a35ec to 40082c9c comparing delete against never-added. But the transform this law names is tombstone AND compaction, and a real compaction folds the tombstones out of the corpus statistics too. Measured across the whole seed matrix, a compacted index is identical to a never-added corpus under the TOTAL lexical observation, zero divergences (compaction_restores_never_added_statistics). The control that stops this being a property of the fixture: drop only the Compact step and the divergences come back (without_the_compaction_step_the_total_projection_diverges), with membership still agreeing -- deleting is not losing.

So the law binds to the TOTAL projection, exactly like merge and reopen, and admits only TieOrder. I built the score-insensitive membership projection for the fallback case and it stays as DIAGNOSTIC evidence only -- it separates "membership broke" from "scores drifted" when a failure occurs, and both planted-invalid controls assert it catches resurrection and loss without leaning on score bits. Binding the law to it would have given up coverage this engine has earned. The capability field is renamed score_insensitive_projection -> compaction_statistics_parity so it names what a runner must actually declare; the registry's skip REASON is still correct for a runner that deletes without compacting, which is why I have not touched it.

FOR THE MATRIX / YOUR FLIPS. On this evidence all three descriptors are flippable to Applies, with these preconditions now executable rather than prose: deterministic merge scheduling (witnessed merge), durable reopen lifecycle (witnessed recovery), compaction statistics parity (witnessed compaction plus total-projection parity). MaintenanceRunnerCapabilities defaults every field to false, so nothing flips by accident, and a_runner_declaring_nothing_reproduces_the_registry_skips still pins the current registry state.

VERIFICATION. The shared checkout has not compiled for much of this session (peer WIP; earlier native_enriched_witness.rs:2172, since landed). Everything below was verified via the sanctioned shadow route -- git archive HEAD into /data/projects/frankensearch-shadow-rm3q3, overlay only my three files, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/cargo-target (no per-task target dir), TMPDIR in the session scratchpad:

  cargo clippy -p frankensearch-quill-gauntlet --features perf-harness --lib --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings
  => zero diagnostics in my three files.
  rustfmt --edition 2024 --check on all three => clean. git diff --check => clean.

PRE-EXISTING RED, not mine and not touched: cargo clippy -p frankensearch-quill-gauntlet --features perf-harness --lib --tests -- -D warnings fails on crates/frankensearch-quill-gauntlet/src/runner.rs:8118 "unused import: Read", introduced by 5d785aa6 (2026-08-02, fix(gauntlet): compile executable identity tests with all features). It reproduces on pure HEAD with none of my files overlaid. My files are clean under the same command; benches are excluded from that lane because perf_matrix.rs carries two further pre-existing lints (significant_drop_tightening at :219, unnecessary_semicolon at :5191).

ONE COMMIT, NOT THREE, and why. The three families share one step executor, one witness struct, and one file; splitting them into three commits would produce checkpoints that do not compile without each other's code, which is worse in a shared checkout than one commit whose message and tests are per-law. The per-law evidence is this comment.

## LANDED: e6.3-three-term-and-associativity-v1 (236f6e75, descriptor fix 69f56c3f)
Full 8 components. Verified on the shadow tree (shared checkout does not compile; peer WIP in
native_enriched_witness.rs), CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/cargo-target, never a per-task dir:
6 passed / 0 failed (2 associativity + 4 registry). Citing N passed, not the word ok.

THE MEASUREMENT CHANGED THE LAW. My first draft declared "rank exact or tie order only" by
analogy with the commutativity pair. That would have been FALSE. At seed 0xe63a55dc0aa5eee,
operands (alpha, gamma, delta), Quill returns the SAME document at the SAME rank with a score
one ULP apart: doc-4@3fdc09b7 vs doc-4@3fdc09b6. Re-association changes the order of finite
additions. So the law compares under the reviewed two-ULP DIV-007 summation-association
envelope and admits RankExact | TieOrder | ScoreEpsilon. The commutativity laws' doc comments
were right to warn that association "can expose parser or score-accumulation behavior".

RED PROOF that the widened class set did not neuter the law: with an operand-drop mutation and
both the precondition and replay guards bypassed so the mutation reaches the comparison, the
seed matrix fails as RankMismatch + CountMismatch.

SCOPE DISCLOSURE, needs a ruling: ScoreEpsilonReason::SummationAssociation is documented as
covering "the fused Quill multi-field scorer and the pinned oracle" -- a CROSS-ENGINE pairing.
This law applies it WITHIN one engine, to two spellings of the same query. Same mechanism,
different reviewed scope. Flagging rather than silently widening an owner-ruled envelope
(bd-55mvg). If DIV-007 is cross-engine only, this law needs its own reviewed reason and I will
take that follow-up.

## NOT LANDED: e6.3-three-term-or-associativity-v1, and why I did not force it
Written, run, and then REMOVED from the working tree rather than committed. Registering a law
as Applies whose test cannot run would be a false coverage claim, and the two ways to make it
green were both forbidden:
  - picking friendlier operands = fixture-fitting to dodge a real divergence;
  - relaxing the shared harness's cross-engine exactness = weakening a gate 10+ other laws
    depend on.

## THE ACTUAL FINDING: a cross-engine divergence on a plain 3-clause OR, no transform involved
The OR law died inside the SHARED harness, not in its own relation. e63_observations_with_config
(engine.rs:3196) asserts the Quill-vs-Tantivy comparison is ComparisonStatus::Exact for every
case it runs, using ComparatorConfig::default() -- i.e. WITHOUT the DIV-007 envelope.

Reproducer, exact:
  corpus: the standard scalar G1A five-document fixture
    doc-1 "alpha beta beta"/guide, doc-2 "alpha gamma"/"alpha overview",
    doc-3 "beta gamma gamma gamma"/alpha, doc-4 "alpha beta gamma delta"/reference,
    doc-5 "delta epsilon"/quiet
  query: (alpha OR gamma) OR delta        <-- the BASELINE spelling, un-transformed
  result: cross-engine RankMismatch at /comparison/subject/hits/2,
          oracle doc-4@3fdc09b6 vs subject doc-4@3fdc09b7 -- one ULP, same document, same rank.
  control: (alpha OR beta) OR gamma passes cross-engine cleanly, so this is operand-specific,
           not a blanket OR problem.

This is DIV-007's mechanism in its ORIGINAL documented scope -- Quill's fused multi-field scorer
versus the pinned oracle associating equivalent finite additions differently. It is not caused by
associativity; my fixture merely reached an operand triple no existing E6.3 fixture covers. Per
the acceptance criteria ("All unexplained divergences enter the versioned Divergence Register")
this belongs in the register; routing to rm3q.8.1.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE HARNESS, pane 3's call: any future law whose fixture happens to surface a
legitimate 1-ULP cross-engine difference will die inside e63_observations before its own
equivalence relation is ever evaluated. The harness's cross-engine precondition is strictly
stronger than the DIV-007 envelope the project has already reviewed and accepted. I am NOT
changing that shared assert unilaterally. If you want the OR law, the options are (i) admit the
DIV-007 envelope in the shared cross-engine assert, or (ii) give the harness a per-case opt-in.
Say which and I will implement it; otherwise the OR law stays unlanded and this divergence stands
on its own as the result.

## HANDOFF NOTE FOR PANE 11 (TealSnow), unsolicited but relevant to your stated blocker
Your tombstone-compaction family is blocked on ScoreSensitiveCorpusStatistics needing "a
score-insensitive projection". Worth checking whether Quill COMPACTION discharges that directly:
a bare delete moves corpus statistics so survivors legitimately shift, but a COMPACTED index can
match the never-added corpus exactly, which would remove the need for a narrowed projection
rather than requiring one to be approved. I have not measured it in your lane and am not
claiming it -- flagging it because it would turn a 4/8 blocked family into a measurable one.

## Provenance nit, unchanged from my proposal, still pane 3's file
runner.rs and engine.rs disagree on three law-ID spellings (positionless-phrase-capability vs
positionless-capability; bulk-publication-cadence vs bulk-publish-cadence;
duplicate-live-id-rejection vs duplicate-id-reject). Different namespaces, nothing vacuous, but a
replay artifact cannot be string-matched to its descriptor. My two laws use the same string in

comments.author: LavenderElk
comments.text:
LavenderElk INTENT + STOP NOTICE on the E6.3 cross-engine harness assert, 2026-08-04.
Posted BEFORE any edit, per the gate-change price. Pane 3 (SandyTern) owns this surface.

## THE ASSERT AND ITS BLAST RADIUS
crates/frankensearch-quill-gauntlet/src/engine.rs:3196, inside
e63_observations_with_config:
    assert_eq!(run.comparison.status, ComparisonStatus::Exact,
               "E6.3 cross-engine case {case_id}: {:?}", run.comparison.divergences);
The harness is constructed with ComparatorConfig::default() -- zero tolerance. There are 32
e63_observations* call sites carrying 13 distinct E6.3 law IDs, so every law's cross-engine
check flows through this one assert.

## I WAS AUTHORIZED TO MAKE IT ADMIT DIV-007 BY DEFAULT. I AM NOT DOING THAT.
The price required citing the reviewed DIV-007 register entry as the authority rather than
convenience. I read it, and it rules against the blanket change in its own text.

docs/contracts/quill-divergence-register.md:257 (DIV-007, owner ruling 2026-08-03, delegated to
SandyGrove, recorded in mail thread bd-55mvg, committed c4fd7369):
    "The comparator's default config REMAINS zero-tolerance; campaign lanes covering composite
     shapes opt in with the typed reason."
A blanket change to the shared assert is exactly the thing that ruling forbids. Citing DIV-007 as
authority while contradicting DIV-007's ruling would be the inverse of the discipline that was
asked for.

The ruling also prescribes the alternative, and there is already precedent for it in-tree:
runner.rs:19122 builds its OWN DifferentialHarness with
ComparatorConfig::default().with_score_epsilon_reason(SummationAssociation), and artifact.rs:5902
does the same with PlatformLibm. The sanctioned pattern is per-lane opt-in.

SO WHAT I INTEND TO LAND, as its own commit, never bundled with a law:
an opt-in seam on the harness -- an e63_observations variant that accepts the comparator config
(or a typed reason) -- so a lane that needs the envelope opts in explicitly while the default
path for the other 12 laws stays byte-for-byte zero-tolerance. Expected win/lose split: ZERO
existing rows change, because no existing law opts in. I will still re-run the full suite before
and after and publish the comparison rather than assert that.

## SECOND FINDING, AND IT IS A SELF-CORRECTION ON WORK I ALREADY LANDED
Reading the register also undercuts the envelope citation in my own AND-associativity law
(236f6e75, descriptor 69f56c3f). I disclosed a scope caveat in that commit -- that
SummationAssociation is documented cross-engine and I applied it within one engine -- but the
register is more specific than I represented, on TWO axes:

  DIV-007 as recorded is (a) CROSS-ENGINE: "Quill's Term scorer ... the pinned oracle expands
  every unfielded term into a two-clause boolean"; and (b) scoped to composite shapes --
  ">=8-leaf pure-disjunctive", "a single top-level leaf boost", or "mixed-occur nesting", with
  the explicit boundary "Pure-disjunctive spliceable shapes are bit-exact under the flatten and
  stay OUTSIDE this class."

My AND law's divergence is WITHIN one engine (two spellings of the same query on Quill) and
CONJUNCTIVE at 3 leaves. That is outside the recorded envelope on both axes. Calling it DIV-007
is proof-class inflation and I am retracting that classification rather than defending it. The
measurement stands -- re-association really does shift a Quill score by 1 ULP at operands
(alpha, gamma, delta) -- but the class I bound it to is not authorized to cover it.

Three ways to correct it, and the choice is a reviewer's, not mine:
  (i) a new register entry for within-engine Boolean re-association ULP shifts, reviewed, and the
      law cites that;
  (ii) the law declares a score-insensitive projection (matched set + rank order, scores
       excluded) so no tolerance class is needed at all;
  (iii) the law goes SkipWithReason until (i) or (ii) is settled.
I lean (i) because the effect is real, reproducible and bounded, and hiding it behind a
score-insensitive projection would discard a genuine measurement. But I am not classifying my own
divergence into an owner-ruled register unilaterally -- that is how a tolerance class quietly
grows to cover whatever needed covering.

## AND IT GETS MORE INTERESTING FOR THE OR CASE
My registered OR divergence (rm3q.8.1: "(alpha OR gamma) OR delta", cross-engine, doc-4
3fdc09b6 vs 3fdc09b7) is 3 leaves, depth-1 grouping, pure Should, no boosts. By the register's
own boundary that is a "pure-disjunctive" shape which should be "bit-exact under the flatten" and
OUTSIDE DIV-007. It is not bit-exact. So either that shape is not spliceable in the sense the
entry means, or the entry's stated boundary is too strong. I have NOT resolved which and I am not
asserting the register is wrong on the strength of one fixture -- but whoever owns bd-55mvg should
know that a 3-leaf pure-disjunctive shape reproduces a 1-ULP cross-engine divergence, because the
entry currently claims that class of shape does not.

## WHAT I AM DOING NEXT
Implementing the opt-in seam only, as its own commit, with the before/after suite comparison
published. I am NOT landing OR associativity on top of it until the classification question above
is answered, because the law would have to cite a class whose authority does not currently cover
its shape -- which is the same defect I am retracting from the AND law. Say which of (i)/(ii)/(iii)
you want and I will implement it for both laws.

title: quill-e6.4: Dynamic public-behavior census and engine-parameterized conformance harvest
description: Replace the stale 90-test target with a reproducible census of the CURRENT incumbent and public lexical contracts. Inventory every test and every public observable at the pinned pre-flip revision; classify each as engine-visible and ported, oracle-internal with documented retirement rationale, duplicate covered by a named shared case, or unresolved blocker. title: quill-e6.6: Statistical conformance and retrieval-quality gates with fixed lower-bound decisions
description:
Unify the campaign statistical-quality work into one source of truth; this subsumes duplicate bd-wfhv.

INPUT CONTRACT: use the exact same pinned corpus/query set/qrels for Quill and the pinned Tantivy oracle. Record corpus, query-set, qrels, generator, engine revision, seed, and executable hashes. Report required slices: identifier, short_keyword, natural_language, path_heavy, code_symbol, real-prose, and CASS-profile.

METRICS:
- Conformance pass rate per query class with exact mismatch classes.
- nDCG@10, MRR, Recall@10 and Recall@100, MAP@10, and Kendall tau/RBO rank agreement; per query and aggregate for both engines plus Quill-minus-Tantivy delta.
- Seeded bootstrap confidence intervals (minimum 2,000 resamples) and Beta-posterior interval for binary conformance where applicable. Decision uses the conservative confidence bound, never a point estimate.
- Preserve raw precision in JSON; human tables may render six decimals. A stable schema/version distinguishes raw from rendered values.

PREDECLARED FLIP RULE: lower 95% bootstrap bound on delta nDCG@10 >= -0.005 in every required slice; lower bounds for MRR and Recall do not cross their registered tolerances; no individual query regresses by >0.05 nDCG without a reviewed Divergence Register entry containing a reproducible fixture and rationale. Exact rank equality is not required when a registered tie law explains it.

RUN VALIDITY: pre-gates reject missing qrels, mismatched corpora, insufficient queries, invalid/duplicate IDs, non-deterministic seeds, or unstable/noisy runs. Rejected runs are still retained as diagnostics but never ratchet baseline state. Ratchet lower bounds cannot regress without a reviewed register entry.

TESTS/LOGGING: metric golden vectors; bootstrap determinism and coverage tests; synthetic known-better/equal/worse engine pairs; per-slice empty/insufficient cases fail closed; artifact schema round-trip; corpus/query/qrels hash mismatch tests; rank-tie metamorphic cases; real Quill/Tantivy e2e. Logs provide progress, sample/query counts, hashes, seed, interval method, decision thresholds fixed before execution, worst queries with redacted bounded diagnostics, and final allow/block reasons.
design:
Freeze a versioned quality-gate manifest and commit corpus/query/qrels/generator hashes before candidate output is inspected. Hard behavioral conformance remains zero-unexplained-mismatch. Quality uses paired query/topic-level hierarchical bootstrap, fixed seeds and both query-weighted and class-macro estimands. Numeric lower-95% bounds are: delta nDCG@10 >= -0.005, delta MRR >= -0.005, delta MAP@10 >= -0.005, delta Recall@10 >= -0.010 and delta Recall@100 >= -0.005 in every required slice. RBO@10 lower bound >=0.98 after registered tie normalization; Kendall tau is reported per query and slice, with any negative outlier reviewed rather than averaged away. No individual query may lose >0.05 nDCG without a reproduced register entry.

Qrels are authored independently of both engines. Real-prose and CASS slices use blind human adjudication, recorded inter-rater agreement and a deterministic conflict-resolution rule. Held-out queries are never used to tune Quill. The manifest defines no-relevant-document handling, family-wise multiplicity across slices/metrics and minimum independent topic/query counts from a pre-run power/sensitivity analysis. Repeated documents or timing iterations are never pseudo-replicates.
acceptance_criteria: Zero unexplained total-contract mismatches. A committed pre-run manifest contains exact numeric tolerances, qrels/query/corpus/generator hashes, independent sampling unit, power-derived minimum slice size, estimands, >=2000 resamples, seeds, held-out partition, no-relevant policy and multiplicity correction before candidate results. Qrels are engine-independent; real-prose/CASS blind adjudication records inter-rater agreement/conflict resolution. Scorecard reports per-query, query-weighted and class-macro metrics for both engines, paired deltas/intervals, effective sample counts, worst-query/register links and raw f64 JSON. Synthetic correlated/nested/better/equal/worse/tie/no-relevant fixtures validate decisions, prevent pseudo-replication and reproduce bit-for-bit under the same seed.

title: quill-e6.7: Fusion end-to-end quality (hybrid pipeline)
description: Verify the real persisted hybrid pipeline end-to-end with Quill versus pinned Tantivy as interchangeable lexical arms. Use identical corpus, real semantic embeddings/index generations, query set, fusion configuration, metadata hydration, filters and reranker policy. Cover lexical-only fallback, semantic-only, quality-only, full progressive, partial quality coverage, negation filtering, sync and async searchers, empty/error paths, restart/reopen, and per-arm contribution attribution. Measure per-query and slice nDCG/MRR/Recall plus rank agreement and paired intervals under the E6.6 statistical contract. RRF rank-only intuition is a hypothesis, not proof: trace any fused divergence to exact lexical/semantic/candidate-budget/filter/hydration stage through total observations. Persist evidence with engine/model/index/corpus/config/binary hashes and bounded redacted diagnostics.
design: Use the facade/public pipeline, not direct rrf_fuse calls as the sole proof. The same test matrix swaps only the lexical backend. Capture stage observations sufficient to localize first divergence without leaking content. Run an optimized real-model lane and a deterministic synthetic fast lane; neither may silently skip required coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Persisted fresh-process Treasure Island plus scaled synthetic/repo/CASS corpora run through both lexical backends and real hybrid orchestration. All topology/fallback/filter/restart modes have explicit expected requested/realized semantics and contribution metrics. Hard contract mismatches are zero or registered blockers; statistical quality meets predeclared E6.6 bounds in every required slice. Evidence pins all revisions/configuration/digests, localizes first divergence, is redacted, and is uploaded on pass or failure.

title: quill-e6.8: Divergence Register population + review workflow
description: FOUNDATION AND CONTINUOUS INTAKE FOR THE VERSIONED DIVERGENCE REGISTER. Own the append-only schema, validator, review projection, redaction policy, campaign ingestion API, and production population workflow used by every E6 campaign. Every observed hard-contract, rank/score, metadata/snippet/explain, error, metamorphic, fuzz, quality, or hybrid mismatch receives a stable ID, first-seen artifact hash, engine/corpus/query/generator revisions, minimized bounded fixture, classification, root cause, consumer impact, disposition and reviewer. Fixed entries retain original evidence plus fixing commit and regression test. Accepted divergences require an explicit equivalence law or consumer-impact rationale and independent fresh-eyes review; they never disappear when current runs turn green. Predicted classes are represented explicitly and can be advanced only to observed or reviewed-retired states. CI validates referential integrity from evidence and tests to register IDs, prevents orphan accepts/fixes, rejects unclassified production mismatches, and supports deterministic ingestion from each campaign. Large or plaintext reproductions remain local; committed artifacts contain minimized synthetic fixtures or hashes and bounded excerpts. This bead closes on the operational foundation and verified live ingestion, then .8.1 proves terminal completeness across all campaigns.
acceptance_criteria: Register schema/version/migration/integrity, append-only successor, review, redaction and deterministic campaign-ingestion tests pass. Production evidence, not only synthetic fixtures, proves at least one live observed mismatch can be ingested, fixed or blocked with immutable first-seen evidence, minimized fixture, exact revisions, reviewer/disposition rules and a regression link; the Basic-field term-frequency divergence is included when its exact campaign receipt lands. title: Terminal Divergence Register census: every campaign mismatch registered, fixed, or blocking
description: Keep the parent register schema/workflow immediately usable: append-only versioned entries, evidence links, mismatch class, fixture, observed and expected behavior, disposition, reviewer identity, timestamps and redacted bounded diagnostics. This terminal census waits for the full metamorphic, 90-test port, statistical scorecard, fusion E2E, structure-aware fuzzing and scaled corpus campaigns. It deterministically joins every emitted mismatch ID against the register and fails if any mismatch is absent, duplicated, silently averaged into a score, or left as an unobserved placeholder. Predicted divergence classes must be forced to observation, retired with proof or remain an explicit flip blocker. TESTS: schema migration, append-only enforcement, evidence hash/reviewer validation, mismatch-to-register census, accepted versus fixed versus blocking precedence, redaction canaries and generated human review table.

No placeholders remain without forced observation or reviewed retirement proof. Every accepted divergence has a reproducible fixture, bounded scope, rationale, reviewer and evidence hash; every unregistered or unresolved behavior mismatch blocks the flip. Generated review tables round-trip to the authoritative schema and redact source/query content.

title: quill-e6.2a: Live oracle campaign activation (default + CASS profiles)
description:
Activate the replay-verifiable E6.2 campaign core against production engines after G1a makes the scalar Quill path executable. G1a retains ownership of the first live default-profile adapter and checkpoint fast run; this bead productionizes that adapter, adds the live CASS-profile Quill adapter, and wires continuous execution against a fresh one-shot Tantivy 0.26.1 oracle.

For each profile, both engines MUST ingest byte-identical replay-verified corpus batches and acknowledge the same analyzer/schema/query contract before execution. The default profile covers term, multi-term, phrase, Boolean, paginated, and counted queries. The CASS profile covers its nonstandard Boolean grammar, structured filters, i64 ranges, and bounded Exact/Prefix/Suffix/Substring/Complex globs, with only reviewed Divergence Register entries classified.

Add a deterministic PR fast lane for changes touching Quill, lexical, fusion, gauntlet, analyzer/schema, toolchain, or campaign fixtures, plus an RCH-required nightly full lane over pinned generated and repository corpora.

Every campaign MUST stamp immutable source and semantic provenance: subject/oracle commit and dirty state, Cargo.lock hash, exact dated Rust nightly plus rustc -Vv release/commit/host, std::char::UNICODE_VERSION, the exact locked unicode-normalization version and applicable Unicode-table version, analyzer/schema/query-profile hashes, corpus/query manifest hashes, and seeds. Missing or mismatched provenance, engine fallback, infrastructure failure, or an UNCLASSIFIED divergence fails closed. CI accepts only campaigns reloaded through ArtifactStore::load_verified_campaign; detached structural report validation is not sufficient evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Production adapters
- Productionize G1a's first live default-profile Quill adapter and add a live CASS-profile Quill adapter.
- QuillSubjectStub is never used by either activation lane.
- Each campaign constructs fresh one-shot subject and oracle instances and exercises ingest -> commit/seal -> open -> parse -> score -> collect.
- Subject/oracle identities are distinct and both acknowledge the exact selected profile contract.

2. Differential coverage
- The default fixture lane covers term, multi-term, phrase, Boolean, pagination, exact count, and doc_count.
- The CASS fixture lane covers AND/OR/NOT precedence, structured filters, ranges, and every bounded glob class.
- Registered divergences require exact register-class matching; no wildcard or silent allowlisting.
- Deliberate identity, semantic-contract, provenance, infrastructure, and UNCLASSIFIED failures prove fail-closed behavior and produce no successful completion report.

3. PR fast lane
- Runs deterministic small fixture/harvested corpora for both profiles when relevant Quill, lexical, fusion, gauntlet, analyzer/schema, toolchain, lockfile, or fixture inputs change.
- Persists campaign artifacts and reloads them through load_verified_campaign.
- Any failed profile fails the CI job.

4. Nightly full lane
- Requires RCH and never falls back to local Cargo.
- Runs both profiles over pinned generated corpora and a content-addressed repository snapshot.
- Archives the complete verified campaign directory.
- A same-seed replay reproduces corpus/query manifests, report hash, and mismatch signatures.
- Record at least one successful full activation run. The E6 epic's two-consecutive-nightly requirement remains the final campaign exit gate.

5. Provenance
- Replace floating nightly with a committed dated nightly.
- Stamp and validate the Rust compiler commit/host, standard-library Unicode version, exact normalization dependency/table version, Cargo.lock hash, source revisions/dirty flags, semantic hashes, seeds, and manifests.
- Add negative tests for every missing or mismatched provenance field.
close_reason: Default and CASS production campaigns activated with exact provenance, verified reload, deterministic replay, CI lanes, and a successful strict-remote full run at 0df9e725.

Mirrors it exactly on the evidence the comparator consumes: fetches limit+tie_expansion_limit (never bare limit), retains raw score BITS and the full DocAddress (segment_ord + segment_doc_id) so TieOrder stays classifiable, computes the cutoff tie group over the EXPANDED fetch before truncating hits to k, and reports cutoff_tie_complete = total_count <= fetch_limit || last_fetched_score != cutoff_score. doc_count comes from searcher.num_docs() since CassTantivyIndex keeps no atomic counter. Plus pub fn cass_document_identity implementing the identity contract, with missing stored fields degrading to ""/0 so a malformed document surfaces as a COMPARABLE identity mismatch rather than aborting the campaign.

ONE DELIBERATE SEMANTIC DIVERGENCE from the default-profile producer, documented in the rustdoc: NO empty-query short circuit. The default profile returns an empty observation for a blank query; under CASS a blank query carrying structured filters is a legitimate FILTER-ONLY BROWSE that matches documents (see the existing all_scores fixture at cass_compat.rs ~3186), so short-circuiting would report zero hits where the engine returns a full filtered page. Whoever writes the Quill-side CASS subject adapter must match this or the empty-query case diverges immediately.

comments.author: MossySpire
comments.text:
MossySpire: CASS CONFORMANCE FACT discovered while pinning cass_oracle_observe_query, worth propagating to the Quill CASS subject adapter. CASS bare terms are PREFIX-matched, not exact. On the cass_result_fixture corpus the query 'alpha' retrieves THREE documents -- 'alpha active' (local-a#0), 'alpha deprecated' (local-b#1), AND 'alphabeta retained' (local-d#5) -- but NOT 'xalpha archived' (local-c#4), which contains the term only as an infix. The CASS schema carries dedicated title_prefix/content_prefix fields and cass_build_tantivy_query expands bare terms across them; that prefix-yes / infix-no asymmetry is the load-bearing semantic.

Consequence for the port: a subject adapter that lowers CASS bare terms to exact Term queries would still pass a naive two-hit assertion on this fixture (both exact matches are present) and be silently wrong on the third. My test asserts the full three-document prefix-expanded set precisely so that failure mode cannot pass. I originally wrote the two-hit expectation myself and the fixture caught me -- worth stating plainly so nobody 'fixes' the expectation back down.

Test cass_oracle_observation_carries_contract_identity_and_full_tie_evidence is GREEN (1 passed) on rch. Covers: source_id#msg_idx identity over the prefix-expanded set, snippets always None, native rank order, filter-only browse (empty query returns all 6 fixture docs -- no short circuit), SourceId structured filter narrowing to exactly one document, and truncation to k preserving both the cutoff tie group and a k-independent total_count.

title: QG-9 validity: prove true cold-open state and separate warm reopen/page-fault costs
description:
QG-9 must measure named open contracts under proved cache/process/fixture truth, not call an in-process reopen cold. Define at least two cells when supported: read-only searcher metadata/map open, and mutable writer/recovery open; never mix LOCK/recovery/GC/fsync work into a cell described only as manifest plus lazy sections. Hoist configuration and all artifact selection outside the timer. Each timed arm is a fresh child from the exact same attested ELF and uses one Quill root plus three byte-equivalent, inode-distinct Tantivy roots for the A/B and independent A/A null. Before every arm, sync every relevant artifact, issue platform-supported per-file cache eviction, and attest with fincore or an equivalent content-bound mechanism that all relevant pages are nonresident; otherwise persist typed NoDecision with zero admitted estimate rows. Parent verifies child PID, nonce, run/source/machine/root receipts and post-open artifact hashes. Use a predeclared 12-round balanced Latin square. Persist raw wall/CPU, major/minor faults, bytes read, peak RSS, mapping/open/first-query components and warm diagnostic reopen values.

Configured scale is not fixture truth. After build and again inside each child after open, record exact public document count for both engines, indexed live count when exposed, and a fixed nonvacuous probe digest/count; empty, partial, differing or inaccessible corpora are NoDecision. Reconstruct absolute Quill/Tantivy and A/B/A/A paired raw streams with stable block/sample IDs and run the repository metric-specific cold-open paired estimator. Admission enforces A/A center, CI width, log-MAD/dispersion, order effect, drift/carryover, sample alignment, absolute-relative reconciliation and source-to-ELF/machine/artifact provenance. Any failed prerequisite/law produces a durable typed NoDecision with diagnostics and zero promotable rows; quarantine is not a substitute.

Scheduled evidence runs only on a stable self-hosted machine identity or an explicitly predeclared, validated normalization contract justified by the same-invocation A/A null; ephemeral hosted VM identities cannot silently promote across machines. Unsupported Apple P/E cache/scheduler proof stays typed NoDecision while retaining clearly diagnostic rows.
acceptance_criteria:
Decision-grade QG-9 evidence names the reader-open and writer/recovery-open cells precisely, excludes config construction from timing, and uses independent fresh child processes over a predeclared 12-round Latin square. Four content-equivalent roots have distinct inodes; every arm has sync plus supported eviction plus content-attested zero residency, same ELF/PID/nonce/run/source/machine/root receipts, and parent post-open rehash. Post-build and post-open exact per-engine document counts equal the manifest and fixed nonvacuous query digests/counts agree; empty/partial/drifted fixtures fail. Raw absolutes and stable paired samples deterministically reproduce the persisted PairedExperimentResult and all A/A center/CI-width/log-MAD/order/drift/carryover/reconciliation laws. Any malformed receipt, cache uncertainty, copy/hash/inode collision, stale/replayed child, wrong ELF/root/machine, count/probe mismatch, estimator error, law failure or insufficient repetitions persists one typed NoDecision, no claimed speed ratio, and zero admitted rows.

Executable collector tests, not DTO-only tests, cover real copy/inode behavior, sync/fadvise/fincore or platform equivalent, fresh PID child, post-open rehash, timer boundaries, reader/writer distinction, count/nonvacuity, deterministic sample pairing, every typed failure and cancellation/timeout. Ratchet tests prove NoDecision never promotes or becomes Quarantine. Stable self-hosted scheduled execution and artifact upload on pass/fail/timeout are required. Warm/unsupported platform diagnostics remain labeled nonadmissible and cannot enter claim estimates.
