title: Add deterministic recovered-byte install and retirement crash matrix
description:
Recovered-byte installation is unit-tested for uninterrupted success/substitution rollback, but not for deterministic crash states after link/exchange, authority retirement, rollback fsync, or final directory fsync. Corrupt MANIFEST and .fec retirement also uses two renames followed by one fsync, so an interruption can leave an orphan canonical sidecar that future opens repeatedly reconsider.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add table-driven fault checkpoints after temp-file fsync, staging-link directory fsync, install link/exchange, rollback and rollback fsync, corrupt-authority retirement, and final directory fsync.
- Exercise present and absent canonical destinations, reopen twice, and prove idempotent authority selection with exact bytes.
- Model interruption between corrupt MANIFEST and .fec retirement and ensure the orphan sidecar is deterministically retired or ignored without repeated recovery ambiguity.
- Advance time beyond the grace interval and prove GC removes every .tmp-repair-*, .tmp-ready-repair-*, and .tmp-corrupt-* orphan without changing canonical bytes; a second sweep is empty.
- Run the matrix with real FEC sidecars rather than mocks.
close_reason: Landed (commit 3445415). (1) Table-driven fault checkpoints via new RecoveredByteInstallCheckpoint observer: temp fsync, staging-link dir fsync, pre/post install link/exchange, rollback exchange + rollback fsync, corrupt-authority retirement, final directory fsync (replaces the single pre-install hook; no-op observer in production). (2) 13 matrix rows x present/absent canonical destinations: post-crash authority proven per checkpoint, convergent retry, byte-stable double reopen, grace-expired GC + empty second sweep. (3) Interrupted corrupt-MANIFEST retirement: with .tmp-corrupt-manifest-* evidence and MANIFEST missing while MANIFEST.prev is valid, the orphan canonical MANIFEST.fec is retired once into a no-replace quarantine — no repeated recovery ambiguity; evidence-free sidecars (legit crash survivors) preserved. (4) GC sweep removes .tmp-repair-*/.tmp-ready-repair-*/.tmp-corrupt-* without touching canonical bytes; second sweep empty. (5) Real FEC sidecars via test_file_protector throughout — no mocks. Verified: quill 351/351 durability, 327/327 default, clippy/fmt clean, workspace green, UBS exit 0.

title: P0: resolve R1 scorer trace by exact repair or controlled-residual hypothesis
description: Consume the invocation trace and choose the evidence-supported branch. If Quill differs because of an implementation, lowering, pivot, refill, or accumulation defect, repair it and retain exact public score-bit parity. Only if the trace proves semantically equivalent physical-layout association behavior may this bead emit a narrow ControlledResidual hypothesis for downstream falsification. AST fold compatibility, one default-layout 1-ULP observation, and generic epsilon are never sufficient.
design: Emit one canonical R1BoundaryResolutionV1 bound to the V7-freeze receipt, source, corpus, query, snapshot, and trace hashes. ExactRepair binds the causal patch plus focused and broad exact replay receipts. ControlledResidual binds the precise aggregate-only hypothesis and required six-arm falsification contract. Neither variant is a waiver.
acceptance_criteria: R1BoundaryResolutionV1 is exactly one of ExactRepair or ControlledResidual, binds the V7 freeze/source/corpus/query/snapshot/trace/receipt hashes, and validates after two fresh reloads. ExactRepair reproduces both Long John Silver mismatches and proves raw score-bit parity on focused and broad campaigns. ControlledResidual proves no leaf, membership, rank, count, cutoff, metadata, snippet, explain, or error divergence and authorizes only the controlled experiment. Variant, source, trace, fixture, query, and receipt mutations fail. Bounded fresh-process JSONL includes phase/status/reason/source/Cargo.lock/ELF/corpus/query/snapshot/trace/receipt hashes, timeout, at most 10000 lines and 8 MiB, redaction canaries, failure-artifact retention, and no raw query/doc/term/vector/path/secret. title: Public strict read-only HNSW load result: distinguish native sidecar from in-memory rebuild
description: HnswIndex::load currently calls crate-private load_with_disposition and discards HnswLoadDisposition. Missing, corrupt, legacy, or source-mismatched sidecars can therefore be rebuilt in memory and returned as if the selected persisted ANN were valid; CASS cannot meet its fail-closed exact-artifact contract or report stale_ann truthfully. Expose one additive typed read-only API from frankensearch-index and the facade: either public load_with_disposition plus public non_exhaustive HnswLoadDisposition, or a stricter load_native that rejects every rebuild disposition. Preserve existing load behavior for callers that explicitly accept rebuilding. The API must not write, replace, rename, chmod, or touch mtime of the selected ANN or FSVI. Structured diagnostics use bounded codes and no paths/vector/query bytes. This is the narrow public witness needed by CASS; it does not substitute for bd-r65a's stronger persisted source-generation/content identity binding.
acceptance_criteria: Public documented typed API distinguishes a graph loaded natively from the exact selected sidecar from every in-memory rebuild path. Missing, corrupt, unsupported-version, truncated, legacy-format, same-doc/different-vector-source, wrong dimension, wrong ordered doc set, and source mismatch fixtures cannot be reported as native. A valid native sidecar stays queryable. Tests snapshot ANN+FSVI bytes, mtimes, permissions, and directory inventory before/after both success and rejection; all remain unchanged. Existing permissive load behavior remains available and separately named/documented. Index-crate unit tests, facade API compile test, CASS fresh-process present/absent/stale fallback test, strict-remote workspace check/clippy/test, rustfmt, and UBS pass with exact SHAs recorded.
notes: FrankenSearch API is on main/master at ad8e29eaa03c9f29abc472d895a0ea9bcbe04ff1; implementation commit 51feeb09 adds HnswIndex::try_load_native, which admits only a current, exact persisted native graph and returns None without rebuilding or mutating for legacy/stale/incomplete/corrupt/non-native graphs. Prior additive disposition API remains available. Strict remote evidence for the final implementation: public strict-load index tests 2/2 green on hz2 job j-29949672659354285; focused index clippy with -D warnings green on ovh-a job j-29949672659354286. Earlier facade and workspace evidence remains: facade ann compile/behavior test green on hz2 job j-29949672659354257; workspace check green on ovh-a job j-29949672659354260. UBS was run against the staged file and reported the inherited hnsw.rs baseline (47 critical heuristic hits / 1243 warnings, dominated by test expects/asserts) while its fmt, clippy, check, test-build, audit, and deny subchecks were clean; the patch introduces no production panic/unwrap surface. title: Retire public raw vector search APIs and infallible cross-tier construction
description:
PUBLIC API RETIREMENT AFTER TYPED MIGRATION. Remove every public or consumer-reachable API that accepts an untyped raw vector slice for a tiered search, applies one vector to multiple spaces, constructs a searcher infallibly, or declares compatibility from embedder ID, display name, dimension, revision string, filename, or boolean allow-mismatch switches. No backwards-compatibility shim, deprecated wrapper, dual-path constructor, relabel helper, or hidden feature flag may preserve the bypass.

A raw vector operation may exist only as a private leaf below a validated BoundQueryEmbedding and retained owner-backed tier handle. The leaf receives one exact tier view and cannot select another tier, alter identity, or outlive the retained owner. Sync, async, progressive, exact, ANN, cache, facade, fsfs, examples, package exports and CASS-facing consumer surfaces must all expose the typed fallible path. Unsupported legacy callers receive a compile error and a direct migration to typed construction rather than runtime guessing.

This bead begins only after bd-9xuj and bd-xomn.3 have migrated real production consumers. It owns final public API removal and negative policy proof, not the underlying identity types or product lifecycle tests.
design:
Delete bypasses at their definitions and migrate all callers in the same train; do not leave wrappers. Keep any unavoidable numeric kernel private to its module and reachable only through a typed owner-backed tier capability. Use compiler visibility, sealed traits and lint or policy scans so downstream crates cannot construct the leaf capability. Public builders are fallible and require validated tier bindings and requested topology.

Maintain a machine-readable inventory of forbidden signatures and symbols across workspace source, public rustdoc JSON or equivalent API inventory, feature combinations, examples and consumer dependency builds. Pin intentional private numeric kernels by exact module and signature so a broad allowlist cannot hide a new public bypass.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Public API and structural scans find zero raw &[f32], Vec<f32>, dimension-only, embedder-id-only, same-vector-two-tier, infallible searcher, allow-mismatch, relabel, legacy mutable-open, or compatibility-wrapper entry points capable of initiating search. Exact allowlisting is limited to private numeric kernels below a typed retained-owner capability.

2. Compile-fail tests prove external callers cannot construct tier search from raw vectors or standalone metadata, cannot call a private leaf, cannot reuse one typed fast value as quality, and cannot bypass the fallible builder. Positive packaged-consumer tests demonstrate the direct typed migration path without a deprecated shim.

3. Sync, async, exact, progressive, ANN, cache, facade, fsfs, examples, all aggregate features, and the CASS-facing package surface build against the raw-retired API. Full feature and consumer matrices catch feature-gated or re-exported bypasses; rustdoc or public-item inventory has no hidden alternate symbol.

4. Runtime parity tests on the migrated typed paths preserve fast-only, QualityOnly, FullProgressive, partial coverage, filters, cancellation, deterministic ordering and errors. Identity mismatch still returns before embedding, owner/index/ANN/cache access or result allocation.

5. A mutation test reintroducing each forbidden signature or public re-export makes the policy gate fail. Workspace check/test, all-features check, warnings-denied lint, formatting, API inventory, compile-fail suite, packaged consumer builds and changed-file scanning pass. Closure records exact removed symbols and consumer replacements and cannot rely on compatibility debt.

title: Producer-authenticated remote API embeddings with per-response space attestation
description: Remote API embeddings are currently admitted when ApiProvider::response_attestation returns None, and ordinary OpenAI/Gemini providers do not attest the producer or vector space. A caller-authored identity JSON proves only operator intent, not which immutable model, tokenizer, preprocessing, pooling, normalization, weights, or implementation produced this response. Same-dimension wrong-space vectors can therefore poison persistent indexes while appearing plausible. Build a production-capable trust contract that distinguishes VerifiedRemote from AssumedRemote, binds every accepted verified response to canonical space and producer identities, and never treats missing attestation as verified.
design: Consume the canonical identity and producer contracts from bd-4v5n; do not define a parallel model-revision type. Introduce an explicit trust level and strict policy at the provider boundary. VerifiedRemote requires a producer-authenticated envelope that binds request nonce or correlation, provider endpoint identity, immutable model/space fingerprint, producer/protocol revision, ordered batch shape, and the exact response payload digest. Trust may come from a pinned signed gateway or an equivalently transport-bound attestation protocol. A deterministic canary may establish an epoch only when the responding authenticated producer also binds each response to that epoch; a startup canary alone is not per-response proof. Operator-supplied identity without producer proof is AssumedRemote: it may be available only through an explicit transient exploratory API, is visibly labeled, and is forbidden for persistent indexing, comparison with verified FSVI generations, semantic-readiness claims, and durable caches. Absence, malformed fields, stale epoch, replay, key drift, wrong endpoint, payload tamper, model drift, or same-dimension wrong space returns typed UnverifiableRemoteSpace before vector admission. Cancellation cannot publish partial batches or advance an attestation epoch. Logs contain bounded safe provider labels and identity/key hashes only, never credentials, query text, response vectors, raw bodies, or sensitive URLs.
acceptance_criteria: Strict mode rejects an otherwise successful response with absent attestation; OpenAI/Gemini direct providers therefore cannot claim VerifiedRemote unless routed through a configured authenticated attester. Valid pinned per-response attestation succeeds and yields identity-bound vectors. Unit, property, protocol, and no-mock local-gateway E2E cover wrong key, key rotation, unknown schema, stale epoch, replayed nonce, changed endpoint/model/weights/tokenizer/preprocessing/pooling/normalization/dimension, batch reordering/truncation, body-digest tamper, midstream drift, cancellation, timeout, and retry. Same ID plus same dimension plus different canonical fingerprint fails before indexing/search/cache work. AssumedRemote is explicit and cannot enter any persistent FSVI, ANN, generation manifest, durable cache, or verified semantic-readiness state; exhaustive guards prove zero writes. A fresh-process test verifies terminal code/category/exit 78/non-retry and lexical fallback with zero admitted semantic scores. Bounded redaction canaries prove secrets/query/vector/raw-error bytes never reach logs or public JSON.
notes: Independent NO-SHIP audit 2026-07-26: api_provider.rs default attestation is None, OpenAI/Gemini do not override it, and api_embedder.rs admits the vectors. This terminal remote API bead is intentionally separate from bd-4v5n foundational/local identity definitions, bd-lk1g daemon protocol attestation, and bd-jbfg persisted index/search integration.
close_reason: Implemented producer-authenticated per-response remote embedding attestation with fresh Cx entropy nonces, pinned endpoint/full identity/space/provider/backend/protocol/generation contracts, exact request/response digests, replay/tamper/drift rejection, explicit transient AssumedRemote isolation, redacted typed failures, and no-mock local gateway coverage. Commit 46ebeebf; strict-remote API tests 354 passed/1 ignored; strict-remote clippy -D warnings passed; rustfmt/diff checks passed; UBS critical=0 with reviewed false-positive security heuristic skipped.

title: Retained composite GenerationSnapshot admission and exact-generation readers
description: Replace path-backed serializable active-generation state with one nonserializable Arc> that owns the exact root, authority pair, external-floor receipt, activation manifest bytes, generation descriptor, retained directory/file handles, FSVI byte owners, lexical/ANN/metadata payloads, reader pin, and bounded health facts. The query hot path obtains a prebuilt snapshot through ArcSwapOption or an equivalent lock-free owned cell; it never reconstructs component paths or mixes separately loaded model/index/current pointers. Fresh open takes shared flock, fences and resolves the exact local pair plus external floor, then opens and validates the entire immutable component closure descriptor-relatively. It rereads the identical pair/floor under shared flock before returning, performs a bounded retry on a concurrent switch, installs only the already-built Arc, and releases the lock. Old Arc snapshots remain byte-exact and queryable across later activation, root pathname replacement, rollback, repair, history pruning, and candidate failure. Fresh readers may serve an exactly externally anchored old head with explicit PendingLocalSuccessor health while mutation is frozen; missing/corrupt externally anchored newest closure, floor uncertainty, fork, or unrelated gap fails closed. Previously retained snapshots are never invalidated by later open failure. TESTS: deterministic reader/publisher barriers at every slot write/sync/floor/lock boundary; old-or-new but never mixed results; long-lived old reader after thousands of publications; root/path/descriptor replacement; component mutation after admission; shared-lock blocking; bounded retry exhaustion; floor unavailable/conflict; duplicate/consecutive/degraded slot pairs; query cancellation; cache replacement failure preserving old Arc; and real vector plus Quill plus optional ANN plus metadata search before/restart/activate/rollback. Instrumented guards prove no embedding, vector, lexical, ANN, cache, or result work occurs before admission. Logs report bounded root/authority/generation/topology hashes without paths, vectors, queries, or document text. Workspace all-feature check/test/clippy/fmt, UBS, strict remote receipts, and no-mock fresh-process evidence are required. Publication and deletion are out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh open double-resolves one local/floor authority under shared flock, owns the complete validated closure, and installs one prebuilt Arc snapshot. Concurrent publication returns old or complete new, never mixed; old snapshots remain exact across activation/path replacement/open failure/rollback. Instrumented tests prove admission precedes all search/cache work. Real restart/search E2E, workspace gates, strict remote receipts, clippy/fmt, and UBS pass.

title: fsfs upgrade-migration compatibility harness: 5 required reason codes have no emitter anywhere in the repo
description:
Discovered by an exhaustive per-MUST grep of docs/fsfs-packaging-release-install-contract.md against the repo while working bd-fsfs-cross-platform-semantic-installer-46z3u (see its 2026-08-04 audit comment; installer commits 4ca62beb + cb201e4c).

The contract's Required Reason Codes list five upgrade.migration.* codes. Unlike the release.* and install.* codes -- which at least appear in schemas/fixtures and the fsfs_packaging_contract/fsfs_upgrade_plan goldens -- these five appear NOWHERE in the repository outside the contract document itself (grep returns 0 files each):

  upgrade.migration.matrix_failed
  upgrade.migration.invariant_violation
  upgrade.migration.quality_regression
  upgrade.migration.rollback_verification_failed
  upgrade.migration.soak_budget_exceeded

They belong to the 'Upgrade and Migration Compatibility Verification Strategy' section, which is normative for all release candidates and mandates: the N-2/N-1/N/rollback version-path matrix; FSVI, FrankenSQLite, and Tantivy index-compatibility coverage against golden snapshots from prior versions; configuration-evolution warnings for deprecated keys; a fixed golden query set with an NDCG drift threshold < 0.01 on migration paths; rollback verification on every migration cycle; and a multi-GB corpus migration soak per release cycle. It also requires four artifacts per run: migration_matrix_report.json, migration_invariants_report.json, migration_quality_regression.json, migration_soak_metrics.json, plus migration_replay_command.txt.

None of that harness exists. This is explicitly NOT installer surface -- install.sh owns install.* and the two upgrade.apply.* codes, all of which are now built and tested -- so it should not be absorbed into the installer bead.

Scope: build the migration-compatibility harness and its artifacts, emitting these five codes from real failure paths, with the golden-snapshot corpus the strategy requires. Gate: a test must go RED when only the emitter under test is disabled.

Not started; filed so the gap is tracked rather than rediscovered by the next per-MUST audit.
close_reason:
DONE. All five upgrade.migration.* codes now have real emitters and tests, on origin/main.

LANDED: crates/frankensearch-fsfs/src/migration_compat.rs at 07cdf90c909ff0ee3d39b2299f75cee76e19ce38 (1048 lines) with its module registration at ff3b86d0; both verified present in origin/main:crates/frankensearch-fsfs/src/lib.rs line 34. That registration mattered: an unregistered .rs is compiled by nothing, so a module without its 'pub mod' line would have been vacuous. Surfaces held: migration_compat.rs (new) and fsfs lib.rs (one mod line). install.sh and the install.*/upgrade.apply.* surface were not touched, per this bead's scope.

BEFORE: rg across the repo excluding docs/ returned ZERO files for each of the five codes. AFTER: each returns exactly one file (the new module). Full contract census re-run at close: all 12 reason codes declared at docs/fsfs-packaging-release-install-contract.md now have at least one home outside docs/ — install.preflight.disk_space_low 6, install.verify.signature_missing 4, release.build.missing_target 3, release.package.checksum_failed 6, release.publish.asset_upload_failed 4, upgrade.apply.rollback_triggered 5, upgrade.apply.unsupported_path 6, and the five migration codes 1 each. No orphans remain. (My first version of that orphan sweep had an rg argument-order bug and errored on every code; its 'no orphans' output was meaningless, so I rewrote it and re-ran before relying on it.)

NOT STUBS — each code is emitted only from a detected condition, and each planted negative targets what a NAIVE emitter gets wrong rather than the obvious failure:
- matrix_failed: every REPORTED path passes but a REQUIRED path is absent from the report; an 'any failure?' check clears an incomplete matrix and lets an unverified upgrade path reach a release candidate. Also: hard fail without recovery guidance, hard fail on a path that must migrate automatically, duplicate rows, and a fresh install that required migration.
- invariant_violation: the invariant flag reads healthy while the SECOND migration run changes the digest (the contract requires idempotence), and a deprecated config key keeps working with NO warning — a silent semantic reinterpretation that looks exactly like success.
- quality_regression: the contract bounds DRIFT ('delta MUST be < 0.01'), so a large FAVOURABLE NDCG swing on the fixed golden query set fails too; a one-sided 'after < before - threshold' emitter waves it through. The bound is strict, so the exact threshold value fails, and a gated path with no measurement at all fails.
- rollback_verification_failed: a cycle where rollback was never ATTEMPTED — nothing failed because nothing ran, which is precisely what a 'did rollback fail?' emitter reports as clean. Unsupported rollback without operator guidance also fails.
- soak_budget_exceeded: a soak comfortably inside its wall-clock budget that peaked over its MEMORY budget, and a soak whose corpus sits below the multi-GB floor the strategy requires; both are invisible to a duration-only check.
All five contract artifacts are rendered: migration_matrix_report.json, migration_invariants_report.json, migration_quality_regression.json, migration_soak_metrics.json (only when the soak lane ran — a skipped lane publishes four artifacts, not a stub fifth), and migration_replay_command.txt.

RED PROOF with per-code isolation: each code is pushed from exactly one evaluate_* function, so the five functions partition the five codes (verified by listing every REASON_* site against its enclosing fn). Disabling all five evaluate_* calls at once took all 12 detection tests RED — matrix 2, invariant 2, quality 3, rollback 2, soak 2, artifacts 1 — while the three tests that legitimately do not depend on an emitter stayed green: a_conformant_run_emits_no_reason_code, a_skipped_soak_lane_emits_nothing, and every_contract_named_migration_code_is_declared_verbatim. Because no test can be satisfied by a different code's emitter, that single run isolates each test to its own emitter. Mutation reverted and 15/15 re-verified green.

MODELING NOTE: clippy flagged struct_excessive_bools and a derivable Eq on the first draft. I did not allow either. RollbackValidation's attempted/full_rollback_supported pair became a RollbackAttempt enum (NotAttempted, Completed, UnsupportedByDesign), which is the better model regardless — 'not attempted' and 'attempted but unsupported' are different contract outcomes and the enum makes that impossible to conflate.

GATES (RCH_WORKER=hz2, --no-default-features because fsfs cannot build on default features without the bundled potion model): migration_compat 15 passed / 0 failed; full fsfs lib 1918 passed / 4 failed; cargo clippy --no-deps -p frankensearch-fsfs --no-default-features --all-targets -- -D warnings clean; rustfmt --edition 2024 --check and git diff --check pass; commit hooks ledger selfcheck 52/52, leakcheck 2/2, gatecheck 9/9, mergecheck 3/3.

THE 4 LIB FAILURES ARE NOT MINE, classified rather than assumed: I grepped the panic field of each. Three fail on field 'fsvi.map_lock' (runtime::tests::live_vector_sink_preserves_old_vector_on_append_failure, ::search_resources_rebind_on_vector_wal_append_and_tombstone, ::watcher_preserves_old_vector_on_append_failure) — that is bd-x06p5's map-lock doctrine residual, which I reported on that bead at 04:37Z before touching any of this work. The fourth, ::model_free_guidance_requires_a_loader_capable_build, is the known loader/model-capability class. ZERO failures mention 'wal.writer_lock', so neither this module nor my earlier bd-xx286 WAL arbiter is implicated. Two of those three names look WAL-related, which is exactly why I checked the error field instead of the test name.

SCOPE BOUNDARY, stated plainly: this delivers the emitters, the detection logic, the artifacts, and the planted-negative coverage the bead's gate required. It does NOT include the golden-snapshot corpus itself (real FSVI/FrankenSQLite/Tantivy snapshots from prior released versions) or the CI lane wiring that would feed real runs into it — those need actual prior-version artifacts and a CI job, and I did not fabricate either. The module consumes a MigrationRun that such a harness would produce. If the fleet wants that corpus and lane, it should be a follow-on bead rather than an implied part of this closure.

title: Optimize vector top-k scan with tiled SIMD dot-product and branchless selection gates
description:
Background:
The existing `frankensearch/benches/search_bench.rs` benchmark includes `vector_search_topk/top10/10000`, and peer swarm work has started a `frankensearch-index` dot-product bench for the brute-force inner loop. Vector scan is the unavoidable hot path for 10k-100k local corpora before ANN thresholds or when exact recall is required.

Candidate lever family:
- Tiled/cache-sized scan over f16 mmap bytes and query lanes.
- Multi-accumulator SIMD/FMA dot-product kernels to reduce dependency chains.
- Branchless cutoff/heap gate or collect-then-select only where it beats the existing BinaryHeap path.
- Optional SoA/block layout experiment only behind a separate measurement gate; no format change unless the old/new FSVI round-trip remains bit-compatible or a migration proof exists.

Measured target workloads:
1. `frankensearch` crate: `vector_search_topk/top10/10000` from `search_bench`.
2. `frankensearch-index` crate: dot-product bench rows for 256 and 384 dims, especially f16 byte path.
3. Limit-all/hybrid corpus test only as a follow-up end-to-end confirmation after the microbench win.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Establish baseline via per-crate rch Criterion run before editing; record worker, command, git SHA, and target dir.
2. Make exactly one source-code lever per commit. No mixed layout+kernel+heap rewrite.
3. Prove behavior unchanged: dot-product correctness tests, NaN/dimension mismatch behavior, top-k ordering/tie-breaking, FSVI round-trip, and relevant crate tests.
4. Rebench on the same workload. Keep only if the decisive ratio is < 0.97 and no tracked workload regresses > 1.03.
5. If ratio is 0.97-1.03 or >1.03, revert the hunk and append the row to docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md with before/after/ratio.
6. Compare against Tantivy-class/original ledger once bd-ui41 exists; until then label results as frankensearch pre-change baseline only.

Alien/optimization mapping:
- /alien-graveyard: vectorized execution + morsel-driven parallelism (§8.2), cache-oblivious data layout (§7.2), constants-kill-you warning (§16.7).
- /alien-artifact-coding: proof obligations are numeric equivalence, deterministic ordering, and bounded fallback to current kernel.
- /extreme-software-optimization: EV score estimate Impact 5 * Confidence 4 / Effort 2 = 10.0, but implementation starts only after baseline.

title: Soft-Delete Tombstones in FSVI
description:
Implement soft-delete tombstones in the FSVI vector index format. Currently, deleting a document requires a full index rebuild. Tombstones allow O(1) logical deletion by flipping a bit in the record's flags field.

## Background

The FSVI format stores document embeddings as fixed-size records with a header containing metadata fields. Each record already has a `flags: u16` field that is currently reserved (always zero). This bead repurposes bit 0 of the flags field as a tombstone marker, enabling O(1) logical deletion without rewriting the index file.

Document deletion is a basic operation that currently requires an expensive full rebuild. For mcp_agent_mail_rust (message archival with TTL), messages expire continuously, and rebuilding the entire index for each expiration is impractical. For xf, users may want to remove specific tweets from search results without re-indexing.

## Design

### Tombstone Flag

```rust
const TOMBSTONE_FLAG: u16 = 0x0001;  // Bit 0 of the flags field
```

The tombstone is set by writing a single u16 to the record's flags offset in the memory-mapped file. This is an atomic write on all supported platforms (u16 is naturally aligned in the FSVI record layout).

### API

```rust
impl VectorIndex {
    pub fn soft_delete(&mut self, doc_id: &str) -> Result<bool, SearchError>;
    pub fn soft_delete_batch(&mut self, doc_ids: &[&str]) -> Result<usize, SearchError>;
    pub fn is_deleted(&self, record_index: usize) -> bool;
    pub fn tombstone_count(&self) -> usize;
    pub fn tombstone_ratio(&self) -> f64;  // tombstones / total records
    pub fn needs_vacuum(&self) -> bool;    // tombstone_ratio > threshold (default: 0.2)
    pub fn vacuum(&mut self) -> Result<VacuumStats, SearchError>;
}

pub struct VacuumStats {
    pub records_before: usize,
    pub records_after: usize,
    pub tombstones_removed: usize,
    pub bytes_reclaimed: usize,
    pub duration: Duration,
}
```

### Search Integration

During top-k scan, skip records with the tombstone flag set:
```rust
if self.is_deleted(record_index) {
    continue;  // Skip tombstoned record
}
```

This adds a single bit-test per record — negligible overhead (< 1ns per record). The BinaryHeap-based top-k selection naturally handles the reduced effective record count.

### Vacuum

When tombstone_ratio exceeds the threshold (default: 0.2, meaning 20% of records are deleted), vacuum rewrites the index without tombstoned records:
1. Scan all records, collecting non-tombstoned ones
2. Write to `.fsvi.new` file
3. Atomic `rename()` over the old file (same pattern as compaction)

Vacuum is semantically identical to compaction — both rewrite the index file. When WAL support is implemented (Idea 1), compaction and vacuum can be unified: compaction merges main + WAL and removes tombstones in a single pass.

### Interaction with WAL (Idea 1)

- WAL entries use the same flags field and can be tombstoned with the same mechanism
- Compaction naturally removes tombstoned entries from both main index and WAL
- A document appended via WAL and then soft-deleted will be tombstoned in the WAL, and the tombstone will be dropped during compaction

## Justification

Document deletion is a basic operation that currently requires an expensive full rebuild. Specific consumer needs:
- **mcp_agent_mail_rust**: message archival with TTL — messages expire continuously, requiring efficient deletion
- **xf**: users may want to remove specific tweets from search results (e.g., deleted tweets, blocked accounts)
- **cass**: old sessions may be archived/deleted to keep the search index focused on recent conversations

Soft-delete with tombstones provides O(1) deletion at the cost of slightly degraded search performance (scanning tombstoned records). Vacuum reclaims this overhead when tombstones accumulate.

## Considerations

- Tombstone persistence: the flags write is immediately durable (mmap'd file, fsync on next batch operation). Individual tombstone writes without fsync are acceptable because tombstones are idempotent — re-deleting is harmless.
- doc_id lookup: soft_delete needs to find the record by doc_id. The current FSVI format stores doc_id hashes in the record. A linear scan of hashes is O(n) but sufficient for individual deletes. For batch deletes, build a hash set first.
- Concurrent access: tombstone writes (single u16) are atomic on all platforms. Readers may see stale (non-tombstoned) records briefly, which is acceptable (eventual consistency for deletes).
- Vacuum threshold: 0.2 (20%) is a reasonable default. Lower values vacuum more often (less scan overhead but more I/O). Higher values tolerate more dead records.

## Testing

- [ ] Unit: soft_delete marks record, is_deleted returns true
- [ ] Unit: soft_delete returns false for non-existent doc_id
- [ ] Unit: soft-deleted records excluded from search results
- [ ] Unit: tombstone_count and tombstone_ratio calculations are correct
- [ ] Unit: needs_vacuum triggers at correct threshold
- [ ] Unit: vacuum removes tombstoned records, search results unchanged for non-deleted docs
- [ ] Unit: vacuum stats (records_before, records_after, bytes_reclaimed) are accurate
- [ ] Unit: batch delete correctly deletes all specified doc_ids
- [ ] Integration: delete + search + vacuum full lifecycle
- [ ] Integration: concurrent delete + search (no corruption)
- [ ] Benchmark: search overhead with various tombstone ratios (0%, 10%, 20%, 50%)
acceptance_criteria:
1. The feature is fully implemented according to this bead design, scope, and referenced files or modules.
2. Integration with dependent components is complete and behavior remains correct across normal and degraded flows.
3. Edge and error cases are explicitly handled with deterministic outcomes and clear reason codes or errors.
4. Unit and integration tests (and e2e where relevant) are added, passing, and include detailed structured logging assertions.
5. Performance and resource expectations in the bead are validated and documented with reproducible evidence.
6. Every explicit checklist item in the bead description is implemented and verified by automated tests or validation commands.

title: storage: make latest-schema open read-only and eliminate concurrent-open BUSY
description: A clean strict-remote reproduction at protected source 6e537b31c502d579ed88ecc5e128b4dcec0810af exposed a schedule-sensitive correctness failure in Storage::open: schema::bootstrap always enters BEGIN IMMEDIATE and unconditionally rewrites the v6 schema marker even when the database is already current. The bootstrap mutex serializes bootstrap calls, but a connection returned by one open may concurrently read while a later redundant bootstrap commits, producing FrankenError::DatabaseBusy with busy_timeout_ms=0. The prior bd-3w1.15.1 stress bead made the race observable but did not remove the redundant write. Make the established-current-schema fast path read-only, preserve migration races and rollback guarantees, and attach exact strict-remote source, lock, dependency, worker, job, and terminal evidence. This is a correctness repair; schedule-sensitive passes are not proof.
design: Use a read-only schema-version preflight before any write transaction. If current_version equals SCHEMA_VERSION, return immediately without BEGIN IMMEDIATE, schema-marker mutation, WAL growth, or lock acquisition beyond the read. Treat only the typed FrankenError::NoSuchTable for schema_version as uninitialized. For missing or older schemas, begin the immediate transaction and re-read the version inside the transaction so concurrent initializers and migrators converge safely. Preserve future-version rejection and rollback after any failed commit. Remove the unconditional terminal INSERT OR REPLACE of the already-current v6 marker. Stage-label exact open, preflight, in-transaction recheck, migration, commit, rollback, and post-open failure boundaries without erasing typed Busy or Locked causes.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Precreate a valid schema-v6 database, set busy_timeout_ms=0, synchronize four threads on a barrier, and run at least 100 rounds in which every thread opens and reads current_version; every result is v6 and no Busy or Locked escapes. 2. The current-schema fast path causes no WAL frame count, WAL file size, or schema marker mutation across repeated opens. 3. A race between fresh initialization and current-schema opens converges on one valid v6 database without partial schema, duplicate migration effects, or suppressed errors. 4. Existing fresh bootstrap, every migration edge, future-version rejection, commit-failure rollback, and retry tests remain green. 5. Diagnostics preserve typed cause and stage while remaining bounded and source-free. 6. Strict-remote repetitions bind exact source SHA, Cargo.lock SHA, frankensqlite 0.1.19 checksum, worker identity, job ID, feature set, and terminal counts. The known clean failure j-29955634073961403 and schedule-sensitive pass j-29955634073961389 remain provenance, not acceptance evidence. 7. Workspace check, clippy -D warnings, formatting, focused storage tests, and UBS on changed files pass.

title: int8 two-pass: bounded-heap parallel pass-1 + find the crossover scale vs parallel exact
description:
Follow-up to bd-b5wl. BlackThrush measured the real InMemoryVectorIndex::search_top_k_int8_two_pass vs the real (parallel + bounded-heap + cutoff) search_top_k and found NO win at top-10/10k (dim256 1.22x SLOWER; dim384 noisy/inconclusive). See docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md. The int8 KERNEL is genuinely ~3x faster, but the two-pass method materializes all N int8 scores into a Vec then selects serially, while the parallel exact never materializes more than the top-k heap.

FIX: replace the pass-1 'parallel collect-all + select_nth' with a parallel BOUNDED-HEAP scan of the top (limit*mult) candidates per chunk + merge (reuse insert_candidate / merge_partial_heaps / HeapEntry with the int8 score cast to f32 — exact for |score|<2^24). This avoids the full-N materialize and matches the exact path's structure, so the 3x int8 dot win should survive.

ALSO: measure the CROSSOVER SCALE. At 10k the parallel exact is ~300us (not a bottleneck). The ADC win likely appears at 100k-1M vectors (where parallel exact slows to ms and int8 bandwidth/3x matters) and/or on the mmap FSVI path (page-fault + f16 decode overhead). Bench exact vs two-pass at N in {10k, 100k, 1M} to find where two-pass wins; only claim a win where ratio<0.97.

GATE: keep only at scales/paths where the real-method head-to-head shows ratio<0.97 with recall>=threshold; else leave as the correct opt-in foundation with no perf claim. Labels: perf, simd, vector-search, bold-verify.
close_reason: Measured: no adverse crossover -- int8 two-pass is tie-or-faster than parallel-exact at every N (500:1.24x, 2k/10k tie, 50k:1.57x; recall 1.0). Parallel pass-1 already shipped; no small-N gate warranted (full-recall short-cut 84fbfa2 covers tiny corpora). See NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md 2026-06-29.

title: Add expected-loss query budget and S3-FIFO cache replay benchmarks for progressive search
description:
Background:
frankensearch sells progressive search: initial results under ~15ms and refined results around ~150ms. README and existing profiling tests expose phase1_p95_us, phase2_p95_us, model_cache_warm_ms, model_cache_cold_ms, candidate_multiplier, and HNSW threshold as tuning surfaces. This bead targets realistic query latency and embedding/model-cache workloads, not synthetic micro-optimizations.

Candidate lever family:
- Replay benchmark for cold/warm model cache, query cache, and embedding cache hit/miss mixes.
- Expected-loss candidate budget controller: choose candidate_multiplier, quality_timeout_ms, and fast_only fallback from measured latency-vs-quality loss.
- S3-FIFO or value-aware cache admission experiment for embedding/model/query cache only after replay traces identify LRU/FIFO churn.

Measured target workloads:
1. `crates/frankensearch-fsfs/tests/benchmark_baseline_matrix.rs` query path metrics: p50/p95/p99, fast tier, quality tier, search RSS.
2. `limit_all_large_corpus_benchmark` hybrid cold/warm summaries for 3k+ docs as an e2e smoke lane.
3. A new per-crate replay bench/test must include Zipf, bursty, scan-heavy, and mixed natural-language query traces.

Acceptance criteria:
1. First commit is measurement-only if no replay harness exists: emit baseline traces and no behavior change.
2. Any adaptive policy has deterministic conservative fallback and budgeted exhaustion behavior: timeout, candidate cap, cache memory cap, and fixed-policy mode.
3. Behavior proof covers result ordering stability where policy should be transparent, explicit quality tradeoff where it is not, and regression bounds for nDCG/recall fixtures.
4. Keep only if p95 or throughput ratio vs pre-change baseline is < 0.97 on the decisive workload and quality stays within declared floor; otherwise revert and write docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.
5. Once bd-ui41 lands, every kept row also records ratio vs Tantivy-class original where meaningful.
6. Build/bench per crate only through rch and agent-specific CARGO_TARGET_DIR; do not run workspace-wide validation for the perf loop.

Alien/optimization mapping:
- /alien-graveyard: S3-FIFO (§15.1), Tail-Safe Adaptive Controller recipe, baseline comparator appendix.
- /alien-artifact-coding: expected-loss model L(action,state), conformal/drift guard, deterministic fallback trigger.
- /profiling-software-performance: cold/warm fingerprint and p50/p95/p99/RSS metrics before changing policy.

Fallback/revert:
Default static config remains the conservative fallback. If calibration data is missing, stale, or unstable, policy must use current deterministic defaults.
close_reason: Ledger-resolved, no new work needed. (1) S3-FIFO admission half LANDED b83b25d (PERF_LEDGER:2144): 4% fewer embed misses on mild Zipf, 14% fewer on scan-polluted streams; cache_replay bench kept as the AC#3 churn-identification artifact. (2) Expected-loss candidate-budget controller REJECTED on structural measurement (NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE:3546): the progressive_replay bench (kept as the AC#1 measurement-only baseline) shows phase-1 fast-tier scan is 0.498ms of a 0.508ms p50 (~98%), phase-2 ~24us (~5%), so a fast_only/skip gate saves <=5% AND is result-altering; candidate_multiplier already at its validated lossless point (mult=3, bd-t8tv). Controller would be adaptive machinery governing a 5% slice. (3) Blocker bd-ui41 CLOSED. No recorded retry-condition holds. Verified 2026-07-09 by cc_fs.

title: Restore full candidate refinement and lexical re-fusion in async TwoTierSearcher
description:
Problem:
Async phase 1 fetches and fuses candidate_multiplier times k candidates, but crates/frankensearch-fusion/src/searcher.rs truncates to the displayed top k before run_phase2. Phase 2 reconstructs fast hits only from that slice, so candidates outside Initial cannot be promoted. It also blends only fast and quality vector scores and does not retain and re-fuse the already-fetched lexical pool. The synchronous searcher retains the full pools, scores them, and re-fuses lexical results.

Acceptance:
- Keep Initial bounded to k while retaining a private full candidate pool for refinement.
- Quality-score every eligible semantic candidate in the configured budget and report that count accurately.
- Retain fetched lexical candidates and rerun the configured fusion strategy after quality blending without a second lexical query.
- Preserve lexical-only provenance, score, and deferred-metadata behavior.
- Add async regressions for candidate_multiplier promotion beyond displayed top-k and for refined ordering that requires lexical re-fusion.
- Preserve fast-only, timeout, cancellation, and refinement-failure behavior.

Evidence:
The top-k handoff is in searcher.rs around lines 767 and 831-837; phase-2 reconstruction/blending is around 1709-1758. The parity model and existing candidate-budget regression live in sync_searcher.rs around 410-545 and sync_searcher_tests.rs around 247-280.
close_reason: Phase 1 now retains full candidate pools (RefinementPools) instead of truncating to displayed top-k. Phase 2 quality-scores the full k*multiplier semantic pool (promotion beyond the Initial page) and re-fuses the retained lexical pool against blended vectors with the configured strategy — sync parity, no second lexical query. Provenance/lexical scores/hydrated metadata preserved; regressions added for multiplier promotion + lexical re-fusion. Committed 9d485d2; fusion suite 893+ green, clippy/fmt clean.

title: Unified semantic zero-signal classification: empty, tombstoned, filtered, k=0, zero-norm, and no-live-vector states
description:
ROOT DEFECT: distinct semantic no-signal states collapse to Ok(empty) or lexical-only output, so callers cannot distinguish a legitimate empty answer from an unusable semantic lane. One versioned ZeroSignalReason must cover brute-force and ANN consistently: newly created empty; never-populated; live records whose stored vectors are all zero, non-finite or otherwise unusable; all tombstoned; WAL-only/zero live; requested k=0; filter excludes all; zero/non-finite query norm; and ANN yields no candidates despite usable live vectors.

Writers reject newly supplied zero/non-finite/unusable vectors. Readers classify legacy or corrupt generations rather than panicking or silently treating them as healthy. Distinguish benign request/state reasons (RequestedKZero, FilterExcludedAll, NewlyCreatedEmpty) from availability failures (NoUsableVectors, AnnCandidateAnomaly). Carry the typed reason through tier stats, TwoTierMetrics, response degradation, doctor and RecoveryPlan. Compatibility is never inferred from empty output.

Logging is state-aware: a legitimate newly created empty index is debug/info, not an unconditional warning; availability transitions log once per generation/state; query-specific k/filter/norm events are bounded. Local diagnostics may include a safe resolved path; telemetry uses a bounded path hash.
design: Compute generation properties at validated open/reload and query-specific properties at the search boundary. Reuse one enum and semantics across exact and ANN implementations. Preserve API Ok(empty) where appropriate while explicit semantic product policy may promote unusable availability through RecoveryPlan. State transitions are first-class and persist/reload deterministically.
acceptance_criteria: Exact and ANN paths classify equivalent states identically under unit and property tests. Cover zero records, all tombstoned, WAL-only, k=0, filter-all, zero/non-finite query, usable and unusable stored vectors, ANN anomaly and normal populated match. Writers reject invalid new vectors; readers classify legacy/corrupt generations. Restart/state-transition E2E proves create -> empty search -> ingest -> search -> tombstone all -> compact/reload -> search. Benign empty states do not warn-storm; availability failures produce bounded typed diagnostics and explicit semantic versus hybrid policy is tested.
notes: TEST AND LOGGING POLICY. NewlyCreatedEmpty is valid and returns Ok(empty) with a typed machine-readable state; it emits at most a bounded info/debug transition event, never warn. CallerRequestedZeroK and FilterEliminatedAll are expected outcomes and do not warn. NoUsableVectors with live records, invalid legacy vectors, or coverage loss emits one bounded warning per generation and state transition, not per query. AnnReturnedEmptyDespiteUsableVectors is an availability anomaly with a typed warning or error according to requested semantic versus hybrid policy. Exact and ANN paths must classify identical fixtures identically. Tests cover repeated-query no-storm behavior, create-search-ingest-search, tombstone-all and compaction/reload transitions. Diagnostics include hashed index/generation identity, record, live, tombstone, WAL and usable-vector counts without query, document or unrestricted path content. TwoTierMetrics and RecoveryPlan carry the same stable code; logs are never the only signal.
close_reason: Completed: unified semantic zero-signal classification landed end-to-end (core/storage/index/fusion/fsfs + lifecycle proofs); evidence chain in final comment

comments.author: MossySpire
comments.text:
MossySpire: HANDING BACK -- the clean fix lands in files BrownCoyote holds. Design recorded so whoever takes it does not re-derive it.

WHY NOT THE TWO SITES THE BEAD NAMES. Warning inside search_top_k_internal (search.rs) or the hnsw k==0 / doc_ids.is_empty() branch fires on EVERY query against an empty index, so satisfying "exactly once" there needs per-instance state -- a OnceLock<()> field on VectorIndex, which lives in lib.rs. Doing it with a module-level static instead is either process-global (only the first empty index of a fast+quality pair ever gets named) or a global Mutex<HashSet<PathBuf>> on the search path. Both are worse than the alternative below.

BETTER DESIGN -- WARN AT OPEN, NOT AT SEARCH. An empty index is a property of the INDEX, not of a query, and it is fully known at open time. Warning there is naturally exactly-once per index with NO guard state at all, and it fires even if the caller never searches. VectorIndex has a path: PathBuf field and record_count(), so the message can name both, as the acceptance requires. Natural home: alongside two_tier.rs resolve_fast_path, which already hard-errors with SearchError::IndexNotFound for the MISSING-file case -- present-but-empty then sits right next to absent at the same level, which is exactly the contrast the bead asks for. two_tier.rs already imports tracing::warn and has ~10 warn! sites, so no new plumbing is needed.

Suggested shape: at open, if record_count() == 0 and wal_entries.is_empty(), warn once naming path + record_count + which tier (fast/quality). Keep it a warn, NOT an error -- an empty index is legitimate immediately after creation, per the bead's own acceptance note.

NOTE ON THE ANN PATH: hnsw.rs already emits a typed signal -- it returns AnnSearchStats { index_size: self.len(), k_returned: 0, .. }, so index_size == 0 IS the empty-index signal, already typed and already crossing the API boundary. Nothing there is silent; the caller simply ignores it. If a warn is still wanted for ANN, the cheaper and more honest fix is at the consumer that discards those stats, not a new log inside the search function.

BLOCKER, NOT A JUDGEMENT: crates/frankensearch-index/src/lib.rs (held to 06:06Z) and two_tier.rs (to 06:03Z) are both exclusively reserved by BrownCoyote, who is actively working this crate -- they filed the sibling bugs bd-07os and bd-jbfg, both in two_tier.rs. Two agents editing frankensearch-index simultaneously is precisely how a textually-clean merge silently invalidates a proof (see bd-bt2t, closed today). I released my search.rs/hnsw.rs reservations and unassigned myself so BrownCoyote can take this together with the rest of the crate in one coherent pass. Offered to them directly in mail.

title: Real-model E2E lanes run inference at opt-level=0; no [profile.test] override exists
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-26 (TealIsland). The workspace Cargo.toml defines [profile.release] and [profile.release-perf] but NO [profile.test] or [profile.dev] override, so cargo test builds every dependency at opt-level=0. The real-model Treasure Island lanes therefore run the MiniLM forward pass unoptimized.

COST, measured on this host (46-core, rayon-parallel, 4600-4700% CPU sustained): a single 339-passage corpus embedding takes minutes rather than seconds. The full 7-test treasure_island_e2e suite performs roughly four full-corpus embeddings (hybrid + two semantic lanes + query embeds) and runs >12 minutes wall clock. The previously recorded semantic-lane figure of 362.27s for 3 tests was collected under this same unoptimized profile.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND SPEED: bd-8w6e's ENGINEERING acceptance criteria explicitly require 'optimized inference'. Under the current profile that criterion is not met by any real-model lane in this workspace, so any bead citing those lanes as evidence is citing unoptimized numbers. This is a correctness-of-evidence issue, not just a developer-comfort issue -- and it silently inflates every timing figure these lanes produce.

PROPOSED FIX (deliberately NOT applied unilaterally): add to workspace Cargo.toml

    [profile.test.package."*"]
    opt-level = 2

or, more surgically, raise opt-level only for the tensor/tokenizer dependencies (frankentorch ft-core/ft-api/ft-autograd, tokenizers, safetensors) so first-party test code stays at opt-level=0 and debuggable.

WHY I DID NOT JUST DO IT: this is a shared build-profile change. It forces a full rebuild for every agent in the fleet, and at the time of filing the working tree carried 51 concurrently-modified files from other agents with several cargo builds in flight. Changing the shared profile mid-session would have invalidated their target dirs without warning. This needs a deliberate fleet-wide moment, ideally announced first.

VERIFY AFTER FIX: re-run 'cargo test -p frankensearch --features quill,native --test treasure_island_e2e' with FRANKENSEARCH_REQUIRE_SEMANTIC_E2E=1 and record the new wall time against the >12min baseline above. Also re-record bd-8w6e's timing evidence, which is currently unoptimized.
close_reason: Fixed in d6100457: [profile.test.package."*"] opt-level=2; verified 6.75x on the full 7-test real-model binary with identical retrieval results

title: Add edge-case tests for quality_comparison and bootstrap_compare
C2/C3: retain admitted immutable FSVI v2 owners and identities through both tiers
description:
OWNERSHIP AND IDENTITY RETENTION FOUNDATION. Every searchable fast or quality tier must retain the complete immutable admitted FSVI v2 owner and validation witness for as long as any vector slice, metadata view, cache key, ANN sidecar, or query guard can observe it. An index may not reduce admission to a fingerprint string, embedder ID, dimension, borrowed byte slice, filename, or copied metadata. The retained owner is the authority for full EmbeddingSpaceIdentity, producer and storage identity, generation and content receipt, document or shard coverage, and lifetime.

Construct in-memory and persistent tier objects only from a validated immutable v2 admission object. Fast and quality tiers retain independent owners and identities, even when dimensions or models happen to match. A legacy FSVI v1 object is represented only as LegacyUnidentified or ReindexRequired and cannot be queried, upgraded by relabel, or converted into a v2 owner without source rebuild. Owner lifetime must prevent use-after-unmap and metadata or bytes TOCTOU across reopen, refresh, cache replacement, generation switch, and concurrent retained readers.

This bead owns create_v2 -> descriptor-safe admission -> load -> retain -> verify primitives and both-tier ownership tests. It does not close sync or async search activation, facade or fsfs production migration, raw public API retirement, recovery, or CASS integration.
design:
Introduce one owner-backed tier handle whose private storage contains the validated immutable bytes or mapping owner, exact v2 admission witness, full identity bundle, generation and content receipts, and coverage witness. Public accessors return typed views tied to the owner lifetime; they never return independently constructible identity strings or unowned raw slices. Both persistent and in-memory representations use the same admission result, and cache or ANN keys are derived from the retained witness rather than caller input.

Admission is descriptor-safe and verifies the whole v2 image before publication. A retained generation N remains queryable while N+1 is admitted and atomically installed. Failed N+1 admission or identity validation cannot modify or evict N. Legacy v1 inspection produces a typed nonsearchable object with concrete reindex guidance. Cross-tier construction requires two independently admitted owners and never clones fast identity onto quality.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A real create_v2 -> reopen -> descriptor-safe admit -> load -> retain -> query-view round trip preserves the complete immutable owner and exact identity, content, generation and coverage witnesses. Positive tests execute for both fast and quality tiers independently; test-only fabricated metadata is insufficient.

2. The owner remains alive across borrowed vector and metadata views, search, cache publication, ANN validation, generation refresh, old-reader retention and concurrent candidate admission. Drop-order, unmap, rename, replace, truncate, descriptor reuse, and metadata/bytes swap tests prove no TOCTOU or dangling view is possible.

3. Same-dimension wrong model, tokenizer, input, producer, quantization, storage, generation, content, corpus/docset, tier swap, same-count FSVI substitution, borrowed fingerprint, and caller-supplied identity fail before any vector read or score. Fast and quality owners and coverage are never aliased merely because identities compare equal on a subset of fields.

4. FSVI v1, missing or incomplete v2 identity, and legacy mutable open return LegacyUnidentified or ReindexRequired and are nonsearchable. No path guesses identity from filename, embedder_id, dimension, revision string, sentinel, config, or another tier; no relabel or compatibility wrapper is introduced.

5. Failed candidate admission or owner validation leaves the previously retained validated owner serving. Structured events report bounded owner, identity, generation, content and coverage digests plus typed recovery, never raw vector, query, document text, secrets, or full paths.

6. Structural and compile-fail tests prevent public construction from a raw slice, standalone fingerprint or dimension-only metadata. Unit, property, concurrency, persisted round-trip and fresh-process tests, warnings-denied lint, formatting, workspace checks and changed-file scanning pass. Closure explicitly states foundation_only=true and cannot close ctzo, bd-9xuj, bd-xomn.3, raw API retirement, fsfs, recovery, or CASS beads.
close_reason: foundation_only=true. C1, C4 verified pre-existing; C2 (filesystem-mutation + refresh classes), C3 and C5 landed at 38b4363c and 69da2faa, both pushed. C5 was VACUOUS at audit -- no refresh/replace/reload entry point existed anywhere on TwoTierIndex, so nothing could evict an owner and nothing could show that it could not; try_replace_admitted_v2 now opens a candidate in full and installs only on complete success, with a refused-quality-tier control proving admit-then-install rather than install-as-each-admits. C3 correction found by writing the test: the identity bundle is SELF-BINDING (producer.space_fingerprint binds the space, space.input_contract_fingerprint binds the input contract, endianness is fixed), so model/tokenizer/dimension/input mismatches cannot even be FROZEN -- they fail one layer earlier than admission, and the test asserts that stronger property rather than pretending admission is first. Red proofs, each applied alone and reverted: owner aliasing reds only the new non-aliasing test (the pre-existing owner test stays green under it, measuring what it never covered); install-fast-before-quality reds the partial-install test; dropping tier attribution reds all four admission tests. One INERT mutation is recorded rather than hidden. 683 passed / 0 failed, clippy -D warnings and rustfmt clean. NOT CLOSED and carved out: bd-vnju1 (C6 compile-fail harness needs a dependency decision I refused to make unilaterally; the structural half landed) and bd-r6lwt (C2 ANN validation, true concurrency, drop order), plus the un-instrumented 'fails before any vector read' ordering. Does not close ctzo, bd-9xuj, bd-xomn.3, raw API retirement, fsfs, recovery or CASS.

title: C1: validated query identity and independent per-tier coverage algebra
description:
FOUNDATION-ONLY IDENTITY AND COVERAGE CONTRACT. Consume the landed canonical embedding identity bundle and make it impossible to construct a query embedding that merely carries plausible metadata. Every BoundQueryEmbedding and tiered query object validates its complete identity, vector dimension, tier role, and stable space fingerprint before it can be stored or passed downstream. Separate semantic-space compatibility from producer compatibility: a space join compares the persisted EmbeddingSpaceIdentity contract, while a producer join requires exact producer identity or an explicit, machine-verifiable foreign-producer conformance certificate. Same dimension, display name, revision string, filename, or a caller-supplied fingerprint is never compatibility.

Define independent requested and realized coverage for fast and quality tiers. Coverage must distinguish missing tier, zero live vectors, complete coverage, partial coverage, disjoint document sets, and unknown or unverified coverage. It binds canonical live-document-set or shard-set witnesses, checked counts, intersection and union facts, and fixed-point ratios without overflow, duplicate inflation, or borrowing one tier witness for the other. RetrievalTopology is derived from validated tier identities plus this coverage algebra; it is not caller prose. Hash embeddings are always explicit nonsemantic HashControl or declared lexical degradation and can never satisfy semantic fast, quality, partial, or full availability.

This bead owns core types, constructors, validation laws, deterministic serialization and exhaustive property tests only. Closing it must not claim that fusion, index, facade, fsfs, CASS, persistence, or recovery call sites are wired; those consumers remain downstream and must present a production call-site census.
design:
Use closed, deny-unknown-fields identity, certificate, topology, and coverage objects with domain-separated stable hashes. Construction validates identity syntax and semantics before storing the vector; checked vector length must equal the validated space dimension. Space validation and producer validation are separate explicit operations so an equivalent-space producer is accepted only with a certificate naming both producer contracts, a frozen conformance-vector manifest, certificate schema, issuer or local policy identity, and exact expiry or revision bounds. No boolean allow_mismatch switch exists.

Represent coverage with independent fast and quality witnesses: requested tier, realized tier, live and indexed counts, canonical docset or ordered-shard digest, intersection or union facts when comparable, and a closed reason when coverage is absent or unknowable. All arithmetic is checked and deterministic; ratios are integer fixed-point and derived, never trusted input. A topology constructor rejects swapped tiers, duplicate tier bindings, cross-generation or cross-docset claims without an explicit partial-coverage witness, semantic labels on hash control, and any claimed complete coverage that cannot be reconstructed.
acceptance_criteria:
1. All public constructors call identity.validate before retaining vector bytes and reject malformed identity, wrong vector length, zero or unsupported dimensions, tier mismatch, unstable or recomputed fingerprint mismatch, and same-dimension wrong space with a typed tier-specific error.

2. Space and producer laws are independently testable. Exact same space plus exact producer succeeds. Same space plus different producer fails unless an explicit validated foreign-producer certificate binds both producers and frozen golden conformance vectors. Certificate mutation, expiry, wrong input contract, wrong tokenizer, storage-only identity substitution, and caller-fabricated fingerprints fail closed.

3. Coverage property tests cover empty, zero-live, missing, complete, subset, superset, disjoint, overlapping, duplicate and reordered documents or shards, unequal generations, unequal corpora, maximum counts, checked-overflow rejection, fixed-point boundary values, and requested-versus-realized topology. No tier may borrow the other tier witness or scalar coverage value.

4. Retrieval topology can be derived only from validated bindings and coverage. Hash is explicitly nonsemantic in every serialized and logged form and cannot satisfy semantic availability. Swapped fast or quality roles, unverified partial coverage, and complete claims without exact witnesses reject.

5. Serde and mutation suites round-trip canonical objects, deny unknown and duplicate fields, preserve stable hashes across process and platform, and change the hash for every semantic mutation. Structured diagnostics contain bounded identity and witness digests only, never query, vector, token, document text, secrets, or full paths.

6. Unit, property, compile-fail, serialization and deterministic fresh-process tests pass with formatting, warnings-denied lint, workspace checks, and changed-file scanning. The closure receipt explicitly reports core type call-site counts and states foundation_only=true; zero production consumers is allowed here but can never close bd-9xuj or any production integration bead.

Exact-source strict RCH proof passed core 1035/0/0, core doctests, embed all-features 487/0/5 ignored, workspace all-target check and Clippy -D warnings, fmt/diff, and exact five-file UBS exit 0. Per-symbol census: the new C1 public activation surfaces have zero downstream product-crate search consumers; recovery_plan internally consumes retrieval_topology_fits_request. This closes only the foundation and does not imply bd-9xuj activation.

title: hnsw_rs 0.3.4 writes reverse edges at the new point's top layer, causing asymmetric underfill
description:
REPRODUCED 2026-07-26 on independent RCH workers: two live orthogonal vectors, k=2/ef=64, but one direction returns only doc-a. Serial construction and serial seeding through m+1 did NOT fix it, disproving the initial-entry-point race as the complete cause.

Captured failing topology: point0 has PointId(0,0) but stores its only edge to point1 in neighborhood layer 1; point1 has PointId(1,0) and stores point0 at layers 0 and 1. A query for point0 descends from the level-1 entry point to point0 via the invalid level-1 cross-edge, then begins base-layer search at point0 whose layer-0 neighborhood is empty, so point1 is unreachable and k underfills.

Upstream hnsw_rs 0.3.4 reverse_update_neighborhood_simple loops over layer l but stores every reverse edge at l_n = new_point.p_id.0 rather than l. This both omits required reverse edges at lower layers and can install edges in a layer higher than the source/target point supports. parallel_insert also has a separate initial-entry race, so both invariants require treatment.
design: DECISION (expanded after exact 0.3.4 source audit and deterministic upstream reproduction): pin a minimal fork based on published hnsw_rs commit 673257c620afd23e5a7e2fb1985244683cc662d0, not the fork default branch. The cumulative candidate through 18a5a1a contains FOUR coupled production fixes: (a) upper greedy descent must not attach a lower-level new point above its sampled level; (b) connection descent begins at min(new_level, previous_max_level), leaving new-only upper layers empty; (c) reverse_update_neighborhood_simple stores reciprocal edges at loop layer l, not at the new point top layer; and (d) search_layer must treat every point whose sampled level is at least the logical layer as participating, because an empty exact-top-level bucket does not mean the logical layer is empty. The last defect is exposed by a deterministic high,high,zero sampled-level sequence. Supporting commits expose actual entry identity for attestation and disable default FFI only so baseline and candidate can coexist in one ELF. The runner decides this cumulative candidate and must never attribute performance causally to only one patch. FrankenSearch defenses are fail-closed: serial construction below the documented 1000-points-per-Rayon-worker threshold; a large parallel graph must pass full topology and directed-reachability attestation or be dropped before exactly one serial rebuild; metadata v5 to v6 semantic invalidation; the same attestation after fresh build, native load, and retained READY reuse; physical source-row mapping and source-extent binding; native tombstone filtering; and canonical VectorIndex exact repair with explicit non-approximate diagnostics. Do not vendor, flatten HNSW, switch engines, retry randomness, weaken result-count or recall tests, or let a repair hide a decision-run candidate defect.
acceptance_criteria: CORRECTNESS: (1) deterministic regressions for captured wrong-layer reverse edges and the high,high,zero exact-level-gap search bug; (2) repeated two-vector bidirectional k=2 search across varied topology orders; (3) n=0/1/2/3/m/m+1 boundaries under serial and concurrent construction; (4) structural attestation on fresh builds, native loads, and every retained-generation reuse path: unique and in-range external/internal identities, valid actual maximum-level entry identity, no neighborhoods above sampled level, valid layer-local targets, finite nonduplicate nonself edges, and directed base-layer reachability from the actual entry to every point; (5) native save/load preserves entry identity and reachability; (6) small and large concurrent-build stress; (7) malformed, disconnected, uncertified, or stale sidecars and READY generations are never republished or served; (8) parallel attestation failure drops the invalid graph before one serial rebuild, serial failure reports both causes and fails closed; (9) exact underfill repair uses authoritative FSVI scoring and current tombstones while TwoTier performs one canonical main plus WAL merge with physical-row identity and public doc-id deduplication; (10) no weakening of recall, persistence, deletion, duplicate-ID, or WAL tests. QUALITY/PERF: provisional smoke may run immediately but remains NoClaim or Quarantine. Decision admission and durable remote operability are separately gated by bd-u3wt.1 and bd-u3wt.2. After both close, run at 50k and 100k or larger with a real manifested corpus, identical config, same-ELF ABBA A/B plus engine-local A/A controls, fresh graph replicas, absolute build docs/s and latency p50/p95/p99, peak RSS, artifact bytes/doc, recall@k against exact, topology counters, raw samples, worker/corpus/config/source/lock/ELF hashes, and supported uncertainty. Any material slowdown or safety-envelope breach triggers the Rust-port optimization gauntlet rather than silent acceptance.

title: HNSW A/B decision admission: freeze corpus/config, replicate query graphs, bind build state, and gate tails
description: The bd-u3wt runner captures useful same-ELF smoke/high-scale evidence but MUST remain fail-closed for performance admission until this task lands. Four gaps: (1) runtime flags and an arbitrary valid manifest can redefine the full experiment; require a versioned, tracked, precommitted contract at one canonical path binding the exact grid, corpus/model/generator identities and byte digests, thresholds, and schema; (2) query timings repeat queries on one graph per engine, pseudo-replicating over stochastic topology; measure latency across ABBA-paired fresh graph replicas/blocks, aggregate passes within query, and use a paired hierarchical graph/query estimator; (3) Allow uses an OR over two co-primary 95% wins and does not infer p95/p99 tails; predeclare one primary or apply explicit multiplicity correction, and report/gate supported tail uncertainty; (4) end-of-run Git/lock state is not proven identical to the state that built the ELF; embed runner/workspace/Cargo.lock/contract hashes at build time and capture matching start/end snapshots. Preserve raw per-graph/per-query/per-pass samples, A/A nulls, RSS, artifact bytes, topology/recall, durable create-new output, and exact executable/dependency provenance. Do not enable Allow or Block performance classification before all four are enforced.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in contract fixture and parser tests reject every single-field drift and untracked/dirty/replaced contracts; full runner requires the exact contract. Query latency uses the predeclared fresh-graph count per engine with ABBA pairing and hierarchical paired CIs; tests prove graph/query pairing and reject mismatched grids. One predeclared primary family or corrected multiple-testing rule controls false positives; p50/p95/p99 absolute and relative estimates include supported uncertainty and insufficient N fails closed. Build-time source/Cargo.lock/contract hashes equal start/end runtime snapshots, with mutation tests. title: HNSW A/B runner operability: bounded children, durable live logs, and remote report retrieval on quarantine
description: The evidence runner currently launches build samples with Command::output() and no per-child deadline. A wedged child can hang the experiment indefinitely; stdout/stderr are retained only in memory until exit, so logs are neither live nor crash-durable and a chatty child can grow memory without bound. Separately, full mode intentionally writes its report and exits nonzero on Quarantine, but standard RCH cargo-run retrieves artifacts only on success and only from narrow target paths; arbitrary --output files and named target/release-perf artifacts can remain stranded on the selected worker. Treat RCH as compile/test transport unless it gains explicit artifact-on-failure support. Implement a pinned-worker measurement wrapper that records worker identity, streams bounded child logs and a run journal to disk, enforces terminate-then-kill deadlines, and always pulls and validates the create-new report plus logs in a finally path regardless of runner exit. Preserve the runner fail-closed behavior; retrieval success must never convert Quarantine into Allow.
acceptance_criteria: Every child process has a predeclared deadline, graceful termination window, forced-kill fallback, bounded memory use, and per-child stdout/stderr files flushed during execution. Unit/integration tests cover success, nonzero exit, timeout, forced kill, signal/panic where portable, chatty output, partial log persistence, and orphan-process cleanup. A documented executable wrapper selects and records one worker, runs the already-built attested ELF, retrieves report/journal/logs on success and failure, validates hashes/schema/create-new semantics locally, and returns the original classification without laundering failure. Tests with a fake remote transport prove retrieval after nonzero Quarantine and failure when any required artifact is absent or altered. Full decision runs may not start until this and bd-u3wt.1 are complete.

title: quill: decode_bitmap_payload trailing_zeros bit-scan (skip zero bits)
description: PROFILE-DIRECTED (post-vint hotspot map 2026-07-23): decode_bitmap_payload 6.8% of query self-time. The inner scan 'for bit_index in 0..8 { if byte&(1<<bit)==0 continue }' visits ALL 512 bit positions (64 bytes x 8) to find the 128 set bits; for larger spans (bitmap is 128 set bits in span 128..512, so 25-100% dense) this wastes up to 384 iterations. Replace with trailing_zeros: 'let mut bits=byte; while bits!=0 { let bit=bits.trailing_zeros(); bits &= bits-1; ... }' — visits exactly the set bits in ascending order, byte-identical (same relative values, same span/cardinality checks). Wins for sparse bitmaps (span>128), wash for span=128 (100% dense). Measure via deterministic instruction-count A/B. KEEP if decidable win, REJECT if wash (dense-dominated workload).
close_reason: KEEP: decode_bitmap_payload set-bits-only trailing_zeros walk, -4.86% total instructions (deterministic A/B 56.514B->53.769B). Profile-directed (bitmap 6.8% of query self-time). Replaced the 512-position bit scan with 'while bits!=0 { trailing_zeros; bits &= bits-1 }' — visits exactly the 128 set bits, skips up to 384 zero bits per sparse span. Byte-identical (existing bitmap invariant tests); 473 green, clippy clean.

title: Versioned QG evidence: absolute values for both engines, paired effects, raw samples, and executable provenance
design: Land the schema and persistence independently of the repaired estimator. Canonically serialize authoritative JSON, publish via unique create-new staging, file fsync, atomic rename, parent-directory fsync, content hash and verified reload. Preserve every attempted terminal artifact append-only; never overwrite decision evidence with provisional output. Store full precision and metric-specific raw sampling hierarchy. Publication is create-new, fsync/atomic/content-hashed, reload-verified, crash-tested and append-only by run ID. Empty/unmeasured runnable cells fail CI. Invalid attempts persist as NoDecision and cannot ratchet. Summaries recompute from raw values at full precision; human tables reconcile exactly; self ELF/source attestations and platform probes fail closed; redaction canaries never enter artifacts.
notes:
CONFIRMED BY REAL RUNS 2026-07-26. Criterion DOES print absolute per-engine timings; the gate artifact throws them away and keeps only ratios. Both runs of QG-1 emitted cells containing exclusively *_quill_over_tantivy and *_tantivy_over_tantivy ratios -- no docs/s, no ms, for either arm.

FIRST ABSOLUTE NUMBERS (from Criterion stdout, fixture bulk/tiny/1/positions_on, release-perf, ovh-a, 10 samples, bench_elf_sha256=6d562276bf6aa2c507d6f510df05446c398057607248935286ffe574c5a8d603):

  quill    time: [11.111 ms  11.491 ms  12.190 ms]   (330 iterations in 5.83 s)

Two observations that ONLY the absolute numbers make visible, which is the entire argument of this bead:

A ratio-only artifact reports one number and conceals that essentially ALL the run-to-run noise is coming from the tantivy arm. That is actionable information -- it says stabilise the oracle arm, not 'collect more samples' -- and the current artifact format destroys it.

ACTION: the harness already has these values in hand at cell-construction time. Persist per-arm absolute p50/p95/p99 plus iteration count and sample count into every cell, alongside the ratio.

Scope:
Create a reproducible per-crate benchmark harness that compares frankensearch against a Tantivy-only incumbent baseline on identical corpora and query sets. Treat Tantivy-only as the hermetic Lucene-class comparator. Meilisearch/Lucene process-level comparators are optional only if they can be run hermetically and recorded separately.

Real workloads:
- 10k, 100k, and limit-all local document corpora.
- Query classes: exact identifier, short keyword, quoted phrase, natural-language intent, high-fanout term, zero-hit term.
- Cold vs warm index open and warm query-cache/model-cache paths.
