1. Harness runs per crate only via rch with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/projects/.rch-targets/frankensearch-cod-a` or successor agent-specific target dir; never workspace-wide.

3. Ledger entries clearly separate wins, regressions, and measurement blockers; no win claim without a same-worker or explicitly comparable run.
4. At least one Tantivy-only baseline and one frankensearch hybrid run use the exact same corpus and query sequence.
5. Conformance stays green for the crate touched by the harness (`cargo test -p <crate>` and `cargo fmt --check` for touched Rust files).
6. Document any Cargo flag mismatch (e.g. `cargo bench --release` rejection) as negative evidence instead of silently changing protocol.

Alien/optimization mapping:
- /profiling-software-performance: defines scenario/fingerprint/hotspot table before code levers.
- /extreme-software-optimization: one lever only after baseline/profile/proof.
- /alien-graveyard: baseline comparator requirement from § Appendix: Baseline Comparators; vectorized execution and query JIT stay candidates only after harness data.

Fallback/revert:
If an external comparator cannot be made hermetic, keep Tantivy-only as the mandatory original baseline and record the reason in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.

title: P0: truthful same-snapshot cutoff and offset completeness authority
description: Post-Salej correctness boundary. Replace boolean cutoff completeness inferred from requested fetch capacity or mutable counters with one engine-native same-snapshot observation bundle. Persist checked absolute ranks. Quill ranked hits and expanded hits remain native TopDocs-style observations over one retained PublishedSnapshot; Tantivy ranked hits and expanded hits remain native TopDocs observations over one pinned Searcher. Exact Count is a separate invocation on that same snapshot/searcher and cannot affect hit selection, tie expansion, or ordering. Exhaustion is only expanded_absolute_end_exclusive == exact_total. An empty page beyond the end proves exact_total <= offset. Zero-limit has no score boundary. Requested capacity proves nothing. Stored V7 bytes and replay remain unchanged.
design: Use a compact closed certificate with M=exact_total, O=offset, L=limit, checked absolute start/end ranks, per-boundary NotApplicable variants, physical snapshot digest, arm provenance digest, native ranked/expanded observation digests, and one-shot same-snapshot authority. The requested page interval is P=[min(O,M), min(checked(O+L),M)). Expanded evidence is E=[a,b) with contiguous unique absolute ranks, len(E)=b-a, and P subset E. Each expanded boundary group has one canonical finite score. Either a=0 or rank a-1 is the immediate strictly-higher predecessor; either b=M or rank b is the immediate strictly-lower successor. Exhaustion is iff b=M=exact_total. L=0 has no boundary; for L>0 an empty page implies M<=O. Count stays observationally separate from ranked TopDocs. Runtime authority lands first; distinct V8 persistence belongs to the downstream schema node.
acceptance_criteria: Validators enforce checked P=[min(O,M),min(O+L,M)) and contiguous unique E=[a,b) with len(E)=b-a and P subset E. Every expanded boundary group has one canonical finite score; a=0 or rank a-1 is immediate strictly higher; b=M or rank b is immediate strictly lower; exhaustion is iff b=M=exact_total. Any certificate that infers completeness or exhaustion from requested capacity, returned_count == exact_total, or Count-derived hit selection rejects; returned_count equality is never authority when O>0, including M=0. Gaps, duplicate ranks, non-adjacent witnesses, noncanonical scores, and overflow reject. L=0 carries no score boundary; for L>0 an empty page proves M<=O. Tests include M=0 with O=0 and O>0, offset 0 and nonzero, limit 0/1/k greater than total, beyond-end empty results, complete and truncated ties at both absolute boundaries, concurrent refresh, and mutation-between-calls symmetrically for Quill and Tantivy. Ranked hits, expanded hits, and separate exact Count share one pinned PublishedSnapshot/Searcher, while Count cannot alter selection/ties/order. Unit/property/mutation proof and bounded fresh-process JSONL include phase/status/reason/source/Cargo.lock/ELF/corpus/query/snapshot/receipt hashes, timeout, at most 10000 lines and 8 MiB, redaction canaries, failure-artifact retention, and no raw query/doc/term/vector/path/secret. Strict remote check/clippy/tests, fmt/diff, and literal changed-file UBS disposition pass. No comparator waiver, performance claim, V7 reinterpretation, or Salej-closure claim is made.

title: Positionless Quill schemas: allow bare term queries and reject only position-dependent operators with typed errors
description: ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED: default-field validation hard-requires positions, so the QG position-free fixture cannot construct a default field and every QG-1 matrix run crashes before producing complete evidence. Position-free text indexing is a valid smaller/faster mode. Bare term, prefix, boolean, range, and other position-independent operators must work; phrase, slop/proximity, span/near, and any operator that actually consumes positions must fail at parse/lowering with a precise typed PositionsRequired error naming schema, field, and operator. Relax default-field validation to require the intended text analyzer without positions=true. Define and test an operator-to-index-capability matrix so later query features cannot silently bypass it. The performance harness keeps both positions_on and positions_off fixtures and logs fixture/schema/operator before work; it never deletes the failing cell or rewrites bare queries as field-qualified workarounds.
design: Validate field existence/analyzer compatibility when selecting defaults, then validate required posting capabilities when lowering each AST operator. Centralize required capabilities rather than scattering phrase special cases. Preserve identical matching/ranking for position-independent queries across positionful and positionless indexes over the same documents; only unsupported operators differ, through typed errors observed by the total comparator.
acceptance_criteria: Positionless schema plus bare term/prefix/boolean/range queries succeeds; phrase/slop/proximity and every position-dependent operator returns typed PositionsRequired with field/operator. Positionful behavior is unchanged. Cross-engine and metamorphic tests prove position-independent doc IDs/order/scores follow registered equivalence laws across positions on/off. A matrix smoke test constructs and queries every QG fixture before release benchmarking. QG-1 completes both positions cells and emits a full provisional artifact.             ...
        });
        return None;   // <-- branch dropped; with both default fields dropped the query lowers to Empty
    }

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE CRASH: the crash was loud and stopped a benchmark. This is silent and wrong at QUERY time. A user phrase-searching a positionless index gets ZERO RESULTS and a correct-looking empty response; the only trace is a diagnostic in ParsedQuery.diagnostics that nothing is obliged to read. The acceptance criteria explicitly require 'phrase/slop/proximity and every position-dependent operator returns typed PositionsRequired with field/operator' — a dropped fragment is neither typed nor returned.

It also means index.rs's phrase-positions guard (~5331) is UNREACHABLE from the parsed path — the parser has already eaten the phrase. That guard only protects AST/preparsed entry points. So today the two paths disagree: AST phrase -> typed error; parsed phrase -> empty result set.

DESIGN QUESTION I AM NOT DECIDING UNILATERALLY: DefaultQueryParser is lenient BY CONTRACT (parse_lenient, 'syntax never becomes a search failure') and returns ParsedQuery, not Result. Making this a hard parse error changes that contract and the public signature. Options:
  (a) keep the parser lenient, but have it emit a machine-checkable capability record on ParsedQuery (not just a free-text diagnostic) that the index layer converts into the typed PositionsRequired before executing;
  (b) let lowering own it: keep the parser branch-drop but have the index layer detect 'query lowered to Empty AND an UnsupportedField/positions diagnostic is present' and return the typed error rather than an empty page;
  (c) change parse to return Result for capability failures (breaks the lenient contract; I would not).
My preference is (a) — the parser stays lenient, the capability failure stays typed and structural, and one place still decides. Needs the query-API owner's call.

TESTS UPDATED accordingly (query.rs, all in my reservation):
- capability_gate_rejects_a_constructed_phrase_on_positionless_fields: builds Query::Phrase directly (the preparsed/AST path, which HAS no parser in front of it), asserts schema+field+operator+capability, and asserts nesting inside a Boolean does not launder it.
- positionless_schema_currently_drops_phrases_to_empty_with_only_a_diagnostic: PINS the gap so it cannot change unnoticed — asserts query == Empty AND that the drop is at least diagnosed. Doc comment says to INVERT this test when the gap is fixed; it blesses nothing.

I replaced my earlier test that asserted the parsed path yields a typed error, because that assertion was simply wrong about the code.

title: Central typed semantic RecoveryPlan and truthful readiness state machine across library, fsfs and CASS
description: FOUNDATION CONTRACT. Define one versioned, typed semantic RecoveryPlan schema and a pure exhaustive planner that maps current semantic state plus requested mode and policy to a truthful next action. Machine and human fields: stable code, schema version, current availability/topology/coverage, explanation, argv array, network_required, consent_required, preserves_old_data, potentially_destructive, retryability, prerequisites, and expected postcondition. Required states include missing model, acquired but unloadable, compatible model but absent index, legacy or identity mismatch, daemon mismatch, empty/all-tombstoned/zero-live index, corrupt or unsafe manifest, stale ANN, incomplete generation, and partial quality coverage. Installing a model never claims semantic searchable until load self-test and a compatible nonempty index pass. Explicit semantic fails closed; hybrid may lexical-fallback only with response degradation metadata. This bead owns the shared type, schema, pure planner, serialization, and golden transition table; product integrations and end-to-end state producers close under a separate terminal integration bead so the common contract can land early.
design: Use an enum-backed state machine and exhaustiveness checks, not error-string parsing. Recovery argv is an array and rendered separately for shells. Stable codes are append-only within a schema version. Planner input includes request mode, interaction/network policy, tier coverage, artifact generations, and full embedding-space compatibility. Redact raw user paths and content from telemetry while retaining bounded hashes and safe display paths for local diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Shared core types and a pure deterministic planner cover every enumerated semantic readiness state and request mode. Golden JSON and schema-version tests lock stable codes and fields; compile-time exhaustive matching prevents new states from being silently ignored. Tests cover argv quoting, interactive/noninteractive/offline policy, daemon-only readiness, acquired-not-indexed, identity mismatch, empty/all-tombstoned, stale ANN, incomplete generation, and partial coverage. The foundation makes no false claim that products are integrated.

title: POLICY FIX: measurement is MANDATORY and immediate; only the CLAIM is gated. Ban 'unmeasured' as a resting state
description:
ROOT POLICY FAILURE: anti-fabrication discipline was misapplied as a reason not to run anything. Ten inactive gates and ten empty *.unmeasured.* artifacts are not rigor; they are missing observability.

POLICY:
1. Measurement begins immediately at the largest affordable scale today. Activation controls public claims, never whether a run occurs or is recorded.
2. Replace the zero-data loop in decision/history machinery: every terminal run status, including MeasuredProvisional, InvalidNull, Quarantine and Block, writes a versioned history artifact. Only Allow may support a public speed claim. Invalid runs retain raw diagnostics but carry NoDecision.
3. Empty/unmeasured is a CI failure for a gate that has a runnable fixture. Unsupported/platform-blocked gates require a typed blocker artifact with exact missing capability and retry condition, not cells:[].
4. Scale ratchets upward: smoke -> medium -> decision scale. Provisional artifacts name scale and never overwrite decision-grade evidence from another corpus/machine. Cheap gates run often; expensive gates are scheduled, not postponed indefinitely.
5. Work breadth order based on decision value and harness validity: repair paired statistics and operation scopes; QG-1 medium with real tokenizer denominator; QG-6 100k realistic query set; QG-2; QG-4 durable commit distribution; QG-3 true visibility; QG-7; QG-9 true cold; QG-5/QG-8; QG-10 deterministic build/dependency facts. Then scale required lanes to 250k/1M where their contract demands it.
6. Every result states what it supports and does not support. Reproduction failure is normal negative evidence, not a reason to avoid first measurement.
7. Any valid Quill regression routes automatically to the profile-first running-the-gauntlet campaign; one measured isomorphic lever per commit, exact conformance proof, A/A+A/B, and explicit keep/reject ledger.

ENFORCEMENT: manifest declares runnable cells, required-versus-diagnostic status, scale ladder, platform needs and maximum evidence age. CI compares manifest to artifacts; missing/stale cells or unsupported zero values fail. History writer tests prove non-Allow outcomes persist. Docs ban uncited speed claims.
acceptance_criteria: No runnable gate rests in an unmeasured/empty state. Every manifest cell has a current provisional/invalid/quarantine/block/allow artifact or typed blocker with retry condition. History writes every terminal status. CI validates scale/provenance/age and prevents provisional evidence from masquerading as decision-grade. All ten gates have at least affordable-scale measurements, and valid regressions have linked gauntlet child Beads.
notes:

WHAT IT DOES ESTABLISH, which is a lot:

title: Quality-parity metrics vs tantivy: nDCG/MRR/Recall/Kendall-tau with bootstrap CIs, not just assertion equality
description:
Today 'comparable search results' is supported by '18 differential tests agree on a 100-document corpus'. That is equality-on-a-toy-corpus, not a retrieval-quality claim, and it is not sufficient to justify making Quill the library default.

TASK: on a SHARED query set over a realistic corpus, compute for Quill and for the pinned tantivy oracle: nDCG@10, MRR, Recall@100, and Kendall tau between the two ranked lists. Report per-query and aggregate with bootstrap confidence intervals. frankensearch-core/src/metrics_eval.rs ALREADY provides ndcg_at_k, mrr, recall_at_k, map_at_k, bootstrap_ci and bootstrap_compare -- this is wiring, not new math.

DECISION RULE (must be fixed BEFORE running, to avoid post-hoc rationalization): the flip is permitted when the lower bound of the bootstrap CI on delta-nDCG@10 (Quill minus tantivy) is >= -0.005, AND no individual query regresses by more than 0.05 nDCG without a Divergence Register entry explaining why.

Rank-order equality is NOT required: Quill vendors tantivy's fieldnorm table and f32 op order, so scores should be near-identical, but ties may order differently and that is acceptable if the register says so.

ACCEPTANCE: a committed artifact with the metric table, CIs, the query set hash, corpus hash, and both engine revisions.

title: Windows safe-handle generation-root authority and durability qualification
description:
Implement the Windows equivalent of the qualified capability-root, persistent writer exclusion, fixed AUTHORITY slots, immutable object creation, retained-handle identity, and durable barrier contract without unsafe code in FrankenSearch and without permissive share-delete/reparse behavior. Select or build an audited safe dependency surface for CreateFile-style component traversal with reparse-point rejection, directory handles, explicit share modes that prevent rename/delete substitution, stable volume/file IDs, owner/DACL validation, byte-range or equivalent crash-releasing exclusion, positional exact I/O, write-through/FlushFileBuffers semantics, and directory/volume capability checks. Unsupported filesystems, remote shares, unknown ACLs, unavailable durable rename/flush semantics, and unqualified Windows versions fail closed before mutation.

The public generation-root API and canonical codecs remain identical to Linux/macOS. Windows-specific substrate plugs into the same pure resolver, external anti-rollback floor, CommitOutcomeUnknown reconciliation, higher-sequence rollback/repair, retained snapshot, and no-deletion retention model. No compatibility shim, pathname reopen, dimension/name inference, canonical-vector replacement, or silent weaker durability profile is allowed.

TESTS: reparse point at every component; junction/symlink/mount-point/alternate data stream; hardlink/file-ID alias; share-delete/rename contention; root/LOCK/AUTHORITY replacement; wrong owner/DACL/inheritance; local NTFS/ReFS qualification; FAT/exFAT/network/SMB unsupported behavior unless separately proven; two real publishers; process termination release; every positional-write/flush/cancel/crash boundary; fresh-process reconcile; long-lived retained reader; and exact zero-I/O typed unsupported cases. Physical Windows CI receipts identify OS build, filesystem, volume flags, binary SHA, and crash/restart method. Workspace cross-target check/clippy/fmt, focused tests, UBS, and no-mock native Windows evidence are required. This bead blocks final removal of production legacy surfaces so Windows users do not lose persisted semantic functionality.
acceptance_criteria: An audited safe-handle substrate provides no-reparse component admission, stable file/volume identity, explicit non-delete sharing, owner/DACL validation, crash-releasing exclusion, positional I/O, and qualified durable barriers without unsafe FrankenSearch code. Native Windows fault/concurrency/restart and cross-target gates pass; unqualified filesystems return typed zero-I/O unsupported. Final legacy removal remains blocked until this receipt is protected.

title: Bound automatic FEC recovery reads and pin same-length bitrot contract
description:
Keeper durable open now invokes FileProtector recovery automatically, but recovery reads .fec sidecars with unbounded fs::read and trusts trailer-derived sizes deeply enough to permit memory exhaustion. Same-length CRC failure also discards every source symbol and succeeds only when repair symbols alone can reconstruct all k source symbols.

Acceptance criteria:
- Bound sidecar bytes before allocation using checked metadata/config-derived limits; reject oversized or inconsistent sidecars with a typed error.
- Use checked arithmetic for trailer/symbol counts and every decode allocation.
- Add hostile oversized/truncated/trailer-count tests through the automatic Keeper recovery path.
- Explicitly choose, document, and test the same-length bitrot contract across supported repair_overhead values: either enforce enough repair symbols for full reconstruction or safely salvage/validate source symbols.
- Preserve current exact-byte validation and fail-closed publication semantics.
close_reason: Bounded sidecar reads (stat-first config-derived cap, typed IndexCorrupted on oversized), exact trailer layout validation (k_source tiles source_len; declared counts must reproduce exact payload size), checked arithmetic throughout, hostile oversized/truncated/forged-count tests at both protector level and through KeeperWriter::open_durable. Same-length contract pinned: repair-only reconstruction with repair>=k enforced at construction (overhead>=1.0) and typed Unrecoverable on short budget; CRC32/xxh3 always re-validated pre-acceptance. Committed 2e02204; durability 139/139, quill+durability 352/352, clippy/fmt clean.

title: HIGH: rebuild merges WAL-resident rows with no liveness check — soft-deleted documents are resurrected as live on the next refresh cycle
description:
Found by user-directed review sweep (MossyPine, 2026-07-31); asymmetry personally re-verified at origin/main refresh.rs:604-646.

DEFECT: rebuild_index has TWO merge loops. The main-slab loop (refresh.rs:604-612) carries an explicit tombstone guard with a fleet-review comment naming the exact bug it fixed: 'tombstoned rows were merged back as live records, resurrecting every soft-deleted document on the next rebuild cycle' — if fast_index.is_deleted(fast_idx) { continue; }. The WAL-resident loop 40 lines below (refresh.rs:644, 'for (doc_id, fast_embedding) in wal_rows') has NO equivalent liveness check, and per the code comment at :598-601 record_count() structurally does not cover WAL rows, so is_deleted(fast_idx) cannot reach them.

FAILURE: append a document (lands in the WAL), then soft-delete it (GDPR erasure request, moderation takedown, user deletion). The next refresh cycle re-adds it as a live record. The deleted document REAPPEARS in search results and persists across subsequent rebuilds. Existing test rebuild_honors_tombstones_and_wal_residents (refresh.rs:1379-1425) deletes a MAIN-SLAB row and appends a NEW doc — the append-then-delete path is untested in both directions.

ROOT CAUSE: the earlier tombstone fix was applied per-loop instead of to a shared liveness predicate, leaving the newer WAL path uncovered.

FIX: extract a single liveness predicate covering both main-slab and WAL-resident rows and apply it to both loops; add the append-then-delete regression in both orders. Marked PLAUSIBLE by the reviewer only pending soft_delete/wal_records semantics from the index crate — the code asymmetry itself is CONFIRMED.

ALSO IN THIS FUNCTION (MEDIUM, confirmed): wal_rows is a HashMap<&str,&[f32]> used BOTH as the lookup map (:612) and as the iteration source (:644), so RandomState makes WAL documents append in a different order every process run — exactly-tied documents swap rank across restarts and the on-disk index is byte-nondeterministic, which breaks golden-artifact harnesses. Fix: iterate a doc_id-sorted view, keep the map for lookups.
close_reason: Already fixed on origin/main; focused locked regression passes

title: FSVI v2 required embedding-space identity with typed blue-green legacy migration
description:
FSVI v1 permits empty embedder revision and production writers/searchers can emit or accept it. Replace this ambiguous contract with identity-complete FSVI v2 plus one durable composite generation authority. V2 persists and validates complete embedding/input/producer/storage/generation identities, ordered live-document-set and vector-content digests, exact layout and WAL state. V1, empty or incomplete identity is inspection-only LegacyUnidentified with typed ReindexRequired and RecoveryPlan; unknown future schema is UpgradeRequired; no dimension/name/path adoption, relabel, copy-conversion, or generic corruption misclassification is allowed.

Migration builds random immutable generations beside the retained incumbent, seals exact vector plus lexical plus ANN plus metadata plus source-checkpoint receipts, and publishes through the fixed two-slot LOCK/AUTHORITY protocol with external anti-rollback floor. There is no manifest/current pathname swap or separate model/index pointer. Crash/cancel/floor ambiguity is reconciled from persisted attempts and exact retained bytes. Rollback and repair publish higher authority sequence records targeting retained generations. Production migration covers library facade, fsfs, fusion/cache, storage sinks, examples, and CASS receipt; final legacy-surface removal waits for exhaustive recovery proof and native Windows substrate so no platform loses functionality. No implicit deletion is authorized.

TESTS: v1/empty/malformed/v2 format matrices; every identity and component mutation; wrong same-dimension model; storage/quantization/docset/vector/source mismatch; authority tears/forks/gaps/unknown outcomes; crash/cancel/disk-full/sync/floor faults; concurrent readers/publishers; old-byte preservation; fresh-process reopen; fast/quality/sharded/partial coverage; real semantic plus lexical queries; higher-sequence rollback/repair; and bounded structured recovery/retention logs. Child beads own granular proofs and strict remote/native platform receipts.
design: FSVI v2 header and WAL bind canonical frozen identities, full-width ArtifactGenerationIdentityV1, input/producer/storage fingerprints, ordered live-docset and vector-content digests, quantization, counts/offsets, and CRC. Published artifacts have no live WAL and are opened through retained immutable owners. The migration hierarchy is xomn.1 corrected composite authority; xomn.2 exhaustive crash/topology proof; xomn.3 every production writer/opener plus fsfs watch staging; xomn.4 final legacy production API removal. xomn.1 is decomposed into canonical codec/resolver, qualified platform root, anti-rollback floor, fixed publisher/reconcile, exact engine receipts, retained snapshot, lifecycle migration, and retention-root accounting. The external floor is never another generation pointer. GC remains eligibility-only absent explicit deletion authorization.
acceptance_criteria: No production writer can emit identity-empty FSVI and no production search path can query legacy or mismatched identity. All vector, lexical, ANN, metadata, source, topology and authority contracts are exact and fresh-process durable. The fixed authority/floor state machine passes every tear/crash/concurrency/reconciliation case and returns typed outcomes without silent fallback. Production facade/fsfs/CASS paths use retained composite snapshots and one authority. Final policy scans find zero non-test legacy constructors, mutable/identity-blind opens, canonical-vector replacement, split CURRENT, pathname adoption, destructive repair, or implicit deletion. Linux/macOS/Windows each have truthful qualified evidence or typed no-I/O unsupported behavior until their native gate is green. Full unit/property/metamorphic/no-mock E2E/logging, strict remote workspace gates, native platform receipts, clippy/fmt, and UBS evidence pass.

title: Composite FSVI v2 generation authority: fixed slots, retained snapshot, and monotone rollback
description:
Build the durable composite authority for identity-complete semantic generations. The root has a cryptographically random RootId; one persistent no-follow LOCK inode; one precreated never-renamed, never-unlinked, exact 8192-byte AUTHORITY inode containing two fixed 4096-byte tear-detecting slots; random create_new immutable activation manifests; and random immutable generation objects containing the exact vector, lexical, ANN, metadata, source-checkpoint, and topology closure. There is no one-file CURRENT rename, canonical-vector replacement, split model/index pointer, pathname adoption, post-authority metadata write, implicit cleanup, or compatibility shim.

Authority sequence is distinct from artifact generation, begins at one, follows canonical physical parity, binds the exact predecessor AuthorityRef, and never wraps. Publication seals and admits the complete candidate first, then under persistent kernel flock and exact descriptor/owner fencing persists an InFlight attempt, writes only the inactive slot, performs the platform durability barrier and exact reread, compare-and-advances an explicit external anti-rollback floor, records completion, installs one retained composite Arc snapshot, and acknowledges only after convergence. Ordinary failure is possible only before any slot-write syscall. From the first possibly issued authority byte or external CAS request, failure is CommitOutcomeUnknown and must be reconciled from exact persisted attempt, both slots, immutable closure, and floor state. Unresolved local/floor state freezes further publication and eligibility decisions.

Fresh readers take shared flock, resolve and fence one exact slot pair plus external floor, open and retain the complete immutable closure, reread the identical authority state, then return one nonserializable owned GenerationSnapshot. Queries never reconstruct paths or mix separately opened generations. Rollback and repair are new higher-sequence activation records targeting retained admitted generations; they never decrement authority or rewrite incumbent bytes. Reader, rollback, repair, history, candidate, attempt, replica, and cross-process pin roots remain retained. This bead and its prerequisite children may compute retention eligibility only and delete nothing.

macOS remains blocked until the separate qualified platform-root bead proves descriptor-relative component walking, ACL-aware owner-private APFS admission, retained owners, and F_FULLFSYNC. Windows full support remains a separate prerequisite to final legacy-surface removal. Source edits and source reservations remain forbidden until this corrected tracker contract and platform prerequisite are protected by the integration lead.
design: The dependency-ordered implementation is: strict canonical authority codecs and pure resolver; qualified Linux/macOS capability-root substrate; linearizable external anti-rollback floor with explicit security profiles; fixed LOCK/AUTHORITY publisher and reconciliation; exact engine component receipts; retained composite snapshot/open; activation/history/time-travel/immutable-repair migration; and retention-root dry-run accounting. The final xomn.1 integration owns only composition and proof. Fixed AUTHORITY uses two authenticated 4096-byte physical frames selected by sequence & 1; genesis may encode one logical head separately in both frames. Frames bind physical slot, RootId, AuthorityRef, predecessor/floor/idempotency facts, canonical padding, CRC, and SHA-256 seal. The AuthorityRef addresses a strict canonical immutable activation object; its generation descriptor binds complete source checkpoint, ordered live-docset, FSVI v2, Quill, HNSW, metadata, storage, coverage, and topology receipts. LOCK uses alternating sealed owner/attempt frames and flock is the sole liveness authority. Platform durability is abstracted but fail-closed: Linux uses qualified file/directory barriers, Apple uses retained-fd F_FULLFSYNC on qualified local APFS, and unsupported targets return typed no-I/O errors. External floor advances only after local full-sync and is never a second generation pointer. Fresh reconciliation and readers use exact local/floor state; an externally anchored old head may remain readable with explicit pending-successor health, while fork, corrupt anchored newest closure, floor unavailability, or unrelated gap fails closed. Arc-owned exact bytes and handles, not mutable mmap/path state, back served snapshots. No file deletion is authorized.
acceptance_criteria: The corrected child graph is green and the final composition proves one composite authority across real fast/quality FSVI v2, Quill, native HNSW, metadata, and source checkpoint. Canonical format/property tests cover every byte/field, resource limit, future schema, parity, duplicate genesis, predecessor chain, one-slot survival, tear, equal divergence, fork, gap, ABA, and u64::MAX. Filesystem tests cover every ancestor/final symlink or swap, owner/ACL/mode/device/nlink drift, persistent flock fencing, stale PID records, two publishers one winner, losing CAS zero pre-boundary mutation, every LOCK/AUTHORITY partial write/sync/cancel/crash, external CAS success/idempotence/timeout/conflict/supersession, and fresh-process exact reconciliation. Readers return old or complete new snapshots, never mixed components; retained old readers survive publication and rollback. Same-count/dimension/vector/docset/generation/tier/lexical/ANN/metadata substitutions fail on the exact role before query work. Rollback and repair advance authority and preserve all old bytes. Inventory proofs show no rename-overwrite, unlink, truncate, canonical-vector replacement, WAL deletion, split CURRENT, or post-authority metadata mutation. No-mock E2E performs build, seal, publish, query, restart, update, crash recovery, higher-sequence rollback, time travel, and dry-run retention with bounded redacted detailed JSONL logs. Strict remote workspace all-target/all-feature check/test/clippy -D warnings, fmt, UBS, Linux receipts, and separately qualified physical macOS receipts pass. Windows final migration waits for its native substrate receipt; typed unsupported must touch nothing before then.

title: FSVI v2 recovery matrix: fault injection, shards, partial coverage, and fresh-process proof
description:
Prove the corrected fixed-slot composite generation authority under the complete failure, currently qualified platform, and topology matrix rather than treating happy-path publication as sufficient. Exercise one-tier, fast+quality, optional exact-ANN, real Quill lexical, metadata/source checkpoint, sharded complete coverage, and explicit partial coverage. Every case records old/proposed AuthorityRef, both authenticated slot states, external-floor state/version, persisted attempt, generation and component digests, ordered document coverage, exact fault boundary, retained objects/readers/pins, recovery classification, and retry/reindex plan. Partial shards may be inspected but never promoted as complete; mixed-generation, duplicate/missing/reordered/tombstoned coverage fails closed. A fresh executable must reconcile every injected interruption without in-memory state.

ACCEPTANCE: pure state/property tests cover every AUTHORITY and LOCK byte tear, short/reordered write, CRC/seal/schema/resource mutation, slot parity, duplicate genesis, predecessor chain, one-slot survival, equal divergence, fork/gap, sequence exhaustion, and local/external cross-product. Deterministic filesystem faults cover artifact/manifest/attempt/slot writes, ENOSPC, platform file/directory durability barriers, cancellation, kill, external CAS applied/not-applied/timeout/conflict/supersession, shared reader locks, root/LOCK/AUTHORITY substitution, and restart after every boundary. Before any slot byte, failed expected-old CAS changes no authority bytes; after the uncertainty boundary, reconciliation returns only an exact typed state. Tests cover higher-sequence rollback/repair, corrupt externally anchored active closure, corrupt rollback target, legacy v1 beside v2, future schema, permissions/ACL/filesystem refusal, reader retention, and retention-root eligibility dry run with zero deletion.

A real no-mock E2E driver executes build, seal, publish, query, interrupt, restart, inspect, reconcile, update, rollback, time-travel, dry-run retention, and re-query across real fast/quality FSVI, Quill, HNSW and metadata with versioned bounded JSONL logs and cryptographic receipts. It uses barriers, subprocess kills, and fault points rather than sleeps or mocks, preserves every incumbent/losing byte, and validates artifacts on every exit path. Until bd-macos-x86-generation-root-qualification-bb39t and bd-windows-generation-root-authority-f77gj close, x86_64 macOS and Windows must compile and return typed UnsupportedPlatform before any generation-root I/O; their native qualification gates only bd-xomn.4 final legacy removal, not this proof or Linux/Apple Silicon semantic delivery. The driver preserves artifacts on every pass/failure/timeout and validates logs/manifests before accepting a result. xomn.2 expands proof only and never repairs production state or deletes files.
acceptance_criteria: Every pure slot/attempt/floor state and every durable syscall/cancel/crash boundary has fresh-process proof over real one-tier, two-tier, Quill, ANN, metadata, shard and partial-coverage topologies. title: Migrate production FSVI writers and openers to retained v2 identity generations
description:
PRODUCTION FSVI V2 MIGRATION. Cut every FrankenSearch writer and opener over from FSVI v1, identity-blind or mutable state, and split paths to the exact identity-complete v2 composite generation authority. The public facade and fsfs production paths must call the real bound embedder operation and create_v2 for each tier, using independently obtained fast and quality model, input, producer, storage, quantization and generation identities. A test-only create_v2 round trip, unused accessor, identity string, dimension, filename, config default, or identity copied from the other tier is not migration.

Inventory and migrate TwoTierIndexBuilder, facade and index builders, fusion open/refresh/rebuild/cache, fsfs create/upgrade/watch/replay/reopen/search/repair, storage pipeline sinks, production examples, and CASS-facing package APIs. Build one random immutable generation containing retained owner-backed fast and quality FSVI v2 artifacts plus lexical, ANN when present, metadata, source and coverage receipts; seal and sync it; publish by expected-old composite authority; drop objects; reopen one retained GenerationSnapshot; then execute typed query, update/delete, watch/replay, restart, rollback and repair without separate model/index/CURRENT paths or post-authority writes.

Existing v1, incomplete identity, wrong space, same-count content substitution, stale ANN/cache, corrupt authority or unsupported platform returns typed inspection, ReindexRequired, recovery or zero-I/O UnsupportedPlatform. It cannot be queried, relabeled, copied, silently hash-degraded or adopted into v2. All existing update, delete, watch, replay, rollback, durability and cancellation functionality is preserved. The terminal cross-repo CASS lifecycle remains downstream.
design:
Consume the protected composite authority, typed per-tier umbrella and fsfs watch-staging gate. Every producer calls the actual embedding bind operation and creates v2 from that bound output; every consumer admits the immutable v2 bytes and retains the complete owner through the query lifetime. Positive and negative call-site inventories cover normal and feature-gated builds. No deprecated wrapper preserves v1 or mutable open.

Use one immutable generation transaction for vector, lexical, ANN, metadata, source, docset and coverage components. Publication, unknown-outcome reconciliation, retained readers, higher-sequence rollback and platform qualification remain exactly as specified by xomn.1 and watch staging.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A machine-readable positive census proves non-test facade and fsfs production calls to the real bound embedding operation and create_v2 for independent fast and quality identities. A negative census proves zero production v1 create, create_with_revision, replace_with_empty, identity-blind or mutable open, relabel, canonical-vector replacement, split CURRENT, unused identity accessor, copied-tier identity or post-authority write. Test-only calls and schema definitions cannot satisfy the positive census.

2. Real facade and fsfs flows build, seal, sync, expected-old publish, drop, fresh-process reopen and query one retained composite generation. QualityOnly directly retrieves quality; FullProgressive independently retrieves both owner-backed tiers and unions candidates. Fast-only and partial coverage remain truthful. Update/delete/watch/replay/restart/rollback/repair and cancellation preserve prior functionality.

3. Hash control, Model2Vec, MiniLM native and API producers have complete independent identity. Tests cover differing and equal dimensions, same-dimension wrong space, tokenizer/input/storage/quantization/producer drift, swapped tiers, same-count FSVI substitution, zero signal, partial docset/shards, stale ANN/cache, concurrent publishers, CommitOutcomeUnknown, higher-sequence rollback and old-reader retention.

4. Legacy v1 and missing/incomplete identity are inspection-only LegacyUnidentified or ReindexRequired; no relabel, copy, filename/id/dimension inference, hash fallback or mixed generation is searchable. Unsupported x86_64 macOS and Windows paths return typed UnsupportedPlatform before generation-root I/O until their qualifier beads close; native qualification gates only final legacy removal.

5. Real facade/fsfs no-mock E2E emits bounded redacted stage, owner, identity, coverage and authority receipts and preserves every prior user-visible feature and byte contract. Provisional exact-dependency CASS package compilation passes, while terminal CASS lifecycle stays downstream. Workspace all-feature check/test, warnings-denied lint, formatting, changed-file scanning, strict remote Linux and physical Apple receipts pass.

title: Differential corpus scale-up: PR 100 -> 10k, nightly 2k -> 250k, plus repo-snapshot and CASS-profile corpora
description:
The PR differential campaign runs on SharedCorpusView::Core100 -- ONE HUNDRED documents (runner.rs:4729-4737, generator.rs:49 CORE_RELEVANCE_DOCUMENT_COUNT=100, index_batch_size 5). Nightly steps to 2,000. generator.rs:37 defines XLARGE_DOCUMENT_COUNT (1M) but it is used ONLY by nightly_xlarge_stream_hash_integrity -- a generator self-check -- never by a differential or a perf run.

100 documents cannot support a decision to make Quill the library default. Whole classes of divergence are unreachable at that scale: multi-segment merge behaviour, tier promotion, block-max/MaxScore pruning (which only engages when postings are long enough -- directly relevant to bd-bt2t where grouped MaxScore prunes ZERO windows), skip-list traversal, fieldnorm quantisation buckets, dictionary restart-group boundaries, and long-posting codec paths (FOR vs bitmap vs partial-VINT selection).

TARGETS:
  - PR lane: 10,000 docs. Must stay under a few minutes; use the existing deterministic generator so it is reproducible from a seed, not a stored blob.
  - Nightly: 250,000+ docs, plus (a) a real repository snapshot and (b) a CASS-profile corpus (agent-session text: code blocks, long lines, mixed languages, heavy punctuation) since CASS is the primary consumer.
  - Keep Core100 as a fast smoke tier. DO NOT DELETE IT -- it is the quick signal.
CORPUS REALISM: include documents that actually exercise the codec branches -- very high-frequency terms (bitmap postings), rare terms, long documents, empty/whitespace-only fields, unicode, and terms crossing restart-group boundaries. A uniform synthetic corpus will pass while hiding exactly the bugs scale is supposed to reveal.

TESTS/LOGGING REQUIRED:
  - Assert the generated corpus actually hits each codec branch (posting-length histogram published as part of the artifact, with a test asserting every branch has >0 documents). A scale-up that never triggers the bitmap path bought nothing.
  - Emit per-tier timing and doc counts so a slow PR lane is diagnosable rather than merely annoying.
  - Record corpus seed + sha256 in the campaign artifact so any divergence is reproducible from the artifact alone.
  - A test asserting the PR lane completes within its time budget, so scale-up cannot silently make CI unusable.
design: Treat scale, realism and branch coverage as separate dimensions. Keep Core100 smoke; generate deterministic 10k PR and at least 250k nightly corpora plus immutable hashed real-repository and CASS-profile snapshots with provenance/redaction policy. Corpus manifests declare field/token/document-length distributions, language/query classes and intended codec/query-engine branches. A preflight measures actual postings/dictionary/segment/merge/pruning/codec coverage and rejects a nominally large but behaviorally shallow corpus. Qrels/query sets are versioned independently from engine output.
acceptance_criteria:
Core100 remains green and cannot satisfy the flip gate alone. PR 10k and nightly 250k-plus campaigns run real Quill and pinned Tantivy over identical hashed corpora and total observations. Real repository and CASS-profile lanes have reproducible provenance and redaction. Coverage artifacts prove every required postings codec, restart group, segment/merge/tombstone/tier/pruning/fieldnorm/query class is exercised or emit an explicit blocker. Seeds/manifests/generator/executable hashes reproduce divergences; per-stage counts/timings and CI budgets are enforced; qrels are independent and no required lane silently skips.

PARALLEL EXECUTION CONTRACT: Scale execution and closure require the ordinary Core V3 observer bd-live-total-lexical-contract-gxwy and the CASS total observer bd-cass-total-lexical-contract-jxyq, but do not wait for the enriched/QG-10 replacement-ready join. Terminal bd-qwkq remains independently mandatory at the release gate and is not weakened by this scheduling edge split.

title: HIGH: A/A null floor is sampled in a disjoint time window from the A/B effect it bounds; effect-stream drift and order-effect are computed but never gated
description:
Found by user-directed review sweep (MossyPine, 2026-07-31, mail #7365). CONFIRMED at origin/main.

DEFECT: benches/perf_matrix.rs:2917-2969 (collect_cell) executes the oracle_null stream to completion, then treatment_null, then the effect stream. The entire statistical safety story - claimed effect must clear 2x the same-invocation A/A floor (PERF_NULL_MARGIN_MULTIPLIER, perf_ratchet.rs:2101-2128) - assumes the null band characterizes noise DURING the A/B measurement; it actually characterizes noise during an earlier phase of the same process. For xlarge cells each sample is a full fresh index build, so the effect phase can begin minutes to hours after the null phase, under different thermal/allocator/page-cache state. Additionally perf.rs:2167-2176 gates intra-stream drift ONLY for the null stream, and effect.order_effect_log (perf.rs:1966-1968) is recorded but never compared against any bound - so a drifting or carryover-asymmetric effect stream is admissible provided the earlier null was quiet.

FAILURE: quiet machine during null (tight A/A CI, small floor) followed by background load or thermal ramp during the effect phase; block pairing cancels only within-block-symmetric noise, so an asymmetric carryover shifts median_log_ratio beyond the stale floor and a gate target with a CI computed under the i.i.d.-blocks assumption reads as a clean PASS/KEEP.

ROOT CAUSE: null and effect phases serialized for implementation convenience (documented in the comment at perf_matrix.rs:2896-2899) while the per-stream drift/order checks were only wired for the null.

FIX: (a) interleave null blocks with effect blocks under one seeded schedule - the QG-6 prepared runner already implements this pattern in-tree; (b) gate effect.drift_log and effect.order_effect_log with the same predeclared bounds already applied to the null. Affects every non-QG-6 KEEP margin, so re-derivation of existing margins should be considered after the fix.

title: Embedding-Stable Document Fingerprinting
description:
Implement content-aware document fingerprinting that detects when a document has changed enough to warrant re-embedding. This bridges the content-hash deduplication layer (bd-3w1.4) and the staleness detector (bd-3w1.12) with embedding-aware change detection.

## Key Insight

Not all document changes affect embedding quality equally. A typo fix doesn't change semantic meaning, but adding a new paragraph does. We need a fingerprint that is stable under minor edits but sensitive to semantic changes.

## Design

```rust
pub struct DocumentFingerprint {
    pub content_hash: u64,           // Full content FNV-1a hash (exact change detection)
    pub semantic_hash: u64,          // SimHash of content (approximate semantic similarity)
    pub char_count: u32,             // Character count (length change detection)
    pub token_estimate: u32,         // Estimated token count (whitespace split)
}

impl DocumentFingerprint {
    pub fn compute(text: &str) -> Self;
    pub fn needs_reembedding(&self, other: &Self, threshold: f64) -> bool;
}
```

## SimHash Algorithm (Charikar 2002)

1. Tokenize text into shingles (3-word windows)
2. Hash each shingle with FNV-1a
3. For each bit position, sum +1 for 1-bits, -1 for 0-bits
4. Final hash: bit i = 1 if sum_i > 0, else 0
5. Hamming distance between SimHashes ≈ 1 - cosine similarity of shingle sets

## Re-Embedding Decision Logic

- If content_hash differs AND hamming_distance(semantic_hash_a, semantic_hash_b) > threshold (default: 8/64 bits = 12.5%): re-embed
- If only content_hash differs but semantic_hash is close: skip re-embedding (minor edit)
- If char_count change > 20%: always re-embed (significant length change)

## Integration with Staleness Detector (bd-3w1.12)

- Store DocumentFingerprint in FrankenSQLite alongside document metadata
- Staleness detector compares stored fingerprints with current content
- Report: "N documents need re-embedding (M changed significantly, K minor edits skipped)"

## Why This Matters

Re-embedding is the most expensive operation in frankensearch (128ms per document for quality tier). For xf with 50K tweets, a full re-index takes ~107 minutes. Smart fingerprinting can skip 60-80% of documents that had only minor edits (e.g., metadata updates, formatting changes), reducing re-index time to ~20-40 minutes.

## Testing

- Unit: identical text → identical fingerprint
- Unit: minor typo → same semantic_hash, different content_hash
- Unit: significant change → different semantic_hash
- Unit: needs_reembedding threshold logic
- Unit: char_count/token_estimate accuracy
- Integration: fingerprint round-trip through FrankenSQLite storage
- Benchmark: fingerprint computation throughput (should be >100K docs/sec)
acceptance_criteria:
1. The feature is fully implemented according to this bead design, scope, and referenced files or modules.
2. Integration with dependent components is complete and behavior remains correct across normal and degraded flows.
3. Edge and error cases are explicitly handled with deterministic outcomes and clear reason codes or errors.
4. Unit and integration tests (and e2e where relevant) are added, passing, and include detailed structured logging assertions.
5. Performance and resource expectations in the bead are validated and documented with reproducible evidence.

title: MMR Diversified Ranking
description:
Implement Maximum Marginal Relevance (MMR) as an optional post-processing step after RRF fusion. MMR re-ranks results to balance relevance with diversity, preventing near-duplicate results from dominating the top-k.

## Background

Hybrid search often surfaces near-duplicate content because both lexical and semantic signals agree that similar documents are relevant. For example, in xf (tweet search), a cluster of retweets or quote-tweets on the same topic may all score highly, pushing diverse but equally-relevant results out of the top-k. MMR (Carbonell & Goldberg, 1998) is the standard approach to mitigating this in information retrieval.

## Algorithm

```
MMR(d) = lambda * Sim(d, q) - (1-lambda) * max_{d' in S} Sim(d, d')
```

Where:
- lambda in [0,1] controls relevance vs diversity tradeoff (default: 0.7)
- Sim(d, q) = existing RRF/blend score (relevance to query)
- Sim(d, d') = cosine similarity between document embeddings (inter-document similarity)
- S = already-selected documents

### Greedy Selection

MMR uses a greedy iterative selection process:
1. Select the highest-scoring document first (pure relevance)
2. For each subsequent selection, compute MMR score for all remaining candidates
3. Select the candidate with the highest MMR score
4. Repeat until k documents are selected

Complexity: O(k * n) where k = desired results, n = candidate pool size. For typical k=10, n=30, this is <1ms.

## Implementation

```rust
pub struct MmrConfig {
    pub lambda: f64,          // Default: 0.7 (relevance-heavy)
    pub enabled: bool,        // Default: false
    pub candidate_pool: usize, // Consider top N candidates for re-ranking (default: 3x limit)
}

pub fn mmr_rerank(
    candidates: &[FusedHit],
    embeddings: &HashMap<String, Vec<f32>>,  // doc_id -> embedding
    lambda: f64,
    limit: usize,
) -> Vec<FusedHit>;
```

The candidate_pool parameter controls how many pre-ranked results to consider for MMR re-ranking. Using 3x the desired limit (e.g., 30 candidates for top-10) provides sufficient diversity without excessive computation. The embeddings map provides the vector representations needed for inter-document similarity computation.

## Justification

Without MMR, top-10 results may contain 3-4 near-identical items, which is a poor user experience. This is especially valuable for:
- **cass** (session search): conversation sessions often have similar content across turns
- **xf** (tweet search): retweets, quote-tweets, and thread replies cluster heavily
- **mcp_agent_mail_rust**: email threads contain highly redundant content

MMR ensures the top-k covers diverse aspects of the query while still prioritizing relevance (lambda=0.7 means relevance is weighted 2.3x more than diversity).

## Considerations

- Embedding access: MMR needs document embeddings for inter-document similarity. These are already available in the FSVI index. The embeddings parameter should be populated from the same index used for search.
- Score normalization: RRF scores and cosine similarities are on different scales. Normalize both to [0,1] before combining in the MMR formula.
- Lambda tuning: provide lambda as a config parameter so consumers can tune it. lambda=1.0 disables diversity entirely (pure relevance), lambda=0.0 is maximum diversity.
- Interaction with explanations (Idea 2): MMR re-ranking should be reflected in HitExplanation.rank_movement.

## Testing

- [ ] Unit: lambda=1.0 produces pure relevance ordering (same order as input)
- [ ] Unit: lambda=0.0 produces maximum diversity ordering (most different items first)
- [ ] Unit: candidate pool exhaustion (fewer candidates than limit returns all candidates)
- [ ] Unit: single candidate is trivially returned
- [ ] Unit: two identical documents — second one is penalized
- [ ] Integration: verify diversity improvement on clustered test corpus (measure pairwise similarity of top-k before/after MMR)
- [ ] Benchmark: MMR overhead for various candidate pool sizes (30, 100, 300)

1. The feature is fully implemented according to this bead design, scope, and referenced files or modules.
2. Integration with dependent components is complete and behavior remains correct across normal and degraded flows.
3. Edge and error cases are explicitly handled with deterministic outcomes and clear reason codes or errors.
4. Unit and integration tests (and e2e where relevant) are added, passing, and include detailed structured logging assertions.
5. Performance and resource expectations in the bead are validated and documented with reproducible evidence.
6. Every explicit checklist item in the bead description is implemented and verified by automated tests or validation commands.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
DESIGN CLARIFICATION: Embedding retrieval for inter-document similarity.

The mmr_rerank() function needs document embeddings to compute inter-document cosine similarity. Three options were considered:

CHOSEN APPROACH: Add VectorIndex::get_embeddings(doc_ids: &[&str]) -> HashMap<String, Vec<f32>> to frankensearch-index. This batch-retrieves embeddings for the candidate pool by:
1. Looking up doc_id_hash in the record table
2. Reading the vector slab at the corresponding offset
3. Converting f16 -> f32 (if quantized)

This keeps MMR decoupled from the index internals — it receives a HashMap and does not care how it was produced. The caller (TwoTierSearcher or consumer) is responsible for populating the HashMap from whatever source has the embeddings.

Cost: For candidate_pool=30 docs at 384 dims: 30 * 384 * 4 bytes = 46KB memory + 30 f16->f32 conversions = <0.1ms. Negligible.

NOTE: VectorIndex::get_embeddings() is a new API that should be added to bd-3un.13 or as a follow-on subtask. It is NOT a new bead — it is a small extension (~20 lines) to the existing VectorIndex API.

title: ann feature does not compile: TierSource rename b1056dd9 missed every cfg(feature=ann) path in two_tier.rs (29 x E0609)
description:

  error: could not compile 'frankensearch-index' (lib test) due to 28 previous errors

title: generation_root residual LOWs: cross-run test-fixture accumulation and Linux/macOS symlink error-kind parity
description:
Carved out of bd-cbz3f (closed 2026-08-04) so its two unresolved LOW findings stay tracked. The four MEDIUM items and the atime LOW in that bead are fixed and each is red-proven; these two are not.

LOW A -- test-fixture accumulation, PARTIALLY improved, not closed.
Original finding: 'persistent test fixtures under target/ accumulate unbounded'. Current state (crates/frankensearch-index/src/generation_root.rs:6634-6690): fixtures no longer live under target/. secure_fixture_base() builds $HOME/.frankensearch-generation-root-tests-<pid>-<epoch_nanos>-<attempt> and pre-creates a bounded pool of FIXTURE_SLOT_COUNT = 512 mode-0700 slots, with fixture_root() asserting the serial never exceeds the pool. So WITHIN a process the fixture count is bounded and the directories are no longer in the build tree.
What is still open: the base directory name embeds pid + epoch_nanos, so every test process creates a NEW base under $HOME, and no cleanup path was found. Repeated local runs therefore still accumulate directories -- just in $HOME instead of target/. Fix options: register a cleanup at process exit, reuse a stable per-user base and clear slots on init, or document the directory and provide a documented purge command.

LOW B -- symlink-at-final-component error-kind parity, NEEDS macOS HARDWARE.
Original finding: 'symlink-at-final-component error-kind differs Linux vs macOS'. Both platforms have coverage -- root_qualification_rejects_symlink_final_component (:10892) and ancestor_and_final_symlinks_fail_without_touching_decoys (:7289) on Linux, macos_absolute_root_route_rejects_ancestor_and_final_symlinks (:12882) on macOS -- but whether the two platforms return the SAME GenerationRootErrorKind for the same input cannot be determined from a Linux host: the macOS arms are cfg'd out and never compiled here. Verifying (and, if they disagree, deciding whether to unify the kind or document the divergence) requires an arm64 macOS run. Consider scheduling alongside bd-poqoh, which is blocked on the same class of hardware, but they are independent pieces of work.

Neither item is a fail-open security defect: LOW A is hygiene, LOW B is cross-platform diagnostic consistency.
close_reason:
Closed at commit 0c4cba6e (pushed to main). Both LOWs addressed; the macOS half of LOW B is a NAMED residual, not a claimed pass.

LOW A -- fixture accumulation FIXED, by a different route than the one prescribed, because the prescribed one does not work here.
secure_fixture_base() minted $HOME/.frankensearch-generation-root-tests-<pid>-<epoch_nanos>-<attempt>, so every test process added a fresh TOP-LEVEL entry to the user's home with no cleanup path. Per-run bases now nest under ONE stable private parent, $HOME/.frankensearch-generation-root-tests/<pid>-<epoch_nanos>-<attempt>. $HOME gains a single entry ever instead of one per run; per-run isolation is unchanged; no deletion code was introduced; and a future purge is now one scoped directory rather than a glob across a home directory.
Adoption of a parent left by an earlier run is GUARDED, not assumed: on AlreadyExists it must still be a real directory via symlink_metadata (never a symlink), owned by whoever owns HOME, and mode exactly 0700. HOME's own uid is the ownership reference, which avoids an unsafe getuid() in a crate that forbids unsafe.

MEASURED LOSS, REVERTED, AND RECORDED IN THE CODE COMMENT so it is not retried: rooting these fixtures at std::env::temp_dir() -- the scratchpad TMPDIR pattern this task specified -- BREAKS them. It failed 74 of the 102 selected generation_root tests with GenerationRootError { kind: WrongOwner, stage: OpenRootRoute, component_index: Some(0), expected: Some(0), observed: Some(1000) }. Route qualification walks the ENTIRE ancestor chain and rejects a shared temp root at its first component, so $HOME is load-bearing for these fixtures rather than incidental. I had checked beforehand that the filesystem-sensitive fixtures (btrfs/statx/chattr/bind-mount/proc-overmount) take their base from dedicated env vars and so were unaffected -- that was the right question but the wrong one to stop at; I verified the filesystem would not change and missed that the ancestor OWNERSHIP chain would. The test suite caught it, not review.
The remaining cleanup half genuinely requires deletion code and stays Rule-1 gated on bd-ymnup, where I recorded this as a second call site of the same policy question plus a third no-deletion option specific to here (stable base + reused slot pool, bounded by FIXTURE_SLOT_COUNT), with its tradeoff named: it would let a slot carry residue between runs, which is an owner call for route-qualification fixtures.

LOW B -- Linux side implemented as a LIVE PROOF; macOS side left as an encoded expectation.
The bead's premise was slightly off: BOTH platforms already assert GenerationRootErrorKind::SymbolicLink, so the expectation was encoded on both sides already. What Linux actually lacked was any coverage of the ANCESTOR-OF-AN-ABSOLUTE-ROUTE shape -- it tested only the final component at root admission (root_qualification_rejects_symlink_final_component) and the confined route (ancestor_and_final_symlinks_fail_without_touching_decoys) -- so for that input the parity claim rested on nothing measurable from this host. Added generation_root::tests::linux::absolute_root_route_rejects_ancestor_and_final_symlinks, mirroring macos_absolute_root_route_rejects_ancestor_and_final_symlinks input-for-input and asserting the kind on BOTH the ancestor and the final arm. It passes by name.
RESIDUAL, NAMED: the macOS arm lives in a cfg(all(target_os = "macos", target_arch = "aarch64")) module that never compiles on a Linux host, so I can prove neither that macOS returns the same kind nor even that that module still compiles -- the same cfg-rot class as bd-rg18d, where an ann-gated module had been uncompilable for four days. Confirming parity needs an arm64 macOS run; schedulable alongside bd-poqoh, which is blocked on the same hardware class. The new test's doc comment says this explicitly so the Linux green is never mistaken for cross-platform proof.

GATES (frankensearch-index):
  cargo test --lib generation_root                      => 102 passed, 0 failed, 15 ignored, 575 filtered out
       -- the IDENTICAL filter and selection that reported 28 passed / 74 failed under the reverted approach, so this is a true before/after rather than a narrowed re-run.
  cargo test --lib generation_root::tests::linux        => 100 passed, 0 failed
  cargo clippy --no-deps -p frankensearch-index --all-targets -- -D warnings => Finished, exit 0
  cargo fmt --check -p frankensearch-index              => clean
  pre-commit ledger gate ran green on the commit itself.

VERIFICATION NOTE worth carrying: my first attempt to run the new test reported 'test result: ok. 0 passed; 692 filtered out' because I guessed the module path (the tests nest as generation_root::tests::linux::, not generation_root::tests::). A filtered cargo test that matches NOTHING is indistinguishable from a pass unless the counts are read. That vacuous ok was what nearly hid the 74-test regression above.

title: 2 ann tests cannot express a post-build tombstone under the bd-x06p5 read-only tier role model
description:
Exposed by bd-rg18d. These tests have not compiled since 2026-07-31 (the ann feature was broken), so they never ran against the reader/writer role enforcement that landed meanwhile in bd-x06p5 / 9019b97f / 2fc8e7be. Once bd-rg18d made the ann feature compile again, they fail at RUNTIME.

FAILING (cargo test -p frankensearch-index --features ann):
  two_tier::tests::ann_wal_merge_matches_canonical_resolution_before_and_after_exact_fallback
  two_tier::tests::ann_wal_shadowed_top_hit_stays_suppressed_through_raw_exact_fallback
Both panic identically:
  post-build tombstone: InvalidConfig { field: "fsvi.writer_lock", value: "soft_delete_batch", reason: "this handle is a shared read-only mapping; reopen with VectorIndex::open_writer before mutating a published FSVI" }

MECHANISM: TwoTierIndex::open builds its fast tier with VectorIndex::open_read_only (two_tier.rs ~571), so the tier is a SHARED READ-ONLY mapping. Both tests want to apply a post-build tombstone to the live index -- soft_delete on the fast tier -- to force the exact-underfill fallback path, asserting a before-state and an after-state on the SAME index object. Under the new role model a TwoTierIndex can never mutate its own fast tier, so that shape is no longer expressible. Note WAL injection in the same tests still works, because wal_entries is an in-memory Vec and touches no mapping.

NOT A REGRESSION FROM bd-rg18d: that bead only migrated field accesses (self.fast_index -> self.fast_tier(), etc.) onto accessors that already existed. The 4 other previously-broken ann tests pass after it, and 98 tests pass in the same run. These 2 fail on a runtime lock contract, not on the rename.

WHY I DID NOT 'FIX' IT: the obvious workaround is a test-only seam that opens the fast tier with VectorIndex::open_writer so the tier is mutable in tests. I deliberately did NOT add that. bd-x06p5 exists to ENFORCE that a published FSVI is not mutated through a shared read-only mapping; adding a test-only writable tier would erode exactly the invariant it just established, which is gate self-weakening dressed up as a test fix. Re-expressing these two tests is a design decision that belongs to the lane that defined the role model.

LIKELY SHAPE OF THE REAL FIX (for whoever owns it): apply the tombstone out-of-band -- drop the index, VectorIndex::open_writer on the fast path, soft_delete, drop the writer, reopen the TwoTierIndex -- and re-inject the WAL entries, since an in-memory WAL does not survive the reopen. That changes the tests from 'tombstone on a live index' to 'tombstone applied between opens', so someone must confirm the fallback path being pinned is still the intended one before adopting it.

SEPARATELY FIXED IN bd-rg18d: the other 2 ann failures were map-lock conflicts (ann_search_excludes_tombstoned_docs, ann_tombstone_filter_uses_doc_id_not_hnsw_position), where a live writable VectorIndex handle was never dropped before TwoTierIndex::open took its shared reader lock. Those were unambiguous -- a drop() before the reopen preserves the test intent exactly -- so they were fixed there rather than filed here.

Planted negative: deleting only writer.soft_delete("doc-delete") makes two_tier::tests::ann_wal_merge_matches_canonical_resolution_before_and_after_post_build_tombstone fail; restored test passes. Gates: cargo fmt --check PASS; rch exec -- cargo clippy --no-deps -p frankensearch-index --features ann -- -D warnings PASS (remote worker vmi1149989); rch exec -- cargo test -p frankensearch-index --features ann -- --test-threads=1 PASS via documented local fallback (no admissible slot): 810 unit passed, integrations 25+6+7+1+1+3, doctests 2+7.

title: CI lane 'cargo test --workspace --all-features' can never pass: quill compile_error! forbids bench-internals + profile-internals
description:
Found while verifying bd-rg18d. This is a CI CONTRACT defect, not a code defect.

crates/frankensearch-quill/src/lib.rs:16 declares an intentional mutual exclusion:
  #[cfg(all(feature = "bench-internals", feature = "profile-internals"))]
  compile_error!("profile-internals is a diagnostic-sidecar feature and must not be linked into a Quill timing build");

--all-features necessarily enables BOTH, so any --all-features build of the workspace is guaranteed to fail by design. That makes these lanes unpassable as written:
  ci.yml:572  cargo test --workspace --all-features -- --nocapture
  ci.yml:704/777/789 reference the same command as a required lane / replay command.
Note ci.yml:371-372 are FINE: they scope --all-features to -p frankensearch and -p frankensearch-fusion, neither of which exposes profile-internals, so those remain valid all-features gates.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT PROBLEM in the same crate: even setting the deliberate compile_error! aside, quill has genuine feature-combination errors that only appear under broad feature sets. From cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features:
  E0252 the name AtomicBool is defined multiple times -- crates/frankensearch-quill/src/index.rs:41. index.rs:17-18 imports AtomicBool under cfg(any(conformance-internals, profile-internals)) and index.rs:40-41 imports it again under cfg(test); with those features on in a test build, both cfgs are live.
  E0782 expected a type, found a trait -- crates/frankensearch-quill/src/argus.rs:5751, 7134, 7187, 7217 (PostingCursor::has_validated_post_move_contract used in type position).
  E0599 no method named has_validated_post_move_contract for Box<dyn argus::PostingCursor> -- argus.rs:7245.
  E0308 mismatched types -- crates/frankensearch-quill/src/index.rs:11108.
crates/frankensearch-quill/ is byte-identical to HEAD (absent from git status), so these are committed, not worktree churn.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND CI COSMETICS: agents are told to verify with --all-features (it is the standard cfg-gated blind-spot check in this repo, and it is exactly how bd-rg18d was found). If the workspace-wide form of that command can never pass, every agent who runs it gets an unattributable red, learns to ignore it, and the next genuine cfg-gated break hides in the noise. bd-rg18d sat undetected for four days behind precisely that noise.

SUGGESTED DIRECTION (needs an owner decision, not mine to make): either give the lane an explicit feature set that respects the declared exclusion (e.g. --all-features minus profile-internals, or per-package all-features lanes like ci.yml:371 already uses), or move the diagnostic sidecar out of the default feature union. Then fix the E0252/E0782/E0599/E0308 sites separately. Do NOT delete the compile_error! -- it encodes a real invariant about timing builds.
close_reason:
Closed at commit d3fe5623 (pushed to main). The nightly lane can run again.

THE DEFECT: cargo test --workspace --all-features could never pass. frankensearch-quill enforces a deliberate exclusivity invariant with a compile_error! in crates/frankensearch-quill/src/lib.rs:16 -- profile-internals is a diagnostic sidecar that must never be linked into a bench-internals timing build, because profile instrumentation corrupts the timings this repo treats as evidence, exactly as quill's own Cargo.toml comment states at the feature definition. --all-features unions both, so the lane died before running a single test.

DIRECTION CHOSEN, and why the other option was refused: fix the LANE, KEEP the guard. This bead offered 'precedence rather than compile_error!' as an alternative. That is worse, not merely different: precedence means one side silently wins, so either a timing build links profile instrumentation anyway or a profiling build silently drops its receipts. Silent degradation of a perf-evidence build is the precise failure class the standing rules forbid, and a loud compile_error! is the correct design. Deleting or softening it would have been the tech debt, not the fix. What is actually true is narrower and is now recorded in the workflow itself: a feature graph with a DECLARED exclusivity invariant has no single all-features build. That is a fact about the graph, not a workaround.

FEATURE-GRAPH FACTS, verified across every workspace Cargo.toml rather than assumed:
  profile-internals is defined ONLY in quill (Cargo.toml:28) and forwarded by NO dependent, so quill can acquire it only by being a SELECTED package under --all-features.
  quill's bench-internals IS forwarded unconditionally by frankensearch-quill-gauntlet (Cargo.toml:60, plus its perf-harness/tantivy-oracle lists at 16 and 23), so deselecting quill does not stop it being compiled.
  Other dependents request nothing conflicting: facade optional + quill?/durability, fsfs durability, fusion optional.

VERIFICATION of the exact new lane form:
  rch exec -- cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features --exclude frankensearch-quill
  => Finished, exit 0. 'Checking frankensearch-quill' IS present in that log, proving quill still builds as a dependency and no coverage was traded away for the fix.
  Workflow parses: python3 yaml.safe_load => YAML OK, 12 jobs. No occurrence of the unpassable form remains (rg 'all-features -- --nocapture' => NONE).

FOUR SITES FIXED, not one: the lane at ci.yml:589, the nightly required_lanes entry at :721, and BOTH perf-gate replay_command fields at :794 and :806. The stale references mattered on their own -- CI artifacts were publishing a replay_command that could not succeed, which is how the contradiction propagated past the single lane.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT ADD: the two quill feature-matrix arms. Both were run and both are RED on pre-existing crate errors, none related to the exclusion:
  arm A (durability,bench-internals,conformance-internals,pruning-conformance,tantivy-oracle): lib OK, lib test 6 errors -- E0252 at index.rs:41, E0782 x4 and E0599 in argus.rs.
  arm B (same but profile-internals): WORSE -- the LIB itself fails, E0308 at index.rs:11108 (Arc::clone(checkpoint) needs an unsize coercion to Arc<dyn QueryWorkCheckpoint>), plus the same test-target errors. profile-internals therefore does not compile at all, the same class as bd-rg18d.
Adding known-red lanes would recreate the exact pathology that let bd-rg18d hide for four days: an always-red gate trains everyone to ignore the signal. Filed as bd-bia9a (P1) with both verbatim arm commands ready to drop in once the crate errors land, and with the explicit instruction not to delete the compile_error!.

PREDICTION RECORDED, NOT MEASURED: the E0252 fires for any test build with conformance-internals on, and pruning-conformance = ["conformance-internals"], so existing dedicated lanes ci.yml:523 and :996 should be red today for the same reason. I did not run those lanes, so bd-bia9a carries this as a prediction to verify rather than a result.

Local pinned nightly-2026-07-20 / rustc 1.99.0-nightly (9f36de775) and the rch remote produce IDENTICAL error sets. The hypothesis was wrong; this is real.

WHY NORMAL BUILDS DO NOT SEE IT: the duplicate import is #[cfg(test)]-gated, so the lib builds fine and only test/bench targets break. Any lane that runs --all-targets (ci.yml:375) is red.

EXACT ERRORS, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude optimize-params -- -D warnings:
  crates/frankensearch-quill/src/index.rs:41:5   error[E0252] the name AtomicBool is defined multiple times
  crates/frankensearch-quill/src/index.rs:41:5   error unused import std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool
  crates/frankensearch-quill/src/index.rs:13393:13 error clippy::similar_names
  crates/frankensearch-quill/src/index.rs:13417:14 error clippy::similar_names
  crates/frankensearch-quill/src/argus.rs:5751:17 error[E0782] expected a type, found a trait
  crates/frankensearch-quill/src/argus.rs:7134:18 error[E0782] expected a type, found a trait
  crates/frankensearch-quill/src/argus.rs:7187:17 error[E0782] expected a type, found a trait

Excluding the crate does not help: other members depend on it, so it is linted as a workspace member regardless, and doing so surfaces a further clippy::too_long_first_doc_paragraph in the quill LIB target.

WHY I DID NOT FIX IT: E0252 alone is trivial, but E0782 and especially E0599 are not mechanical. has_validated_post_move_contract exists 5 times in argus.rs yet is not callable on Box<dyn PostingCursor>, which points at the unforgeable-ValidatedPostMoveContract design in 7a174fd5 ('fix(quill): unforgeable ValidatedPostMoveContract for posting cursors').
