title: Release lane emits release.inventory.* instead of the two contract-declared release.* codes
description:
Found during the bd-fsfs-cross-platform-semantic-installer-46z3u per-MUST re-audit (2026-08-04). Not hardware-blocked, so it is filed out of that bead rather than left inside its residual.

docs/fsfs-packaging-release-install-contract.md declares twelve Required Reason Codes. Ten now have emitters. These two have NONE, anywhere in the repo:
  release.build.missing_target
  release.publish.asset_upload_failed
They appear only in schemas/fixtures, schemas/fixtures-invalid, the two fsfs goldens, and the contract doc — i.e. they are DECLARED DATA with no emitting code. rg --no-ignore over install.sh, .github/workflows/, and crates/*/src finds no emitter.

Meanwhile .github/workflows/ci.yml DOES emit ten reason codes in its release lanes, none of which the contract declares:
  release.inventory.{archive_set_mismatch, checksum_mismatch, exact_six, malformed_checksum, metadata_count, metadata_field, metadata_name, missing_archive_pair, missing_pairs, unexpected_or_duplicate_pair}

So the release lane invented a parallel vocabulary rather than emitting the contract's. Two defensible fixes and the choice is the owner's: (a) emit the contract codes at the release-build missing-target and release-publish asset-upload failure points (ci.yml:1523 release-build, :1708 release-build-lite, :1861 release-publish), keeping release.inventory.* as finer-grained detail; or (b) amend the contract's Required Reason Codes list to declare the inventory vocabulary that is actually in use. I did not attempt (a) here: I cannot execute GitHub Actions to verify a workflow edit, and a YAML change asserted green without a run would be worthless evidence.

METHOD WARNING for whoever takes this — .gitignore contains '/*.sh', so ripgrep's default traversal SKIPS install.sh and uninstall.sh even though git tracks them. title: Retire the sync searcher's raw cross-tier query vector (bd-ctzo 4c)
description:
The sync progressive path (`crates/frankensearch-fusion/src/sync_searcher.rs`) cannot be brought
under typed owner-backed activation without changing its public API, and its current defect is worse
than "fast-pool rescoring".

FINDING (bd-ctzo slice 4c scoping, 2026-08-04). `SyncTwoTierSearcher::search_internal(query_vec:
&[f32], ...)` takes ONE raw vector and uses it for BOTH tiers:
`self.index.quality_scores_for_hits(query_vec, &fast_hits)` scores the QUALITY index with the
FAST-space query. The async path's C2 defect was that quality only rescored a fast-selected pool;
here the vector itself is cross-space. There is no embedder on this type at all, so there is nothing
to derive a quality-space embedding from and nothing to join an identity against: a raw `&[f32]`
carries no space, no producer, and no storage contract.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE MIGRATION. `admit_semantic_query` (the async C1 guard) has no analogue here.
On an owner-backed index the sync path can prove NOTHING about the caller's vector -- not for the
quality tier and not for the fast tier. So slice 4c is not "mirror the async change"; it is the raw
public-API retirement the ctzo bead lists as downstream, applied to this one type: `search_collect`
/ `search_collect_with_filter` / `search_iter` / `search_iter_with_filter` must take
`TieredQueryEmbeddings` (per-tier `BoundQueryEmbedding`) instead of `&[f32]`.

WHY THIS WAS NOT DONE INSIDE bd-ctzo. Deciding what a raw-vector caller should get on an
owner-backed index is a policy choice with no obviously right default -- refuse outright, degrade to
fast-only with a typed skip_reason, or keep serving cross-space quality scores -- and guessing it
would have changed sync behaviour on a guess rather than on evidence. Every canonical production
index on disk is still v1 (no admitted owner), so the defect is currently unreachable in production
and this is not urgent; it becomes reachable the moment v2 generations are published canonically.

BLAST RADIUS: `SyncTwoTierSearcher` is publicly re-exported from the facade
(`frankensearch/src/lib.rs`) and used by three benches (`progressive_replay`, `sync_int8_fetch`,
`collect_limit_all`) and `frankensearch/examples/bench_quick.rs`. Those callers all synthesize their
own query vectors, so they need identity fixtures, not just a signature change.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. The sync entry points take per-tier bound query embeddings; a raw cross-tier `&[f32]` is not
   representable in the signature.
2. On an admitted owner-backed index every identity join completes before any vector read, with the
   same typed refusal fields the async path uses.
3. A legacy v1 index stays searchable, asserted by a test, exactly as the async path preserves it.
4. A test proves the quality tier is never scored with a fast-space vector -- planted negative, not
   an assertion about the current code.
5. Benches, examples and the facade re-export are updated; workspace check/clippy/fmt clean.
close_reason: Sync entry points take TieredQueryEmbeddings; per-tier space join runs before any vector read; quality tier scored with the quality query; independent retrieval gated on attested identity to match the async path. Red proofs on all three guards, each failing exactly one test. Gates: fusion --lib 959/6 pre-existing, sync 10/10, parity 19/19, clippy -D warnings clean.

title: Exact-generation source_checkpoint convention is split: three producers accept it, metadata derives it, and drift is attributed to the wrong role
description:
All four exact-generation component producers now exist, and three of them disagree with the fourth
about where source_checkpoint comes from. Nothing enforces agreement, and admit() will attribute the
resulting failure to the wrong role.

EVIDENCE, all landed and pushed:
  vector  (e7b611c9, bd-cycdy)  vector_component_receipt(witness, docs, source_checkpoint: [u8;32])
  ann     (e7b611c9, bd-cycdy)  ann_component_receipt(receipt, docs, source_checkpoint: [u8;32])
  lexical (d300f838, bd-qblyy)  ExactLexicalSnapshotDescriptor::exact_lexical_component_receipt(
                                    &self, source_checkpoint: [u8;32])
  metadata(f64401bd, bd-uu0ly)  ExactComponentReceiptV1::for_metadata_manifest(manifest, bytes,
                                    documents)  -- DERIVES the checkpoint from
                                    manifest.commit_range via generation_source_checkpoint_v1 and
                                    deliberately refuses a caller-supplied value.

So three roles ACCEPT an opaque 32 bytes and one COMPUTES them. For a real four-role join to admit,
the caller must pass exactly generation_source_checkpoint_v1(&manifest.commit_range) to the other
three. That requirement is written down nowhere, is not exported as a step anyone is told to take,
and is not checked.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A DOC GAP: the metadata role is the one that is RIGHT. It derives its value
from the artifact that actually records the commit window. When a caller passes anything else to the
other three -- a commit sha, a nonce, a timestamp, a zero -- admit() compares against the VECTOR
anchor and reports CheckpointDrift naming "metadata", because metadata is the role that disagrees
with the (wrong) anchor. The single component that computed its checkpoint correctly is the one the
error blames. That inverts the whole point of role attribution, which rds6v's acceptance requires
("rejected on the correct role").

I own the odd one out: I chose derivation on bd-uu0ly and flagged the convention question for pane 10
as keystone owner on that bead's close, then again on bd-cycdy's. It is still unanswered. This bead
exists so the answer is not made implicitly by whoever writes the first real four-role caller.

OPTIONS, for the keystone owner to choose:
 (a) Export the derivation as the documented way to obtain a checkpoint, and have the three
     accepting producers document that their parameter MUST be generation_source_checkpoint_v1 of
     the generation's commit range. Cheapest; keeps metadata's fail-closed property; still
     unenforced.
 (b) Give the join a typed SourceCheckpointV1 newtype constructible only by derivation, so an
     arbitrary [u8;32] cannot be passed to any producer. Enforced by the type system; touches all
     four signatures and three closed beads.
 (c) Drop derivation from metadata and make it caller-supplied like the rest. Restores uniformity
     but loses the property that a metadata receipt cannot name a checkpoint its own manifest does
     not support, which was a deliberate fail-closed choice.

My recommendation is (b) if cdny8 has not started, (a) if it has -- (c) trades a real safety property
for symmetry and I would argue against it.

ACCEPTANCE: a four-role join built from the REAL producers -- FSVI witness, Quill descriptor, native
HNSW receipt, and GenerationManifest, over one document set -- admits. Today no test anywhere
constructs that; every join test in the tree pairs real receipts with hand-built stand-ins for the
other roles, which is exactly why the split went unnoticed. A paired control must show that a caller
using a non-derived checkpoint is rejected naming the role that actually drifted, not metadata.

Blocks bd-retained-composite-generation-snapshot-cdny8 in practice: it is the first consumer that
must join all four, and this is the first thing it will hit. bd-7hvtf is in flight on the descriptor-
relative admission surface and may hit it sooner.
close_reason: Unified in 0aac47f4 (pushed). SourceCheckpointV1 newtype with derive(&CommitRange) as its ONLY constructor; the three accepting producers (vector/ANN in exact_component_adapters, lexical in keeper) now take it instead of a bare [u8;32], so an arbitrary array is not a value any producer can be given. Metadata unchanged -- it was already deriving and was already right. Took option (b) over (a) because a convention enforced only by a doc comment is the same defect written down. Wire field stays [u8;32] via one-way to_bytes(), so no fixture or golden moves. PER-PRODUCER PLANTED NEGATIVES: every_non_anchor_role_is_blamed_for_its_own_checkpoint_drift drifts ANN, lexical and metadata each ALONE and asserts the error names that same role, with an all-agreeing control; the anchor case is separate (a_drifted_anchor_is_reported_against_the_roles_that_disagree_with_it) because 'the anchor moved' is a different failure from 'a component drifted' and conflating them caused the original misattribution. NEGATIVE RESULT RECORDED: re-adding a from_bytes escape hatch reddens NO test -- the guarantee is the absence of a constructor, which no runtime test can observe -- so enforcement is a compile_fail doctest pinned to E0423, verified load-bearing (making the field pub turns it red). The code pin caught my own wrong guess: I predicted E0603. The old zero-placeholder test no longer compiles by construction and was replaced with no_commit_range_derives_the_zero_placeholder_checkpoint across six ranges. Gates: core 1103/0, index 701/0, quill 553/0, doctests incl. the new compile_fail, clippy -D warnings clean on core and index, fmt clean; quill's single clippy error is a pre-existing unreadable-literal at HEAD line 14595, outside every hunk here. title: cass-compat lane: pre-existing unused imports in index_builder.rs break clippy
description:
Found while building the bd-8nqz.5 cass-compat receipt (60cf93d1). NOT caused by that work — my diff adds no imports.

cargo clippy --no-deps -p frankensearch --no-default-features --features cass-compat --lib -- -D warnings exits 101 on:
  frankensearch/src/index_builder.rs:42  unused import: frankensearch_lexical::TantivyIndex
  (a second unused import in the same file, frankensearch_core::traits::LexicalWrite)

These are inherited reds on a lane whose clippy was evidently never run: ci.yml only does 'cargo check -p frankensearch --lib --no-default-features --features cass-compat' (ci.yml:381), and check does not run clippy. The imports are presumably used under other feature combinations and need cfg gating for this lane.

Filed rather than absorbed into the receipt so the fix lands with its own owner and its own gate decision — in particular whether the cass-compat lane should gain a clippy step in CI, since without one this will silently recur.
close_reason:
FIXED AND VERIFIED at 63c699c6 (pushed, main and master). TopazCat, 2026-08-04.

THE CENSUS WAS OFF BY ONE TARGET, and the correction matters for the gate choice. I filed this as
"line 42 plus a second import in the same file". Under `--lib` there is exactly ONE red; the other
two only appear once the lib TEST target is compiled:
  index_builder.rs:42   TantivyIndex   (lib)
  index_builder.rs:1097 LexicalWrite   (lib test)
  index_builder.rs:1105 TantivyIndex   (lib test)
A gate written only as `clippy --lib` would therefore have closed one third of this bug and looked
green. That is why the CI step added here is two invocations, not one.

ROOT CAUSE, not symptom. All three were gated `#[cfg(feature = "lexical-tantivy")]` while every use
site sits under `all(quill, lexical-tantivy)` (the blue-green/direct arms of open_lexical_reader,
and the tantivy-generation test) or under `all(lexical, not(quill))` (the standalone reader/writer
at 899/1021). `cass-compat = [lexical-tantivy]` enables the namespace WITHOUT enabling either arm,
so the imports were genuinely unreachable there. Each cfg now mirrors its own use sites exactly.
Deliberately NOT done: no `allow(unused_imports)`, and nothing deleted. The `all(lexical,
not(quill))` disjunct is unsatisfiable today because `lexical = ["quill"]`, but the code it guards
is still in the file, so the import must stay in sync with it or decoupling those features later
turns this into a compile error instead of a lint.

THE GATE DECISION THIS BEAD ASKED FOR: yes, the lane gains clippy. New ci.yml step "cargo clippy
(cass-compat lane) (bd-6281c)", placed next to the QG-10 guard and leaving QG-10's own lines
untouched. Two commands because neither covers the other:
  cargo clippy -p frankensearch --lib --no-default-features --features cass-compat -- -D warnings
  cargo clippy -p frankensearch --no-default-features --features hash,cass-compat --all-targets -- -D warnings
The first is the lane exactly as ci.yml:381 checks it (no hash). The second is the feature shape a
real CASS consumer resolves (CASS uses hash,cass-compat,ann,native) and is the only one that reaches
the lib test target. `--all-targets` on cass-compat WITHOUT hash is not usable as a gate: the
examples and tests/*.rs targets hard-require HashEmbedder and fail E0432 on every narrow lane,
which is why CI checks those lanes at --lib in the first place.

RED PROOF: with the three cfgs reverted in place (Edit, not stash) both new gate commands exit 101
and name all three imports by file:line. GREEN after restore: both exit 0, zero warnings. Exit codes
captured unpiped.

REGRESSION EVIDENCE: QG-10's existing check lines all exit 0 (--features quill, --features
lexical-tantivy, --features cass-compat at --lib, and -p frankensearch --all-targets --all-features).
cargo test -p frankensearch --lib --no-default-features --features cass-compat => 35 passed / 0
failed / 0 filtered out, including all three bd-8nqz.5 receipt tests by name.
scripts/check_feature_matrix.sh --mode validate => PASS ("cass-compat resolves Tantivy and excludes
Quill"). cargo fmt --check, git diff --check, ubs (0 critical) clean. Commit hooks: ledger selfcheck
52/52, leakcheck 2/2, gatecheck 9/9, mergecheck 3/3. python3 yaml.safe_load parses ci.yml.

ONE FALSE ALARM I CHASED SO NOBODY ELSE DOES: a mid-run `clippy --features quill --all-targets`
reported E0308 in frankensearch-quill's lib. It is NOT a real red — this is a shared checkout and a
peer was mid-edit in crates/frankensearch-quill/src/keeper.rs; `cargo check -p frankensearch-quill`
exits 0 now. Nothing filed.

FOUND, NOT FIXED, NOT MINE: under cass-compat the facade's open_lexical_reader resolves to the
`not(any(lexical, quill))` stub and returns Ok(None) even though Tantivy is compiled in, so
open_hybrid reports no lexical arm on that lane. That is backend-SELECTION semantics, owned by
bd-8nqz.4's deterministic-selection contract, not import hygiene. Not filed as a separate bead
because it may be intentional — cass-compat is documented as a namespace-compatibility lane for
consumers that drive frankensearch::lexical_tantivy directly, which is exactly what CASS does.
Whoever closes bd-8nqz.4 should confirm that reading is deliberate.

title: Clean-checkout admissible native enriched receipt run for bd-8nqz.4.1
description:
ENVIRONMENTAL PRECONDITION, not missing code. bd-8nqz.4.1 slices 1-8 built and red-proved every
mutation class its acceptance names, but the acceptance also requires CLEAN STRICT-REMOTE tests on
the exact frozen candidate, and that cannot be produced from the shared checkout.

WHY. GauntletProducerBuildIdentity is sealed by the build script from the checkout it compiled in.
In /data/projects/frankensearch that checkout is permanently dirty with concurrent agents' work, so
source_git_dirty=true. The receipt assembled there LOADS (integrity holds: manifests, engine
identities, producer identity and every verdict replay) and is correctly INADMISSIBLE by its own
VerifiedNativeEnrichedReceiptV1::require_release_admissible(). That is the right answer, which is
exactly why it cannot stand in for the clean run.

WHAT IS NEEDED: build and run the witness from a checkout that is clean at the candidate SHA, so
the sealed producer reports source_git_dirty=false and source_verification=GitCheckoutVerified,
then assemble a both-engines receipt and record its address.

    cargo test -p frankensearch-quill-gauntlet --features tantivy-oracle \
        --test native_enriched_witness_live

A `git archive` export is NOT sufficient: with no .git present the build script reports the
revision as "unavailable", which validate_recorded_producer_source only accepts together with
source_dirty=true. A linked worktree at the candidate SHA, or a CI lane, does satisfy it.

COST TO WEIGH BEFORE PICKING A WORKTREE: a second source path against the shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR
forces a full rebuild and thrashes the target dir every other agent is using, and this repo already
carries a worktree-sprawl rationalization effort. A CI lane is probably the cheaper instrument.

ACCEPTANCE: a receipt whose require_release_admissible() returns Ok, produced by a binary whose
sealed identity is clean and whose source revision equals the frozen candidate SHA, with its
content address recorded here. bd-8nqz.4.1 closes against that address.

comments.text:
ADOPTED (ubuntu, in_progress). Waiting on the prepared clean clone path + pinned revision. Four
constraints the clone must satisfy, posted BEFORE the pin so it does not have to be redone.

1. PIN AT 1ef51ff0 OR LATER. Earlier revisions cannot satisfy this bead:
     917be00b   first revision where the both-engines assembly test exists at all
     1ef51ff0   adds the address/admissibility EMITTER -- without it the run proves admissibility
                and records nothing, which is the one thing this bead asks for
   Anything older than 917be00b has no such test; anything between the two runs but emits no address.

2. THE FEATURE IS LOAD-BEARING, not a nicety. require_release_admissible() refuses a receipt with
   both_engines_observed=false, and that flag is only true under the Tantivy arm. The exact command:

     cargo test -p frankensearch-quill-gauntlet --features tantivy-oracle \
         --test native_enriched_witness_live a_both_engines -- --nocapture

   A default-feature run is GREEN and INADMISSIBLE, which is the trap: it looks like a pass.

3. .git MUST BE PRESENT AND THE TREE CLEAN. The producer identity is sealed by the build script from
   the checkout it compiles in. A `git archive` export reports the revision as "unavailable", which
   validate_recorded_producer_source accepts only together with source_dirty=true -- so an export is
   green and still inadmissible. A clone or linked worktree at the pinned SHA gives
   source_git_dirty=false and source_verification=GitCheckoutVerified. Do not let any tool write into
   the tree between checkout and build (a formatter or a stray artifact re-dirties it).

4. HARVEST THESE FIVE LINES from stdout; they are the deliverable:
     NATIVE_ENRICHED_RECEIPT_ADDRESS=<64 hex>
     NATIVE_ENRICHED_RECEIPT_PRODUCER_REVISION=<40 hex>
     NATIVE_ENRICHED_RECEIPT_PRODUCER_DIRTY=false
     NATIVE_ENRICHED_RECEIPT_SOURCE_VERIFICATION=GitCheckoutVerified
     NATIVE_ENRICHED_RECEIPT_ADMISSIBLE=yes

BASELINE FROM THE SHARED TREE, recorded so the clean result is checkable rather than merely
asserted. Run here at 5eb995d5 just now:
  ADDRESS=9d283b3445b042ac24f2c1d9d65af62c416acc1af4acdad8cca74d0aa70dde31
  PRODUCER_REVISION=5eb995d524705ef8b17834e9ce005125179b9af2 DIRTY=true
  SOURCE_VERIFICATION=GitCheckoutVerified
  ADMISSIBLE=no reason=receipt producer provenance is dirty

THE CLEAN ADDRESS MUST DIFFER FROM THAT BASELINE, and if it does not, something is wrong. The
producer's revision, dirty flag and executable digest are all inside the domain-separated hashed
body, so a genuinely clean run at a different revision CANNOT reproduce 9d283b34... An identical
address would mean the receipt was not rebuilt from the clean tree.

WHAT I WILL DO WITH IT: verify the five lines, record the address on this bead and on bd-8nqz.4.1,
close 4snp4, then close 4.1 on the slice chain 1-8 plus that address.
